findings.problem: The neighbour table keeps only the six highest-scoring neighbours, sorted by score, so the lowest-scoring neighbours drop out. The DRC table (ISO COD) stops at Congo 5.6 and omits Burundi (5.4), Central African Republic (3.7) and South Sudan (3.4). All three are land neighbours and their scores appear elsewhere on this batch (CAR and South Sudan in the DRC RELATED lines, Burundi in the Congo RELATED line). Germany (DEU) shows the same shape: the table stops at Belgium 8.5 and omits Poland 8.5 and Netherlands 8.4, which appear in its own RELATED lines. China (CHN) shows six rows out of 14 land neighbours. Result: a traveller sees the neighbourhood as safer than it is, because the worst neighbours are hidden.
findings.expected: Show every land neighbour that has an official score (or at least not drop the lowest ones). Do not sort or truncate the neighbour table by score, so that the riskiest neighbours stay visible.
findings.verification: opus: src/lib/neighbors.ts getNeighbors sorts real borders by score and does .slice(0, 6). COD has 9 borders: Burundi 5.4, CAR 3.7 and South Sudan 3.4 are dropped. CAR and South Sudan then turn up in COD's RELATED lists instead. DEU drops France 8.1, Netherlands 8.4 and Poland 8.5. CHN shows Bhutan, Mongolia and other high scorers but hides Afghanistan 3.6, Myanmar 4.1, Russia 4.1, North Korea 4.8 and Pakistan 5.1. The cap removes the riskiest neighbours.

findings.quote: TITLE: Ist Antarktis sicher? Unvollständige Datenlage (2026)
findings.problem: The title pattern 'Ist {Name} sicher?' drops the article for feminine and plural names. ATA: 'Ist Antarktis sicher?' and H1 'nach Antarktis zu reisen?'. ATF: 'Ist Französische Süd- und Antarktisgebiete sicher?' (H1 'nach Französische Süd- und Antarktisgebiete'). BES: 'Ist Karibische Niederlande sicher?'. BVT: 'Ist Bouvetinsel sicher?'. CXR: 'Ist Weihnachtsinsel sicher?'. FRO: 'Ist Färöer sicher?' (H1 'nach Färöer'). The H1s also use 'nach' with these territories, where German uses 'in die' or 'auf die'.
findings.expected: ATA: 'Ist die Antarktis sicher?' and H1 'Ist es aktuell sicher, in die Antarktis zu reisen?'. ATF: 'Sind die Französischen Süd- und Antarktisgebiete sicher?'. BES: 'Sind die Karibischen Niederlande sicher?'. BVT: 'Ist die Bouvetinsel sicher?'. CXR: 'Ist die Weihnachtsinsel sicher?'. FRO: 'Sind die Färöer sicher?'.
findings.verification: opus: Verified: 'Ist Antarktis sicher?', 'Ist Französische Süd- und Antarktisgebiete sicher?', 'Ist Karibische Niederlande sicher?', 'Ist Bouvetinsel sicher?', 'Ist Weihnachtsinsel sicher?', 'Ist Färöer sicher?', each with an H1 using 'nach ...'. Countries such as CHE, GBR, NLD and COM already get articles and number agreement, so territories are missing from the German grammar table. The broken grammar is in TITLE and H1.

findings.quote: Ist Norfolkinsel sicher?
findings.problem: Article missing in TITLE and H1: NFK „Ist Norfolkinsel sicher?“ and „nach Norfolkinsel zu reisen?“; HKG „Ist Sonderverwaltungsregion Hongkong sicher?“; MAC „Ist Sonderverwaltungsregion Macau sicher?“. Norfolkinsel and Sonderverwaltungsregion are feminine and need 'die'.
findings.expected: 'Ist die Norfolkinsel sicher?' (H1 with 'auf die Norfolkinsel zu reisen' reads more naturally for an island); 'Ist die Sonderverwaltungsregion Hongkong sicher?'; 'Ist die Sonderverwaltungsregion Macau sicher?'
findings.verification: opus: NFK, HKG and MAC TITLE/H1 read 'Ist Norfolkinsel sicher?' and 'Ist Sonderverwaltungsregion Hongkong/Macau sicher?' with no article and 'nach …' in the H1. These are feminine nouns that need 'die' (and 'Hongkong'/'Macau' alone would be more natural). Because it is in the TITLE/H1, severity is raised.

findings.quote: the lowest-rated is exposure to natural hazards: 2.3 out of 10 on the INFORM scale, where 10 is the highest exposure
findings.problem: On the stated scale 2.3 is low exposure, yet the sentence names it the weakest area. The same happens on 14 scored pages with values under 5 (CHE 2.3, DNK 2.2, EST 1.6, AUT 2.5, ARM 'The main concern is exposure to natural hazards: 3.6 out of 10'). DZA reads 'The main concern is poor access to health care: 3.9 out of 10 on the INFORM scale, where 10 is the worst access', the same inversion on the access scale. The INFORM figure also rarely matches the pillar shown on the same page (ALB: 'exposure to natural hazards: 5.4 out of 10' beside 'Natural hazards 5.8/10').
findings.expected: Quote the pillar score for the main concern; use the INFORM value only when it is high on its own scale, and say 'low exposure' when it is low.
findings.verification: opus: On CHE the SUMMARY says 'All five areas score at least 7 out of 10; the lowest-rated is exposure to natural hazards: 2.3 out of 10 ...', a low-exposure value presented as the weakness. DZA calls 3.9/10 'poor access to health care' and ARM calls 3.6 'the main concern'. The INFORM-vs-pillar mismatch on ALB (5.4 vs 5.8) is two different scales, not an error.

findings.quote: Voyager au Guinée-Bissau
findings.problem: One country-preposition lookup gives the wrong article for four names, which breaks TITLE and SUMMARY. GNB: TITLE 'Voyager au Guinée-Bissau : est-ce sûr ? 6.0/10 (2026)' and SUMMARY 'Pour un voyage au Guinée-Bissau' (Guinée-Bissau is feminine, so 'en'); the COMPARISON HEADING and Q3 repeat 'au Guinée-Bissau'. KOR: TITLE 'Voyager au Corée du Sud : est-ce sûr ? 8.1/10 (2026)' and SUMMARY 'Pour un voyage au Corée du Sud' (should be 'en Corée du Sud'). MKD: TITLE 'Voyager au Macédoine du Nord : est-ce sûr ? 7.6/10 (2026)' and SUMMARY 'Pour un voyage au Macédoine du Nord' (should be 'en Macédoine du Nord'). MAF: TITLE 'Voyager au Saint-Martin : est-ce sûr ? Données partielles (2026)', and HERO and COMPARISON HEADING 'au Saint-Martin' (should be 'à Saint-Martin').
findings.expected: 'Voyager en Guinée-Bissau', 'Voyager en Corée du Sud', 'Voyager en Macédoine du Nord', 'Voyager à Saint-Martin', with the matching 'Pour un voyage en/à ...' and 'Comment la sécurité en/à ... se compare-t-elle'. Fix the gender and preposition entries for these four places in the lookup.
findings.verification: opus: The TITLE lines read verbatim 'Voyager au Guinée-Bissau', 'Voyager au Corée du Sud' and 'Voyager au Macédoine du Nord', with matching 'Pour un voyage au ...' in the SUMMARY; MAF reads 'Voyager au Saint-Martin'. All are wrong: it should be 'en' for the first three and 'à Saint-Martin'. JEY 'Voyager au Jersey' (should be 'à Jersey') has the same bug.

findings.quote: Ist Britisches Territorium im Indischen Ozean sicher?
findings.problem: German needs the article and an inflected adjective: 'das Britische Territorium im Indischen Ozean' (neuter). The H1 reads „Ist es aktuell sicher, nach Britisches Territorium im Indischen Ozean zu reisen?“ (no article, uninflected adjective, 'nach' for a territory). The same bare form is in the DESCRIPTION, the COMPARISON HEADING („Wie sicher ist Britisches Territorium …“), and the FAQ („… über Britisches Territorium …“). Compare the correct „Sind die Marshallinseln sicher?“ on MHL.
findings.expected: TITLE 'Ist das Britische Territorium im Indischen Ozean sicher?'; H1 'Ist es aktuell sicher, in das Britische Territorium im Indischen Ozean zu reisen?'
findings.verification: opus: TITLE, H1, DESCRIPTION and COMPARISON heading on IOT all use the bare, uninflected 'Britisches Territorium im Indischen Ozean' with 'Ist …' and 'nach …'. This is ungrammatical German in the TITLE/H1.

findings.quote: Ist Nördliche Marianen sicher?
findings.problem: 'Nördliche Marianen' is plural, so the verb must be 'Sind', and the article is missing. The H1 („Ist es aktuell sicher, nach Nördliche Marianen zu reisen?“) and the COMPARISON HEADING („Wie sicher ist Nördliche Marianen …“) repeat the error. The same site renders 'Sind die Malediven sicher?' (MDV) and 'Sind die Marshallinseln sicher?' (MHL) correctly.
findings.expected: 'Sind die Nördlichen Marianen sicher?'; H1 'Ist es aktuell sicher, in die Nördlichen Marianen zu reisen?'; heading 'Wie sicher sind die Nördlichen Marianen …'
findings.verification: opus: MNP TITLE says 'Ist Nördliche Marianen sicher?' and H1 says 'nach Nördliche Marianen zu reisen'. Plural with a singular verb and no article is ungrammatical, while MDV and MHL get 'Sind die …' right.

findings.quote: Ist Palästinensische Autonomiegebiete sicher?
findings.problem: Ungrammatical in TITLE and H1: 'Ist' with a plural name and no article. The page repeats the errors: H1 'nach Palästinensische Autonomiegebiete zu reisen?' (wrong preposition for the plural area and wrong adjective ending); COMPARISON HEADING 'Wie sicher ist Palästinensische Autonomiegebiete im Vergleich …'; SUMMARY 'Die Sicherheitsbewertung für Palästinensische Autonomiegebiete'; FAQ 'Nein — Palästinensische Autonomiegebiete zählt derzeit …' and 'Die stärkste Säule von Palästinensische Autonomiegebiete ist …'.
findings.expected: Sind die Palästinensischen Autonomiegebiete sicher? / in die Palästinensischen Autonomiegebiete zu reisen? / Wie sicher sind die Palästinensischen Autonomiegebiete … / Die Palästinensischen Autonomiegebiete zählen … / Die stärkste Säule der Palästinensischen Autonomiegebiete ist …
findings.verification: opus: PSE.de has 'Ist Palästinensische Autonomiegebiete sicher?' (TITLE), 'nach Palästinensische Autonomiegebiete zu reisen?' (H1), 'Wie sicher ist Palästinensische Autonomiegebiete im Vergleich ...', 'Nein — Palästinensische Autonomiegebiete zählt' and 'Säule von Palästinensische Autonomiegebiete'. A plural name with no article and the wrong verb number is ungrammatical German in TITLE and H1.

findings.quote: Voyager au Géorgie du Sud : est-ce sûr ? Données partielles (2026)
findings.problem: Wrong gender and preposition in TITLE. 'Géorgie du Sud' is feminine, so it takes 'en'. The same error recurs in HERO and COMMUNITY ('Avez-vous déjà voyagé au Géorgie du Sud ?'). Other TITLE errors in the batch: SMR 'Voyager au Saint-Marin : est-ce sûr ?' (should be 'à Saint-Marin'), SPM 'Voyager au Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon' (should be 'à Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon'), and SLV 'Voyager en El Salvador' (usual French is 'au Salvador').
findings.expected: Voyager en Géorgie du Sud ; Voyager à Saint-Marin ; Voyager à Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon ; Voyager au Salvador (verify the usual form against the French editor's style guide).
findings.verification: opus: TITLE really reads 'Voyager au Géorgie du Sud' (feminine, needs 'en'), as do 'Voyager au Saint-Marin' and 'Voyager au Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon' (cities/islands without article take 'à'). The community block repeats 'au Géorgie du Sud'. SLV's 'en El Salvador' is also non-standard French ('au Salvador').

findings.quote: Ist Salomonen sicher?
findings.problem: Salomonen is a plural country name used without an article, so the TITLE 'Ist Salomonen sicher?' and the H1 'nach Salomonen zu reisen?' are ungrammatical. The FAQ repeats it: 'Salomonen ist für die meisten Reisenden ausreichend sicher', 'Die stärkste Säule von Salomonen ist …', 'Für Salomonen sticht kein einzelner Faktor …'.
findings.expected: Sind die Salomonen sicher? / in die Salomonen zu reisen? / Die Salomonen sind für die meisten Reisenden ausreichend sicher / Für die Salomonen sticht kein einzelner Faktor …
findings.verification: opus: SLB.de TITLE reads 'Ist Salomonen sicher?' and the H1 reads 'nach Salomonen zu reisen?'. The FAQ has 'Für Salomonen sticht kein einzelner Faktor'. A native speaker would write 'Sind die Salomonen sicher?' and 'auf die Salomonen / zu den Salomonen'.

findings.quote: Voyager au Cité du Vatican : est-ce sûr ? Données partielles (2026)
findings.problem: 'Cité' is feminine, so 'au Cité' is wrong in the page TITLE. The same error recurs in DESCRIPTION, H1, COMPARISON HEADING ('au Cité du Vatican'), the FAQ answers ('concernant Cité du Vatican') and the community prompt ('au Cité du Vatican').
findings.expected: 'Voyager à la Cité du Vatican : est-ce sûr ?' (or 'Voyager au Vatican'), with the article fixed everywhere it appears.
findings.verification: opus: VAT.fr TITLE is exactly 'Voyager au Cité du Vatican : est-ce sûr ? Données partielles (2026)'. 'Au Cité' is a gender error: it should be 'à la Cité du Vatican' or 'au Vatican'. The error is also in the comparison heading and the community prompt ('Avez-vous déjà voyagé au Cité du Vatican'). The H1 and DESCRIPTION do not contain it, so the finding overstates where it appears.

findings.quote: Ja, mit etwas Vorsicht — Kuba ist für die meisten Reisenden ausreichend sicher
findings.problem: The first FAQ verdict is set from the score band and ignores the advisories on the same page. CUB: verdict 'ausreichend sicher', but SUMMARY counts 13 'überdenken' and 2 'nicht reisen' out of 19, and the FAQ says 'Die vorherrschende Empfehlung lautet, eine Reise nach Kuba zu überdenken'. BHR: verdict 'Ja, mit etwas Vorsicht — Bahrain ist für die meisten Reisenden ausreichend sicher' versus 13 'überdenken' and 4 'nicht reisen' out of 23. ARE: 'Ja, im Allgemeinen — Vereinigte Arabische Emirate gelten als sicheres Reiseziel' versus 10 'überdenken' and 1 'nicht reisen' out of 21.
findings.expected: Verdict and advisory summary must agree. Use 'Ja' only when the prevailing advisory is normal or raised caution; otherwise use a cautious or 'Reise überdenken' verdict.
findings.verification: opus: CUB: FAQ 'Ja, mit etwas Vorsicht — Kuba ist für die meisten Reisenden ausreichend sicher', while SUMMARY counts 13 überdenken + 2 nicht reisen of 19 and FAQ 3 says the prevailing advice is to reconsider. BHR (13+4 of 23) and ARE ('Ja, im Allgemeinen ... sicheres Reiseziel', 7.3 'niedriges Risiko', 10+1 of 21) are the same. The score barely reacts when most governments are at level 3. The verdict template should also check the advisory majority.

findings.quote: keine stuft es über einen Hinweis niedriger Stufe hinaus ein
findings.problem: Clumsy, machine-like German in the standard advisory sentence, used on dozens of pages. It hides the real maximum level (see GAB).
findings.expected: '... und keine Regierung stuft es höher als auf der niedrigsten Warnstufe ein.'
findings.verification: opus: The sentence appears on 124 de pages, and on GAB.de it is factually false. The same page says '7 empfehlen erhöhte Vorsicht, 2 raten, die Reise zu überdenken, und 1 rät von allen Reisen ab', and the advisory list includes Poland at Stufe 3 'Unikaj podróży'. Yet the FAQ says 'Die meisten Regierungen empfehlen ... nur normale Vorsicht, und keine stuft es über einen Hinweis niedriger Stufe hinaus ein', and 'die meisten' is used for exactly 10 of 20. The real problem is reassurance that misstates the advisory consensus, not the clumsy German, so I upgraded it to a high-severity contradiction.

findings.quote: Das Gesamtbild ist beruhigend: Die meisten Regierungen empfehlen für Grenada nur normale Vorsicht, und keine stuft es über einen Hinweis niedriger Stufe hinaus ein.
findings.problem: The FAQ3 template says no government rates the place above the lowest notice level, but on 22 pages the same page's SUMMARY lists elevated advisories. GRD SUMMARY: „13 empfehlen normale Vorsicht und 6 empfehlen erhöhte Vorsicht“; KAZ: „9 empfehlen erhöhte Vorsicht“; GRC: „2 empfehlen erhöhte Vorsicht“; IRL: „1 empfiehlt erhöhte Vorsicht“. The reassurance is false on all 22 pages (GRC, GRD, IRL, ISL, ITA, JPN, KAZ, KIR, KNA, KOR, LCA, LTU, LUX, LVA, MHL, MKD, MNE, MNG, MUS, NAM, NLD, NOR).
findings.expected: Use the 'keine über normale Vorsicht' sentence only when the SUMMARY counts for erhöhte Vorsicht, Reise überdenken and von allen Reisen abraten are all zero. Otherwise state the split, e.g. 'Die meisten Regierungen empfehlen normale Vorsicht, sechs empfehlen erhöhte Vorsicht.'
findings.verification: opus: GRD FAQ3 has the quoted sentence while its SUMMARY says 6 of 19 recommend erhöhte Vorsicht. seo.ts buildAdvisoryAnswer chooses the 'normal' copy from the modal level alone, so the 'keine stuft es … hinaus' clause appears on 124 de pages. That includes pages with Level 3/4 advisories: GAB (2 überdenken, 1 von allen Reisen ab), BWA, SUR, SYC, SLB, STP.

findings.quote: Ja, mit etwas Vorsicht — Jordanien ist für die meisten Reisenden ausreichend sicher
findings.problem: The 'Ja' verdict follows the score band, but the same page's advisory answer says the predominant recommendation is to reconsider the trip. JOR FAQ3: „Die vorherrschende Empfehlung lautet, eine Reise nach Jordanien zu überdenken“; SUMMARY: 9 erhöhte Vorsicht, 13 'überdenken', 2 'von allen Reisen ab' of 24. Same pattern on ISR ("Ja, mit etwas Vorsicht — Israel ist für die meisten Reisenden ausreichend sicher"; 11 überdenken + 6 von allen Reisen ab of 23) and KWT ("Ja, mit etwas Vorsicht — Kuwait …"; 14 + 3 of 21).
findings.expected: No unqualified 'Ja' when a majority of advisories says reconsider or do not travel. The verdict should carry the advisory split, e.g. 'Ja, mit Vorsicht — die meisten Regierungen raten jedoch, die Reise zu überdenken.'
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on JOR FAQ1, and the same page's FAQ3 says 'Die vorherrschende Empfehlung lautet, eine Reise nach Jordanien zu überdenken'. ISR and KWT have the same split (moderate-band 'Ja … ausreichend sicher' against a reconsider-majority). The verdict template follows only the score band and ignores the advisory consensus.

findings.quote: Hauptrisiko: Gesundheit (4.2)
findings.problem: On 37 pages the DESCRIPTION's 'Hauptrisiko' names a pillar that is not the lowest displayed pillar (ignoring asterisked low-coverage pillars). GIN names Gesundheit 4.2 while PILLAR BARS show Regierungsführung 2.7/10 and FAQ1 says „vor allem Regierungsführung (2.7/10) den Wert nach unten ziehen“. KAZ names Naturgefahren 6.4 with Regierungsführung at 3.9; JOR names Konflikt 6.7 with Naturgefahren at 5.7; GUY names Kriminalität 5.9 with Naturgefahren at 5.7. The rule also flips: governance is the named Hauptrisiko on HUN, LTU, MDV, MKD, MLT and MNE. MOZ names Konflikt 5.5 as 'Hauptrisiko' and in FAQ1 as „Die stärkste Säule von Mosambik ist Konflikt (5.5/10)“.
findings.expected: One documented rule for 'Hauptrisiko' (e.g. the lowest pillar with sufficient coverage), applied to every page. DESCRIPTION, PILLAR BARS and FAQ1 must name the same pillar, and a pillar cannot be both the strongest and the main risk.
findings.verification: opus: Verified examples: GIN 'Hauptrisiko: Gesundheit (4.2)' while bars show Regierungsführung 2.7 with no asterisk; KAZ names Naturgefahren 6.4 while Regierungsführung is 3.9; JOR names Konflikt 6.7 while Naturgefahren is 5.7; MOZ names Konflikt 5.5 as Hauptrisiko and its FAQ1 calls it the strongest pillar. HUN and MKD do name governance. The pick rule is inconsistent and does not follow the bars.

findings.quote: Am meisten Aufmerksamkeit verdient ein Klima von Gewalt und Unsicherheit
findings.problem: A vague phrase stands in for the main risk on 7 pages: ISR and IRQ („Das größte Risiko ist ein Klima von Gewalt und Unsicherheit“); JOR, KWT, KEN, LBY and MEX („Am meisten Aufmerksamkeit verdient ein Klima …“). It names no indicator or pillar score, and it is attached to GPI values near the peaceful end of the 1–5 scale: KWT 1,81 („1 (am friedlichsten)“), JOR 1,91. The sibling phrase „mangelnde öffentliche Sicherheit“ (7 pages, e.g. KGZ 2,05, LKA 2,13, LSO 2,33) has the same problem.
findings.expected: Name the pillar and the score the page already reports (e.g. 'Kriminalität 6.3/10') and quote the GPI value with its direction (e.g. '1,81 auf einer Skala von 1 (am friedlichsten) bis 5, also im friedlichen Bereich').
findings.verification: opus: The SUMMARY template names the GPI-overall indicator 'ein Klima von Gewalt und Unsicherheit' even when the attached GPI value is near the peaceful end. Examples: KWT 1,81, JOR 1,91 and QAT 1,68 ('Am meisten Aufmerksamkeit verdient ein Klima von Gewalt und Unsicherheit'). QAT is a 7.4 'niedriges Risiko' country. In the SUMMARY this misrepresents peaceful Gulf states as violent. The sibling 'mangelnde öffentliche Sicherheit' has the same issue with moderate GPI values, e.g. KGZ 2,05.

findings.quote: Das Gesamtbild ist beruhigend: Die meisten Regierungen empfehlen für Salomonen nur normale Vorsicht, und keine stuft es über einen Hinweis niedriger Stufe hinaus ein.
findings.problem: The FAQ3 'beruhigend' sentence appears on exactly the 24 scored pages where 'normale Vorsicht' is the most frequent advisory label (checked: 24 of 24, no exceptions), so the branch is a plurality test. On 20 of those 24 the same page's SUMMARY lists higher advisories, which makes 'keine stuft es über einen Hinweis niedriger Stufe hinaus ein' false: SLB 10 normal / 9 erhöhte / 1 überdenken; SWE 14 / 6; USA 13 / 3; VNM 12 / 9; STP 10 / 6 / 1; NRU 14 / 3; PLW 15 / 2; POL 16 / 3; SUR 9 / 7 / 2; TON 15 / 4; VUT 14 / 5; WSM 15 / 3. 'Die meisten' is also false where normal caution is exactly half (SLB 10 of 20; SUR 9 of 18).
findings.expected: Derive the sentence from the actual split, e.g. 'Von 20 Regierungen empfehlen 10 normale Vorsicht, 9 erhöhte Vorsicht und 1 rät, die Reise zu überdenken.' Use 'beruhigend' and 'keine stuft … ein' only when every advisory is normale Vorsicht, and 'die meisten' only above 50 %.
findings.verification: opus: Confirmed on SLB.de: the summary gives 10 normale Vorsicht, 9 erhöhte Vorsicht and 1 überdenken, yet the FAQ says 'Die meisten ... nur normale Vorsicht, und keine stuft es über einen Hinweis niedriger Stufe hinaus ein'. GAB (2 überdenken, 1 von allen Reisen ab), STP, SUR, SYC and BWA get the same sentence, and 10 of 20 is not 'die meisten'.

findings.quote: Alle fünf Bereiche erreichen mindestens 7 von 10; am niedrigsten bewertet ist die Ausbreitung von Epidemien: 3,2 von 10
findings.problem: NRU, PLW, TUV and TWN say every pillar is at least 7/10, but their own PILLAR BARS contradict this: NRU Regierungsführung 5.4 and Kriminalität 5.7; PLW Regierungsführung 5.4 and Kriminalität 5.7; TUV Regierungsführung 4.7 and Kriminalität 5.7; TWN Naturgefahren 6.2 and Gesundheit 6.7. The FAQ repeats the error: NRU 'Selbst die schwächste Säule, Gesundheit (7.6/10)' and 'insgesamt bewegen sich die fünf Säulen zwischen 7.6/10 und 8.9/10'; PLW 'Selbst die schwächste Säule, Naturgefahren (7.9/10)'; TUV 'Selbst die schwächste Säule, Gesundheit (7.0/10)'; TWN 'Selbst die schwächste Säule, Kriminalität (7.5/10)'. The footnotes on the low bars say low-coverage pillars are reduced or excluded, but the text never says that.
findings.expected: Derive 'mindestens 7' and 'schwächste Säule' from the displayed pillar values and name the actual minimum. If low-coverage pillars are excluded from the claim, say so explicitly. Use 'im risikoarmen Bereich' only when the minimum supports it.
findings.verification: opus: The NRU.de SUMMARY says 'Alle fünf Bereiche erreichen mindestens 7 von 10', but its bars show Regierungsführung 5.4 and Kriminalität 5.7, and the FAQ calls Gesundheit 7.6 the 'schwächste Säule'. PLW, TUV and TWN (Naturgefahren 6.2, Gesundheit 6.7) behave the same way. Low-coverage pillars are silently dropped from the claim.

findings.quote: The overall picture is reassuring: most governments advise only normal precautions for Gabon, and none currently raises it above a low-level advisory.
findings.problem: 26 of the 27 scored pages that carry this sentence have at least one government above normal precautions in their own SUMMARY counts. GAB: 7 advise increased caution, 2 reconsidering travel and 1 advising against all travel, yet the FAQ says none is above a low-level advisory. For GAB and BWA (1 reconsidering) the statement is plainly false; ALB (8 increased caution) and ARG (7) present a split that includes increased caution as reassuring.
findings.expected: Quote the real split from the SUMMARY and drop 'reassuring' and 'none above a low-level advisory' unless no government is above normal precautions.
findings.verification: opus: GAB.en FAQ has the exact sentence. Its own SUMMARY says only 10 of 20 advise normal precautions, with 7 at increased caution, 2 at reconsider and 1 against all travel (Taiwan Level 4 'leave immediately'). So both 'most governments' and 'none above a low-level advisory' are false. The template ignores the actual distribution.

findings.quote: Yes, generally — the United Arab Emirates is considered a safe destination
findings.problem: Q1 gives a safe verdict while Q4 on the same page says 'The prevailing guidance is to reconsider travel to the United Arab Emirates' (ARE: 10 advise reconsidering travel and 1 against all travel, of 21). Same clash on BHR ('Yes, with some caution — Bahrain is reasonably safe for most travelers' vs 'reconsider travel to Bahrain', 17 of 23 at reconsider or worse) and BLR ('Yes, but only with real caution — Belarus carries meaningful risk' vs 'Most governments now advise against all travel to Belarus', 16 of 19 at reconsider or worse). CUB has the same pattern.
findings.expected: Make the verdict agree with the advisory majority on the same page, or explain in the SUMMARY why the band sits above what the advisories suggest.
findings.verification: opus: On ARE, Q1 says 'considered a safe destination' while Q4 says 'The prevailing guidance is to reconsider travel', and the SUMMARY counts 11 of 21 at reconsider or worse. BHR (17/23), CUB (15/19) and BLR (16/19, 12 of them against all travel) show the same verdict-vs-advisory clash on the page.

findings.quote: Generally safe 8 7.6 out of 10 Safety Score
findings.problem: A standalone rounded digit sits between the verdict and the score (ALB, BIH, CHL: '8' for 7.6; AFG: 'Not recommended 4 3.6 out of 10'). If it is a badge it reads as a stray number in running text; if not, it is a stray placeholder.
findings.expected: Remove the digit or give it an accessible label so it is not read as text.
findings.verification: opus: Not a stray placeholder. ScoreHero.astro shows country.scoreDisplay (Math.round(score)) as the giant 6xl/8xl number, with '7.6 out of 10' in smaller type below it. ALB's hero headline number is '8' for a 7.6 (a different band: ≥8 = very low risk), and AFG's is '4' for 3.6. The most prominent number on the page disagrees with the real score.

findings.quote: the area that needs the most attention is health, at 4.2/10
findings.problem: On 41 of the 65 full-score pages the DESCRIPTION 'Top concern' is not the lowest pillar, and on 37 the FAQ 2 'needs the most attention' pillar differs from the 'above all by' pillar in FAQ 1. In 38 of those 41 the skipped pillar is governance, which is the lowest bar. GIN: PILLAR BARS show Governance 2.7/10 below Health 4.2/10, yet FAQ 1 says health is pulled down 'above all by governance (2.7/10)' while FAQ 2 and the DESCRIPTION ('Top concern: health (4.2).') name health. HTI: DESCRIPTION says 'Top concern: conflict (3.2).' while the bars show Governance 2.4/10, and the [B21] boilerplate ('Another area to watch is governance, at #/#.') sits under the 'main concern is conflict' answer, so the lowest pillar is called 'another area to watch'. NIC: FAQ 2 names crime (6.3/10) as the area needing most attention, but FAQ 1 names governance (1.7/10) as the largest drag on the same page.
findings.expected: One rule applied on every page: the top concern and the 'needs the most attention' pillar are the lowest-scoring pillar (or the rule is stated and applied to governance as well). DESCRIPTION, SUMMARY, FAQ 1 and FAQ 2 must name the same pillar. A 4.2/10 pillar should not be called the area needing most attention when a 2.7/10 pillar sits on the same page.
findings.verification: opus: GIN: bars Governance 2.7 < Health 4.2, FAQ1 says 'above all by governance (2.7/10)' while FAQ2/DESCRIPTION name health and FAQ2 says 'No single factor stands out as critical'. NIC (governance 1.7 vs FAQ2 crime 6.3) and HTI ('Another area to watch is governance, at 2.4/10' under 'main concern is conflict, 3.2') match too. Cause: selectDriverPillar (country-summary.ts) picks the direct-risk pillar with the largest weighted drag and leaves governance out, while the FAQ1 'normal' template uses the plain lowest pillar.

findings.quote: A: Yes, with some caution — Israel is reasonably safe for most travelers:
findings.problem: The verdict says Israel is 'reasonably safe for most travelers' with 'some caution', but the same page's SUMMARY counts 17 of 23 governments advising reconsidering travel (11) or against all travel (6), and FAQ 3 calls 'reconsider travel' the prevailing guidance. JOR has the same split (13 reconsider and 2 against of 24; 'Yes, with some caution — Jordan is reasonably safe for most travelers') and KWT too (14 reconsider and 3 against of 21; 'Yes, with some caution — Kuwait is reasonably safe for most travelers'). On a safety question the headline verdict contradicts the advisory majority the same page summarises.
findings.expected: When most advisories say reconsider or do not travel, the verdict should say so, or explain the gap between the score band and the advisories. Keep the verdict, SUMMARY and FAQ 3 consistent on each page.
findings.verification: opus: ISR: 'Yes, with some caution — Israel is reasonably safe for most travelers' sits beside a SUMMARY where 11 of 23 governments advise reconsidering travel and 6 advise against all travel, and FAQ3 says 'The prevailing guidance is to reconsider travel'. JOR (13+2 of 24) and KWT (14+3 of 21) show the same split. The score band (6.0 and 6.9, Moderate) does not reflect a majority of reconsider/do-not-travel advisories.

findings.quote: The main concern is a climate of violence and insecurity: the Global Peace Index scores the country 1.81 on a scale from 1 (most peaceful) to 5 (GPI 2026).
findings.problem: The qualifier ignores the number. On a scale where 1 is most peaceful, 1.81 (KWT) and 1.91 (JOR) sit at the peaceful end, yet the sentence calls it 'a climate of violence and insecurity'. Seven pages use that phrase with values 1.81 to 3.12 (IRQ, ISR, JOR, KEN, KWT, LBY, MEX). Seven others say 'poor public safety' for GPI safety-and-security values of 2.05 to 2.70 on a 1 (safest) to 5 scale (GUY, KGZ, LKA, LSO, MRT, NAM, NIC). On JOR and KWT the DESCRIPTION's 'Top concern' is conflict (6.7/10), which is not even the lowest bar.
findings.expected: Choose the qualifier from the value and the scale direction (a 1.8 on a 1-to-5 most-peaceful scale is at the peaceful end; 2.0 to 2.7 is mid-scale), or state only the value and the scale. Use 'main concern' only for the pillar that is actually lowest.
findings.verification: opus: The KWT SUMMARY really says 'The main concern is a climate of violence and insecurity: the Global Peace Index scores the country 1.81 on a scale from 1 (most peaceful) to 5', and JOR says 1.91. Pages in the corpus use the phrase for values as low as 1.68. 'Poor public safety' is used for GPI safety-and-security values from 1.98 up. The qualifier is fixed text that does not depend on the value.

findings.quote: Top concern: crime (6.0).
findings.problem: The 'Top concern' label in DESCRIPTION (and the 'main concern' sentence in SUMMARY) often names a pillar that is not the lowest in PILLAR BARS. NPL: crime 6.0 vs governance 5.1, and the same page's FAQ calls governance the 'above all' drag. THA: 'Top concern: conflict (6.3)' is its highest pillar. TUR: conflict 6.7 vs governance 3.1. UGA: health 4.8 vs governance 3.3. USA: crime 6.9 vs natural hazards 5.4. Very low risk pages get labels too, e.g. POL 'Top concern: governance (7.3)'.
findings.expected: Name the lowest pillar, or omit the label when every pillar is at least 7. Use one selection rule across DESCRIPTION, SUMMARY and FAQ.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on NPL's DESCRIPTION. The 'Top concern' pillar is not the lowest bar: NPL names crime 6.0 though governance is 5.1, and its own FAQ Q1 says governance is the 'above all' drag. THA names conflict 6.3, its highest pillar, and the same FAQ answer also calls conflict its strongest pillar. TUR names conflict 6.7 (governance 3.1), USA crime 6.9 (natural hazards 5.4), TCD conflict 4.7 (governance 1.6). Yet ROU, SRB and POL do name governance, so one rule is not applied consistently.

findings.quote: All five areas score at least 7 out of 10; the lowest-rated is the spread of epidemics: 3.2 out of 10 on the INFORM scale
findings.problem: Self-contradictory: it says all areas score at least 7, then names a 'lowest-rated' area at 3.2 on a different scale (INFORM, where 10 is worst). The bars contradict it too: NRU governance 5.4 and crime 5.7; TUV governance 4.7 and crime 5.7. The same template gives indicator values that read as pillar scores: POL 'weak governance: 4.2 out of 10' while its governance pillar is 7.3; ROU 'weakest area is weak governance: 4.9 out of 10' while its pillar is 5.9.
findings.expected: Use 'at least 7' only when every bar is at least 7, and name the lowest pillar with its bar value. Keep INFORM or V-Dem values out of the pillar sentence, or label them as indicators on their own scale.
findings.verification: opus: The NRU SUMMARY quote is verbatim, and the bars show governance 5.4* and crime 5.7*. TWN says 'at least 7' with bars of 6.2* and 6.7*. The template seems to skip low-coverage pillars but still shows them in the bars. It also names an indicator on another scale as the 'lowest-rated' area: POL 'weak governance: 4.2 out of 10' beside a governance bar of 7.3.

findings.quote: The overall picture is reassuring: most governments advise only normal precautions for the Seychelles, and none currently raises it above a low-level advisory.
findings.problem: Hard-coded template that contradicts the page's own advisory counts whenever a government advises reconsidering travel: SYC (1 in SUMMARY), SUR (2), STP (1), SLB (1). On SLB, 10 of 20 advisories is half, not 'most'. 'Low-level' is undefined, and the claim 'none raises it above a low-level advisory' also sits oddly beside 'increased caution' counts such as SWE 6 and SRB 7.
findings.expected: Build the sentence from the counts: give the number advising normal precautions and the highest level in use. Drop 'reassuring' whenever any government advises reconsidering travel or not travelling.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is verbatim on SYC. The same sentence appears on SYC, SUR, STP and SLB, whose SUMMARYs list 1, 2, 1 and 1 governments advising reconsidering travel (a level-3 advisory). So 'none currently raises it above a low-level advisory' is false. On SLB, 10 of 20 is not 'most'. The sentence is on 124 en pages.

findings.quote: The main concern is a climate of violence and insecurity: the Global Peace Index scores the country 1.81 on a scale from 1 (most peaceful)
findings.problem: The same template sentence is used on five pages. Each quotes a GPI overall score on the page's own 1 (most peaceful) to 5 scale, whose midpoint is 3. KWT (1.81) and JOR (1.91) sit in the more peaceful half; KEN (2.45) and IRQ (2.66) are also below the midpoint, and only ISR (3.12) is above it. KWT's own GPI safety-and-security row is 1.69 and its UCDP conflict deaths are 0, so the sentence contradicts the numbers printed next to it and tells travellers the main risk is violence when the page's data do not show it.
findings.expected: Use the 'climate of violence' wording only when the GPI overall score is above the midpoint or a violence indicator supports it; otherwise state the main driver actually shown on the page, or use a neutral sentence.
findings.verification: opus: Confirmed on KWT, which says 'climate of violence' while showing GPI overall 1.81 (normalized 0.73), GPI safety 1.69 and 0 UCDP deaths. The conflict pillar (6.7) is pulled down by the advisory consensus (14 reconsider, 3 do not travel), which selectPillarDriver cannot describe, so it falls back to GPI overall and calls a fairly peaceful score violent. JOR (1.91) has the same flaw. IRQ (2.66) and ISR (3.12) are fair uses.

findings.quote: All five areas score at least 7 out of 10; the lowest-rated is the spread of epidemics
findings.problem: False on Nauru (NRU). The same template makes the same false claim on Palau (PLW: 'All five areas score at least 7 out of 10; the lowest-rated is exposure to natural hazards'). The PILLAR BARS on both pages show Governance 5.4/10 and Crime 5.7/10. selectDriverPillar in src/lib/country-summary.ts only considers pillars with enough coverage, but the allGood copy in src/i18n/country-summary-copy.ts hard-codes 'All five areas', so the sentence names the lowest of the covered pillars (on Nauru Health 7.6, not the lowest shown).
findings.expected: Either say the three areas with enough data score at least 7/10 and name the lowest of those, or include the low-coverage pillars in the claim and name the true lowest pillar.
findings.verification: opus: The NRU and PLW summaries both say 'All five areas score at least 7 out of 10', but their own pillar bars show Governance 5.4/10 and Crime 5.7/10. The headline claim is false on the page that carries it.

findings.quote: The main concern is armed conflict
findings.problem: On 12 of the 18 scored pages that name a main concern, the SUMMARY names a theme that is not the lowest pillar in PILLAR BARS. Examples: THA names armed conflict, but Conflict 6.3/10 is its highest pillar and Governance 4.4/10 its lowest. SWZ and SLV say 'poor public safety' while Governance is their lowest pillar (3.6 and 3.3) and Crime is 6.0 and 6.6. The 'poor public safety' sentence is applied to GPI safety scores of 2.35 to 2.82, which the page's own Crime bar rates 5.8 to 6.6 out of 10, i.e. mid-scale.
findings.expected: Name the weakest pillar (or the indicator driving it) from the same data shown in PILLAR BARS, and drop the sentence when the data does not support it.
findings.verification: opus: THA SUMMARY says 'The main concern is armed conflict' but its PILLAR BARS put Conflict 6.3/10 highest and Governance 4.4/10 lowest. SWZ and SLV name 'poor public safety' while Governance (3.6, 3.3) is far below Crime (6.0, 6.6), yet ROU, SRB and SVK do name governance, so the selection is inconsistent across pages.

findings.quote: All five areas score at least 7 out of 10; the lowest-rated is poor public safety
findings.problem: The sentence says all five areas are at 7.0 or above, but the PILLAR BARS on the same page show lower bars. TWN: Natural hazards 6.2 and Health 6.7, both with zero indicator rows (dataCompleteness 0). TUV: Governance 4.7 (coverage 0.25) and Crime 5.7 (zero indicator rows). TUV's 'lowest-rated' is also an indicator (epidemic risk 4.5 on a higher-is-worse scale), not a pillar. Cause: country-summary.ts selectDriverPillar() falls back to the 'allGood' frame using only pillars with coverage >= 0.30, so uncovered pillars are ignored, while driverAllGood in country-summary-copy.ts hard-codes 'All five areas'. Any page where covered direct-risk pillars are all 7.0+ and an uncovered pillar is lower gets the same false claim.
findings.expected: Write 'All five areas' only when every displayed pillar is at 7.0 or above. Otherwise name the lowest displayed pillar, mark uncovered pillars as no data, and never call an indicator a pillar.
findings.verification: opus: TUV and TWN SUMMARY both say 'All five areas score at least 7 out of 10', but TUV's bars show Governance 4.7 and Crime 5.7, and TWN's show Natural hazards 6.2 and Health 6.7. TWN also calls public safety the 'lowest-rated' area while its crime bar (7.5) is above two other bars, and TUV names an INFORM indicator (4.5 epidemics) as 'lowest-rated' while its Health bar is 7.0.

findings.quote: El panorama general es tranquilizador: la mayoría de los gobiernos solo recomiendan precauciones normales para Gabón y ninguno lo sitúa por encima de un aviso de bajo nivel.
findings.problem: Template sentence in the advisories answer says no government rates the country above the lowest advisory level. On 26 pages the SUMMARY of the same page counts governments advising 'extremar la precaución' (some also 'reconsiderar' or 'desaconsejan todo viaje'), so the reassurance contradicts the page's own numbers. GAB: SUMMARY has 7 extremar, 2 reconsiderar, 1 desaconseja todo viaje. BEL: 8 extremar. CPV: 8 extremar. BWA: 7 extremar and 1 reconsiderar. Also ALB, ARG, ATG, AUS, AUT, BGR, BIH, BRB, BRN, BTN, CAN, CHE, CYP, DEU, DMA, DNK, ESP, EST, FIN, FJI, FSM, GBR. BEL's FAQ also says 'bastan las precauciones normales de sentido común' [B14] while 8 governments advise extremar.
findings.expected: Derive the advisory sentence from the breakdown: do not say no government is above the lowest level when any government advises extremar la precaución or worse; state the counts instead of 'tranquilizador'.
findings.verification: opus: GAB.es FAQ Q3 has the exact sentence, while SUMMARY lists 7 extremar, 2 reconsiderar, 1 desaconseja, and the advisory list shows Nivel 3 (Polonia, Irlanda) and Nivel 4 (Taiwán). ALB (8 extremar), DEU (5 extremar) and BRN (2 extremar) use the same reassurance, so the template ignores the breakdown.

findings.quote: Sí, pero solo con verdadera precaución — Bielorrusia presenta un riesgo considerable
findings.problem: The verdict is 'Sí' while the same page's advisories answer says a majority of governments advise against all travel. BLR: verdict 'Sí, pero solo con verdadera precaución'; advisories answer 'La mayoría de los gobiernos desaconsejan ya todo viaje a Bielorrusia' (12 of 19 per SUMMARY). CUB: verdict 'Sí, con cierta precaución — Cuba es un destino razonablemente seguro para la mayoría de los viajeros' vs 'La recomendación predominante es reconsiderar el viaje a Cuba' (13 reconsiderar, 2 desaconsejan). ARE: verdict 'Sí, en general — ... se considera un destino seguro' vs predominant 'reconsiderar' (10 of 21). BHR: verdict 'razonablemente seguro para la mayoría' vs predominant 'reconsiderar' (13 of 23). The verdict appears to follow the score band alone, not the advisories.
findings.expected: The verdict must reflect the advisory picture: cap the wording when the predominant advice is reconsider or the majority advise no travel, or reconcile the two answers on the page.
findings.verification: opus: BLR verdict is 'Sí, pero solo con verdadera precaución' while SUMMARY says 12 of 19 governments advise against all travel and Q3 says most advise against all travel. CUB ('razonablemente seguro', 13 of 19 reconsiderar plus 2 no viajar) and ARE ('se considera un destino seguro', 10 reconsiderar plus 1 no viajar of 21) contradict their own advisory answers in the same way.

findings.quote: Ningún factor destaca como crítico en Azerbaiyán: el área que requiere más atención es salud, con 6.6/10.
findings.problem: The main-risk pillar named in DESCRIPTION ('Mayor riesgo') and FAQ Q2 is not the lowest pillar in PILLAR BARS on 34 of 63 scored pages (BWA and CPV are exact ties), and FAQ Q1 on the same page names another pillar as the one that drags the score most ('y, sobre todo, por ...'). AZE: governance is 2.9/10 and Q1 says it drags most, yet Q2 and DESCRIPTION name health (6.6/10) and SUMMARY names epidemics. BGD: Q1 governance 3.5/10 vs Q2 criminalidad 5.7/10. CHN: Q1 governance 4.3/10 vs Q2 criminalidad 6.0/10. AFG: Q1 governance 1.8/10 vs 'La principal preocupación en Afganistán es conflicto, con 3.0/10'. BRA: DESCRIPTION 'Mayor riesgo: conflicto (6.2)' while criminalidad is 5.7/10. Governance is the lowest pillar on 35 scored pages, and DESCRIPTION names it on only 4 (BGR, BIH, CYP, CZE).
findings.expected: One rule for weakest/main risk used identically by DESCRIPTION, SUMMARY and FAQ Q1/Q2, consistent with the PILLAR BARS ranking. If governance is excluded from 'risk', say so on the page.
findings.verification: opus: AZE: PILLAR BARS show Gobernanza 2.9 as the lowest pillar, yet DESCRIPTION and Q2 name salud 6.6 as the main risk and Q2 says no factor is critical. GAB names criminalidad 5.6 although gobernanza 4.6 and salud 5.2 are lower, and its Q1 says governance drags the score most. The main-risk rule skips governance without saying so.

findings.field: DESCRIPTION 'Mayor riesgo' vs PILLAR BARS and FAQ
findings.quote: Mayor riesgo: salud (4.2).
findings.problem: The DESCRIPTION's 'Mayor riesgo' pillar is not the lowest bar on 41 of the 65 scored pages (37 with no low-coverage footnote; governance is the lowest unfootnoted bar in 35 of those 37). GIN: bars read 'Gobernanza 2.7/10 | Salud 4.2/10' and FAQ A1 says 'sobre todo, por gobernanza (2.7/10)', yet the DESCRIPTION and FAQ A2 name salud. Same pattern: NIC 'Mayor riesgo: criminalidad (6.3).' with 'Gobernanza 1.7/10'; GTM 'Mayor riesgo: criminalidad (6.0).' with 'Gobernanza 5.0/10'. Cause (src/): country-summary.ts selectDriverPillar keeps governance out of DIRECT_RISK_PILLARS (line 136) and ranks by weight x -ln(score); seo.ts:262 reuses it for the DESCRIPTION and seo.ts:849 for FAQ A2, while FAQ A1 uses the lowest eligible pillar (seo.ts:836). One page therefore carries two 'weakest' definitions. Rebuilt from the batch's rounded bar values, the rule reproduces 64 of 65 DESCRIPTION picks.
findings.expected: One definition of the main risk per page, consistent with the bars: name the lowest pillar, or say openly that governance is a structural score and not a risk driver. Never print a 'Mayor riesgo' that the page's own bars contradict.
findings.verification: opus: GIN DESCRIPTION 'Mayor riesgo: salud (4.2).' while bars show Gobernanza 2.7 and FAQ A1 says 'sobre todo, por gobernanza (2.7/10)'. NIC (crime 6.3 vs gobernanza 1.7 and riesgos naturales 5.0) and GTM have the same mismatch. The page uses two different 'weakest' definitions.

findings.field: FAQ A1 verdict vs FAQ A3 advisories
findings.quote: Israel es un destino razonablemente seguro para la mayoría de los viajeros
findings.problem: The verdict reads 'Sí, con cierta precaución' with 'razonablemente seguro para la mayoría de los viajeros' on ISR, JOR and KWT, but the same page's FAQ A3 says the predominant advice is to reconsider travel ('La recomendación predominante es reconsiderar el viaje a Israel'). ISR: 11 reconsider and 6 do not travel, of 23 governments; JOR: 13 and 2, of 24; KWT: 14 and 3, of 21. The verdict and the modal advisory level point in opposite directions on the same page.
findings.expected: Let the verdict respect the modal advisory level, or state the conflict in the verdict sentence (e.g. 'con cierta precaución; la mayoría de los gobiernos aconseja reconsiderar el viaje').
findings.verification: opus: ISR, JOR and KWT FAQ A1: 'Sí, con cierta precaución — ... razonablemente seguro para la mayoría de los viajeros', while A3 says 'La recomendación predominante es reconsiderar el viaje'. ISR has 11 reconsider and 6 do not travel, of 23.

findings.quote: Mayor riesgo: conflicto (5.4).
findings.problem: On 34 of the 64 scored pages, the 'Mayor riesgo' value in DESCRIPTION and the FAQ sentence 'el área que requiere más atención' name a pillar that is not the lowest on that page. The FAQ 'se ve lastrada por ... y, sobre todo, por ...' sentence and PILLAR BARS name the true lowest pillar (governance is the weakest in 30 of the 34). VEN: bars 'Gobernanza 1.5/10', FAQ 'sobre todo, por gobernanza (1.5/10)', yet DESCRIPTION says 'Mayor riesgo: conflicto (5.4)'. Same pattern: TJK criminalidad 6.8 vs gobernanza 2.3; PRK conflicto 4.8 vs gobernanza 2.4; ZWE salud 5.6 vs gobernanza 3.0; PHL conflicto 6.1 vs gobernanza 3.7; OMN salud 6.9 vs riesgos naturales 5.1.
findings.expected: Name the lowest-scoring pillar as the main risk, or state in the methodology that governance is excluded from the ranking; use the same pillar in DESCRIPTION, SUMMARY, FAQ and PILLAR BARS.
findings.verification: opus: VEN DESCRIPTION says 'Mayor riesgo: conflicto (5.4)' while bars show Gobernanza 1.5 and the FAQ says 'sobre todo, por gobernanza (1.5/10)'; OMN says salud 6.9 while Riesgos naturales 5.1 and Gobernanza 5.8 are lower. The main-risk picker skips pillars, so different fields on the same page name different main risks.

findings.quote: Ningún factor destaca como crítico en San Vicente y las Granadinas: el área que requiere más atención es criminalidad, con 4.0/10.
findings.problem: 46 of 64 scored pages answer 'cuál es el mayor riesgo' with 'Ningún factor destaca como crítico', and 43 of those also name a 'principal riesgo' or 'principal preocupación' in the SUMMARY. VCT is the sharpest case: its SUMMARY says 'El principal riesgo es la delincuencia violenta', while the FAQ calls its 4.0/10 criminalidad pillar not critical. Same on UGA ('Ningún factor destaca como crítico en Uganda: ... salud, con 4.8/10') and ZAF (criminalidad 4.5/10). A reader gets two opposite answers on the same page.
findings.expected: Keep one answer. If the SUMMARY names a main risk, or any pillar is below 5/10, drop 'Ningún factor destaca como crítico' and name the risk with its score.
findings.verification: opus: VCT FAQ says 'Ningún factor destaca como crítico... criminalidad, con 4.0/10' while its SUMMARY says 'El principal riesgo es la delincuencia violenta'. UGA (salud 4.8) and ZAF (criminalidad 4.5) do the same, and VEN even has gobernanza 1.5. A pillar in the danger band gets called non-critical.

findings.quote: ninguno lo sitúa por encima de un aviso de bajo nivel
findings.problem: 20 scored pages say 'la mayoría de los gobiernos solo recomiendan precauciones normales ... y ninguno lo sitúa por encima de un aviso de bajo nivel', while their own SUMMARY counts governments recommending extremar la precaución and/or reconsiderar el viaje: VNM (9 extremar), SLB (9 extremar and 1 reconsiderar), SUR (7 extremar and 2 reconsiderar), SYC (3 extremar and 1 reconsiderar). Also NRU, PLW, POL, PRT, SGP, SRB, STP, SVN, SWE, TON, TUV, URY, USA, VCT, VUT, WSM.
findings.expected: Use the SUMMARY counts (for example 'nueve gobiernos recomiendan extremar la precaución') and say 'ninguno' only when no issuer is above precauciones habituales.
findings.verification: opus: VNM, SLB and SUR all say 'ninguno lo sitúa por encima de un aviso de bajo nivel'. Their SUMMARYs count 9 extremar (VNM), 9 extremar + 1 reconsiderar (SLB) and 7 extremar + 2 reconsiderar (SUR). The FAQ understates the advisories.

findings.quote: Las cinco áreas obtienen al menos un 7 sobre 10
findings.problem: On NRU, PLW, TUV and TWN the SUMMARY says all five areas score at least 7/10, and the FAQ says the five pillars sit between 7.6 and 8.9 (NRU), 7.9 and 8.9 (PLW), 7.0 and 8.9 (TUV) and 7.5 and 8.5 (TWN), and that no pillar signals significant risk. PILLAR BARS show Gobernanza 5.4 and Criminalidad 5.7 (NRU, PLW), Gobernanza 4.7 and Criminalidad 5.7 (TUV), Riesgos naturales 6.2 and Salud 6.7 (TWN). The asterisk 'poca cobertura' note does not make these claims true. The FAQ 'lastrada' sentences on TON, STP, WSM and VUT never mention their asterisked pillars, which are the lowest bars on those pages.
findings.expected: Claim that all areas are at least 7 only when every bar is 7 or more. For low-coverage pillars show 'datos insuficientes' instead of a number, and name them in the FAQ when they are the weakest.
findings.verification: opus: NRU SUMMARY says 'Las cinco áreas obtienen al menos un 7 sobre 10' while its bars show Gobernanza 5.4* and Criminalidad 5.7*. TWN says the same while showing Riesgos naturales 6.2* and Salud 6.7*. The claim leaves out low-coverage pillars that are still shown with numbers.

findings.quote: Le tableau d'ensemble est rassurant : la plupart des gouvernements ne recommandent que des précautions normales pour Belgique
findings.problem: The template adds 'et aucun ne le place au-dessus d'un avis de faible niveau', which is false when the SUMMARY breakdown shows governments recommending 'vigilance renforcée' (above normal precautions). On 20 of the 27 non-partial pages that carry this sentence, the SUMMARY breakdown shows that: BEL (8 of 19 'vigilance renforcée'), ALB (8 of 20), CYP (6 of 20), BIH (7 of 19), GAB (7 'vigilance renforcée', 2 'sauf raison impérative', 1 'déconseille formellement tout voyage'). A reassurance the page's own numbers do not support.
findings.expected: Generate the sentence from the same counts as the SUMMARY (e.g. '8 gouvernements sur 19 recommandent une vigilance renforcée'), and never call the advisory picture reassuring when any government advises against non-essential travel.
findings.verification: opus: BEL: 8 of 19 governments say 'vigilance renforcée'. GAB: 7 say vigilance renforcée, 2 'sauf raison impérative' and 1 'déconseille formellement tout voyage'. Both pages still say 'aucun ne le place au-dessus d'un avis de faible niveau'. On GAB this is plainly false on a safety-relevant point.

findings.quote: La consigne dominante est de reconsidérer tout voyage aux Émirats arabes unis
findings.problem: A 'yes' verdict is followed by an advisory line saying the dominant advice is to reconsider all travel. ARE: 'Oui, en général — Émirats arabes unis est une destination considérée comme sûre' (band 'risque faible', HERO 'Généralement sûr'), yet SUMMARY shows 10 governments advising against non-essential travel and 1 against all travel out of 21. Same on BHR ('Oui, avec quelques précautions — Bahreïn est une destination raisonnablement sûre pour la plupart des voyageurs'; 17 of 23 governments advise against non-essential or all travel) and CUB ('Oui, avec quelques précautions — Cuba est une destination raisonnablement sûre'; 15 of 19).
findings.expected: Make the Oui/Non verdict and the HERO band follow the advisory consensus, or state explicitly that the country is safe for most travellers although most governments advise against non-essential travel. The verdict lines must not give opposite messages.
findings.verification: opus: ARE answers 'Oui, en général … considérée comme sûre' (HERO 'Généralement sûr', 7.3). Its own SUMMARY lists 10 governments advising against non-essential travel and 1 against all travel out of 21. latest.json confirms level 3 from the US, Canada, Germany, Ireland and Belgium, and level 4 from Singapore. BHR and CUB show the same clash: a 'Oui' verdict next to 'La consigne dominante est de reconsidérer tout voyage'. The verdict and the advisory consensus give opposite messages.

findings.quote: Équateur ne présente aucun facteur véritablement critique
findings.problem: Template sentence on 49 pages that contradicts the same page's SUMMARY when the SUMMARY names a main risk. ECU SUMMARY: 'Le principal risque est la criminalité violente : 45,7 homicides pour 100 000 habitants (Banque mondiale, 2023).' The FAQ then says there is no truly critical factor. Same on BHS ('Le principal risque est la criminalité violente : 32,2 homicides' vs 'Bahamas ne présente aucun facteur véritablement critique'), COL ('Le principal point de vigilance est le conflit armé : 612 personnes' vs 'Colombie ne présente aucun facteur véritablement critique') and BLR (12 governments 'déconseillent formellement tout voyage' vs 'Biélorussie ne présente aucun facteur véritablement critique').
findings.expected: Do not write 'aucun facteur véritablement critique' when the SUMMARY names a principal risque. Name that same risk in the FAQ, and keep the 'no critical factor' line only for pages with no named main risk.
findings.verification: opus: ECU SUMMARY: 'Le principal risque est la criminalité violente : 45,7 homicides pour 100 000 habitants', with the crime pillar at 4.4/10. Its FAQ opens 'Équateur ne présente aucun facteur véritablement critique'. The template appears on 146 fr pages, including ECU, COL and BLR. Downplaying one of the world's highest homicide rates misleads a safety decision.

findings.quote: ne présente aucun facteur véritablement critique
findings.problem: The sentence 'X ne présente aucun facteur véritablement critique' appears on 51 of the 83 pages in this file, whatever the pillar or advisory picture. It is contradicted on the same page in several cases: NIC (Gouvernance 1.7/10 in the pillar bars), MOZ (Gouvernance 3.4/10), GIN (Gouvernance 2.7/10), GNB (Gouvernance 2.8/10), JAM (SUMMARY: 49,4 homicides per 100 000 inhabitants as the principal vigilance point), KNA (SUMMARY: 64,2 homicides per 100 000 as the principal risk), IRQ (SUMMARY: 16 of 22 governments 'déconseillent formellement tout voyage').
findings.expected: Delete the sentence, or gate it on the data (no pillar below a set threshold and only a minority of advisories saying do not travel). Otherwise name the weakest pillar and its value in the same sentence, e.g. 'La gouvernance, à 1.7/10, est le point le plus faible.'
findings.verification: opus: The sentence appears verbatim on NIC (Gouvernance 1.7), GIN (Gouvernance 2.7) and KNA (64,2 homicides). On IRQ it appears even though 16 of 22 governments say do not travel. The sentence is not gated on the data.

findings.quote: La consigne dominante est de reconsidérer tout voyage au Koweït
findings.problem: Answer 1 is the band template 'Oui, avec quelques précautions — X est une destination raisonnablement sûre pour la plupart des voyageurs', but answer 3 on the same page says the dominant advisory is 'reconsidérer tout voyage'. KWT: 14 of 21 governments 'déconseillent le voyage sauf raison impérative' and 3 'déconseillent formellement tout voyage'. ISR: 'La consigne dominante est de reconsidérer tout voyage en Israël' with 11 + 6 of 23 advisories. JOR: 'reconsidérer tout voyage en Jordanie' with 13 + 2 of 24.
findings.expected: The 'Oui ... raisonnablement sûre pour la plupart des voyageurs' verdict is not used where the dominant advisory is 'reconsidérer tout voyage' or stronger; the first and third answers must agree.
findings.verification: opus: Confirmed on three pages: KWT (6.9: 14+3 of 21 reconsider or do not travel), ISR (6.0: 11+6 of 23) and JOR (6.9: 13+2 of 24). All three open with 'Oui, avec quelques précautions — ... raisonnablement sûre pour la plupart des voyageurs' while answer 3 says 'La consigne dominante est de reconsidérer tout voyage'. The verdict is not gated on the advisory consensus, and the scores also look high for that consensus.

findings.quote: Le tableau d'ensemble est rassurant : la plupart des gouvernements ne recommandent que des précautions normales pour Suriname, et aucun ne le place au-dessus d'un avis de faible niveau.
findings.problem: Hard-coded reassurance template. It says 'rassurant' and that no government places the country above a low-level advisory, but the same page's SUMMARY reports advisories that are higher: SUR has 7 'vigilance renforcée' and 2 'déconseillent le voyage sauf raison impérative'. Same contradiction on SLB (9 vigilance renforcée, 1 sauf raison impérative), STP (6 vigilance renforcée, 1 sauf raison impérative) and SRB (7 vigilance renforcée). SGP and SVN have 1 vigilance renforcée each and the same claim.
findings.expected: Make the sentence conditional on the advisory mix: say 'rassurant' only when no government issues anything above 'précautions habituelles'; otherwise name the dominant level and the strictest one, e.g. 'la consigne la plus stricte émane de...'.
findings.verification: opus: Same FAQ sentence appears verbatim on SUR, SLB, STP, SRB, SGP and SVN. On each, SUMMARY lists higher advisories: SUR 7 vigilance renforcée plus 2 'sauf raison impérative', SLB 9 plus 1, STP 6 plus 1, SRB 7, SGP and SVN 1 each. So 'aucun ne le place au-dessus d'un avis de faible niveau' is false.

findings.quote: Risque principal : criminalité (6.8).
findings.problem: The 'Risque principal' in DESCRIPTION, and the FAQ sentence 'le domaine qui demande le plus d'attention est le pilier …' in the 'plus grand risque' answer, name a pillar that is not the lowest one on the same page. The page's own PILLAR BARS and FAQ Q1 show a lower pillar. TJK: bars show 'Gouvernance 2.3/10' while DESCRIPTION and FAQ name criminalité 6.8, and FAQ Q1 says 'surtout par gouvernance (2.3/10)'. Same pattern on TKM (criminalité 6.5 vs gouvernance 2.3), TCD (conflit 4.7 vs gouvernance 1.6 and santé 3.9), TGO (conflit 6.1 vs gouvernance 3.9), TUR (conflit 6.7 vs gouvernance 3.1), TUN (criminalité 5.9 vs gouvernance 5.1), TZA (conflit 5.6 vs santé 5.0) and SWZ (criminalité 6.0 vs gouvernance 3.6).
findings.expected: The 'Risque principal' and 'le plus d'attention' pillar must be the lowest-scoring pillar shown on the page (or the page must explain why it is excluded), and must match Q1's 'surtout par …' pillar.
findings.verification: opus: Checked TJK, TKM, TCD, TGO, TUR, TUN, TZA and SWZ. On each, DESCRIPTION 'Risque principal' and the FAQ 'le plus d'attention' name a pillar that is not the lowest one. Examples: TJK names criminalité 6.8 while the bars show Gouvernance 2.3; TCD names conflit 4.7 while santé 3.9 and criminalité 4.1 are also lower; TZA names conflit 5.6 against santé 5.0. FAQ Q1 on the same pages says 'surtout par gouvernance/santé'. On TUR and THA, conflit is named both as the area needing most attention and as the strongest pillar ('Côté points forts, le pilier conflit arrive en tête').

findings.quote: aucun ne le place au-dessus d'un avis de faible niveau.
findings.problem: The reassuring template sentence ('la plupart des gouvernements ne recommandent que des précautions normales … et aucun ne le place au-dessus d'un avis de faible niveau') contradicts the advisory counts on the same page. SYC SUMMARY says '3 recommandent une vigilance renforcée et 1 déconseille le voyage sauf raison impérative', so one government is above the lowest level. SWE SUMMARY has '6 recommandent une vigilance renforcée' and TON has '4 recommandent une vigilance renforcée'. The sentence is wrong wherever any advisory is above 'précautions habituelles'.
findings.expected: Only state that no government sits above the lowest level when the SUMMARY counts show only 'précautions habituelles'. Otherwise say the highest advisory level and how many issuers use it.
findings.verification: opus: The FAQ sentence 'aucun ne le place au-dessus d'un avis de faible niveau' appears on SYC, SWE, TON and TUV. On SYC the SUMMARY says '3 recommandent une vigilance renforcée et 1 déconseille le voyage sauf raison impérative'. On SWE the SUMMARY says '6 recommandent une vigilance renforcée', on TON 4 and on TUV 3. The sentence is false on every one of these pages and understates the advisories.

findings.quote: Venezuela ne présente aucun facteur véritablement critique : le domaine qui demande le plus d'attention est le pilier conflit, à 5.4/10.
findings.problem: The FAQ2 answer names the pillar that needs most attention as one that is not the lowest. On the same VEN page, governance is 1.5/10 (lowest) and FAQ1 says the score is pulled down 'surtout par gouvernance (1.5/10)'. The same template mismatch appears on USA (FAQ2 'le pilier criminalité, à 6.9/10' while FAQ1 says 'surtout par risques naturels (5.4/10)', the lowest pillar; DESCRIPTION also says 'Risque principal : criminalité (6.9)'), UGA (FAQ2 'pilier santé, à 4.8/10' vs governance 3.3/10 lowest), UZB, ZWE, YEM, VNM and ZMB. 'Aucun facteur véritablement critique' is asserted even when a pillar sits at 1.5/10.
findings.expected: Use the same lowest-scoring pillar in DESCRIPTION, FAQ1 and FAQ2 on each page. Do not claim 'aucun facteur véritablement critique' when a pillar is at 2/10 or below.
findings.verification: opus: Quote is on VEN.fr: FAQ2 names conflict (5.4) and says 'aucun facteur véritablement critique', while FAQ1 on the same page says the score is pulled down 'surtout par gouvernance (1.5/10)', and governance 1.5 is the lowest bar. UGA (FAQ1 'surtout par gouvernance (3.3/10)' vs FAQ2 santé 4.8) and USA (FAQ1 'surtout par risques naturels (5.4/10)' vs FAQ2 criminalité 6.9) show the same pattern. Cause in seo.ts: A1 uses the lowest eligible pillar, but A2 uses selectDriverPillar, which skips governance, and the 'mid' A2 variant claims nothing critical without checking whether a pillar sits at 1.5/10.

findings.quote: aucun ne le place au-dessus d'un avis de faible niveau.
findings.problem: The FAQ3 answer calls the advisory picture 'rassurant' and says no government places the country above a low-level advisory. The same page's SUMMARY reports heightened warnings: VNM '9 recommandent une vigilance renforcée' (of 21), URY '6 recommandent une vigilance renforcée' (of 20), VCT '4 recommandent une vigilance renforcée' (of 14), USA '3 recommandent une vigilance renforcée' (of 16). The template verdict contradicts the counts a traveller is shown.
findings.expected: Describe the actual distribution and the highest advisory level (e.g. 'neuf gouvernements recommandent une vigilance renforcée'). Drop 'rassurant' whenever any government advises heightened vigilance or above.
findings.verification: opus: The template's claim is real: buildAdvisoryAnswer in seo.ts picks the 'normal' sentence from the modal (most common) level alone and never checks maxLevel. In this batch the extra advisories (USA, URY, VNM, VCT) are only Level 2, which is a borderline case. But GAB.fr gets the same 'rassurant… aucun ne le place au-dessus d'un avis de faible niveau' sentence while it lists Level 3 (Poland, Ireland) and Level 4 (Taiwan) advisories, and SUR has Level 3 ones. So the sentence is plainly false on some pages.

findings.quote: Sì, in genere — Emirati Arabi Uniti è una destinazione considerata sicura
findings.problem: The verdict says 'considerata sicura' while the page's own advisories say the prevailing advice is to reconsider travel. ARE: SUMMARY has 10 of 21 governments 'invitano a riconsiderare il viaggio' and 1 'sconsiglia qualsiasi viaggio', and FAQ Q3 says 'L'indicazione prevalente è di riconsiderare il viaggio negli Emirati Arabi Uniti'. Same pattern: BLR 'Sì, ma solo con vera cautela' while 12 of 19 'sconsigliano qualsiasi viaggio' and FAQ Q3 says 'La maggior parte dei governi sconsiglia ormai del tutto i viaggi in Bielorussia'; CUB 'ragionevolmente sicura' with 13 of 19 reconsider and 'L'indicazione prevalente è di riconsiderare il viaggio a Cuba'; BHR 'ragionevolmente sicura' with 13 reconsider and 4 do-not-travel of 23. Understated 'No' verdicts: CAF ('viaggiare richiede grande prudenza') with 18 of 20 'sconsigliano qualsiasi viaggio'; BFA with 14 of 20.
findings.expected: Verdict wording, and the score's advisory modifier, must reflect the advisory consensus; no 'considerata sicura' where the prevailing advice is reconsider or do-not-travel.
findings.verification: opus: ARE: 'Sì, in genere — … considerata sicura' (7.3), while 10 of 21 governments say reconsider plus 1 do-not-travel, and FAQ Q3 says the prevailing advice is to reconsider. BLR answers 'Sì, ma solo con vera cautela' with 12 of 19 do-not-travel. CUB and BHR are 'ragionevolmente sicura' with a majority saying reconsider. These are misleading safety verdicts. The CAF/BFA 'understated' part is rejected: both pages answer 'No — … ad alto rischio', which fits.

findings.quote: Il quadro complessivo è rassicurante: la maggior parte dei governi raccomanda solo precauzioni normali per Gabon e nessuno lo colloca oltre un avviso di basso livello.
findings.problem: The sentence says 'nessuno lo colloca oltre un avviso di basso livello', while GAB's own SUMMARY lists '2 invitano a riconsiderare il viaggio e 1 sconsiglia qualsiasi viaggio'. BWA: SUMMARY has '1 invita a riconsiderare il viaggio' with the same reassurance. The sentence appears on 43 pages, including grey pages where the site says no score is published (ABW: 'Per questa destinazione non possiamo ancora dare un punteggio di sicurezza ufficiale' followed by 'Il quadro complessivo è rassicurante'). Where 'maggiore prudenza' is common (ALB 8 of 20, BEL 8 of 19), 'rassicurante' is an editorial judgement the counts do not support.
findings.expected: Use reassurance wording only when no government advises reconsidering or not travelling, and never on grey pages.
findings.verification: opus: The GAB FAQ says 'nessuno lo colloca oltre un avviso di basso livello', but its own list shows Poland L3, Ireland L3 and Taiwan L4, and only 10 of 20 recommend normal precautions, which is not 'la maggior parte'. BWA shows the same pattern with Taiwan L3. The sentence is factually false. The grey-page sub-claim (ABW: 7 of 8 at L1) is weak, but the core problem is real.

findings.quote: La principale criticità è un clima di violenza e insicurezza: il Global Peace Index assegna al paese 1,81 su una scala da 1 (massima pace) a 5 (GPI 2026).
findings.problem: The GPI value cited as the main criticality sits in the better half of the 1-5 scale (1 = most peaceful): Kuwait 1.81, Jordan 1.91 ('La principale criticità è un clima di violenza e insicurezza ... 1,91 ...'), Kyrgyzstan 2.05 ('La principale criticità è la scarsa sicurezza pubblica: il Global Peace Index valuta sicurezza e protezione 2,05 ...'), Guyana 2.70. About 14 pages use this main-risk sentence (IRQ, ISR, JOR, KEN, KWT, LBY, MEX, GUY, KGZ, LKA, LSO, MRT, NAM, NIC). The 'scarsa sicurezza pubblica' variant also lacks the preposition ('valuta ... a 2,05') and places '(GPI 2026)' after the scale.
findings.expected: Do not call a GPI value below 3 the main criticality. Either show what the number means ('il GPI è 1,81 su 5, tra i paesi più pacifici') or name the pillar that actually drives the score. Fix 'valuta ... a' and move '(GPI 2026)' before the scale.
findings.verification: opus: KWT SUMMARY calls 'un clima di violenza e insicurezza' the main issue and backs it with GPI 1,81 on a 1-5 scale where 1 is most peaceful. JOR does the same with 1,91, and KGZ cites 2,05 for 'scarsa sicurezza pubblica'. These numbers show peacefulness, not a problem, so the SUMMARY misleads. The finding's count is slightly off: ISR uses the 'Il rischio principale' variant with 3,12, which is a real concern. 'valuta ... 2,05' is acceptable Italian, so that part is not an issue.

findings.quote: La principale criticità è la scarsa sicurezza pubblica
findings.problem: On 43 pages the SUMMARY opens its main-risk sentence with 'La principale criticità è' or 'Il rischio principale è', while FAQ Q2 on the same page says 'Nessun singolo fattore emerge come critico per X'. Examples: NPL (SUMMARY 'La principale criticità è la scarsa sicurezza pubblica' vs FAQ 'Nessun singolo fattore emerge come critico per Nepal'), NZL (SUMMARY 'La principale criticità è l'esposizione ai rischi naturali' vs FAQ 'Nessun singolo fattore emerge come critico per Nuova Zelanda'), PHL (SUMMARY 'La principale criticità è il conflitto armato' vs FAQ 'Nessun singolo fattore emerge come critico per Filippine').
findings.expected: One verdict per page from one rule: name the main risk in SUMMARY and FAQ Q2 (for example 'Il rischio principale è X, con v/10'), or when no pillar is critical say so in both places.
findings.verification: opus: The NPL, NZL and PHL SUMMARY lines open with 'La principale criticità è …', and on the same pages FAQ Q2 says 'Nessun singolo fattore emerge come critico per …'. Both name the same pillar, but they disagree on whether anything is critical. The worst case is TCD (4.3/10, 'Non raccomandato', Governance 1.6): its Q2 still says 'Nessun singolo fattore emerge come critico per Ciad'.

findings.quote: Rischio principale: criminalità (6.0)
findings.problem: On 34 pages the DESCRIPTION 'Rischio principale: X (v)' names a different pillar from the one FAQ Q1 says weighs most ('più di tutto, Y (v/10)'). In all 34 pages Y is the lowest bar on the page and X is a higher pillar; SUMMARY and FAQ Q2 follow X. Examples: NPL (DESCRIPTION 'Rischio principale: criminalità (6.0)'; PILLAR BARS 'Governance 5.1/10'; Q1 'più di tutto, governance (5.1/10)'), PHL (DESCRIPTION 'Rischio principale: conflitto (6.1)'; bars 'Governance 3.7/10'; Q1 'più di tutto, governance (3.7/10)'), TJK (DESCRIPTION 'Rischio principale: criminalità (6.8)'; bars 'Governance 2.3/10'; Q1 'più di tutto, governance (2.3/10)').
findings.expected: Use one definition of main risk for DESCRIPTION, SUMMARY, FAQ Q1 and FAQ Q2 (for example the lowest or most-weighted pillar, stated as the rule), so the snippet, the summary and the FAQ name the same pillar with the same value.
findings.verification: opus: Checked on the pages. NPL: DESCRIPTION 'Rischio principale: criminalità (6.0)', Q1 'più di tutto, governance (5.1/10)'. PHL: 'conflitto (6.1)' while Governance is 3.7 and Rischi naturali 3.8. TJK: 'criminalità (6.8)' while Governance is 2.3. The snippet's main risk ignores much lower pillars, which is misleading in search results.

findings.quote: nessuno lo colloca oltre un avviso di basso livello
findings.problem: On 20 pages FAQ Q3 says 'Il quadro complessivo è rassicurante' and 'nessuno lo colloca oltre un avviso di basso livello', while the SUMMARY of the same page counts governments that 'raccomandano maggiore prudenza' or invite to reconsider or advise against travel. Examples: NRU (SUMMARY '3 raccomandano maggiore prudenza'), PLW ('2 raccomandano maggiore prudenza'), SGP ('1 raccomanda maggiore prudenza'). SLB (10 of 20 advisories normal) and SUR (9 of 18) also say 'la maggior parte dei governi raccomanda solo precauzioni normali', which is not a majority.
findings.expected: Generate Q3 from the counts: use 'la maggior parte' only when normal advisories exceed half, use 'nessuno ... oltre' only when no government is above normal, and otherwise state the counts (for example 'tre governi raccomandano maggiore prudenza').
findings.verification: opus: For NRU, PLW and SGP (level-2 issuers only) it is arguable whether level 2 counts as a 'basso livello' advisory. The claim is plainly false elsewhere: SLB (1 says reconsider, only 10 of 20 normal), SUR (2 reconsider, 9 of 18 normal) and SYC (1 reconsider) all say 'nessuno lo colloca oltre un avviso di basso livello' and 'la maggior parte … precauzioni normali'.

findings.quote: Tutte e cinque le aree raggiungono almeno 7 su 10
findings.problem: On NRU, PLW, TUV and TWN the SUMMARY says all five pillars reach at least 7/10, and FAQ Q1 says 'Tutti e cinque i pilastri ottengono buoni punteggi' (FAQ Q2 on NRU says 'i cinque pilastri si collocano tra 7.6/10 e 8.9/10'). PILLAR BARS on those pages show two pillars below 7 (NRU Governance 5.4 and Criminalità 5.7; PLW 5.4 and 5.7; TUV 4.7 and 5.7; TWN Rischi naturali 6.2 and Salute 6.7), all marked with the low-coverage asterisk that the claim silently drops. On NRU, PLW, POL, PRT, SGP, SVN, SWE and TUV the same sentence continues 'la più bassa riguarda ...: X su 10 nella scala INFORM, dove 10 indica ...', which puts an inverted INFORM risk figure (SWE '2,5 su 10') straight after 'almeno 7 su 10'.
findings.expected: Compute 'almeno 7' over the pillars that are shown, or state which asterisked pillars are excluded; name the lowest pillar on the same 0-10 safety scale, not an INFORM risk value.
findings.verification: opus: The NRU and PLW SUMMARY says 'Tutte e cinque le aree raggiungono almeno 7 su 10', but the bars show Governance 5.4 and Criminalità 5.7, both asterisked. TWN shows Rischi naturali 6.2 and Salute 6.7. FAQ Q2 on NRU gives 'tra 7.6/10 e 8.9/10'. On SWE, 'la più bassa' is followed by an inverted INFORM figure ('2,5 su 10 … dove 10 indica l'esposizione più alta'), which reads like nonsense next to 'almeno 7'.

findings.quote: la più bassa riguarda la scarsa sicurezza pubblica: il Global Peace Index valuta sicurezza e protezione 1,67
findings.problem: The SUMMARY calls a Global Peace Index safety value at the safe end of its 1-5 scale the main or lowest risk. TWN: 'la più bassa riguarda la scarsa sicurezza pubblica: il Global Peace Index valuta sicurezza e protezione 1,67 su una scala da 1 (massima sicurezza) a 5', while its own pillars read 6.2 to 8.5. QAT: 'La principale criticità è un clima di violenza e insicurezza: il Global Peace Index assegna al paese 1,68 su una scala da 1 (massima pace) a 5', on a page where Criminalità 8.3 is the strongest pillar. TJK: 'La principale criticità è la scarsa sicurezza pubblica ... 1,98'. The adjective is fixed by template: 'scarsa sicurezza pubblica' appears on 14 pages with values from 1,67 to 2,82, and 'clima di violenza e insicurezza' on 7 pages with values from 1,68 to 3,12 (e.g. SAU 2,07).
findings.expected: Choose the wording from the value (a 1.7 on a 1 = safest scale is not 'scarsa'); if the indicator is not in the risky half of its scale, name the weakest pillar instead.
findings.verification: opus: Quotes verified. TWN calls a GPI value of 1,67 (where 1 = safest) 'scarsa sicurezza pubblica'. QAT calls GPI 1,68 'un clima di violenza e insicurezza', and Qatar really is one of the most peaceful countries in the GPI. The adjective is fixed by the template rather than chosen from the value, so a near-best value is presented as the main danger in the SUMMARY.

findings.quote: Sì, sicuro per viaggiare 9 8.5 su 10
findings.problem: The HERO shows an unexplained integer before the score ('Prestare attenzione 7 6.8 su 10' on NPL). For the same displayed 8.5, PRT reads '9 8.5 su 10' while POL and NZL read '8 8.5 su 10'; USA reads '8 7.5 su 10' and VCT '7 6.5 su 10'. The integer looks rounded from unrounded values, so the badge can disagree with the decimal beside it.
findings.expected: Drop the integer, or derive it from the displayed decimal so the same score always shows the same integer.
findings.verification: opus: In ScoreHero.astro the big hero number is country.scoreDisplay, an integer rounded from the raw score, while the line below shows score.toFixed(1). PRT (8.537) shows '9 8.5', NZL (8.496) shows '8 8.5', USA (7.519) shows '8 7.5', VCT (6.505) shows '7 6.5'. The page's largest number therefore disagrees with the title's x.x/10 and differs between countries with the same displayed score.

findings.quote: Sim, mas apenas com cautela real — Bielorrússia apresenta um risco considerável
findings.problem: The Q1 verdict answers 'Sim' from the index alone. On BLR the same page's SUMMARY counts 12 of 19 governments as 'desaconselham qualquer viagem' (plus 4 'reconsiderar a viagem'), and FAQ Q3 says 'A maioria dos governos já desaconselha qualquer viagem à Bielorrússia'. Same mismatch on BHR (Q1 'Sim, com alguma cautela — Barein é um destino razoavelmente seguro para a maioria dos viajantes' vs Q3 'A orientação predominante é reconsiderar a viagem ao Barein'; 17 of 23 governments reconsider or do not travel), CUB (Q1 'Sim, com alguma cautela — Cuba é um destino razoavelmente seguro'; 15 of 19) and ARE (Q1 'Sim, em geral — Emirados Árabes Unidos é um destino considerado seguro'; 11 of 21). On BLR, B23 ('A maioria das viagens corre bem') is attached to the 'Sim' verdict. The verdict follows the index only and ignores the advisory majority that the same page reports.
findings.expected: When most governments advise reconsidering or not travelling, the verdict must reflect it (for example 'Não recomendado' or 'Reconsidere a viagem'), or the verdict sentence must name the split in the same breath. Do not attach 'A maioria das viagens corre bem' to pages where most governments say not to travel.
findings.verification: opus: BLR Q1 says 'Sim, mas apenas com cautela real' and adds B23 'A maioria das viagens corre bem', while the SUMMARY counts 12 of 19 governments as 'desaconselham qualquer viagem' and Q3 says 'A maioria dos governos já desaconselha qualquer viagem'. BHR (13 reconsider + 4 do not travel of 23), CUB (13+2 of 19) and ARE (10+1 of 21) also get 'Sim' verdicts. The verdict follows the index only.

findings.quote: a área que exige mais atenção é a de saúde, com 6.6/10
findings.problem: On 39 of the 62 pages with a 'Maior risco' line, DESCRIPTION, SUMMARY or FAQ name a pillar that is not the lowest bar on the same page (the FAQ's 'área que exige mais atenção' differs from the lowest bar on 35 of 49 pages). AZE: PILLAR BARS 'Governança 2.9/10' is lowest, yet the FAQ names saúde 6.6/10 and DESCRIPTION says 'Maior risco: saúde (6.6)'. AFG: DESCRIPTION 'Maior risco: conflito (3.0).' while 'Governança 1.8/10' is lowest, and boilerplate B22 calls governança only 'também merece atenção'.
