CHN: 'Maior risco: criminalidade (6.0).' while Riscos naturais 4.4/10 and Governança 4.3/10 are lower. CRI contradicts itself: DESCRIPTION and FAQ Q2 say criminalidade (6.7), but Q1 says 'sobretudo, por riscos naturais (5.2/10)', which is the lowest bar. Governança is skipped on some pages and named on others (BGR, CYP and CZE name it), so the selection rule is inconsistent. The cause was not traced in code; a stale or different pillar snapshot, or an undocumented exclusion of low-coverage pillars, would fit the pattern.
findings.expected: One selection rule across DESCRIPTION, SUMMARY and FAQ: name the lowest displayed pillar (including governança), and say explicitly when low-coverage pillars are excluded. Drop 'área que exige mais atenção' and 'também merece atenção' wording where that pillar is the lowest.
findings.verification: opus: AZE DESCRIPTION 'Maior risco: saúde (6.6)' and Q2 name saúde, while the bars show Governança 2.9 and Riscos naturais 5.6, and Q1 on the same page says 'sobretudo, por governança'. CHN names criminalidade 6.0 over Riscos naturais 4.4 and Governança 4.3. CRI Q1 names riscos naturais 5.2 but DESCRIPTION and Q2 name criminalidade 6.7. BGR does name governança, so there is no consistent rule.

findings.quote: O panorama geral é tranquilizador: a maioria dos governos recomenda apenas precauções normais para o Gabão e nenhum o coloca acima de um aviso de baixo nível.
findings.problem: Template sentence that conflicts with the same page's SUMMARY breakdown on 26 scored pages in this batch (ALB, ARG, ATG, AUS, AUT, BEL, BGR, BIH, BRB, BRN, BTN, BWA, CAN, CHE, CPV, CYP, DEU, DMA, DNK, ESP, EST, FIN, FJI, FSM, GAB, GBR). GAB's SUMMARY lists 7 'recomendam cautela redobrada', 2 'recomendam reconsiderar a viagem' and 1 'desaconselha qualquer viagem', yet the FAQ says no government places Gabão above a low-level advisory. BWA (7 cautela redobrada plus 1 reconsiderar), BEL (8 of 19 cautela redobrada) and ALB (8 of 20) are the same. Any government above 'precauções normais' makes 'nenhum o coloca acima de um aviso de baixo nível' false.
findings.expected: Derive the sentence from the highest advisory level in the page's own counts. Drop 'tranquilizador' and the 'nenhum' clause whenever any government advises more than normal precautions.
findings.verification: opus: GAB SUMMARY: 7 cautela redobrada, 2 reconsiderar, 1 desaconselha qualquer viagem. The FAQ still says 'nenhum o coloca acima de um aviso de baixo nível'. BWA has 1 reconsiderar with the same sentence. BEL and ALB (only level 2) are arguable, but GAB and BWA are plainly false.

findings.quote: Maior risco: conflito (5.5).
findings.problem: The 'Maior risco' pick (DESCRIPTION) and the FAQ 'área que exige mais atenção' do not follow the weakest pillar. Across 65 scored pages the named pillar differs from the lowest full-coverage pillar on 37 pages. Governança is the lowest pillar on 41 pages but is named on only 6 (HUN, LTU, MDV, MKD, MLT, MNE). MOZ names conflito (5.5/10) as the biggest risk, yet the same page's FAQ says 'O pilar mais forte de Moçambique é conflito (5.5/10)' while governança is 3.4/10. KHM says 'Maior risco: conflito (6.1)' with governança at 2.5/10, and its FAQ A1 names governança as the 'sobretudo' drag. NIC names criminalidade (6.3) with governança at 1.7/10. The boilerplate B22 then calls a 2.9/10 governança only 'também merece atenção' (LBN). The pattern looks like a fixed pillar order that skips governança rather than a lowest-score rule (inferred from the batch, not checked in code).
findings.expected: Name as the main risk the lowest full-coverage pillar, consistently in DESCRIPTION, SUMMARY and both FAQ answers (Q1 'sobretudo, por X' and Q2 'área que exige mais atenção'). If a low-coverage pillar is excluded, say so. B22 must not downplay a pillar under 3/10.
findings.verification: opus: MOZ DESCRIPTION says 'Maior risco: conflito (5.5)' and FAQ Q2 says 'a área que exige mais atenção é a de conflito, com 5.5/10' and then 'Seu pilar mais forte é o de conflito, com 5.5/10'. Conflict is the highest pillar there, and governança is 3.4. KHM names conflito 6.1 while saúde 5.6, riscos naturais 5.7 and governança 2.5 are all lower. HTI's B22 calls governança 2.4/10 only 'também merece atenção'. So the risk pick does not follow the pillar scores.

findings.quote: O panorama geral é tranquilizador: a maioria dos governos recomenda apenas precauções normais para Granada e nenhum o coloca acima de um aviso de baixo nível.
findings.problem: The FAQ Q3 sentence says no government places the country above a low-level advisory and calls the picture 'tranquilizador'. On 22 scored pages the same page's SUMMARY lists governments advising 'cautela redobrada' (or reconsider / do not travel): GRD 6 of 19, KAZ 9 of 20, NLD 6 of 20, MNG 7 of 19. Those governments sit above the 'precauções normais' tier, so the sentence is false on those pages and reassuring in a way a traveller would act on. 'um aviso de baixo nível' is also not idiomatic pt.
findings.expected: Derive the sentence from the actual split, e.g. 'a maioria recomenda precauções normais, mas 6 de 19 recomendam cautela redobrada'. Use 'nenhum acima' and 'tranquilizador' only when no government advises more than normal precautions.
findings.verification: opus: The in-batch examples (GRD 6/19, etc.) only reach 'cautela redobrada', which can fairly be called low-level, so that part of the argument is weak. But the same template sentence appears on pages where it is plainly false. GAB has 2 governments saying reconsider and 1 saying do not travel, and only 10 of 20 advise normal precautions. BWA, SYC, SLB, STP and SUR also have reconsider-level advisories. On all of these the page still says 'nenhum o coloca acima de um aviso de baixo nível'.

findings.quote: Sim, com alguma cautela — Israel é um destino razoavelmente seguro para a maioria dos viajantes
findings.problem: The verdict 'Sim, com alguma cautela … razoavelmente seguro para a maioria dos viajantes' contradicts the same page's Q3 'A orientação predominante é reconsiderar a viagem'. ISR: 11 governments reconsider and 6 advise against any travel, out of 23. JOR: 13 + 2 of 24. KWT: 14 + 3 of 21. The verdict is the headline answer to 'É seguro viajar…?' and reads as safer than the advisories on the same page.
findings.expected: The verdict must follow the predominant advisory. When most governments advise reconsidering or not travelling, the verdict should not say 'razoavelmente seguro para a maioria dos viajantes'.
findings.verification: opus: ISR's verdict reads 'Sim, com alguma cautela — Israel é um destino razoavelmente seguro para a maioria dos viajantes'. On the same page, 11 governments say reconsider and 6 say do not travel out of 23, and Q3 says 'A orientação predominante é reconsiderar a viagem'. JOR (13+2 of 24) and KWT (14+3 of 21) have the same verdict and the same contradiction.

findings.quote: A principal preocupação é um clima de violência e insegurança: o Global Peace Index dá ao país 1,81 em uma escala de 1 (mais pacífico) a 5
findings.problem: SUMMARY names the GPI signal as 'A principal preocupação' on 12 pages (GUY, JOR, KEN, KGZ, KWT, LBY, LKA, LSO, MEX, MRT, NAM, NIC); IRQ uses 'O principal risco é um clima de violência' with 2,66. Their quoted values run from 1,81 to 2,70 on a 1–5 scale where 1 is 'mais pacífico' or 'mais seguro', so all sit below the scale midpoint of 3. KWT's own figure (1,81, 'mais pacífico') sits next to 'principal preocupação é um clima de violência'. JOR's lowest pillar is riscos naturais (5,7/10), not the GPI signal. The GPI item appears to be picked regardless of its value.
findings.expected: Name a main concern only when it is the lowest-scoring signal and its value is on the unsafe side. Otherwise state the value and the scale direction without a superlative.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on KWT: 'A principal preocupação é um clima de violência e insegurança' with GPI 1,81 (JOR has 1,91), both near the peaceful end. KWT's crime pillar is 7.0 and one of its highest. MEX (2,65) and IRQ (2,66) are genuinely bad GPI values, because the real GPI range is about 1.1 to 3.4. So the reviewer's 'below midpoint 3' reasoning is wrong for those two, but the low-value cases are real.

findings.quote: O principal risco é a criminalidade violenta: 64,2 homicídios por 100 mil habitantes (Banco Mundial, 2023).
findings.problem: On 47 scored pages the SUMMARY says 'O principal risco é…' or 'A principal preocupação é…' while FAQ Q2 says 'Nenhum fator isolado se destaca como crítico' (KNA: 'Nenhum fator isolado se destaca como crítico para São Cristóvão e Nevis'; same on GRC). On IRQ the FAQ says no factor stands out while 16 of 22 governments advise against all travel, and the SUMMARY names 'um clima de violência e insegurança' as the main risk.
findings.expected: Use one framing per page. If the SUMMARY names a main risk, the FAQ should not say no factor stands out. If none stands out, the SUMMARY should not name one.
findings.verification: opus: KNA's SUMMARY says 'O principal risco é a criminalidade violenta: 64,2 homicídios por 100 mil', but its FAQ Q2 says 'Nenhum fator isolado se destaca como crítico para São Cristóvão e Nevis'. IRQ says the same 'nenhum fator isolado' while 16 of 22 governments advise against all travel. Severity raised to high because the IRQ case misleads a safety decision.

findings.quote: Maior risco: criminalidade (6.8)
findings.problem: The 'Maior risco' label (DESCRIPTION, and the FAQ Q2 'área que exige mais atenção') names a pillar that is not the lowest bar on 34 of the 64 covered pages. On 30 of those 34, governança is the lowest unflagged bar and is never named. Examples: TJK bars show 'Governança 2.3/10' and FAQ Q1 says 'sobretudo, por governança (2.3/10)', yet DESCRIPTION and Q2 name criminalidade (6.8). USA names criminalidade (6.9) while its lowest bar is 'Riscos naturais 5.4/10'. THA names conflito (6.3) as the biggest risk although 'Conflito 6.3/10' is its highest bar. On 30 pages, FAQ Q1 ('sobretudo, por X') and Q2 ('área que exige mais atenção é a de Y') name different pillars on the same page.
findings.expected: Derive 'Maior risco' from the same pillar scores the bars show (lowest unflagged pillar) and use that pillar in Q1, Q2, SUMMARY and DESCRIPTION alike. If governança is excluded from 'risk' by design, say so and remove 'sobretudo, por governança' from Q1. The strongest pillar must never be labelled the main risk.
findings.verification: opus: Checked TJK, USA and THA. TJK: DESCRIPTION and Q2 name criminalidade (6.8), but the bars show Governança 2.3, Riscos naturais 6.2 and Saúde 6.6, and Q1 says 'sobretudo, por governança (2.3/10)'. USA names criminalidade 6.9 while Riscos naturais is 5.4. THA names conflito 6.3 as the biggest risk although it is the highest bar and Q1 calls it 'O pilar mais forte'.

findings.quote: Nenhum fator isolado se destaca como crítico para Nova Zelândia
findings.problem: Template contradiction on 43 of the 64 covered pages: the SUMMARY names a main concern ('A principal preocupação é…' or 'O principal risco é…') while FAQ Q2 says 'Nenhum fator isolado se destaca como crítico'. NZL SUMMARY: 'A principal preocupação é a exposição a riscos naturais'; NZL FAQ: 'Nenhum fator isolado se destaca como crítico para Nova Zelândia'. The denial is also false where one pillar sits well below the rest: VCT criminalidade 4.0/10 against 6.8 to 8.7 for its unflagged pillars; SRB governança 4.5/10 against 7.6 to 8.2.
findings.expected: Use one rule for SUMMARY and FAQ: if the SUMMARY names a main concern, the FAQ names the same pillar and does not deny it; if no pillar is clearly lowest, the SUMMARY does not say 'a principal preocupação é'. Remove 'Nenhum fator isolado se destaca como crítico' wherever a pillar sits well below the others.
findings.verification: opus: 'Nenhum fator isolado se destaca como crítico' appears in Q2 even where one pillar is far below the rest: VCT criminalidade 4.0 (51,3 homicides per 100k), SRB governança 4.5 against 7.6 to 8.2, TJK governança 2.3. The NZL wording on its own is mild, but denying a critical factor on these pages is misleading.

findings.quote: As cinco áreas têm pelo menos 7 de 10; a mais baixa é a exposição a riscos naturais: 2,3 de 10 na escala do INFORM, sendo 10 a exposição mais alta
findings.problem: Nine pages open with 'As cinco áreas têm pelo menos 7 de 10' (NRU, PLW, POL, PRT, SGP, SVN, SWE, TUV, TWN). The same sentence then names an INFORM sub-indicator as 'a mais baixa' (the weakest area) although its scale is inverted (10 = worst, so 2,3 is low exposure); 3,2 or 3,8 sits inside a sentence that says every area is at least 7. On NRU, PLW, TUV and TWN the bars also show flagged pillars below 7 (NRU 'Governança 5.4/10 *', 'Criminalidade 5.7/10 *'; TUV 4.7 and 5.7; TWN 6.2 and 6.7), yet the NRU FAQ says 'os cinco pilares variam de 7.6/10 a 8.9/10'.
findings.expected: Name the weakest safety pillar with its own 0-10 safety score (NRU: governança 5.4/10, flagged for low coverage), and quote INFORM values only with their direction, e.g. 'exposição a riscos naturais: 2,3 numa escala INFORM em que 10 é a maior exposição'. Drop 'As cinco áreas têm pelo menos 7 de 10' whenever a bar is below 7.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on PLW, CHE and IRL. NRU, TUV and TWN open with 'As cinco áreas têm pelo menos 7 de 10' while their bars show 5.4/5.7 (NRU), 4.7/5.7 (TUV) and 6.2/6.7 (TWN). The NRU FAQ says 'os cinco pilares variam de 7.6/10 a 8.9/10'. The claim that the INFORM direction is not stated is wrong ('sendo 10 o risco mais alto' is printed), but the contradiction with the bars is real.

findings.quote: O panorama geral é tranquilizador: a maioria dos governos recomenda apenas precauções normais para o Suriname
findings.problem: The same FAQ Q3 template contradicts the SUMMARY on SUR, SYC, STP and SLB. SUR SUMMARY: '9 recomendam as precauções normais, 7 recomendam cautela redobrada e 2 recomendam reconsiderar a viagem', so 'nenhum o coloca acima de um aviso de baixo nível' is false, and 9 of 18 is not 'a maioria'. SYC and STP each have one government recommending reconsidering travel; SLB has 10 of 20 normal (exactly half, not a majority) and one reconsideration.
findings.expected: Use 'tranquilizador' and 'nenhum o coloca acima de um aviso de baixo nível' only when no government advises reconsidering travel and normal precautions are a strict majority. Otherwise state the split, e.g. 'duas autoridades recomendam reconsiderar a viagem'.
findings.verification: opus: The SUR FAQ says 'nenhum o coloca acima de um aviso de baixo nível' and 'a maioria' while the SUR SUMMARY says 9 normal, 7 increased caution and 2 reconsider (9 of 18 is not a majority). SLB has 10 of 20 normal and 1 reconsider and gets the same text. The advisory summary is false and reassuring.

findings.quote: A principal preocupação é um clima de violência e insegurança: o Global Peace Index dá ao país 1,68 em uma escala de 1 (mais pacífico) a 5
findings.problem: The 'main concern' sentence is attached to the GPI value without checking it. QAT's 1,68 sits at the peaceful end of its own scale ('1 (mais pacífico)'), and SAU's 2,07 is also 'mais pacífico'. TJK (1,98) and TKM (2,17) call public insecurity the main concern on a '1 (mais seguro)' scale, and TWN's 'a mais baixa é a insegurança pública' uses 1,67 on the same scale. The main-concern claim is not tied to the pillar scores.
findings.expected: Name a main concern only when the GPI value is in the worse half of its scale; otherwise drop the GPI clause. The main concern should be the weakest pillar from the bars (see the first finding).
findings.verification: opus: QAT SUMMARY: 'A principal preocupação é um clima de violência e insegurança: o Global Peace Index dá ao país 1,68 em uma escala de 1 (mais pacífico) a 5'. The figure cited is near the peaceful end, so the sentence contradicts itself. SAU (2,07) is similar. The main-concern text is not tied to the bars: QAT's lowest bar is Governança 5.9.

findings.quote: Sim, seguro para viajar 9 8.5 de 10
findings.problem: The large integer next to the score is rounded from unrounded values, so one displayed score gets two integers: 8.5 shows '8' on NZL and POL but '9' on PRT; 7.5 shows '7' on SUR but '8' on USA; 6.5 shows '6' on TJK but '7' on VCT. The reader sees '9' beside '8.5 de 10'.
findings.expected: One rule computed on the displayed one-decimal score (for example round half up), so that 8.5 always shows the same integer on every page.
findings.verification: opus: The HERO on PRT.pt reads 'Sim, seguro para viajar 9 8.5 de 10', while NZL and POL show '8 8.5 de 10'. latest.json gives scoreDisplay 9 for PRT (8.5367), 8 for NZL (8.4956) and POL (8.4603), 8 for USA (7.5186) against 7 for SUR (7.4984), and 7 for VCT (6.5052) against 6 for TJK (6.4564). So the big integer is rounded from the raw score and contradicts the one-decimal score shown next to it in the hero.

findings.quote: 对安哥拉而言，没有任何单一因素构成突出风险：最需要关注的领域是健康，得分为4.9/10。
findings.problem: '没有任何单一因素构成突出风险' is hard-wired in the zh 'mid' band (src/lib/country-faq-copy.ts a2.mid, about line 578). On 47 pages the SUMMARY names a main risk on the same page (AGO: '主要风险是就医不便'; BHS: '主要风险是暴力犯罪'). Several answers then add the boilerplate [B18] ('造成这一低分的主要指标是社会安全与治安（全球和平指数）。') right after 'no single factor' (GAB, ERI, CUB), and CHN calls crime at 6.0 a 'low score' through the same clause. The 'biggest risk' question therefore gets two incompatible answers.
findings.expected: When the SUMMARY names a main risk, the FAQ should name the same pillar as the main risk. Reserve 'no single factor stands out' for pages whose SUMMARY also names no main risk.
findings.verification: opus: The Q2 'mid' variant runs for driver pillars from 4.0 to 7.0 (seo.ts weakestBand: critical <4), while the summary frames a pillar under 5.0 as 'mainRisk'. AGO (health 4.9, SUMMARY '主要风险是就医不便') and BHS (crime 4.9, homicide 32.2/100k, SUMMARY '主要风险是暴力犯罪') both get '没有任何单一因素构成突出风险'. The zh wording also drops the English 'as critical' nuance. This is misleading on the 'biggest risk' question.

findings.quote: 对几内亚而言，没有任何单一因素构成突出风险：最需要关注的领域是健康，得分为4.2/10。
findings.problem: On 47 of the 65 scored pages the SUMMARY names a main risk ('最需关注的是…' or '主要风险是…'; GIN: 主要风险是就医不便：INFORM评分为8.1/10，10分最差（INFORM Risk 2026）。) while the FAQ answer to the biggest-risk question says no single factor stands out. The page gives two opposite answers to the question a traveller asks. Examples: GIN, GMB, GRD (SUMMARY 最需关注的是暴力犯罪 vs FAQ no single factor).
findings.expected: Name the same main risk in SUMMARY and FAQ, or say in both that no factor dominates. Drop the 'no single factor' sentence from the template whenever SUMMARY sets a main risk.
findings.verification: opus: GIN FAQ2 says 没有任何单一因素构成突出风险 while the SUMMARY says 主要风险是就医不便 (8.1/10) and governance is 2.7. The same sentence appears on KNA (homicide 64.2 per 100k, 犯罪 4.3) and ISR (conflict 4.1, most governments reconsider or avoid), where it is misleading.

findings.quote: 五个方面的评分均不低于7/10
findings.problem: Stated as fact on NRU, PLW, TUV and TWN, but each page's own PILLAR BARS show a pillar below 7 (NRU: 治理 5.4/10 and 犯罪 5.7/10 marked *; PLW: same; TUV: 治理 4.7/10 * and 犯罪 5.7/10 *; TWN: 自然灾害 6.2/10 * and 健康 6.7/10 *). The FAQ repeats it: NRU says the lowest pillar is 健康 (7.6/10) and the five pillars lie between 7.6 and 8.9; PLW says the five pillars all perform well; TWN says the same with 犯罪 7.5 as lowest. The starred low-coverage pillars are left out of the min/max claim but are still displayed, and the same FAQ attaches B12 (only routine precautions are needed) on all four pages.
findings.expected: Compute min/max and all-good claims only over pillars the reader sees as counted, or state that starred pillars are excluded from these claims. Never write that no pillar is below 7 while a displayed bar is below 7.
findings.verification: opus: Checked NRU, PLW, TUV and TWN. Each SUMMARY says 五个方面的评分均不低于7/10, but the bars on the same page show starred pillars below 7 (NRU 治理 5.4 and 犯罪 5.7, TUV 治理 4.7, TWN 自然灾害 6.2 and 健康 6.7). The FAQ's 均表现良好 / 介于 7.6/10 到 8.9/10 claims and B12 likewise skip the starred pillars.

findings.quote: 没有任何单一因素构成突出风险：最需要关注的领域是自然灾害，得分为6.5/10。
findings.problem: On 46 pages the biggest-risk answer says no single factor stands out, then names one pillar as the area to watch, while the same page's SUMMARY names a main risk. NZL: SUMMARY says 最需关注的是自然灾害风险, while the FAQ says no single factor stands out and names 自然灾害 6.5/10. VCT: SUMMARY says 主要风险是暴力犯罪 (51.3 homicides per 100k), while the FAQ says no single factor stands out and names 犯罪 4.0/10. A traveller reads two opposite answers to the same question.
findings.expected: Use one answer per page. If the SUMMARY names a main concern, the FAQ names the same one and does not say no factor stands out. Use the no-risk wording only when no pillar is flagged.
findings.verification: opus: VCT's FAQ says 没有任何单一因素构成突出风险 while naming 犯罪 4.0/10, and its SUMMARY says 主要风险是暴力犯罪 (51.3/100k). VEN uses the same wording with 治理 at 1.5 and NZL with a named concern. The template fires on 146 zh pages.

findings.quote: 没有任何一国将其提升至低级别以上的警告
findings.problem: On 20 pages the FAQ says no government raised its advice above the low level, while the same page's SUMMARY counts governments at 提高警惕 or 重新考虑出行. SWE SUMMARY: 6个建议提高警惕. VNM: 9 at 提高警惕. SLB: 9 at 提高警惕 plus 1 at 重新考虑出行. SUR: 7 plus 2. SVN and SGP: 1 each. SLB (10 of 20) and SUR (9 of 18) also say 多数 when the normal-precaution count is exactly half. The clause appears in 40 FAQ answers in total, including 16 unscored pages.
findings.expected: Generate the clause only when the SUMMARY count of non-normal advisories is zero, and use 多数 only for more than half. Otherwise state the count, for example 有6个政府建议提高警惕.
findings.verification: opus: The FAQ says 没有任何一国将其提升至低级别以上的警告 while the SUMMARY reports raised levels: SWE 6 at 提高警惕, SUR 2 at 重新考虑出行, NRU 3 at level 2. SLB says 多数 with exactly 10 of 20 at normal precautions.

findings.quote: Alle fünf Bereiche erreichen mindestens 7 von 10
findings.problem: False on this page. PILLAR BARS show 'Kriminalität 5.5/10' and 'Regierungsführung 6.0/10', both footnoted for low data coverage. The FAQ repeats the error: 'Selbst die schwächste Säule, Gesundheit (7.1/10), liegt im risikoarmen Bereich' and 'insgesamt bewegen sich die fünf Säulen zwischen 7.1/10 und 8.8/10', while the displayed range is 5.5 to 8.8. The footnote does not make the sentence true.
findings.expected: Name the displayed lowest pillar (Kriminalität 5.5/10) and the displayed range, or drop the claim. Treat low-coverage pillars the same way in SUMMARY and FAQ.
findings.verification: opus: BRN SUMMARY says 'Alle fünf Bereiche erreichen mindestens 7 von 10', but its PILLAR BARS show 'Kriminalität 5.5/10' and 'Regierungsführung 6.0/10' (low-coverage footnote). The FAQ also gives the range as 7.1–8.8. The text skips low-coverage pillars while the bars show them, so the SUMMARY makes a false statement.

findings.quote: All five areas score at least 7 out of 10; the lowest-rated is the spread of epidemics: 5.5 out of 10
findings.problem: PILLAR BARS shows Crime 5.5/10 and Governance 6.0/10, both flagged 'low data coverage'. The SUMMARY still says all five areas are at least 7/10, the FAQ says 'All five pillars score well for Brunei: even the weakest, health (7.1/10)' and 'its five pillars range from 7.1/10 to 8.8/10', and DESCRIPTION names health (7.1) as top concern. FSM has the same gap (governance 5.2 and crime 5.7 flagged, yet FAQ: 'pulled down by natural hazards (7.0/10) and above all by health (6.8/10)').

findings.verification: opus: GAB FAQ: 'Das Gesamtbild ist beruhigend: Die meisten Regierungen empfehlen ... nur normale Vorsicht, und keine stuft es über einen Hinweis niedriger Stufe hinaus ein.' findings.quote: 总体情况令人安心：多数政府对加蓬仅建议采取正常预防措施，没有任何一国将其提升至低级别以上的警告。
findings.problem: Same page, SUMMARY: '在为加蓬发布旅行警告的20个国家政府中，10个建议采取正常预防措施，7个建议提高警惕，2个建议重新考虑出行，1个建议避免一切旅行。' So 10 of 20 is not a majority, and 3 governments sit above caution, which makes both the '多数政府' and the 'no country above the low level' claims false. BWA has the same false clause (SUMMARY: '1个建议重新考虑出行'). Cause: seo.ts buildAdvisoryAnswer (about lines 984-985) picks the consensus band by plurality, and the zh a3Consensus.normal string (country-faq-copy.ts about line 595) hard-codes both the majority wording and the 'nothing above' clause whenever the normal level is the plurality.
findings.expected: Use the real counts, e.g. '10 of 20 governments advise normal precautions; 3 advise reconsidering travel or avoiding it'. Use 多数 only for a strict majority. Never say no country is above the low level when any level-3 or level-4 advisory exists.
findings.verification: opus: The GAB FAQ shows the quote, and the SUMMARY on the same page gives 10 normal / 7 caution / 2 reconsider / 1 avoid out of 20 (Poland L3, Ireland L3, Taiwan L4 in the cards). Cause in seo.ts buildAdvisoryAnswer: the modal level is 1 by plurality (ties go up, but 10 beats 7), and a3Consensus.normal claims a majority and 'none above low-level' without checking maxLevel. BWA has the same false clause (1 reconsider). The English template has the same bug.

FAQ2 even says in one answer that conflict needs the most attention and then 'Its strongest pillar is conflict at 5.5/10'. Conflict is the highest bar. The drag-based driver picker chooses conflict because of its 30% weight.

findings.field: DESCRIPTION; FAQ A1 vs A2; SUMMARY
findings.quote: Mayor riesgo: conflicto (5.5).
findings.problem: Conflicto is the strongest pillar on MOZ: bars 'Gobernanza 3.4/10 | Salud 4.9/10 | Riesgos naturales 5.0/10 | Criminalidad 5.3/10 | Conflicto 5.5/10' and FAQ A1 'El pilar más fuerte de Mozambique es conflicto (5.5/10)'. Yet the DESCRIPTION calls it the main risk, FAQ A2 says 'el área que requiere más atención es conflicto, con 5.5/10', and the SUMMARY says 'La principal preocupación es el conflicto armado'. The driver rule ranks weight x -ln(score), so the 30%-weight conflict pillar at 5.5 outranks crime (25%, 5.3) and health (20%, 4.9).
findings.expected: A page's strongest pillar must not be its 'main risk'. Require the driver to sit below the page's lowest-scoring or average pillar, or fall back to 'no factor stands out'. Re-check MOZ DESCRIPTION, SUMMARY and A2 together.

findings.quote: le domaine qui demande le plus d'attention est le pilier conflit, à 5.5/10
findings.problem: Conflit (5.5/10) is the highest of the five pillars on this page (PILLAR BARS: Gouvernance 3.4/10 | Santé 4.9/10 | Risques naturels 5.0/10 | Criminalité 5.3/10 | Conflit 5.5/10). Answer 1 calls it the strongest pillar ('Le pilier le plus solide de Mozambique est conflit (5.5/10)'). Yet answer 2, the DESCRIPTION ('Risque principal : conflit (5.5)') and the SUMMARY ('Le principal point de vigilance est le conflit armé') make it the main concern. The lowest pillar, gouvernance (3.4/10), appears only as a secondary drag. The main-risk selector returned the strongest pillar.
findings.expected: Name the weakest or most damaging pillar (governance 3.4/10 here), or explain explicitly that conflict is the largest weighted drag despite its score. A top-scoring pillar must not be labelled 'risque principal' or 'point de vigilance'.
findings.verification: opus: On MOZ, Conflit 5.5 is the highest pillar bar, and answer 1 calls it the strongest pillar. Yet DESCRIPTION 'Risque principal : conflit (5.5)' and answer 2 call it the main concern, and answer 2 also says 'Côté points forts, le pilier conflit arrive en tête, à 5.5/10'. The same pillar is called both the weakest and the strongest.

findings.quote: La principale criticità è il conflitto armato: 585 persone uccise in conflitti armati nel 2025 (UCDP).

FAQ A1 says 'Il pilastro più solido di Mozambico è conflitto (5.5/10)' and PILLAR BARS list Governance 3.4, Salute 4.9, Rischi naturali 5.0, Criminalità 5.3, Conflitto 5.5. Yet the SUMMARY, the DESCRIPTION ('Rischio principale: conflitto (5.5)') and FAQ Q2 ('l'area che richiede più attenzione è il pilastro conflitto, con 5.5/10') all make it the main risk. Governance (3.4), the real weakest pillar, is never named. Cause: the driver is the direct-risk pillar with the largest weight x -ln(score) (pillarDrag in src/lib/country-summary.ts). Conflict has a 30% weight, so it wins even though it is the best-scoring pillar.
findings.expected: Never call the strongest pillar the 'principale criticità' or the 'area che richiede più attenzione'. Pick the driver by shortfall relative to the page's own pillars, not by weight x -ln(score).
findings.verification: opus: On the MOZ page conflict (5.5) is the highest pillar bar. FAQ A1 says 'Il pilastro più solido di Mozambico è conflitto (5.5/10)'. Yet SUMMARY, DESCRIPTION ('Rischio principale: conflitto (5.5)') and FAQ A2 all make conflict the main risk. The page contradicts itself, and the contradiction is in SUMMARY.

PILLAR BARS shows conflict at 5.5 as the HIGHEST of the five (治理 3.4, 健康 4.9, 自然灾害 5.0, 犯罪 5.3). The page gives opposite rankings of the same pillar, and the search snippet carries the wrong one.

findings.verification: opus: MOZ DESCRIPTION says 最需关注：冲突（5.5分）, yet conflict 5.5 is the highest bar (治理 3.4, 健康 4.9, 自然灾害 5.0, 犯罪 5.3). FAQ2 calls conflict both the area of most concern and 其表现最强的支柱是冲突 in the same answer.

findings.quote: Les cinq domaines obtiennent au moins 7 sur 10
findings.problem: SUMMARY says all five pillars score at least 7/10, but PILLAR BARS show Gouvernance 5.4/10 and Criminalité 5.7/10 (both marked as low data coverage). FAQ Q1 says 'même le plus faible, le pilier santé (7.6/10)' and FAQ Q3 says 'ses cinq piliers s'échelonnent de 7.6/10 à 8.9/10', which is also contradicted by 5.4 and 5.7. The same contradiction appears on PLW: SUMMARY 'Les cinq domaines obtiennent au moins 7 sur 10' vs Gouvernance 5.4/10 and Criminalité 5.7/10, and FAQ 'ses cinq piliers s'échelonnent de 7.9/10 à 8.9/10'. The reassuring claim overstates the page's own pillar data.
findings.expected: Either exclude the low-coverage pillars from 'les cinq domaines' and from the range, or state explicitly that two pillars are below 6/10 and are excluded from the score. Keep SUMMARY, FAQ and PILLAR BARS in agreement.
findings.verification: opus: NRU and PLW SUMMARY both say 'Les cinq domaines obtiennent au moins 7 sur 10', but PILLAR BARS show Gouvernance 5.4 and Criminalité 5.7 (low coverage). FAQ 'ses cinq piliers s'échelonnent de 7.6/10 à 8.9/10' (NRU) and '7.9/10 à 8.9/10' (PLW) also leave them out. The comparison tables show the same 5.4/5.7 values, so the claim is false on the page.

findings.quote: Corée du Nord ne présente aucun facteur véritablement critique
findings.problem: The FAQ says there is no truly critical factor, but the same page says 12 of 18 governments 'déconseillent formellement tout voyage' (SUMMARY), HERO labels the place 'Non recommandé' at 4.8/10 'risque élevé', and the FAQ's own Q3 says these warnings 'sont assez graves pour peser fortement sur notre indice'. The 'aucun facteur critique' sentence understates the page's own conclusion for a travel-safety decision.
findings.expected: Drop the 'aucun facteur véritablement critique' sentence for places where most governments advise against all travel, and name the conflict/governance exposure that drives the 'ne pas voyager' advisories.
findings.verification: opus: PRK FAQ Q2: 'Corée du Nord ne présente aucun facteur véritablement critique', while the same page has HERO 'Non recommandé', Gouvernance 2.4/10, 12 of 18 governments advising against all travel, and FAQ Q3 saying these warnings weigh heavily on the score. Calling nothing critical is misleading for a safety decision.

findings.quote: The main concern is a climate of violence and insecurity: the Global Peace Index scores the country 1.68 on a scale from 1 (most peaceful) to 5 (GPI 2026).
findings.problem: 1.68 on a 1 (most peaceful) to 5 scale is near the peaceful end, so naming violence and insecurity as the main concern misleads a traveller. QAT bars put governance 5.9/10 lowest and conflict 6.8/10. The same wording with SAU's GPI 2.07 (SUMMARY) is also weak.
findings.expected: Name the lowest pillar (governance 5.9/10) and quote the GPI value in its own direction. Do not use 'climate of violence' for a near-most-peaceful reading.
findings.verification: opus: The QAT SUMMARY quote is verbatim. A GPI of 1.68 on a 1 to 5 scale is near the most peaceful end, so 'a climate of violence and insecurity' describes that reading wrongly. The heavy level-3 advisories for Qatar are a separate signal that the sentence does not cite. The bars put governance 5.9 lowest.

findings.quote: The main concern is a climate of violence and insecurity: the Global Peace Index scores the country 1.68
findings.problem: A GPI score of 1.68 on the 1-to-5 scale (1 = most peaceful) is one of the more peaceful values on this site (Norway 1.69 and Poland 1.62, both on their own pages). The named driver is the least-bad displayed line of the Conflict pillar, roughly 8.3/10 on its own scale. The pillar's 6.8 sits below every displayed conflict input (GPI overall about 8.3, militarisation 6.9, UCDP 6 deaths), so the drag comes from the advisory-consensus term, which the page never names. The sentence presents a peaceful score as a climate of violence.
findings.expected: Name the real driver (the advisory consensus, if that is what pulls the pillar down), or do not frame a line whose own value is good as the main concern.
findings.verification: opus: The QAT summary calls 'a climate of violence and insecurity' the main concern and cites GPI overall 1.68, a peaceful value (NOR is about 1.69 on this site). The lower Conflict pillar (6.8) is driven by advisories: 11 governments say reconsider and 1 says avoid all travel. The cited evidence contradicts the framing.

findings.quote: Ja, mit etwas Vorsicht — Saudi-Arabien ist für die meisten Reisenden ausreichend sicher
findings.problem: The verdict says Saudi Arabia is safe enough, but the advisory answer on the same page says 'Die vorherrschende Empfehlung lautet, eine Reise nach Saudi-Arabien zu überdenken' (SUMMARY: 4 erhöhte Vorsicht, 12 überdenken, 5 von allen Reisen ab, i.e. 17 of 21). The same contradiction appears on QAT ('Ja, im Allgemeinen — Katar gilt als sicheres Reiseziel' vs 'vorherrschende Empfehlung lautet, eine Reise nach Katar zu überdenken'; 11 überdenken and 1 nicht reisen of 23) and PAK ('Ja, aber nur mit wirklicher Vorsicht' vs 'vorherrschende Empfehlung lautet, eine Reise nach Pakistan zu überdenken'; 14 of 24).
findings.expected: Use a verdict that matches the advisory majority (for example 'Nein' or 'Mit Vorsicht überdenken' when most governments advise reconsidering or not travelling), or keep the verdict and drop the 'vorherrschende Empfehlung' sentence.
findings.verification: opus: SAU.de FAQ1 says 'Ja, mit etwas Vorsicht — ... ausreichend sicher', while the summary lists 12 überdenken and 5 von allen Reisen ab out of 21, and FAQ3 says 'Die vorherrschende Empfehlung lautet, eine Reise ... zu überdenken'. QAT ('Ja, im Allgemeinen', 11 überdenken + 1 nicht reisen of 23) and PAK show the same verdict-vs-advisory contradiction.

findings.quote: the area that needs the most attention is conflict, at 6.3/10
findings.problem: Conflict 6.3/10 is Thailand's highest pillar, and the same page's Q1 says 'conflict (6.3/10) is Thailand's strongest pillar'. SUMMARY ('The main concern is armed conflict') and DESCRIPTION ('Top concern: conflict (6.3)') repeat the error. The weakest pillar is governance 4.4/10, named only as the 'above all' drag in Q1.
findings.expected: Name governance 4.4/10 as the main concern. Do not say the strongest pillar needs the most attention.
findings.verification: opus: THA's bars put conflict 6.3 highest and governance 4.4 lowest. Q1 says 'conflict (6.3/10) is Thailand's strongest pillar'. Q2 says conflict 'needs the most attention' and then 'Its strongest pillar is conflict at 6.3/10' in the same answer. DESCRIPTION and SUMMARY also name conflict. Real southern-insurgency deaths do not excuse calling the strongest pillar the top concern.

findings.quote: All five areas score at least 7 out of 10; the lowest-rated is poor public safety: the Global Peace Index rates safety and security at 1.67
findings.problem: Bars show natural hazards 6.2/10 and health 6.7/10, both below 7. The 'lowest-rated' area is named as poor public safety, though crime is 7.5/10 on the bars. The GPI value 1.67 on a 1 (safest) to 5 scale is a near-safest reading, not poor safety. The FAQ repeats the error: 'even the weakest, crime (7.5/10), sits in the low-risk band' and 'range from 7.5/10 to 8.5/10' (bars run 6.2 to 8.5; 6.2 and 6.7 are in the Moderate band).
findings.expected: Name natural hazards 6.2/10 as the weakest pillar, correct the band claim (Moderate for 6.2 and 6.7), and do not describe a GPI 1.67 as poor safety.
findings.verification: opus: The TWN SUMMARY quote is verbatim, and the bars show natural hazards 6.2* and health 6.7*, both below 7. Calling a GPI safety and security reading of 1.67 (1 = safest) 'poor public safety' inverts its meaning. The FAQ's '7.5 to 8.5' range is also wrong.

findings.quote: Taiwan affiche de bons scores sur les cinq piliers : même le plus faible, le pilier criminalité (7.5/10)
findings.problem: The SUMMARY says 'Les cinq domaines obtiennent au moins 7 sur 10 ; le moins bien noté est l’insécurité', and the FAQ says the weakest pillar is criminalité at 7.5 with all five between 7.5 and 8.5. The page's own PILLAR BARS show 'Risques naturels 6.2/10' and 'Santé 6.7/10' (both flagged as low coverage, but still shown). TUV has the same error: its SUMMARY says 'Les cinq domaines obtiennent au moins 7 sur 10' while its PILLAR BARS show 'Gouvernance 4.7/10' and 'Criminalité 5.7/10', and its FAQ says 'même le plus faible, le pilier santé (7.0/10)'.
findings.expected: The claims that all pillars are at least 7 and that the weakest pillar is X must match the displayed pillar values. Low-coverage pillars should be excluded from these statements, or the statement should be qualified.
findings.verification: opus: On TWN, the SUMMARY says 'Les cinq domaines obtiennent au moins 7 sur 10' and the FAQ says the weakest pillar is criminalité 7.5, with all five between 7.5 and 8.5. The bars show Risques naturels 6.2 and Santé 6.7, both with low-coverage asterisks. On TUV, the same SUMMARY and FAQ name santé 7.0 as weakest while the bars show Gouvernance 4.7 and Criminalité 5.7. The SUMMARY claim contradicts the bars shown on the same page.

findings.quote: Am meisten Aufmerksamkeit verdient ein Klima von Gewalt und Unsicherheit: Der Global Peace Index bewertet das Land mit 1,68
findings.problem: A fixed phrase, 'ein Klima von Gewalt und Unsicherheit', is the main concern on QAT, SAU, VEN, TUR, TCD, PRK and SSD (and 'Das größte Risiko ist ein Klima …' on PRK, SSD and TCD), whatever the GPI value: 1,68 (QAT), 2,07 (SAU), 2,52 (VEN), 2,61 (TUR), 2,77 (TCD), 2,85 (PRK), 3,12 (SSD). On this GPI scale 1 is 'am friedlichsten', so QAT's value is one of the most peaceful readings, and the same QAT SUMMARY says the best pillar is Kriminalität 8.3/10. The phrase does not name the pillar or indicator that drives the score; the QAT FAQ names Konflikt 6.8/10 as the main concern.
findings.expected: Build the concern sentence from the actual driver (the lowest pillar or indicator) and word it by value. Do not use 'Klima von Gewalt und Unsicherheit' when the GPI value is in the peaceful half of the scale.
findings.verification: opus: The SUMMARY uses the fixed label 'ein Klima von Gewalt und Unsicherheit' for the GPI-overall driver whatever its value: QAT 1,68, KWT 1,81 and JOR 1,91 are in the peaceful part of the 1-5 scale, and QAT's own best pillar is Kriminalität 8.3. The label is fine for SSD and AFG but misleading for low values, and it sits in the SUMMARY.

findings.quote: The main concern is poor public safety: the Global Peace Index rates safety and security at 1.98 on a scale from 1 (safest) to 5
findings.problem: 'poor public safety' is a fixed topic string for the GPI safety-and-security indicator (indicator-copy.ts line 88), printed whatever the value. On the page's own 1 (safest) to 5 scale, the cited values are 1.67 (TWN), 1.98 (TJK), 2.17 (TKM), 2.39 (TUN), 2.41 (URY), 2.45 (USA) and 2.49 (ZMB): all on the safer half of the scale. The pipeline normalises them to 6.3 to 8.3 out of 10 (TJK 7.6, TWN 8.3). The crime pillar that drives the sentence (TJK 6.8) is pulled toward a prior because its homicide input is missing (coverage 0.5). TWN's sentence also calls public safety the 'lowest-rated' area although its crime pillar is 7.5 and natural hazards is 6.2.
findings.expected: Pick the adjective from the value (never 'poor' for a GPI safety reading in the safer half), or use a neutral topic such as 'public safety'. Say when a driver pillar rests partly on a prior.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on TJK. The same fixed 'poor public safety' wording is printed for GPI safety values 1.67 (TWN), 2.41 (URY) and 2.45 (USA), all in the safer half of the 1-5 scale; calling Taiwan's public safety 'poor' in the SUMMARY is misleading. Examples: TJK, TWN, URY.

findings.quote: Tchad ne présente aucun facteur véritablement critique : le domaine qui demande le plus d'attention est le pilier conflit, à 4.7/10.
findings.problem: The template claim 'ne présente aucun facteur véritablement critique' is shown on pages where a pillar is far below the safe range. TCD has gouvernance 1.6/10 and santé 3.9/10 on its own PILLAR BARS. The same sentence appears with governance 2.3/10 (TJK, TKM), 3.1/10 (TUR) and 3.6/10 (SWZ). This reassures travellers about a weak area and is misleading for a safety decision.
findings.expected: Name the weakest pillar and its score, and do not say there is no critical factor when a pillar is at or below about 4/10. Use a graded wording instead.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on TCD exactly as given. TCD is in the 'risque élevé' band, its SUMMARY says 8 governments advise against all travel, and its bars show Gouvernance 1.6 and Santé 3.9. 'Ne présente aucun facteur véritablement critique' also appears on TJK and TKM (governance 2.3), TUR (3.1) and SWZ (3.6). This template reassures the reader in a way that is misleading for a safety decision.

findings.quote: Generally safe 7 7.3 out of 10 Safety Score
findings.problem: The 'Generally safe' band (7.3/10, 'low risk') sits directly above the page's own advisory breakdown: 'Of the 21 governments ... 1 advises normal precautions, 9 advise increased caution, 10 advise reconsidering travel and 1 advises against all travel.' So 11 of 21 governments advise reconsidering or avoiding travel (10 at Level 3, including Canada, US, Germany, Poland, Ireland, Spain and Taiwan; Singapore at Level 4). Most governments warn against non-essential travel, which the 'Generally safe' label does not convey. BHR shows the same pattern: 6.6/10 'Exercise caution' with 17 of 23 governments at reconsider or worse. Uncertain: I did not check whether these advisory levels are current, so the claim rests on the page's own evidence.
findings.expected: A place where most governments advise reconsidering or avoiding travel should not sit in the 'Generally safe' band. The advisory consensus should cap the score (about 7.0 or lower), or the band wording should reflect the advisories.
findings.verification: opus: Verified on ARE: 'Generally safe 7 7.3 out of 10' (data score 7.27) with 10 of 21 governments at Level 3 (CA, US, DE, PL, HU, CZ, IE, BE, ES, TW) and Singapore at Level 4. That is 52% at reconsider or worse. The same pattern holds for BHR (6.57, 74% at L3+), KWT (6.94, 81%) and QAT (7.44, 52%), so the advisory consensus barely moves Gulf scores. I corrected the constraint to below 7.0 so ARE leaves the 'Generally safe' band.

findings.quote: BLR | Belarus | 5.5 | 162 | high caution | conf=5.6 crim=5.8 heal=7.8 gove=3.8 envi=6.9 | L1x1 L2x2 L3x4 L4x12 | - | 0 (2025) | none (2 votes)
findings.problem: Twelve of the government advisories in the batch are Level 4 (do not travel), and four more are Level 3, yet the score sits in the 'high caution' band (5-6) rather than 'danger' (<5). Russia, with an almost identical advisory profile (L4x13, L3x6), is rated 4.1 'danger'. Widely known in 2025-2026: the US, UK and most EU governments advise against all travel to Belarus, and foreign nationals have been arbitrarily detained there. The score's apparent 'high caution' reading comes from the zero conflict-death count and the health and crime pillars, which do not offset the advisory consensus. A traveller reading 'high caution' would underestimate a risk that most governments tell them to avoid.
findings.expected: Belarus should fall in the danger band, at or below 5.0, close to the level its advisory consensus implies and not far above Russia's 4.1.
findings.verification: opus: Table and latest.json both show Belarus at 5.54 (high caution) with 12 of 19 advisories at Level 4, including the US, UK, Canada, Australia, Germany, France, New Zealand and Ireland. The main risks for foreigners are arbitrary detention, the closed EU borders and the nearby war. Belarus is the only Level-4-majority country in the dataset scoring above 5.0, while North Korea, which has a similar low-crime, political-risk profile, scores 4.83. So a bound at the danger-band edge holds for any formula that respects near-universal government consensus.

findings.quote: 13 advise reconsidering travel and 2 advise against all travel
findings.problem: Uncertain. 15 of 19 advisories are reconsider or avoid, yet the HERO score is 6.2 ('Exercise caution'), essentially equal to Djibouti's 6.3. Djibouti's advisories show only 5 of 21 at reconsider or avoid. The score may under-weight the advisory consensus, but the page does not show how the conflict pillar is built.
findings.expected: Check whether advisory severity is diluted in the score; a sound formula should place a place where most governments advise reconsidering travel clearly below a place with few such advisories.
findings.verification: opus: CUB.en shows 6.2, 'Exercise caution', moderate risk, while 15 of 19 advisories are level 3-4, including UK, Canada, Germany, France, Australia, Netherlands and Switzerland, so the hero is misleading for a travel decision. latest.json shows this is systematic: other places where most advisories are at level 3 or 4 score 6-7.4 too (KWT 6.94 at 81%, SAU 6.24, BHR 6.57).

findings.quote: Conflict deaths (UCDP) | 5
findings.problem: The HERO band is 'Exercise caution' (6.2), but the conflict inputs are 2025 values (UCDP 5 deaths in 2025; GPI 2026, which covers 2025). The German Foreign Office Saudi page (fetched; 'Stand 15.10.2026', unchanged since 11.10.2026) is a whole-country Reisewarnung: 'Vor Reisen nach Saudi-Arabien wird gewarnt'. It cites Houthi drone and missile strikes since early September 2026 in several provinces, airports as the main targets, and a warning against using Riyadh airport. The page's 17 of 21 advisories at Level 3 or 4 are visible, but the headline band and the conflict pillar do not reflect the 2026 escalation. How far the score should move is for the formula team; the inputs predate the event.
findings.expected: Give conflict inputs a recency rule, or flag them as dated before the band is shown. At minimum the HERO should not show a caution band over a country-wide government warning without a dated note.
findings.verification: opus: I could not verify the 2026 Houthi escalation, but the page alone shows the problem. SAU's HERO reads 'Exercise caution 6 6.2' and 'moderate risk', while its own summary lists 12 governments advising reconsidering travel and 5 against all travel (17 of 21). Germany, New Zealand, Poland, Czechia and Singapore are at Level 4. SAU still scores above TGO (6.0), which has only 1 Level 3 and 1 Level 4 advisory, so the score does not reflect the advisory consensus.

findings.quote: The main concern is violent crime: 5.1 homicides per 100,000 people (World Bank, 2021).
findings.problem: Liechtenstein has about 40,000 residents (my estimate), so 5.1 per 100,000 is roughly two killings in one year. A rate built on two cases is statistical noise, and the methodology says small-population homicide rates are damped (P_HALF). The value is from 2021 and is the only crime input on the page, so it also sets the Crime bar (6.6/10), the lowest on a page rated 8.2 'very low risk'. Presenting it as the main concern overstates the risk for a traveller.
findings.expected: Do not headline a five-year-old rate built on a few cases. Apply the population damping before naming crime as the main concern, and say how small the base is.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on the LIE page. In latest.json the crime pillar's only input is wb_homicide, normalised to 0.915, which is good. The pillar is still 0.664 because the population-damped homicide input gets little weight and the value is pulled toward the prior. The summary then headlines a 2021 rate built on about 2 cases (pop. about 40k) as 'the main concern' for one of the safest places listed. The low pillar comes from the prior, not from the data.

findings.quote: 最需关注的是暴力与不安全：全球和平指数对该国的评分为1.68（1–5分，1分最和平；GPI 2026）。
findings.problem: GPI runs from 1 to 5 with 1 = most peaceful, so 1.68 is near the best end, yet the SUMMARY makes it the top concern. The same direction error appears on TWN (SUMMARY: 评分最低的是社会治安欠佳：…为1.67（1–5分，1分最安全）), TJK (最需关注的是社会治安欠佳：…为1.98（1–5分，1分最安全）) and TKM (…为2.17). QAT's FAQ also lists GPI overall peacefulness among its lowest-scoring conflict indicators; if 1.68 is that indicator, the two statements conflict.
findings.expected: Show the GPI direction in the label, or choose the concern from indicators that are poor on the page's own scale. A near-best GPI reading should not be labelled 欠佳.
findings.verification: opus: QAT's SUMMARY makes GPI 1.68 (1 = most peaceful, near the top of the world ranking) its top concern. TWN labels a GPI safety score of 1.67 '社会治安欠佳'. A favourable value is presented as the main weakness in the SUMMARY.

findings.problem: Aruba's table tags Haiti, Dominican Republic and Grenada as 'nearby', but each is roughly 700-900 km away. The only genuinely close neighbour listed is Venezuela (about 30 km), and it is tagged nearby along with the far ones. Aruba is also a partial-data page, so the table itself conflicts with the design (see ALL/partial-data finding).
findings.expected: 'nearby' applies only to close countries. Far countries are removed from the table or shown without that tag. Aruba's table should be built from real proximity, not from a shared-region or shared-score rule.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on ABW.en. Nearby is computed from country centroids, so Colombia (centroid 1014 km away, real coast about 150 km away) is left out, while Grenada (900 km) and Haiti (782 km) are tagged 'nearby'. Venezuela is also tagged, at a centroid distance of 598 km. The table therefore misses Aruba's most relevant mainland neighbour.

findings.quote: How does Turkey compare to its neighbouring countries?
findings.problem: The neighbour rows are the six highest-scoring real neighbours (getNeighbors in src/lib/neighbors.ts sorts by score and slices to 6), so the least-safe neighbours are dropped and never named on the page. TUR: Iran 3.9 and Syria 3.7 are land neighbours but appear nowhere on the page, and Iraq 4.4 is shown as the weakest neighbour. SAU: Iraq 4.4 and Yemen 3.4 are absent, so Saudi Arabia (6.2) looks like the weakest of its neighbours. RUS: only Finland 8.8 to Poland 8.5 are shown; Ukraine 3.9, North Korea 4.8, Belarus 5.5, Azerbaijan 6.4, China 7.1, Georgia 7.3, Kazakhstan 7.3 and Mongolia 7.5 are dropped, and Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, China and Mongolia are never named. The same cut drops POL Ukraine 3.9 (never named), ZMB DR Congo 3.8 and Mozambique 5.5 (never named), TZA Burundi 5.4 and DR Congo 3.8 (never named), UKR Russia 4.1 and SDN South Sudan 3.4 (both still named under 'same region'). Site-wide 19 countries have more than six scored neighbours (e.g. CHN drops Afghanistan 3.6, Myanmar 4.1, Pakistan 5.1). Not a far-away-row case: reported because the cut systematically hides the least-safe neighbours and flatters the neighbourhood; drop it if the batch rule must be strict.
findings.expected: List every real neighbour that has an official score (worst case 14, Russia and China), with a scrollable table or show-all toggle if needed. If a cap stays, choose it by border length or geography rather than score, and say 'showing 6 of N neighbours'. Never remove the lowest-scoring neighbours silently.
findings.verification: opus: getNeighbors sorts by official score and slices to 6 (src/lib/neighbors.ts:255-256). SAU's table has no Iraq or Yemen, and neither name appears anywhere on SAU.en.txt, so Saudi Arabia (6.2) shows as the weakest of its neighbours. RUS shows only Finland to Poland; Kazakhstan, China, Mongolia and Azerbaijan are never named. 20 borderMap entries have more than 6 neighbours.

findings.quote: RELATED "Related Countries > In the same region": Eswatini 6.7 ; Malawi 6.6 ; Zambia 6.8
findings.problem: 'In the same region' uses six continent-scale buckets (src/lib/regions.ts: europe, asia, africa, americas, oceania, middle_east) and fills the three slots by closest total score only (selectRelated). The picks are routinely on the far side of the continent: SEN gets Eswatini (~6,700 km), Malawi (~6,100 km) and Zambia (~5,600 km); ZAF gets Egypt (~6,250 km); SYC gets Morocco (~7,600 km); TLS gets Kazakhstan (~8,500 km); URY gets the United States (~9,200 km); NZL gets Palau (~6,700 km); PAK gets North Korea (~5,100 km). Distances are approximate, from country-coords.json. The heading promises a neighbourhood, so readers take these as nearby, but they are effectively random picks from a 30-to-60-country bucket.
findings.expected: Use sub-regions (West, East, Southern and North Africa; South, East, Southeast and Central Asia), or sort by distance inside the region, or retitle the block 'Same continent' and show distance. Drop the block when the bucket spans more than about 3,000 km.
findings.verification: opus: regions.ts has only six continent-scale buckets, and 'In the same region' orders by closest total score. SEN's page lists Eswatini, Malawi and Zambia (6,710 / 6,126 / 5,621 km by coords). STP lists Algeria and Tunisia, and SGP lists Japan and South Korea. This is the same kind of 'similar countries' nonsense the blogger complained about.

findings.quote: In the same region": Myanmar 4.1 ; North Korea 4.8 ; Cambodia 5.9
findings.problem: 'In the same region' is built at continent level, so it picks distant places while closer peers go missing. AFG lists Myanmar, North Korea and Cambodia (East and Southeast Asia) instead of South or Central Asian states. AGO lists Côte d'Ivoire (West Africa). BEN lists Madagascar (East Africa / Indian Ocean). BDI lists Cameroon (Central Africa). ARM and AZE list Gulf states and Israel (UAE, Qatar, Oman; Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Israel) instead of Caucasus or Turkish-Iranian peers. ATG lists United States, Costa Rica and Suriname for a Caribbean island.
findings.expected: 'In the same region' uses a sub-region or closer grouping, so that the peers a traveller would compare are shown (Central/South Asia for AFG, Caribbean islands for ATG, Caucasus for ARM and AZE).
findings.verification: opus: The finding's opening quote is malformed (a stray quote mark and the heading label), but every quoted list is on the pages. AFG shows Myanmar, North Korea and Cambodia; ARM shows UAE, Qatar and Oman; AZE shows Bahrain, Saudi Arabia and Israel; ATG shows Suriname, the United States and Costa Rica; BEN shows Madagascar. regions.ts uses six continent-level buckets (europe, asia, africa, americas, oceania, middle_east, with ARM and AZE placed in middle_east), so the same-region lists pick distant peers by score.

findings.quote: Timor-Leste 7.2 ; Sri Lanka 7.3 ; Kazakhstan 7.3
findings.problem: "In the same region" appears to use a continent-level grouping ("the Americas", "Asia", "Africa") rather than a real sub-region, so it lists countries a traveller would not consider regional peers. Examples: BRN lists Kazakhstan (Central Asia) for Brunei (Southeast Asia). CAN lists Uruguay, Barbados and Chile for Canada ("Uruguay 7.8 ; Barbados 7.7 ; Chile 7.6"). BTN lists Taiwan, South Korea and Japan (East Asia) for Bhutan (South Asia), while its real South Asian neighbours appear only in the neighbour table.
findings.expected: Use sub-regions (South Asia, Southeast Asia, Central Asia, North America, South America, Caribbean, West/Central/East Africa) for the "same region" list, or drop the list when only a continent-level group is available.
findings.verification: opus: I checked the pages. BRN 'In the same region' gives 'Timor-Leste 7.2 ; Sri Lanka 7.3 ; Kazakhstan 7.3'. CAN gives 'Uruguay 7.8 ; Barbados 7.7 ; Chile 7.6'. BTN gives 'Taiwan 7.9 ; South Korea 8.1 ; Japan 8.1'. BRA gives 'El Salvador 6.6 ; Bolivia 6.5 ; Saint Vincent and the Grenadines 6.5'. src/lib/regions.ts only uses continent-level regions (europe/asia/africa/americas/oceania/middle_east), and those are sorted by closest score. As a result Canada's 'region' is South America and the Caribbean, which is the same kind of irrelevant 'similar countries' list the blogger criticised.

findings.quote: In the same region": Sao Tome and Principe 6.8 ; Zambia 6.8 ; Cabo Verde 6.9
findings.problem: "In the same region" is a whole continent, sorted by score proximity, not a real region. DZA (North Africa) shows Zambia and Sao Tome and Principe. ERI shows Mozambique and Cameroon. EGY shows South Africa and Kenya. GAB shows Zimbabwe and Cote d'Ivoire. GHA shows Tunisia (North Africa) for a West African country. FIN shows Ireland and Luxembourg and omits Sweden and Norway, which are in its own table. EST shows Norway and Czech Republic and omits Latvia and Finland, which are in its own table. GEO shows Bosnia and Herzegovina, Moldova and Albania and omits Armenia and Azerbaijan, which are in its own table. GBR and FRA show Slovakia, Poland, Romania, Greece and Bulgaria.
findings.expected: Region built from sub-regions (North Africa, West Africa, Nordics, Baltics, South Caucasus, Western Europe). Real neighbours already in the table should appear first in the region list.
findings.verification: opus: Batch lines match exactly: DZA region = Sao Tome and Principe/Zambia/Cabo Verde, ERI = Cameroon/Mozambique/Burundi, EGY = Kenya/Djibouti/South Africa, GAB = Cote d'Ivoire/Zimbabwe/Angola, GHA includes Tunisia, FIN = Ireland/Denmark/Luxembourg, EST = Norway/Czech Republic/Luxembourg, GEO = Bosnia/Moldova/Albania, FRA = Romania/Greece/Bulgaria, GBR = Spain/Slovakia/Poland. 'In the same region' is a continent-wide list picked by score proximity, so it shows far-off countries (the 'Antarctica/Israel for Ecuador' kind of complaint) and skips the real neighbours already in the table.

findings.quote: RELATED "Related Countries > In the same region": Thailand 6.4 ; Turkmenistan 6.4 ; Tajikistan 6.5
findings.problem: The 'In the same region' list appears to be drawn from the whole continent, ranked by score closeness, rather than from the subregion. Indonesia (IDN) lists Turkmenistan and Tajikistan (Central Asia) as same region. Guinea-Bissau (GNB) lists Madagascar (East African island) and Guinea (GIN) lists Uganda (East Africa) and Congo (Central Africa). A traveller reading 'same region' gets countries thousands of km away from the page's own country.
findings.expected: Select 'same region' from the subregion (for example Southeast Asia for Indonesia, West Africa for Guinea-Bissau and Guinea), or relabel the list 'same continent' so the label matches what was actually selected.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on the IDN page, and the GNB (Madagascar), GIN (Uganda, Congo) and GRD (Argentina) pages show the same pattern. getRegion in src/lib/regions.ts maps countries to continents ('asia', 'americas', 'africa'), so 'In the same region' actually means 'same continent, closest score'. That puts Central Asian states next to Indonesia, which is the 'similar countries' complaint again.

findings.quote: Tajikistan 6.5 ; Turkmenistan 6.4 ; Nepal 6.8
findings.problem: The 'In the same region' list is not regional. LAO (Southeast Asia) gets Central Asian Tajikistan and Turkmenistan plus South Asian Nepal. KAZ (Central Asia) gets Sri Lanka, Timor-Leste and Brunei, while its actual regional peers Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan (already in its neighbour table) are never listed. LBR (West Africa) gets Comoros and Tanzania (East Africa / Indian Ocean), with only Benin as a West African entry. KGZ gets Maldives, Vietnam and Brunei, with no Central Asian peer. JPN and KHM show the same pattern (Bhutan, India, Bangladesh). The list looks like a loose continent-wide or score-based pick, not a region.
findings.expected: Same-subregion countries (for example the UN M49 subregion, or a curated list), excluding land neighbours already in the comparison table. If no true regional peers exist, omit the list.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on LAO.en.txt exactly. The 'In the same region' lists are not regional: KAZ gets Sri Lanka, Timor-Leste and Brunei; KGZ gets Maldives, Vietnam and Brunei; LBR gets Comoros and Tanzania; KHM gets India and Bangladesh; JPN gets Bhutan. It looks like a continent-wide pick by closest score. Small correction: JPN's list is Bhutan, Malaysia, Singapore, not 'India, Bangladesh'.

findings.quote: China 7.1 ; Kyrgyzstan 7.0 ; Uzbekistan 7.0
findings.problem: The 'In the same region' lists are continent-wide, and the picks look score-matched rather than regional. Examples: MDV (Maldives) lists China, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan, which are East and Central Asia and not South Asia. LSO (Lesotho) lists Gambia, Ghana and Cabo Verde, which are West Africa, about 4,000 km away. MDG (Madagascar) lists Guinea-Bissau, Benin and Togo (West Africa). MLI (Mali) lists Somalia, Central African Republic and DRC, which are East and Central Africa. MAR (Morocco) lists Namibia and Lesotho, which are southern Africa. LBY (Libya) lists Nigeria, Ethiopia and Burundi, which are sub-Saharan. LKA (Sri Lanka) lists Kazakhstan and Timor-Leste. LCA (Saint Lucia) lists Guatemala, which is Central America. Each row's score is close to the page's own score, which suggests selection by score within a continent. A traveller reading 'same region' would expect neighbourhood or sub-region peers.
findings.expected: Restrict 'same region' to the sub-region (South Asia, West Africa, Southern Africa, Caribbean, and so on), or relabel it 'same continent' and state that. Where a sub-region has fewer than three scored countries, say so rather than filling the list with distant countries.
findings.verification: opus: Verified on the pages. MDV lists 'China 7.1 ; Kyrgyzstan 7.0 ; Uzbekistan 7.0', LSO lists Gambia/Ghana/Cabo Verde, MAR lists Namibia/Lesotho/Gambia, LBY lists Nigeria/Ethiopia/Burundi, and LKA lists Timor-Leste/Kazakhstan/Brunei. comparisons.ts confirms that 'Same region' is ordered by closest total score within a continent-sized region, so these labelled regional peers are thousands of km away and picked by score. This is the same 'similar countries' complaint the blogger made.

findings.quote: Kazakhstan 7.3 ; Malaysia 7.6 ; Sri Lanka 7.3
findings.problem: 'In the same region' behaves as a whole-continent bucket, not a sub-region, so it lists far-away places. Examples: Mongolia (East Asia) gets Malaysia and Sri Lanka (Southeast and South Asia). Mauritania (West Africa) gets Uganda and Congo (quoted as 'Guinea 5.7 ; Uganda 5.8 ; Congo 5.6'). Niger (West Africa Sahel) gets DR Congo and Somalia ('Democratic Republic of the Congo 3.8 ; Somalia 3.8 ; Mali 3.7'). Nigeria gets Burundi, and Namibia gets Morocco. The label 'same region' overstates the match for a traveller.
findings.expected: Same-region picks should come from the same UN sub-region (or a named regional bloc), or the heading should be changed to 'same continent'.
findings.verification: opus: MNG.en shows 'In the same region': Kazakhstan 7.3 ; Malaysia 7.6 ; Sri Lanka 7.3. MRT.en shows Guinea, Uganda and Congo, NER.en shows DR Congo, Somalia and Mali, NGA.en shows Burundi and NAM.en shows Morocco. src/lib/regions.ts has only 6 continent-scale regions (europe, asia, africa, americas, oceania, middle_east), so 'same region' really means 'same continent', which is the kind of distant pick the blogger complained about.

findings.quote: la peor valorada es la exposición a peligros naturales: 2,5 sobre 10 en la escala de INFORM, donde 10 es la exposición máxima
findings.problem: Where the SUMMARY calls an indicator the 'principal preocupación' or the 'peor valorada' area, the raw number sits at the safe end of its own scale: SWE 2,5 exposure (10 = maximum); NRU and SVN 3,2 on the same kind of scale; QAT 'La principal preocupación es un clima de violencia e inseguridad' with GPI 1,68 on a 1 (máxima paz) to 5 scale; TWN 'la peor valorada es la inseguridad ciudadana' with GPI 1,67 on a 1 (máxima seguridad) to 5 scale; TJK (1,98) and SAU (2,07) similar. A low raw value is read as a large concern.
findings.expected: Name the weakest pillar and its score instead. Call an indicator a 'principal preocupación' only when its value is in the risk half of its scale, and state the direction of the scale.
findings.verification: opus: QAT gives 'La principal preocupación es un clima de violencia e inseguridad' with GPI 1,68 (a very peaceful value), and TJK does the same with GPI safety 1,98, while governance is their lowest pillar. SWE's 'peor valorada' wording is fine because it is framed inside 'all areas ≥7'; the problem is the 'principal preocupación' cases.

findings.quote: la note de 1,91 sur une échelle de 1 (le plus pacifique) à 5
findings.problem: The SUMMARY calls an indicator the 'principal point de vigilance' (or 'le moins bien noté') while its own scale puts the value at the favourable end. GPI (1 = most peaceful, 5 = least): JOR 1,91 ('Le principal point de vigilance est un climat de violence ...'), KWT 1,81, KGZ 2,05 (main vigilance point 'l'insécurité'), LKA 2,13, LSO 2,33, NAM 2,37. INFORM (10 = worst): IRL 2,3 ('le moins bien noté est l'exposition aux risques naturels'), ISL 2,5, LVA 2,4, NOR 2,8, MNG 3,3 and MDA 3,4 (both 'principal point de vigilance'). LUX: 'le moins bien noté est la criminalité violente : 1,5 homicides pour 100 000 habitants (Banque mondiale, 2022)'. A reader cannot reconcile 'point de vigilance' with a value at the best end of its scale.
findings.expected: Quote as the main vigilance point only a value that is poor on its own scale, and say which pillar it belongs to. When the weak pillar is driven by another factor (conflict deaths, advisories), name that factor instead.
findings.verification: opus: JOR and KWT name 'un climat de violence et d’insécurité' as the 'principal point de vigilance' with GPI 1,91 and 1,81, which are near the peaceful end of the 1-5 scale. Conflict is not even their weakest pillar; the real driver is advisories. MDA (INFORM 3,4) is similar. The LUX, IRL and NOR cases say 'le moins bien noté' (lowest-rated), which is fair for very safe countries; those parts are not a problem.

findings.quote: le moins bien noté est la propagation d’épidémies : 4,2 sur 10 selon INFORM, 10 correspondant au risque le plus élevé
findings.problem: SUMMARY calls an indicator the 'moins bien noté' area, but the pillar minimum on SGP is Santé 7.9/10 (and the same sentence says 'Les cinq domaines obtiennent au moins 7 sur 10'). On SVN, 'le moins bien noté est l'exposition aux risques naturels : 3,2 sur 10' while the pillar minimum is Risques naturels 7.3/10. On a 10-equals-highest-risk scale, 4.2 and 3.2 are low-risk values, so calling them the weakest point is misleading.
findings.expected: Name the weakest pillar (with its score) as the weakest point. Present indicator values as risk levels, e.g. 'risque d'épidémies faible (4,2/10, INFORM)', not as 'moins bien noté'.
findings.verification: opus: The SGP and SVN SUMMARY text is verbatim. The indicator does belong to the lowest pillar (SGP Santé 7.9, epidemic 4.2; SVN Risques naturels 7.3, exposure 3.2). But 'Les cinq domaines obtiennent au moins 7 sur 10 ; le moins bien noté est … 4,2 sur 10' puts a pillar score and a reversed-scale risk value side by side, and reads as self-contradictory.

findings.quote: Come si confronta la sicurezza in Nuova Zelanda con quella dei paesi confinanti?
findings.problem: 42 pages ask about 'paesi confinanti' (bordering countries) without 'e vicini'. For island states without land borders this is inaccurate, e.g. NZL, PLW, TWN and PHL.
findings.expected: 'paesi vicini' or 'paesi della regione' for island states; keep 'confinanti' for states with land borders.
findings.verification: opus: The it 'country.compare_title' says 'paesi confinanti' (bordering) whenever no nearby fillers are added, but the neighbour set includes maritime neighbours. NZL's table lists Australia and Fiji under 'paesi confinanti', and AUS, JPN, FJI, CUB, BRB and LCA get the same heading. The English 'neighbouring' is fine; the Italian wrongly claims land borders.

findings.quote: 评分最低的是自然灾害风险：INFORM评分为2.3/10，10分表示暴露程度最高
findings.problem: The sentence names a pillar as weakest and cites an INFORM value on a scale where 10 = highest exposure. A value of 2.3 is low exposure, which is favourable, so the figure does not support the label. The same template appears on NRU (3.2, 10 = highest risk), SVN (3.2, exposure), SWE (2.5, exposure), PRT (3.8, 10 = worst), POL (4.2, 10 = worst), SGP (4.2, highest risk) and TUV (4.5, highest risk). The sentence mixes a pillar-score direction (low = weak) with an indicator-risk direction (high = weak).
findings.expected: Cite an indicator whose direction matches the claim and state that direction in the same sentence, or drop the INFORM figure and give only the weakest pillar and its score.
findings.verification: opus: On PLW, SWE and NRU, '评分最低的是…：INFORM评分为2.3/10' uses 评分 both for the pillar ranking (high = good) and for an INFORM risk value (low = good). A reader can take 2.3/10 as the pillar score, which clashes with the 7.9 bar. The scale direction is stated, so this is confusing rather than outright false.

findings.quote: 而拉低总分的主要是自然灾害（7.6/10），尤其是治理（4.5/10）。
findings.problem: The main-drag template (拉低总分的主要是X，尤其是Y) appears on 55 pages. On SRB it names natural disasters (7.6, a low-risk score) as the main drag and only then governance (4.5, the lowest pillar) as 尤其是. NZL does the same: 主要是健康（7.9/10），尤其是自然灾害（6.5/10）. 尤其是 joins two different pillars as if one were a subset of the other, and the main pillar is often not the lowest.
findings.expected: Name the lowest pillar as the main drag, or define drag as weighted contribution and say so. Use a coordinating phrase such as 其次是 for the second pillar.
findings.verification: opus: SRB reads 拉低总分的主要是自然灾害（7.6/10），尤其是治理（4.5/10）, and NZL reads 主要是健康（7.9/10），尤其是自然灾害（6.5/10). The lowest pillar is put second, under 尤其是, as if it were a subset of a higher-scoring pillar.

findings.quote: How does Brazil compare to its neighbouring countries? ... Guyana | 6.7 | 7.6 | 5.9 | 6.2 | 5.0 | 5.7
findings.problem: The table is labelled "neighbouring countries" but omits three land neighbours of Brazil: Bolivia, Colombia and Venezuela. Bolivia (6.5) and Colombia (5.9) have official scores that the page itself shows in its RELATED section ("Bolivia 6.5" in "In the same region"; "Colombia 5.9" in "similar risk profile"). The neighbour table is therefore incomplete while the related lists name those same countries.
findings.expected: Include every land neighbour that has an official score, including Bolivia, Colombia and Venezuela, in the neighbour table.
findings.verification: opus: In the BRA table, the neighbours shown are Uruguay, Suriname, Argentina, Paraguay, Peru and Guyana. borderMap lists 9 Brazilian borders, but selectComparison caps the neighbours at 6, ranked by score. Bolivia (6.5), Colombia (5.9) and Venezuela (4.8, 'Not recommended') are therefore cut. A table titled 'its neighbouring countries' drops exactly the riskiest borders, which skews the comparison upward.

findings.problem: The Cocos (Keeling) Islands sit in the eastern Indian Ocean, roughly 1,700 km from Singapore and about 1,800 km from peninsular Malaysia. Tagging both as "nearby" and listing their full scores (8.7 and 7.6) under a place that has no official score ("Partial data") implies a regional comparison that does not exist. A traveller could read Singapore's score as a proxy for the islands.
findings.expected: No comparison table on a Partial-data page, or only real neighbours that are genuinely close. Remote territories should not be given a "nearby" tag for places 1,000+ km away.
findings.verification: opus: CCK.en.txt does show 'Singapore nearby | 8.7 | ...' and 'Malaysia nearby | 7.6 ...'. The coordinates in country-coords.json are centroids: CCK [-12.12, 96.9] to SGP [1.3, 103.8] is about 1,700 km and to MYS about 1,900 km, both inside NEARBY_MAX_KM=2000. Indonesia is the real closest landmass (Java is about 1,000 km away), but its centroid [-2, 118] puts it past 2,000 km, so it is dropped. Christmas Island and Australia, the owner, are not shown either. The 'nearby' rows are distant places picked because of how centroids fall. The page has no score of its own, so I set severity to medium, not high.

findings.problem: The table is tagged 'nearby' for Malawi (landlocked, roughly 1,000 km away) and Seychelles (roughly 1,500 km away). Tanzania, the closest mainland neighbour (roughly 400 km, score 6.2), is missing from the table. It appears only in this page's 'In the same region' line, where it is listed as 'Tanzania 6.2'. The nearby tag and the neighbour list therefore do not match real proximity.
findings.expected: Add Tanzania to the neighbour rows. Tag 'nearby' only for states that are actually close, and drop distant ones.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is exact. COM has only 2 border entries (MDG, MOZ), so 2 'nearby' fillers are picked by centroid distance (Malawi 1055 km, Seychelles 1150 km, Tanzania 1177 km). In reality the Tanzanian coast is much closer to the Comoros than landlocked Malawi or Mahé, but Tanzania's inland centroid pushes it out. Tanzania then appears only in the 'same region' line. Root cause: centroid-based distance and an incomplete maritime border map.

findings.problem: Greece (roughly 700 km away) appears as an untagged neighbour row, while the closest states, Syria and Israel (roughly 200 to 400 km), do not appear anywhere on this batch, so their scores could not be checked. Lebanon and Palestine are tagged nearby. The row set mixes distance-based and loosely chosen neighbours.
findings.expected: Add Syria, Israel and Egypt if they have official scores. Tag Greece as nearby or drop it from the neighbour rows.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is exact. The finding's argument about Greece is wrong: borderMap CYP:[TUR, GRC] is a deliberate and defensible maritime link (Greek islands are about 300 km away). The real gap is different. Syria (scored 3.7, the closest coast at about 100 km) and Israel (scored 6.0) are missing, while Palestine is tagged nearby because its West Bank centroid (393 km) beats Israel (482) and Syria (508). Centroid distance hides the closest and riskiest neighbour.

findings.quote: Tanzania 6.2 ; Liberia 6.1 ; Djibouti 6.3
findings.problem: The 'In the same region' label is applied to whole continents, and the rows are picked by score closeness. Every row sits within 0.3 points of the page's own score. Examples: Liberia (West Africa, several thousand km from the Comoros) for COM; Mauritania (West Africa) for COG (Congo); Tunisia (North Africa) for CPV (Cabo Verde); Paraguay (landlocked South America) for DMA (Dominica); South Africa for DJI (Djibouti); Mali (West Africa) for COD (DRC); Maldives and Brunei (South and Southeast Asia) for CHN (China); Suriname (South America) for CRI (Costa Rica, Central America); Ecuador (South America) for CUB (Cuba). Travellers read 'same region' as geography, so these are misleading.
findings.expected: Use a real sub-region (West, Central, East and Southern Africa; Caribbean; Central America; South America; East Asia) or drop the 'same region' label and say 'similar score on the same continent'.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on the COM page (line 'In the same region': Tanzania 6.2 ; Liberia 6.1 ; Djibouti 6.3), not DJI. selectRelated filters by the continent-level getRegion (africa/americas/asia...) and orders by closest total score. That gives Liberia for Comoros, South Africa for Djibouti, Paraguay for Dominica, Suriname/United States for Costa Rica and Ecuador for Cuba under the label 'In the same region'. This is the same kind of score-driven 'related' list the blogger criticised. Template issue (ALL).

findings.quote: Antigua and Barbuda nearby | 7.5
findings.problem: The 'nearby' rows for the Dominican Republic include Antigua and Barbuda (roughly 900 km) and Saint Kitts and Nevis (roughly 800 km), but omit Cuba (roughly 600 km, score 6.2 on the CUB page) and the Bahamas (roughly 500 km, score 6.8 on the CYM page). The Cuba page (CUB) has the same gap: its table lists United States, Jamaica and Mexico but omits Haiti (score 3.7, shown in the DOM table) and the Bahamas (score 6.8, shown on the CYM page). Haiti shares the island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic and is a direct land neighbour of it. The Caribbean neighbour lists look hand-picked, not built from distance or borders.
findings.expected: Build Caribbean 'nearby' and neighbour lists from geography (land or maritime borders, distance). For DOM this means Haiti and Cuba. For CUB it means Haiti and the Bahamas.
findings.verification: opus: The quote text is on the DOM page. Haiti IS already in the DOM table (untagged border row), so that part of the claim is wrong. The DOM fillers are chosen by centroid (Jamaica 762, St Kitts 814, Antigua 903 km), which ranks Cuba (1032) and the Bahamas (1013) further away than Antigua, although both are closer to Hispaniola. The CUB gap is real: borderMap CUB = [USA, MEX, JAM] leaves out Haiti (scored 3.7, about 77 km across the Windward Passage) and the Bahamas (6.8, very close).

findings.problem: Algeria is missing from "How does Western Sahara compare to neighbouring and nearby countries?". Algeria borders Western Sahara by land and has an official score (6.8 on the DZA page). Instead the table shows "Senegal nearby" and "Mali nearby". Neither Senegal nor Mali borders Western Sahara, and Mali is far away. The grey own row is correct.
findings.expected: Add the Algeria row. Drop Senegal and Mali, or tag them as regional rather than nearby.
findings.verification: opus: The ESH table lists Morocco, Senegal, Mauritania and Mali as 'nearby' but not Algeria. Algeria shares a short land border with Western Sahara near Tindouf and has a scored page (6.8), so it qualifies; it even appears as 'nearby' on the GIB table. Neither Senegal nor Mali borders Western Sahara. Morocco and Mauritania are real land neighbours yet are also tagged only 'nearby'.

findings.problem: Brazil is missing from the table. It is a land neighbour of French Guiana and has an official score (6.6, shown in the Guyana table), yet Barbados (about 1,200 km away) and Trinidad and Tobago (also about 1,200 km away) are shown as 'nearby'.
