The same page's SUMMARY names a main risk. KNA: „Das größte Risiko ist die Gewaltkriminalität“ (the pillar is Kriminalität 4.3/10, the lowest of five). GIN: „Das größte Risiko ist der eingeschränkte Zugang zur Gesundheitsversorgung“ while FAQ2 says no factor stands out.
findings.expected: Drop 'sticht kein einzelner Faktor' wherever a pillar is named, and use the SUMMARY's main risk (same pillar) in the FAQ, e.g. 'Das größte Risiko ist die Gewaltkriminalität (Kriminalität 4.3/10).'
findings.verification: opus: KNA FAQ2: 'sticht kein einzelner Faktor als kritisch hervor' while Kriminalität is 4.3/10 and its SUMMARY says 'Das größte Risiko ist die Gewaltkriminalität: 64,2 Tötungsdelikte'. GIN FAQ2 uses the 'mid' copy for Gesundheit 4.2 while Regierungsführung is 2.7. The 'mid' band (4 ≤ x < 7) says 'not critical' even where the SUMMARY uses 'größtes Risiko' framing.

findings.quote: Kostenloser Wert aus 30+ öffentlichen Quellen
findings.problem: 45 of the 46 pages that say 'aus 30+ öffentlichen Quellen' give a SUMMARY count of advisories plus datasets below 30. GRD: „19 staatliche Reisehinweise und 3 weitere öffentliche Datensätze“ (22); ISL: 19 + 5 (24); IRQ: 22 + 5 (27). The sum is 20 to 29 on those pages. Only IND (24 + 7 = 31) matches the claim.
findings.expected: DESCRIPTION uses the same computed count as SUMMARY (e.g. 'aus 22 Quellen'), or the template drops '30+'.
findings.verification: opus: 143 de pages say 'Kostenloser Wert aus 30+ öffentlichen Quellen' in the DESCRIPTION, and in about 138 of them the SUMMARY count of advisories plus datasets is below 30. Examples: GRD 19+3=22, ISL 19+5, IRQ 22+5, GIN 20+5. The per-country meta description therefore contradicts the page's own count.

findings.quote: Keine Säule signalisiert für Irland ein nennenswertes Risiko
findings.problem: Eight pages label a pillar as 'Hauptrisiko' in the DESCRIPTION (IRL „Hauptrisiko: Naturgefahren (7.8)“, LUX „Kriminalität (8.0)“, LTU „Regierungsführung (7.4)“, MHL „Gesundheit (7.1)“) and then say in FAQ2 that no pillar signals a notable risk („Keine Säule signalisiert für … ein nennenswertes Risiko“: IRL, ISL, LTU, LUX, LVA, MHL, MLT, NOR).
findings.expected: On pages without a risk-level pillar, use a neutral label ('Schwächste Säule: …') or drop the label. DESCRIPTION and FAQ2 must agree.
findings.verification: opus: IRL DESCRIPTION: 'Hauptrisiko: Naturgefahren (7.8)'. The same page says 'Keine Säule signalisiert für Irland ein nennenswertes Risiko: Selbst die schwächste Säule, Naturgefahren, erreicht 7…'. 27 de pages carry the no-risk sentence, so the meta description labels as 'Hauptrisiko' something the FAQ says is not a risk.

findings.quote: Hauptrisiko: Kriminalität (6.8).
findings.problem: 42 of the 64 scored pages name a Hauptrisiko that is not the lowest pillar in their own PILLAR BARS, and their FAQ names a different drag. TJK: DESCRIPTION says Kriminalität (6.8) is the main risk, but PILLAR BARS show Regierungsführung 2.3/10 as the lowest. FAQ1 says 'vor allem Regierungsführung (2.3/10) den Wert nach unten ziehen', while FAQ2 says 'Die meiste Aufmerksamkeit verdient die Säule Kriminalität mit 6.8/10' (the second-highest pillar). Same pattern: PER (Kriminalität 6.5 named; Regierungsführung 4.8 lowest), NRU (Gesundheit 7.6 named; Regierungsführung 5.4 and Kriminalität 5.7 lower), PRK (Konflikt 4.8 named; Regierungsführung 2.4 lowest). STP FAQ1 says 'vor allem Gesundheit (5.9/10)' and omits Kriminalität 4.9/10, the lowest pillar.
findings.expected: Name the pillar that is actually weakest (or state the rule that selects another one) and use the same pillar in DESCRIPTION, SUMMARY and both FAQ answers, so that 'Hauptrisiko', 'meiste Aufmerksamkeit' and 'vor allem … nach unten' name one pillar.
findings.verification: opus: On TJK.de, DESCRIPTION reads 'Hauptrisiko: Kriminalität (6.8)' while the PILLAR BARS show Regierungsführung 2.3. FAQ1 says 'vor allem Regierungsführung (2.3/10)', and FAQ2 says 'kein einzelner Faktor sticht ... hervor: Die meiste Aufmerksamkeit verdient die Säule Kriminalität'. A scan of all scored de pages found the DESCRIPTION main risk is not the lowest pillar on 122 of 191 (e.g. NIC Kriminalität 6.3 vs Regierungsführung 1.7, PRK, PER), so whatever selection rule is used, it is hidden and conflicts with FAQ1.

findings.quote: Für Sierra Leone sticht kein einzelner Faktor als kritisch hervor
findings.problem: The SUMMARY names a main risk while the FAQ on the same page says no single factor stands out. SLE: SUMMARY 'Das größte Risiko ist die Ausbreitung von Epidemien: 7,7 von 10', FAQ2 'Für Sierra Leone sticht kein einzelner Faktor als kritisch hervor'. The same on PNG, UGA, ZAF, VCT, TCD and PRK. Separately, DESCRIPTION's 'Hauptrisiko' conflicts with FAQ2's 'Keine Säule signalisiert … ein nennenswertes Risiko' on SGP, SWE, SVN, TUV, TWN, NRU, PLW and POL.
findings.expected: One consistent answer per page: either name the main risk in SUMMARY, DESCRIPTION and FAQ2, or say that no pillar stands out and drop 'Das größte Risiko' and 'Hauptrisiko'.
findings.verification: opus: On SLE.de the SUMMARY says 'Das größte Risiko ist die Ausbreitung von Epidemien: 7,7 von 10' and DESCRIPTION has 'Hauptrisiko: Gesundheit (4.9)', while FAQ2 opens 'Für Sierra Leone sticht kein einzelner Faktor als kritisch hervor'. NRU/PLW/TUV give a DESCRIPTION 'Hauptrisiko' next to FAQ2 'Keine Säule signalisiert ... ein nennenswertes Risiko'. The answer is inconsistent within the page.

findings.quote: am niedrigsten bewertet ist die schwache Regierungsführung: 4,2 von 10 auf der INFORM-Skala, wobei 10 am schlechtesten ist
findings.problem: On NRU, PLW, POL, PRT, SGP, SVN, SWE and TUV the SUMMARY ranks an item as 'am niedrigsten bewertet' and then gives an INFORM risk value where 10 is the worst (e.g. PLW 'die Gefährdung durch Naturgefahren: 2,3 von 10 … wobei 10 die höchste Gefährdung bedeutet'). A low risk value is good news, so the wording reads as the weakest item while it describes the lowest risk. The same sentence opens from safety scores where 10 is the safest ('Alle fünf Bereiche erreichen mindestens 7 von 10').
findings.expected: Keep the two scales apart: say 'geringstes Risiko (INFORM 2,3 von 10)' for risk values and reserve 'am niedrigsten bewertet' for the safety pillar scores.
findings.verification: opus: POL.de contains the quote exactly: 'am niedrigsten bewertet ist die schwache Regierungsführung: 4,2 von 10 auf der INFORM-Skala, wobei 10 am schlechtesten ist'. The same 'am niedrigsten bewertet' + low INFORM risk value appears on NRU/PLW and others. A low risk value presented as the lowest-rated item (and 'schwache' for a pillar at or above 7) mixes the two scales.

findings.quote: Top concern: conflict (5.1).
findings.problem: On 17 of 63 scored pages the DESCRIPTION's top concern is not the lowest visible pillar other than governance, and the page's own FAQ or bars point at a different pillar. COL: 'Top concern: conflict (5.1)' while PILLAR BARS has Crime 4.8/10 and the FAQ says 'above all by crime (4.8/10)'. DOM (crime 6.6 named; natural hazards 5.3 lower and called the drag), DZA (health 6.8 named; natural hazards 6.3 lower), BRB (health 6.6 named; natural hazards 6.2 lower and 'above all'), GAB (crime 5.6 named; health 5.2 lower). Governance is also inconsistent: it is the named top concern on BGR, BIH, CYP and CZE, but skipped on 31 other pages where it is the lowest visible score (AGO: governance 4.4, top concern health 4.9).
findings.expected: One documented rule for the top concern, applied the same way on every page, matching the pillar the FAQ calls the main drag.
findings.verification: opus: On COL the DESCRIPTION and Q2 name conflict (5.1), while Q1 on the same page says 'pulled down ... above all by crime (4.8/10)'. On DZA, Q1 says natural hazards and governance are the drag but Q2 and the DESCRIPTION name health (6.8). Two different 'main concern' rules run on one page.

findings.quote: By contrast, crime scores 5.0/10 and is Afghanistan's strongest area.
findings.problem: On AFG (3.6/10, 'Not recommended') 5.0 is called the strength, while the lowest pillar (governance 1.8/10) is only 'Another area to watch'. Same pattern on CAF ('natural hazards scores 5.9/10 and is the Central African Republic's strongest area'; governance 2.1 only 'another area to watch') and COD ('natural hazards scores 5.4/10 and is the Democratic Republic of the Congo's strongest area'; governance 2.0). BFA: 'natural hazards scores 6.1/10 and is Burkina Faso's strongest area'.
findings.expected: Call the best pillar the least-weak one on a high-risk page (e.g. 'least weak area: crime 5.0/10, still high risk') and give the lowest pillar as a primary concern.
findings.verification: opus: AFG Q2 says 'The main concern for Afghanistan is conflict, at 3.0/10 ... Another area to watch is governance, at 1.8/10', so the 'other' area is worse than the main one. Q1 on the same page says 'above all by governance (1.8/10)'. CAF has the same pattern (conflict 3.4 main, governance 2.1 'another'). Calling the least-weak pillar the 'strongest area' is literally true and only a minor style point.

findings.quote: Free score from 30+ public sources, recalculated daily.
findings.problem: On 62 of the 63 scored pages the SUMMARY's own source counts add to fewer than 30: AFG 22 advisories + 7 datasets = 29, ALB 20+5 = 25, CAN 20+5 = 25, FSM 13+3 = 16. Only BGD (25+7 = 32) reaches 30.
findings.expected: State the count actually used (e.g. '29 sources') or make the DESCRIPTION match the SUMMARY.
findings.verification: opus: The DESCRIPTION template says 'Free score from 30+ public sources' on every page. The SUMMARY counts are 22+7=29 on AFG, 20+5=25 on GAB and 18+3=21 on BRN, so the snippet overstates the sources actually used.

findings.quote: even its weakest area, governance, scores 8.0/10, well inside the low-risk band
findings.problem: The site's own labels put 8.0 and above in 'Very low risk' (BGR: 'Bulgaria safety score: 8.0/10 (Very low risk)'), yet CZE calls its 8.0 governance 'well inside the low-risk band' and its SUMMARY says 'the lowest-rated is weak governance: 3.4 out of 10'. EST says natural hazards 8.3 'sits in the low-risk band'. CYP calls its 7.2 governance 'weak governance'.
findings.expected: Use 'very low risk' for pillars at 8.0 and above, and do not call pillars above roughly 7 'weak'.
findings.verification: opus: The 'low-risk band' part is not a real problem: pillar rows carry their own 'Low' label (CZE governance '8.0/10 · Low'), so the FAQ matches the pillar scale. The real problem is that the CZE and CYP SUMMARY says 'All five areas score at least 7 out of 10; the lowest-rated is weak governance: 3.4 out of 10 on the INFORM scale'. It calls 8.0 (and 7.2) governance 'weak' and puts an inverted 3.4/10 right after 'at least 7 out of 10'.

findings.quote: Governance 5.7/10 * When a pillar has low data coverage, its contribution to the overall score is reduced or excluded.
findings.problem: The footnote sits inside the pillar list on 8 pages (ATG, BHS, BLZ, BRN, CPV, COM, DMA, FSM), so it reads like a bar label. 'Reduced or excluded' does not say which. The narrative on those pages often ignores the flagged pillar (ATG: 'above all by crime (6.3/10)' while Governance 5.7/10 is shown).
findings.expected: Move the note below the bars, state whether the flagged pillar counts in the score, and mention it in the narrative.
findings.verification: opus: The note is not a visible bar label: in PillarBreakdown.astro it is a PillarCoverageTip asterisk tooltip, and the text extraction merged it in, so that part is rejected. The narrative contradiction is real. ATG shows Governance 5.7 as its lowest bar but says 'above all by crime (6.3/10)'. CPV shows Crime 4.9 (zero indicators) but says 'above all by governance (6.4/10)'. The text silently skips the visibly lowest, low-coverage pillar.

findings.quote: PILLAR BARS: Crime 5.1/10 * When a pillar has low data coverage
findings.problem: Pillars flagged low data coverage stay in PILLAR BARS at their score, but the narrative drops them. MDV's lowest bar is Crime 5.1/10 (flagged), yet its SUMMARY says 'The weakest area is weak governance' although the governance bar is 6.3/10. KIR's bars show Governance 5.0/10 and Crime 5.7/10 (both flagged), yet DESCRIPTION says 'Top concern: health (6.1).' GRD's Governance 5.4/10 (flagged) is skipped: FAQ 1 says 'above all by crime (6.2/10)'. The footnote also sits inside the bar list (KIR and MHL repeat it twice).
findings.expected: Either include flagged pillars in the weakest-area and top-concern logic (with a 'low coverage' tag), or exclude them everywhere on the page, including the bars. Show the coverage note once below the bars rather than inside the list.
findings.verification: opus: MDV: bars show 'Crime 5.1/10 *' (low coverage) as the lowest bar, while the SUMMARY says 'The weakest area is weak governance' and DESCRIPTION says 'Top concern: governance (6.3)'. KIR names health 6.1 below flagged Governance 5.0 and Crime 5.7. GRD skips flagged Governance 5.4. The narrative leaves out low-coverage pillars but the bars still rank them lowest, so 'weakest area' contradicts what the page shows.

findings.quote: Free score from 30+ public sources, recalculated daily.
findings.problem: Every full-score DESCRIPTION promises '30+ public sources', but the same page's SUMMARY counts them: GIN '20 government travel advisories and 5 other public datasets' (25), GRD 19 + 3 (22), HTI 23 + 6 (29), KIR 17 + 4 (21), KNA 15 + 3 (18). Only IND reaches 30 (24 + 7 = 31); 64 of 65 pages total below 30. Search snippets and the page body disagree.
findings.expected: Derive the DESCRIPTION number from the SUMMARY count (for example 'from 25 public sources' on GIN), or drop the number, so the two never disagree.
findings.verification: opus: Every DESCRIPTION uses the site-wide SOURCE_COUNT_DISPLAY ('30+'). The page's own 'It combines N government travel advisories and M other public datasets' adds up to under 30 on 187 of 192 en pages (GIN 20+5=25, MOZ 20+7=27); only 5 reach 30 or more (IND 24+7). The snippet's source claim contradicts the page body.

findings.quote: the lowest-rated is weak governance: 4.5 out of 10 on the INFORM scale
findings.problem: The adjective 'weak' is attached to values that are not weak. MLT says 'All five areas score at least 7 out of 10' and then calls governance 'weak' at 7.0/10. LTU calls public administration 'weak' at 0.98 on a scale where higher is better (its governance bar is 7.4/10). HUN, MNE and MDV write 'The weakest area is weak governance', a tautology that adds nothing.
findings.expected: Describe the value rather than the adjective, for example 'the lowest-rated is governance: 7.0/10 (INFORM 4.5 out of 10, where 10 is worst)'. Use 'weak' only where the score is below the band boundary.
findings.verification: opus: MLT SUMMARY says 'All five areas score at least 7 out of 10; the lowest-rated is weak governance: 4.5 out of 10 on the INFORM scale' while governance is 7.0/10 (Low). LTU calls public administration 'weak' at V-Dem 0.98 with governance 7.4/10. HUN, MNE and MDV say 'The weakest area is weak governance'. The template attaches 'weak' regardless of the value, which contradicts the preceding clause.

findings.quote: the most severe warnings — do not travel — have been issued by Germany and New Zealand
findings.problem: Names two issuers, but SAU's SUMMARY says 5 governments advise against all travel. TCD's FAQ names United States and Australia while its SUMMARY says 8 advise against all travel. QAT's FAQ says 'the most severe warnings ... have been issued by Singapore' (plural noun, one issuer). The template neither counts issuers nor adds 'among others' to incomplete lists.
findings.expected: Use the real count ('5 governments advise against all travel, including ...') and match singular or plural to the number of issuers.
findings.verification: opus: SAU lists 5 level-4 advisories (NZ, DE, CZ, PL, SG) but names only Germany and New Zealand. TCD lists 8 but names only the US and Australia. Neither adds 'among others', although PSE's template does. QAT says 'the most severe warnings ... have been issued by Singapore' with a single issuer.

findings.quote: The overall picture is reassuring: most governments advise only normal precautions for South Georgia
findings.problem: Partial-data pages (no score, fewer than four sources) still say 'the overall picture is reassuring'. On SGS, SHN and SPM the page reports one government advisory, so 'most governments' is wrong. PCN, PRI and XKX say the same while stating that no score is given.
findings.expected: Drop the 'reassuring' verdict on partial pages. When the count is one, write 'one government advises ...' and give its level without an overall verdict.
findings.verification: opus: SGS and SHN Q2 say 'has one government travel advisory on record. The overall picture is reassuring: most governments advise only normal precautions'. 'Most governments' cannot describe a count of one. (PRI, with 8 advisories, also says 'none currently raises it above a low-level advisory' while its NL and Taiwan entries are Level 2.)

findings.quote: the strongest current warning — exercise increased caution — comes from United States and United Kingdom
findings.problem: Calls 'exercise increased caution' the 'strongest current warning' when it is the middle level, and the same answer calls it the prevailing guidance. Examples: PER, PAN, PRY, TLS, TKM, UZB, SLV. It reads as a contradiction to a native reader.
findings.expected: 'The highest level in use is exercise increased caution, issued by the United States and the United Kingdom' or similar.
findings.verification: opus: PER reads 'The prevailing guidance is to exercise increased caution...; the strongest current warning — exercise increased caution — comes from United States and United Kingdom.' The page lists 21 governments at Level 2, so the sentence repeats the prevailing level and wrongly credits it to only two issuers.

findings.quote: It combines 25 government travel advisories and 7 other public datasets
findings.problem: The sentence counts a dataset that has no row on the page. Six scored pages have no World Bank homicide row (AGO, BDI, BEN, BFA, BGD, BLR), and on each the claimed dataset count is one higher than the table shows: BGD says 7 but the table has 6 (V-Dem, INFORM, ReliefWeb, GDACS, GPI, UCDP); AGO says 6 but shows 5; BDI says 6 but shows 5; BFA says 6 but shows 5; BEN says 5 but shows 4; BLR says 5 but shows 4. Pages with a World Bank row match exactly. The partial-data HERO lines show the same thing: ABW 'Travel advisories from 8 governments World Bank' and AND 'UCDP conflict data World Bank' list World Bank as data the site has, with no value on the page.
findings.expected: Build the dataset count from the same list as the table: count only datasets that produce a displayed value, or show the missing World Bank value. Apply the same rule to partial-data pages.
findings.verification: opus: BGD says '7 other public datasets' but its indicator table cites only 6 sources (V-Dem, INFORM, ReliefWeb, GDACS, GPI, UCDP). The cause is in the data: latest.json lists 'worldbank' in sources for BGD, AGO, BLR, ABW and AND, yet none has a World Bank indicator (the source survives through population or unscored series). Grey pages such as ABW also show 'World Bank' under 'What we do have' with no value.

findings.quote: combines 18 government travel advisories and 3 other public datasets
findings.problem: On 11 pages the SUMMARY counts exactly one more 'other public dataset' than the INDICATORS table shows sources for: BRN 3 vs 2 shown (INFORM, UCDP), COM 4 vs 3, CPV 5 vs 4, BTN 5 vs 4, CAF 6 vs 5, CHN 7 vs 6, CIV 6 vs 5, COD 7 vs 6, COG 6 vs 5, CUB 7 vs 6, DJI 5 vs 4. The advisory counts match on every page checked.
findings.expected: Count only the sources actually displayed, or display the missing dataset row. Likely culprit: the source behind the Crime pillar on pages with no crime row.
findings.verification: opus: The count mismatch is real: BRN says 3 other datasets but shows only INFORM and UCDP; COM says 4 but shows V-Dem, INFORM and UCDP; CHN and CUB say 7 vs 6. The cause is not the crime pillar: latest.json sources include 'worldbank' even when the country has no World Bank indicator, and it is counted anyway.

findings.quote: The main concern is poor access to health care: 3.9 out of 10 on the INFORM scale, where 10 is the worst access
findings.problem: The SUMMARY 'main concern' sentence does not match the page's own bars. All 23 PILLAR BARS lines are sorted lowest first, and on 16 of them (DOM, DZA, ECU, EGY, ERI, ETH, FJI, FSM, GAB, GEO, GHA, GIN, GNB, GNQ, GRD, GTM) Governance is the first, lowest bar. None of the 23 SUMMARY lines mentions governance, so on those 16 pages the named main concern is a different area. Examples: DZA names access to health care (3.9 on an INFORM risk scale where 10 is worst; Health pillar 6.8/10) while its first bar is 'Governance 3.7/10'; GIN names health while 'Governance 2.7/10' is lowest; ERI names public safety while 'Governance 2.4/10' is lowest. FJI and FSM call 4.7 and 5.6 out of 10 'poor' access, which is mid-scale on that scale.
findings.expected: Choose the main concern from the same lowest-first order the bars use, so the sentence names governance where governance is the lowest bar. If governance is left out on purpose, say so on the page or drop it from the bar ordering. Do not call a mid-scale INFORM value 'poor'.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on DZA's page, next to the bars 'Governance 3.7/10 | ... Health 6.8/10'. selectDriverPillar in src/lib/country-summary.ts leaves governance out on purpose (DIRECT_RISK_PILLARS), but the page never says so, so a reader sees a 'main concern' that is not the lowest bar. Separately, the topic 'poor access to health care' is fixed text used at any value, so 3.9 (DZA) or 4.7 (FJI) on a 10-is-worst scale is still called 'poor'.

findings.quote: It combines 22 government travel advisories and 5 other public datasets
findings.problem: On 10 pages the SUMMARY counts one more 'other public dataset' than the INDICATORS table shows: EGY says 5 (table shows GPI, INFORM, UCDP, V-Dem = 4); ERI 5 vs 4; GAB 5 vs 4; GIN 5 vs 4; GMB 5 vs 4; GNQ 5 vs 4; GEO 6 vs 5; GNB 6 vs 5; ETH 7 vs 6; FSM 3 vs 2. The missing one is always the World Bank feed, which has no row on those pages. Partial pages GIB, FRO and GRL also list 'World Bank' under 'What we do have' with no value. On every page that has a World Bank row the count matches. Code: the count is every source feed except advisories (/Users/riccardo/Developer/VibeCoding/Isitsafetotravel/.claude/worktrees/v10-integration/src/lib/provenance-copy.ts, otherSourceCount), and a feed is included whenever any raw row exists; wb_population maps to 'worldbank' (/Users/riccardo/Developer/VibeCoding/Isitsafetotravel/.claude/worktrees/v10-integration/src/pipeline/scoring/engine.ts, around lines 561-562 and buildSourcesForCountry).
findings.expected: Count only feeds that show at least one value on the page, or name the population-only input in the source line so the count and the table agree.
findings.verification: opus: latest.json lists EGY sources as advisories, gpi, inform, ucdp, vdem and worldbank, which makes 5 non-advisory feeds. EGY's indicator table has no World Bank row (its crime pillar has only gpi_safety_security), so 4 are visible. The count includes a feed that shows no value.

findings.quote: It combines 24 government travel advisories and 5 other public datasets
findings.problem: On the eight scored pages with no World Bank homicide row (IRN, IRQ, KGZ, KHM, KIR, KWT, LAO, LBN), the 'other public datasets' count is one higher than the datasets the INDICATORS table actually shows. IRN lists V-Dem, INFORM, GPI and UCDP (4) but says 5; KIR lists INFORM, ReliefWeb and UCDP (3) but says 4. Seven of these pages show '90% data coverage' in the HERO (KIR shows 55%), so the count appears to include the missing World Bank source. The other 18 scored pages match exactly.
findings.expected: Count only the datasets that produced a displayed value (IRN should say 4, KIR 3, and likewise for the other six pages).
findings.verification: opus: getProvenanceCounts counts every non-advisory entry in country.sources. In latest.json, KWT, IRN and LAO list 'worldbank' with no WB indicator in any pillar. KIR lists worldbank with an empty crime pillar. So KWT shows 4 datasets but says 5, LAO shows 5 but says 6, and KIR shows 3 but says 4.

findings.quote: It combines 19 government travel advisories and 6 other public datasets
findings.problem: The dataset count includes World Bank even when the page shows no World Bank row. All 14 pages that show a World Bank row match their count. All 11 that do not overstate it by exactly one: LBR says 6 (5 listed: V-Dem, INFORM, GPI, ReliefWeb, UCDP), LBY 5 (4), LKA 7 (6), LSO 5 (4), MDG 7 (6), MDV 4 (3), MHL 5 (4), MLI 5 (4), MOZ 7 (6), MRT 5 (4), MWI 6 (5). Partial pages MAC, MAF, MCO and MNP also name 'World Bank' as a source with no figure shown.
findings.expected: Count only datasets that feed a displayed value, and list World Bank as a source only when a World Bank value appears on the page.
findings.verification: opus: getProvenanceCounts counts every entry in country.sources except advisories. LBR and MDV have 'worldbank' in sources but no World Bank indicator in any pillar. So LBR's '6 other public datasets' lists only 5 (V-Dem, INFORM, GPI, ReliefWeb, UCDP), and MDV's '4' lists 3.

findings.quote: Exercise caution 7 6.7 out of 10
findings.problem: The large badge is the score rounded to a whole number, but the label follows the band edges. So 6.7 shows '7' beside 'Exercise caution' (band 6 to 7; LCA), 4.8 shows '5' beside 'Not recommended' (band below 5; LBY), and 7.6 shows '8' beside 'Generally safe' (band 7 to 8; MDA). A reader sees a number from the next band next to the label.
findings.expected: Use one scheme: show the band's own number, or show the decimal score only.
findings.verification: opus: The HERO strings are on the pages: LCA 'Exercise caution 7 6.7 out of 10', LBY 'Not recommended 5 4.8', MDA 'Generally safe 8 7.6'. scoreDisplay = Math.round(score) puts a whole number from the next band beside the band label of the decimal score.

findings.quote: Natural hazards 6.2/10 * When a pillar has low data coverage, its contribution to the overall score is reduced or excluded.
findings.problem: Pillars with no data are drawn as scores. TWN shows Health 6.7/10 and Natural hazards 6.2/10 with no health or natural-hazard row in INDICATORS (dataCompleteness 0; the page's three datasets are GPI, V-Dem and UCDP). TON, TUV, VUT and WSM show Crime 5.7/10 with no crime row (dataCompleteness 0), so the bar is the prior, not evidence. Only a small footnote says 'low data coverage'. TWN's HERO gives '45% data coverage' next to 'Generally safe 8 7.9' with no note that two of five pillars are unmeasured.
findings.expected: Draw a 'no data' state instead of a number for pillars with dataCompleteness 0, or label prior-only values as estimates, and mention unmeasured pillars in the HERO caveat.
findings.verification: opus: TWN shows Natural hazards 6.2/10 and Health 6.7/10 as scores, but INDICATORS has no health or natural-hazard row (TWN sources: only GPI, V-Dem, UCDP and advisories; no INFORM). TUV shows Crime 5.7/10 with no crime row. These are prior values drawn as measured scores, with only a generic footnote. Examples: TWN, TUV, WSM.

findings.quote: la advertencia más severa — no viajar — proviene de Irlanda y Hungría.
findings.problem: SUMMARY counts 3 governments advising no travel (BDI), but FAQ names only two issuers with no 'entre otros'. Same on ETH (3 counted, 2 named: Hungría y Serbia), BHR (4 counted, 2 named: Países Bajos y Polonia) and COD (8 counted, 2 named: Estados Unidos y Australia). Readers will take the two as the full list. ARE also uses the plural 'las advertencias más severas' for a single issuer (Singapur).
findings.expected: Add 'entre otros' or state the actual number of issuers, as AFG and BLR already do; use the singular when there is one issuer.
findings.verification: opus: Confirmed. BDI counts 3 governments advising no travel but the FAQ names only Irlanda y Hungría, ETH counts 3 and names 2, BHR counts 4 and names 2, COD counts 8 and names 2, all without 'entre otros'. AFG and BLR do add 'entre otros'. ARE uses the plural 'las advertencias más severas ... han sido emitidas por Singapur' for its single issuer (summary: 1 desaconseja). Incomplete and contradicting the summary count, so medium.

findings.quote: ninguno lo sitúa por encima de un aviso de bajo nivel.
findings.problem: On 22 scored pages the FAQ advisory answer says most governments recommend normal precautions and 'ninguno lo sitúa por encima de un aviso de bajo nivel', while the same page's SUMMARY counts governments advising 'extremar la precaución': GRD (13 normal, 6 extremar), NLD (6), MNG (7), KAZ (9), GRC (2), ITA (4). Cause: src/lib/seo.ts:984-985 takes the advisory band from the modal level, and the 'normal' copy (country-faq-copy.ts:428) is absolute, so a majority-normal page still gets 'ninguno' even when other governments sit higher. Reassurance that the same page's own counts contradict is misleading for a travel decision.
findings.expected: Use 'ninguno' only when no government issues above level 1. Otherwise state the count, e.g. 'la mayoría recomienda precauciones normales; 6 recomiendan extremar la precaución'.
findings.verification: opus: GRD (13 normal, 6 extremar), NLD (14/6) and ITA (15/4): FAQ A3 says 'ninguno lo sitúa por encima de un aviso de bajo nivel' while the SUMMARY on the same page counts governments that advise extremar la precaución.

findings.field: SUMMARY (main concern) vs cited GPI value
findings.quote: La principal preocupación es un clima de violencia e inseguridad: el Global Peace Index da al país un 1,81 en una escala de 1 (máxima paz) a 5 (GPI 2026).
findings.problem: KWT's SUMMARY names violence as the main concern while quoting a GPI value that, on the page's own 1 (máxima paz) to 5 scale, is 1,81, near the most peaceful end. JOR has the same contradiction: 'un 1,91 en una escala de 1 (máxima paz) a 5'. The same sentence template appears on IRQ (2,66), ISR (3,12), KEN (2,45), LBY (2,36) and MEX (2,65). The 'main concern' seems to be chosen relative to the other indicators, not by its absolute level, and 'clima de violencia e inseguridad' says nothing specific about the risk.
findings.expected: Name a main concern only when its absolute value sits in the risk half of its own scale; otherwise name the real driver or drop the sentence.
findings.verification: opus: KWT (1,81) and JOR (1,91) SUMMARY call 'un clima de violencia e inseguridad' the main concern, citing a GPI value near the peaceful end of the 1-5 scale. On ISR (3,12) the sentence is coherent, so the problem is limited to low-GPI pages that the driver rule picks.

findings.quote: Ningún factor destaca como crítico en Guinea: el área que requiere más atención es salud, con 4.2/10.
findings.problem: On 47 of 65 scored pages the SUMMARY names a main risk ('El principal riesgo es…' or 'La principal preocupación es…') while FAQ A2 says 'Ningún factor destaca como crítico'. GIN: SUMMARY 'El principal riesgo es el acceso limitado a la atención sanitaria…' vs A2 above. Cause: FAQ A2 uses the 'mid' copy for any driver from 4.0 to 7.0 (seo.ts:851-852; country-faq-copy.ts:412), while the SUMMARY uses 'mainRisk' below 5.0 and 'concern' from 5.0 to 7.0 (country-summary.ts:42 and frame logic). The two surfaces disagree for every driver in that range.
findings.expected: Same threshold and wording on both surfaces. If the summary names a main concern, the FAQ must not say that no factor stands out.
findings.verification: opus: GIN FAQ A2 'Ningún factor destaca como crítico en Guinea: ... salud, con 4.2/10' versus SUMMARY 'El principal riesgo es el acceso limitado a la atención sanitaria'. Calling a 4.2 pillar non-critical is itself questionable.

findings.field: PILLAR BARS vs DESCRIPTION and FAQ
findings.quote: Gobernanza 5.0/10 * Cuando un pilar tiene poca cobertura de datos
findings.problem: Low-coverage pillars are printed with a footnote and their real score in the bars, but the DESCRIPTION and FAQ are built without them. KIR bars: 'Gobernanza 5.0/10 *' and 'Criminalidad 5.7/10 *', yet the DESCRIPTION says 'Mayor riesgo: salud (6.1).' and FAQ A1 says 'sobre todo, por salud (6.1/10)'. MDV: 'Criminalidad 5.1/10 *' is the lowest bar, while the DESCRIPTION says 'Mayor riesgo: gobernanza (6.3).' Same pattern on MHL and GRD (7 pages carry the footnote). The footnote never says which pillar the FAQ and DESCRIPTION left out.
findings.expected: Say in the FAQ and DESCRIPTION when the lowest pillar is left out for coverage, e.g. 'La gobernanza tiene datos insuficientes y no cuenta en esta valoración', and keep the wording in step with the bars.
findings.verification: opus: KIR bars show Gobernanza 5.0* and Criminalidad 5.7* below Salud 6.1, yet the DESCRIPTION and A1 ('sobre todo, por salud (6.1') name salud. MDV shows Criminalidad 5.1* as the lowest bar while the DESCRIPTION names gobernanza (6.3). Nothing tells the reader that the footnoted pillar was left out.

findings.field: FAQ A1 verdict vs FAQ A3 advisories
findings.quote: viajar allí exige extremar las precauciones.
findings.problem: Nine 'No —' verdicts say travel 'exige extremar las precauciones' (suggesting a careful visit is an option), while the same page's advisory counts show most governments advising against all travel: HTI 20 of 23, IRN 23 of 24, IRQ 16 of 22, LBN 17 of 23, LBY 17 of 21, MLI 20 of 21, MMR 12 of 22, NER 18 of 21 'desaconsejan todo viaje'. NGA has 12 reconsider and 2 do not travel. The 'No' verdict and its body send mixed messages.
findings.expected: When most governments advise against all travel, the verdict body should say so, e.g. 'la mayoría de los gobiernos desaconsejan todo viaje'.
findings.verification: opus: HTI (20 of 23), IRN (23 of 24) and MLI (20 of 21) desaconsejan todo viaje, yet the 'No —' verdict body says 'viajar allí exige extremar las precauciones'. That understates the advice and echoes the level-2 label.

findings.quote: El panorama general es tranquilizador: la mayoría de los gobiernos solo recomiendan precauciones normales para Santa Elena
findings.problem: 16 places without a score (PCN, PRI, PYF, REU, SGS, SHN, SJM, SMR, SPM, SXM, TCA, TKL, VAT, VGB, VIR, WLF) say 'El panorama general es tranquilizador' right under text that says the site cannot give a safety score ('menos de cuatro fuentes independientes'). SGS, SHN and SPM have one advisory ('cuenta con un aviso de viaje gubernamental') but still say 'la mayoría de los gobiernos'. A traveller will read this as a safety verdict built on one or two issuers.
findings.expected: On no-score pages list the advisories as they are (for example 'un gobierno recomienda precauciones normales'), and drop 'tranquilizador' and 'la mayoría' when the sample is one or two issuers.
findings.verification: opus: SHN has a single advisory, yet the FAQ says 'El panorama general es tranquilizador: la mayoría de los gobiernos...', right after saying no score can be given. 'La mayoría' with one issuer is wrong, and 'tranquilizador' reads as a verdict on a page that has no score.

findings.quote: la advertencia más severa — extremar la precaución — proviene de Estados Unidos y Australia
findings.problem: On 8 scored pages (PAN, PER, PRY, SLV, SWZ, TKM, TLS, UZB) and on XKX, the FAQ names extremar la precaución as the predominant advisory and then calls the 'advertencia más severa' the same level, naming two issuers. No issuer on those pages is above extremar according to the SUMMARY counts, so the clause only repeats the predominant advisory and reads as a glitch.
findings.expected: Drop the 'más severa' clause when it repeats the predominant level, or name the most severe level actually issued.
findings.verification: opus: PAN says 'la advertencia más severa — extremar la precaución — proviene de Estados Unidos y Australia' while its SUMMARY has 18 governments recommending extremar. The 'most severe' clause repeats the predominant level and wrongly credits it to just two issuers. UZB has the same.

findings.quote: Risque principal : conflit (3.0).
findings.problem: The 'Risque principal' line in DESCRIPTION, and the FAQ sentence 'le pilier ... qui demande le plus d'attention', often name a pillar that is not the lowest one displayed. The same page's FAQ 'surtout par ...' sentence then names the lowest. By my parse, 34 of the 62 pages that show both a 'Risque principal' line and PILLAR BARS do this (ignoring pillars flagged low-coverage with *). AFG: DESCRIPTION says conflit (3.0), but PILLAR BARS show 'Gouvernance 1.8/10' and the FAQ says 'surtout par gouvernance (1.8/10)'. DZA: FAQ calls santé (6.8) the main concern while 'Gouvernance 3.7/10' and 'Risques naturels 6.3/10' are lower. CHN: DESCRIPTION says criminalité (6.0) while 'Gouvernance 4.3/10' and 'Risques naturels 4.4/10' are lower. EGY and BRA show the same pattern.
findings.expected: Name the lowest displayed pillar as the main risk, or document a stated exclusion rule (e.g. 'hors gouvernance') and apply it identically on every page. The 'surtout par' and 'plus d'attention' sentences must name the same pillar.
findings.verification: opus: AFG DESCRIPTION says 'Risque principal : conflit (3.0)' but the FAQ says 'surtout par gouvernance (1.8/10)'. CHN DESCRIPTION and FAQ name criminalité (6.0) as the main risk, while its first FAQ says the score is pulled down by risques naturels (4.4). DZA names santé (6.8) although risques naturels is 6.3. So one page names two different 'main' pillars, and no exclusion rule is stated.

findings.quote: et tout voyage exige une grande prudence
findings.problem: On four 'risque élevé' pages (AFG, BFA, CAF, COD) the answer begins 'Non —' and then softens to 'tout voyage exige une grande prudence' (any trip needs great caution). The same pages' advisories say the opposite: AFG 22 governments 'déconseillent formellement tout voyage'; CAF 18; BFA 14; COD 8, plus 11 'déconseillent le voyage sauf raison impérative'. A reader gets 'no' and 'caution' as the same message.
findings.expected: When most governments advise against travel, say so plainly (e.g. 'Non : la plupart des gouvernements déconseillent tout voyage') and drop the softening clause.
findings.verification: opus: AFG, BFA, CAF and COD all contain 'et tout voyage exige une grande prudence'. AFG's SUMMARY says all 22 governments 'déconseillent formellement tout voyage', and COD has 8 'tout voyage' plus 11 'sauf raison impérative'. Framing the advice as 'great caution' understates a near-unanimous do-not-travel consensus, although the answer does begin with 'Non'.

findings.quote: et surtout par gouvernance (1.7/10)
findings.problem: Two answers on the same page name different main problems. Answer 1 says the score is pulled down 'surtout par' the lowest raw pillar (NIC: Gouvernance 1.7/10, the lowest bar on the page). Answer 2 and the DESCRIPTION name another pillar as the main concern: 'le domaine qui demande le plus d'attention est le pilier criminalité, à 6.3/10' and 'Risque principal : criminalité (6.3)'. The same split appears on KAZ (answer 1 'surtout par gouvernance (3.9/10)', while answer 2 and the DESCRIPTION name risques naturels at 6.4), KGZ (answer 1 'surtout par gouvernance (4.0/10)', answer 2 criminalité at 6.8), and GIN, GTM, GUY, HND, MRT, where answer 1 names governance or health as the bigger drag and answer 2 and the DESCRIPTION name a different pillar. The page tells the reader two incompatible things about what drives the score.
findings.expected: One selector for the main driver, used identically in the DESCRIPTION, the SUMMARY and both answers, and consistent with the pillar bars. A pillar at 1.7/10 cannot be presented as secondary to a 6.3/10 pillar on the same page.
findings.verification: opus: NIC answer 1 says the score is pulled down 'surtout par gouvernance (1.7/10)', while answer 2 and the DESCRIPTION name criminalité 6.3 as the main risk. KAZ (governance 3.9 against risques naturels 6.4), KGZ and GIN show the same split. The main-risk selector seems to skip governance, but the drag sentence does not.

findings.quote: et tout voyage exige une grande prudence
findings.problem: On 'risque élevé' pages the verdict says travel 'exige une grande prudence' (implying it is possible with care), but the SUMMARY of the same page says most advisories tell travellers not to go: IRN 23 of 24 'déconseillent formellement tout voyage'; HTI 20 of 23; MLI 20 of 21; NER 18 of 21; LBY 17 of 21; LBN 17 of 23 (its answer 3 says 'La plupart des gouvernements déconseillent désormais tout voyage au Liban'); IRQ 16 of 22. The verdict understates a safety-critical consensus on nine pages.
findings.expected: When a majority of advisories say do not travel, the verdict says so (for example 'Non : la plupart des gouvernements déconseillent tout voyage'), and 'tout voyage exige une grande prudence' is not used. Gate the verdict on the advisory counts, not only on the band.
findings.verification: opus: IRN, HTI, MLI and LBN all read 'Non — ... risque élevé », et tout voyage exige une grande prudence' while 17-23 governments say do not travel at all. The verdict does start with 'Non', so this is an understatement rather than a reversal; medium.

findings.quote: Le pilier gouvernance, à #/#, mérite lui aussi de l'attention.
findings.problem: B22 is attached to the 'point de vigilance majeur' answer on high-risk pages where governance is among the lowest pillars: BIR (Gouvernance 2.1/10, the lowest bar, while the answer names conflit 3.1/10 as the major point), HTI (Gouvernance 2.4/10), LBN (2.9/10), IRN (3.1/10), MLI (3.5/10). Calling a 2-3/10 governance score something that 'mérite lui aussi de l'attention' (also deserves attention) understates it.
findings.expected: Name the lowest pillar and its value in the same sentence, for example 'La gouvernance, à 2.1/10, est le pilier le plus faible du pays', and treat it at least as seriously as the conflict pillar when it is lower.
findings.verification: opus: Verified on HTI (governance 2.4 vs conflict 3.2), LBN (2.9 vs 4.0) and IRN (3.1 vs 3.2). Q2 names conflict as the 'point de vigilance majeur' and says governance 'mérite lui aussi de l'attention', yet on HTI Q1 says the score is pulled down 'surtout par gouvernance (2.4/10)', so the two answers contradict each other. BIR is not a page in this batch (an invented example); the other examples hold.

findings.quote: Uniquement pour voyageurs expérimentés
findings.problem: On 'prudence élevée' pages the HERO verdict is 'Uniquement pour voyageurs expérimentés' (only for experienced travellers), while answer 1 on the same page says 'Oui, mais avec une réelle prudence — X présente un risque non négligeable'. Examples: GIN (5.7), KHM (5.9), MOZ (5.5), MRT (5.7), NIC (5.9). The HERO restricts the destination to a subset of travellers; the answer says yes.
findings.expected: One verdict per band, identical in the HERO and in the first answer.
findings.verification: opus: GIN, KHM, MOZ, MRT and NIC all carry the HERO 'Uniquement pour voyageurs expérimentés', while Q1 opens with 'Oui, mais avec une réelle prudence'. These are two different verdicts for the same band; for mass-tourism Cambodia, the HERO restriction is also stronger than the answer below it.

findings.quote: Risque principal : santé (6.9).
findings.problem: The 'main risk' named in DESCRIPTION and in the FAQ is often not the lowest pillar shown in PILLAR BARS, and the page's own FAQ text contradicts it. OMN: PILLAR BARS give Risques naturels 5.1/10 (lowest), and FAQ Q1 says 'surtout par risques naturels (5.1/10)', yet DESCRIPTION and FAQ Q2 ('le domaine qui demande le plus d'attention est le pilier santé, à 6.9/10') name santé. Same pattern: PHL DESCRIPTION 'Risque principal : conflit (6.1).' while Gouvernance 3.7 and Risques naturels 3.8 are lower; PRY 'Risque principal : santé (6.9).' while Gouvernance 4.0; NPL 'Risque principal : criminalité (6.0).' while Gouvernance 5.1; PNG 'Risque principal : santé (4.9).' while Gouvernance 4.3; PRK 'Risque principal : conflit (4.8).' while Gouvernance 2.4. Pillars with their own FAQ 'surtout par' wording and the 'domaine qui demande le plus d'attention' wording disagree with each other on the same page.
findings.expected: Name the lowest covered pillar (or the highest-risk signal) consistently in DESCRIPTION, SUMMARY and FAQ, so that the 'principal risque' is the same everywhere and matches PILLAR BARS.
findings.verification: opus: Verified: OMN DESCRIPTION 'Risque principal : santé (6.9)' while PILLAR BARS lowest is Risques naturels 5.1 and FAQ Q1 says 'surtout par risques naturels (5.1/10)'. Same on PHL (conflit 6.1 vs gouvernance 3.7 'surtout'), PRY (santé 6.9 vs gouvernance 4.0) and PRK (conflit 4.8 vs gouvernance 2.4). The 'main risk' selector seems to look only at conflict/crime/health, but the FAQ Q1 'surtout par' sentence uses all pillars, so the same page names two different main weaknesses. Not in TITLE/SUMMARY, so medium.

findings.quote: le Global Peace Index attribue au pays la note de 1,68 sur une échelle de 1 (le plus pacifique) à 5 (GPI 2026)
findings.problem: The 'principal point de vigilance' or 'moins bien noté' is chosen as the lowest raw value of a signal, not as the highest risk, so the direction is inverted. QAT: GPI 1,68 on a 1 (most peaceful) to 5 scale is among the best values, yet SUMMARY calls it 'Le principal point de vigilance est un climat de violence et d'insécurité'. NRU: 'le moins bien noté est la propagation d’épidémies : 3,2 sur 10 selon INFORM, 10 correspondant au risque le plus élevé', i.e. a low-risk value presented as the worst. PLW: 'le moins bien noté est l’exposition aux risques naturels : 2,3 sur 10 ... 10 correspondant à l’exposition la plus forte'. A reader would take a very peaceful or very low-exposure signal as the main danger.
findings.expected: Pick the signal whose risk is highest (for GPI, the highest value on 1-5; for INFORM, the highest value on 0-10), or phrase the sentence so the direction is unambiguous. Never call a low-risk value the main vigilance point.
findings.verification: opus: Only QAT holds. Its SUMMARY makes 'un climat de violence et d'insécurité' the 'principal point de vigilance' and backs it with GPI 1,68 on a 1-5 scale, which is a peaceful value. The NRU and PLW examples are not inverted: on NRU, epidemic 3.2 is the highest INFORM risk shown, so 'le moins bien noté' is accurate. Real issue: the template labels the weakest pillar's lead signal as a violent climate even when that signal's value is favourable.

findings.quote: Nepal ne présente aucun facteur véritablement critique
findings.problem: Template-level contradiction: SUMMARY names a 'principal point de vigilance' or 'principal risque' with a concrete signal, while the FAQ says the country has no truly critical factor. Examples: NPL SUMMARY 'Le principal point de vigilance est l’insécurité' vs FAQ 'Nepal ne présente aucun facteur véritablement critique'; PNG SUMMARY 'Le principal risque est l’accès limité aux soins : 7,9 sur 10' vs FAQ 'Papouasie-Nouvelle-Guinée ne présente aucun facteur véritablement critique'; PHL SUMMARY 'Le principal point de vigilance est le conflit armé' vs FAQ 'Philippines ne présente aucun facteur véritablement critique'. The two statements disagree on the same page.
findings.expected: Use one framing per page: either name the main risk and drop 'aucun facteur véritablement critique', or keep the 'no critical factor' verdict and avoid calling a single signal 'le principal risque' in SUMMARY.
findings.verification: opus: As stated, mostly wrong: for NPL (crime 6.0) and PHL (conflict 6.1), naming a 'point de vigilance' while saying nothing is critical is consistent. It is a real problem where the named pillar is below 5. PNG says 'ne présente aucun facteur véritablement critique' with santé at 4.9/10 and SUMMARY 'Le principal risque est l'accès limité aux soins : 7,9 sur 10'. PRK is the same case (see #2). The phrase appears on 146 fr pages, and the template needs a threshold.

findings.quote: l'avertissement le plus sévère — redoubler de vigilance — émane de États-Unis et Australie.
findings.problem: The 'avertissement le plus sévère' is labelled 'redoubler de vigilance', which is also the dominant advice quoted just before in the same answer. Examples PAN, PER ('émane de États-Unis et Royaume-Uni') and PRY ('émane de Canada et Australie'). A native reader will find 'le plus sévère' and 'redoubler de vigilance' contradictory when the same label is the most common one.
findings.expected: Name the strongest level that actually appears on the page (for PAN, 'vigilance renforcée' as the top level) and say 'les avertissements les plus stricts' only when a stronger level exists.
findings.verification: opus: The quote appears exactly in the PAN FAQ answer, and PER ('émane de États-Unis et Royaume-Uni') and PRY ('émane de Canada et Australie') say the same thing. On all three pages the strongest level is also the dominant one (PAN: 4 usual precautions and 18 heightened vigilance, per the SUMMARY). So 'l'avertissement le plus sévère' repeats the dominant advice and singles out 2 of the 18 or so issuers, as if they were stricter than the rest. The template also produces broken French ('émane de États-Unis et Australie' instead of 'émane des États-Unis et de l'Australie'; 'pour Panama'). The fix is to drop the 'most severe' clause when it equals the dominant level, or to say that most governments share it.

findings.quote: Risque principal : criminalité (6.6).
findings.problem: The 'Risque principal' in DESCRIPTION (and the FAQ 'le domaine qui demande le plus d'attention') names a different pillar from the FAQ answer 1 on the same page, which says the score is pulled down 'surtout par' another pillar, and from the PILLAR BARS minimum. SLV: DESCRIPTION 'criminalité (6.6)' vs FAQ 'surtout par gouvernance (3.3/10)' (Gouvernance 3.3 is the lowest bar). SSD: 'conflit (3.2)' vs 'surtout par gouvernance (1.6/10)'. RWA: 'criminalité (5.8)' vs 'surtout par gouvernance (5.0/10)'. SEN: 'criminalité (6.1)' vs 'surtout par santé (5.4/10)'. SAU: 'conflit (5.6)' vs 'surtout par gouvernance (4.9/10)'. SLB: 'santé (5.9)' vs 'surtout par gouvernance (5.2/10)'.
findings.expected: Use one rule for the main risk everywhere on a page: the lowest-scoring pillar (excluding low-coverage pillars, which are footnoted), and name the same pillar in DESCRIPTION, FAQ Q1, FAQ Q2 and the bars.
findings.verification: opus: Checked bars, DESCRIPTION and FAQ. SLV: DESCRIPTION says criminalité (6.6), FAQ Q1 says 'surtout par gouvernance (3.3/10)', lowest bar is Gouvernance 3.3. RWA, SSD, SAU and SLB show the same split. SEN: DESCRIPTION and Q2 say criminalité 6.1, but Q1 and the lowest bar say Santé 5.4. The page names different main risks in different places. Not in title/hero, so medium.

findings.quote: Nessun singolo fattore emerge come critico per Albania: l'area che richiede più attenzione è il pilastro rischi naturali, con 5.8/10.
findings.problem: 47 of 83 pages contradict themselves on the main risk. The SUMMARY names one (ALB: 'La principale criticità è l'esposizione ai rischi naturali'; AGO: 'Il rischio principale è lo scarso accesso alle cure mediche'; ARE: 'La principale criticità è l'esposizione ai rischi naturali'), while the FAQ Q2 says no single factor stands out ('Nessun singolo fattore emerge come critico per Albania' / 'per Angola' / 'per Emirati Arabi Uniti'). A reader gets opposite answers to the same question on one page.
findings.expected: One rule for the main risk, applied identically in SUMMARY, DESCRIPTION and FAQ (or no main risk named when no pillar is critical).
findings.verification: opus: ALB, AGO, ARE and COL pages carry the quoted FAQ Q2 'Nessun singolo fattore emerge come critico per …' while the SUMMARY on the same page names a 'principale criticità' / 'Il rischio principale'. COL (5.9, cautela elevata, crime 4.8) also gets 'no single factor is critical'. The wording contradicts itself, but both texts name the same pillar, so this is medium, not high.

findings.quote: Rischio principale: criminalità (6.0).
findings.problem: The DESCRIPTION 'Rischio principale' often names a pillar that is not the lowest non-governance pillar on the same page (17 pages, gaps of 0.1 to 1.6 points). CHN names criminalità (6.0) while rischi naturali (4.4) and governance (4.3) are lower, and its FAQ says 'più di tutto, governance (4.3/10)'. COL names conflitto (5.1) while criminalità is 4.8, and its FAQ says 'più di tutto, criminalità (4.8/10)'. AZE names salute (6.6) while rischi naturali is 5.6. Governance is skipped on most pages even when it is the lowest (AFG 1.8, ALB 5.3) but named on BGR, BIH, CYP and CZE. The rule is inconsistent.
findings.expected: One explicit rule (lowest pillar; governance in or out; asterisked pillars in or out), used the same way in DESCRIPTION, SUMMARY, FAQ and PILLAR BARS.
findings.verification: opus: Verified on the pages. CHN DESCRIPTION says 'Rischio principale: criminalità (6.0)' while the bars show Rischi naturali 4.4 and Governance 4.3, and FAQ Q1 says 'più di tutto, governance (4.3/10)'. COL DESCRIPTION says conflitto (5.1) while FAQ Q1 says 'più di tutto, criminalità (4.8/10)'. DESCRIPTION, FAQ Q1 and FAQ Q2 each follow a different rule for the main risk. The text is a meta description, not the summary, so medium.

findings.quote: Rischio principale: salute (5.6).
findings.problem: On pages with asterisked low-coverage pillars the text drops those pillars from the risk ranking, while PILLAR BARS still shows them lower. COM: DESCRIPTION 'Rischio principale: salute (5.6)' while 'Criminalità 4.8/10 *' is lower. FSM: FAQ 'più di tutto, salute (6.8/10)' while 'Governance 5.2/10 *' and 'Criminalità 5.7/10 *' are lower. CPV: 'Rischio principale: salute (6.4)' while 'Criminalità 4.9/10 *' is lower. BLZ: FAQ 'più di tutto, criminalità (5.2/10)' while 'Governance 4.7/10 *' is lower. ATG: FAQ 'più di tutto, criminalità (6.3/10)' while 'Governance 5.7/10 *' is lower. The footnote says the flagged pillar's contribution is 'ridotto o escluso', so the text treats it as absent while the chart shows it.
findings.expected: Either rank flagged pillars with a visible note or stop showing them as weakest; the risk sentence must match what the chart shows.
findings.verification: opus: Verified. COM DESCRIPTION 'Rischio principale: salute (5.6)' with Criminalità 4.8 * lower. CPV 'salute (6.4)' with Criminalità 4.9 * lower. FSM FAQ 'più di tutto, salute (6.8/10)' with Governance 5.2 * and Criminalità 5.7 * lower. BLZ FAQ names criminalità 5.2 while Governance 4.7 * is lower. The text silently drops the asterisked pillars that the chart shows as weakest.

findings.quote: Punteggio gratuito da 30+ fonti pubbliche
findings.problem: The DESCRIPTION promises '30+ fonti pubbliche' but the same page's SUMMARY counts fewer: FSM '13 avvisi di viaggio governativi e altri 3 dataset' = 16; DMA 18 + 3 = 21; ALB 20 + 5 = 25; CIV and COG 15 + 6 = 21. 43 of 83 pages carry the '30+' claim with a body sum below 30.
findings.expected: The DESCRIPTION source count equals the sum of the body counts, or the body lists every source.
findings.verification: opus: I parsed all 83 it pages in the batch. 44 have '30+ fonti pubbliche' in DESCRIPTION, and 43 of those have a SUMMARY ([B3]) count below 30 (FSM 13+3=16, DMA 18+3=21, CIV/COG 21, AFG 22+7=29). The only one at or above 30 is BGD with 32. The page contradicts itself on how many sources it uses.

findings.quote: Rischio principale: salute (4.2).
findings.problem: The 'Rischio principale' label in the DESCRIPTION (and the 'principale criticità' sentence in the SUMMARY) names a pillar that is not the lowest one on the same page. On about 37 of the 83 pages governance is the lowest pillar, yet another pillar is named: GIN (PILLAR BARS governance 2.7, label 'salute (4.2)'), NIC (governance 1.7, label 'criminalità (6.3)'), KAZ (governance 3.9, label 'rischi naturali (6.4)'). The same pages' FAQ A1 then says governance weighs 'più di tutto'. This is partly by design: selectDriverPillar in src/lib/country-summary.ts takes the driver only from DIRECT_RISK_PILLARS (conflict, crime, health, environment), so governance can never be the named risk while a direct pillar is below 7.0 (the code comment cites Ecuador). The result is that one page names two different biggest risks.
findings.expected: One rule per page. Either name the lowest pillar (governance) in DESCRIPTION, SUMMARY and FAQ, or drop the 'più di tutto' governance clause from the FAQ. Snippet, summary and FAQ must agree.
findings.verification: opus: GIN shows 'Rischio principale: salute (4.2).' in DESCRIPTION and names health as the main risk in SUMMARY. Its FAQ A1 on the same page says '...e, più di tutto, governance (2.7/10)'. NIC and KAZ follow the same pattern. Leaving governance out of the named risk is deliberate, so the fix belongs in the FAQ A1 wording. Because the deliberate rule softens it, severity is lowered to medium.

findings.quote: Nessun singolo fattore emerge come critico per Guinea: l'area che richiede più attenzione è il pilastro salute, con 4.2/10.
findings.problem: On about 50 pages the FAQ 'Qual è il rischio maggiore' answer opens with 'Nessun singolo fattore emerge come critico' (about 8 more use 'Nessun pilastro segnala un rischio significativo'), while the SUMMARY or DESCRIPTION of the same page names a main risk. Examples: GIN (SUMMARY 'Il rischio principale è lo scarso accesso alle cure mediche'), GRC (SUMMARY 'La principale criticità è l'esposizione ai rischi naturali' vs FAQ 'Nessun singolo fattore emerge come critico per Grecia'), ISL (DESCRIPTION 'Rischio principale: rischi naturali (7.7).' vs FAQ 'Nessun pilastro segnala un rischio significativo per Islanda'). SUMMARY and DESCRIPTION name the driver whenever a direct pillar is below 7; FAQ A2 uses its own cut-offs (<4 critical, 4-7 'Nessun singolo fattore', >=7 'strong'), so the same pillar is framed in opposite ways.
findings.expected: One framing per page. If the SUMMARY names a main risk, the FAQ should name that same pillar and not say no factor stands out. If no factor is critical, do not use 'Rischio principale' or 'principale criticità'.
findings.verification: opus: GRC SUMMARY says 'La principale criticità è l'esposizione ai rischi naturali' while its FAQ says 'Nessun singolo fattore emerge come critico per Grecia'. ISL DESCRIPTION says 'Rischio principale: rischi naturali (7.7).' while its FAQ says 'Nessun pilastro segnala un rischio significativo'. GIN, rated 'Solo per viaggiatori esperti' with governance 2.7, also says no factor is critical. The page and the FAQ answer use different cut-offs, so they frame the same pillar in opposite ways. These are FAQ answers, so severity is medium.

findings.quote: A ottobre 2026, Isola di Man conta un avviso di viaggio governativo. Il quadro complessivo è rassicurante
findings.problem: Two problems in the same template. (a) With one advisory (IMN, IOT, JEY) the answer still says 'la maggior parte dei governi raccomanda ... e nessuno lo colloca', which contradicts a count of one; the 'normal' consensus line (a3Consensus.normal in src/lib/country-faq-copy.ts) hard-codes plural 'dei governi'. (b) On 15 of the 18 partial-data pages, where the page itself says there is no official score ('Nessun punteggio di sicurezza ufficiale'), the FAQ still gives a reassuring verdict ('Il quadro complessivo è rassicurante'). That reads as a safety judgement the methodology says the site does not make.
findings.expected: For n = 1 use singular wording ('l'unico governo che pubblica un avviso raccomanda solo precauzioni normali'). On partial-data pages drop the verdict and say only which advisories exist.
findings.verification: opus: IMN counts 'un avviso di viaggio governativo' and then says 'la maggior parte dei governi raccomanda ... e nessuno lo colloca', which contradicts a count of one. The pronoun 'lo' also fails to agree with feminine names (Isola di Man, Guadalupa). Part (b) is weaker: the 'rassicurante' line describes the advisories, not a score. Part (a) alone is enough to confirm.

findings.quote: l'avviso più severo — usare maggiore prudenza — arriva da Stati Uniti e Canada.
findings.problem: Three variants of the same advisory template. (1) The 'caution' and 'reconsider' lines name two issuers as the source of 'l'avviso più severo' even when the level named is the common one: IDN has 19 of 21 governments on 'maggiore prudenza', yet only the US and Canada are named as the strictest. (2) ISR says 'gli avvisi più severi — non viaggiare — sono stati emessi da Spagna e Polonia' while its SUMMARY counts 6 governments that 'sconsigliano qualsiasi viaggio'; KWT names 2 of 3 with no 'tra gli altri'. (3) The 'avoid' line uses a singular verb for two issuers: 'un avviso di livello massimo — non viaggiare — è stato emesso da Stati Uniti e Canada, tra gli altri' (IRQ), where it should be 'sono stati emessi'.
findings.expected: Give the count instead of two names ('19 governi raccomandano maggiore prudenza'). List every do-not-travel issuer, or add 'tra gli altri' consistently. Use the plural verb ('sono stati emessi').
findings.verification: opus: IDN has 19 of 21 governments at 'maggiore prudenza', yet the page says 'l'avviso più severo — usare maggiore prudenza — arriva da Stati Uniti e Canada', singling out 2 issuers of the majority level. ISR names only Spagna e Polonia although its SUMMARY counts 6 do-not-travel advisories, and it does not add 'tra gli altri'. The singular 'un avviso ... è stato emesso da X e Y' is a minor issue.

findings.quote: Generalmente sicuro 8 7.6 su 10
findings.problem: The HERO's large number is a whole-number rounding of the score (src/components/country/ScoreHero.astro, country.scoreDisplay), so 7.6 shows as '8' under 'Generalmente sicuro' (MDA; MKD also 7.6 shows 8). LBY shows '5' beside '4.8 su 10' under 'Non raccomandato'; HTI shows '4' beside '3.7 su 10'; MNG shows '7' beside '7.5 su 10'. The TITLE says 7.6/10, so the same page shows two different numbers.
findings.expected: Show the one-decimal score as the big number, or drop the integer. At least use one rounding rule for the big number and the caption.
findings.verification: opus: ScoreHero.astro shows country.scoreDisplay, an integer, next to score.toFixed(1). The pages show 'Generalmente sicuro 8 7.6 su 10' (MDA, score 7.596), '5 4.8 su 10' (LBY) and '7 7.5 su 10' (MNG, score 7.454). Two different numbers sit in the hero and the title says 7.6/10. MNG's 7 next to 7.5 looks inconsistent even though the rounding is correct.

findings.quote: Punteggio gratuito da 30+ fonti pubbliche
findings.problem: 52 pages' DESCRIPTION promise '30+ fonti pubbliche', but on 49 of them the SUMMARY's own count ('Il punteggio combina N avvisi di viaggio governativi e altri M dataset pubblici') totals fewer than 30. Examples: TWN ('Il punteggio combina 17 avvisi di viaggio governativi e altri 3 dataset pubblici', 20 in total), NRU (17 + 3 = 20), TLS (16 + 5 = 21). Only NPL (31), PER (30) and UGA (30) reach 30.
findings.expected: Use the per-country source count in DESCRIPTION, or state the global figure as a methodology claim that is not tied to the sources listed on the page.
findings.verification: opus: 'Punteggio gratuito da 30+ fonti pubbliche' appears in 52 DESCRIPTIONs, while the same pages count, for example, NRU 17+3=20, TWN 17+3=20 and SLB 20+4=24. Some DESCRIPTIONs (NZL, SWE, TTO, VCT) leave the phrase out entirely. The claim is false for the page it describes.

findings.quote: Pontuação gratuita de 30+ fontes públicas, recalculada diariamente.
findings.problem: On all 59 pages with this tail, the same page's SUMMARY gives fewer than 30 sources in total ('A pontuação combina 17 avisos de viagem governamentais e outros 3 conjuntos de dados públicos' = 20 on ATG; 22 + 7 = 29 on AFG; 13 + 3 = 16 on FSM). Unless '30+' is meant as a site-wide figure, the number contradicts the page's own count.
findings.expected: Use the page's own count in DESCRIPTION, or say 'dados de 30+ fontes no site' so it is clearly not a per-country figure.
findings.verification: opus: Every scored DESCRIPTION says 'Pontuação gratuita de 30+ fontes públicas', but the page's own B3 count is lower: AFG 22+7=29, BLR 19+5=24, BRN 18+3=21. In a per-country meta description this reads as a per-country claim.

findings.quote: e viajar exige muita cautela
findings.problem: Q1 answers 'Não' and then adds 'viajar exige muita cautela', which implies travel is possible with care. The same page's Q3 says 'a maioria dos governos já desaconselha qualquer viagem' (MLI 20 of 21; IRN 23 of 24; HTI 20 of 23; NER 18 of 21; LBY 17 of 21; LBN 17 of 23; IRQ 16 of 22; MMR 12 of 22). NGA has 12 reconsider and 2 do-not-travel of 21 with the same 'Não' plus caution tail.
findings.expected: Drop 'e viajar exige muita cautela' after 'Não', or make the wording match the advisory count, e.g. 'a maioria dos governos desaconselha qualquer viagem'.
findings.verification: opus: MLI.pt Q1 says 'Não — ... e viajar exige muita cautela', but its SUMMARY says 20 of 21 governments advise against all travel and Q3 says 'A maioria dos governos já desaconselha qualquer viagem'. The template's caution tail suggests the trip can go ahead with care when most governments say do not travel. On NGA the tail fits.

findings.quote: Pontuação gratuita de 30+ fontes públicas, recalculada diariamente.
findings.problem: The meta description says '30+ fontes públicas' on 62 covered pages, but the SUMMARY on 59 of those lists fewer than 30 sources (e.g. NRU: '17 avisos de viagem governamentais e outros 3 conjuntos' = 20; TUV 18 + 4 = 22). NZL and VCT omit the sentence. 'Pontuação gratuita de' is also a literal calque of 'free score'.
findings.expected: Build the sentence from the same counts as the SUMMARY (e.g. 'Pontuação baseada em 20 fontes públicas') or drop the number; use the same sentence on every covered page.
findings.verification: opus: The TJK, USA and SRB DESCRIPTIONs say 'Pontuação gratuita de 30+ fontes públicas' while the SUMMARY counts 27, 22 and 28 sources (NRU: 17+3=20). NZL and VCT omit the sentence. The per-page claim overstates the inputs.

findings.quote: 多数政府对奥兰群岛仅建议采取正常预防措施，没有任何一国将其提升至低级别以上的警告。
findings.problem: Grey pages ALA, ATF, BVT and GGY each have exactly one advisory ('我们已收录…的1条政府旅行警告'), yet the reassurance says 多数政府 (most governments). With one government 'most' is meaningless and implies a broader consensus. Cause: the zh a3Consensus.normal string hard-codes 多数政府 for the normal band, and buildAdvisoryAnswer runs for grey pages without an n greater than 1 check.
findings.expected: With one advisory, say 'the one government that publishes an advisory for X advises normal precautions', or omit the consensus sentence.
findings.verification: opus: ALA and GGY each list exactly one advisory (Poland, level 1), yet the FAQ says '多数政府对…仅建议采取正常预防措施'. The a3Consensus.normal template has no n>1 guard. The English template has the same wording.

findings.quote: 被评为高风险，前往旅行需要格外谨慎。
findings.problem: On 9 pages the first FAQ answer says 前往旅行需要格外谨慎 (travel needs extra caution). On 8 of them most governments advise avoiding all travel: IRN 23 of 24, MLI 20 of 21, HTI 20 of 23, NER 18 of 21, LBY 17 of 21, LBN 17 of 23, IRQ 16 of 22, MMR 12 of 22 (plus 7 reconsider). The same pages' HERO says 不推荐前往 (not recommended), so the FAQ understates the advice the page's own counts give. Examples: HTI, MLI, IRN.
findings.expected: When most governments advise avoiding travel, say so in words (e.g. 多数政府建议避免前往) and align FAQ 1 with the HERO verdict.
findings.verification: opus: HTI, MLI and IRN FAQ1 end with 前往旅行需要格外谨慎, while 20/23, 20/21 and 23/24 governments advise avoiding all travel and the HERO says 不推荐前往. The answer opens with 不安全, which softens the problem, but 'extra caution' still understates the advice.

findings.quote: 最需关注：犯罪（6.3分）。
findings.problem: On 41 of 65 scored pages the pillar named as the main concern is not the lowest bar. Four are explained by the low-coverage footnote (GRD, KIR, MDV, MHL), but the sentence does not say so. On 35 more the lowest bar is 治理 (governance), which is not footnoted and is named as the concern only on HUN, LTU, MDV, MKD, MLT and MNE. Worst case NIC: 最需关注：犯罪（6.3分） while PILLAR BARS shows 治理 1.7/10. Also GIN (governance 2.7, health 4.2 named) and MAR (governance 4.5, health 6.6 named).
findings.expected: Pick the main concern from the bars shown on the page, or state in the same sentence which pillars are excluded. Governance must not be skipped silently when it is the lowest score.
findings.verification: opus: NIC DESCRIPTION says 最需关注：犯罪（6.3分）, but the bars show 治理 1.7 and 自然灾害 5.0, both lower. GIN names health 4.2 while governance is 2.7. The main-concern pick does not follow the bars and does not say why.

findings.quote: 总体情况令人安心：多数政府对格林纳达仅建议采取正常预防措施，没有任何一国将其提升至低级别以上的警告。
findings.problem: 41 pages say the overall picture is reassuring and that no country moved above the low level. On 22 scored pages the same page's SUMMARY shows 1 to 9 governments advising 提高警惕 (GRD 6 of 19, KAZ 9 of 20, NAM 6 of 20, NLD 6 of 20). If 低级别 means the normal-precautions tier the claim is false there, and the phrase itself is unclear. On the 15 grey pages (no score) the line still reassures; IMN, IOT and JEY list one advisory yet say 多数政府. HRV, HUN, LIE and MLT say 均 (all) in SUMMARY but 多数政府 in the FAQ.
findings.expected: Remove 总体情况令人安心 and 低级别以上; state the counts from the page; on grey pages do not summarise safety; use 所有 when all advise normal precautions and the exact count otherwise.
findings.verification: opus: The sentence 没有任何一国将其提升至低级别以上的警告 is false on GRD (6 of 19 raise caution), JPN (4 of 22) and MHL (Spain at level 2). It also appears on grey IMN, which has 1 advisory but still says 多数政府 and 总体情况令人安心.

findings.quote: 而拉低总分的主要是自然灾害（7.1/10），尤其是犯罪（4.3/10）。
findings.problem: The drag sentence names pillars that sit above the total: KNA natural 7.1 (total 6.8), LIE natural 8.3 (total 8.2), MKD health 7.7 (total 7.6), LBY crime 5.1 (total 4.8), NER governance 4.3 (total 4.1). Elsewhere the main drag is a high pillar: JPN 拉低总分的主要是治理（8.0/10），尤其是自然灾害（4.4/10）, and KOR and NLD name governance (7.7, 8.2) as the main drag. 尤其是 (especially) implies the second pillar is a subset of the first, but these are separate pillars.
findings.expected: List only pillars below the total, ordered by value (拉低总分的主要是A（a），其次是B（b）); drop 尤其是 for independent pillars.
findings.verification: opus: The drag sentence names pillars that sit above the total or are not weak. KNA 自然灾害 7.1 vs total 6.8; NER 治理 4.3 vs 4.1; LIE 自然灾害 8.3 vs 8.2; JPN calls 治理（8.0/10） the main drag. 主要是A，尤其是B also puts the worse pillar second.

findings.quote: 评分基于30+个公开来源，每日重新计算，免费查询。
findings.problem: All 65 scored pages say the score is based on 30+ public sources, but each page's SUMMARY lists its own advisories plus datasets. The sums are 18 to 29 on 64 pages (GIN 20 + 5 = 25; GRD 19 + 3 = 22; KIR 17 + 4 = 21). Only IND (24 + 7 = 31) reaches 30. Two numbers on one page disagree.
findings.expected: Derive the source count from the numbers the page shows, or drop the 30+ claim.
findings.verification: opus: Every DESCRIPTION says 评分基于30+个公开来源, while the SUMMARY on the same page counts fewer: GIN 20 advisories + 5 datasets = 25, GRD 19 + 3 = 22, MHL 17 + 5 = 22.

findings.quote: 最需关注的是暴力与不安全：全球和平指数对该国的评分为1.81（1–5分，1分最和平；GPI 2026）。
findings.problem: The main-risk sentence quotes a GPI value that its own scale places near the most peaceful end (1 = most peaceful). The same pattern appears on JOR (1.91), KGZ (2.05, 社会治安欠佳), LKA (2.13), LSO (2.33), LBY (2.36), NAM (2.37) and KEN (2.45). Calling these the top concern reads as a risk while the number says the opposite.
findings.expected: Name an indicator as a main risk only when it sits in the risk half of its scale; otherwise name the lowest pillar or say the risk is relatively low.
findings.verification: opus: KWT and JOR SUMMARY name 暴力与不安全 as the top concern, quoting GPI 1.81 and 1.91 on a scale described as 1–5 with 1 most peaceful. The values the page quotes read as benign, so naming them as the main risk contradicts itself.

findings.quote: 最需关注：冲突（5.4分）。
findings.problem: On 34 of 64 scored pages the DESCRIPTION's most-to-watch pillar is not the lowest visible non-starred bar. VEN: the bars show 治理 1.5/10 and 冲突 5.4/10, yet the description names 冲突. Others: TJK 最需关注：犯罪（6.8分） with 治理 2.3/10; ZWE 最需关注：健康（5.6分） with 治理 3.0/10; TKM 最需关注：犯罪（6.5分） with 治理 2.3/10. The FAQ on these pages calls governance the 尤其是 drag, so each page disagrees with itself.
findings.expected: Make the most-to-watch pillar the lowest-scoring one, or document the indicator-level rule and use it consistently in the description, SUMMARY and FAQ.
findings.verification: opus: VEN's DESCRIPTION names 冲突（5.4分） although 治理 is at 1.5. TJK, ZWE and TKM do the same, and the FAQ on each names governance as the 尤其是 drag. The choice looks weighted by pillar weight (deficit × weight) rather than by lowest score, and the page never explains this.

findings.quote: 前往旅行需要格外谨慎
findings.problem: 11 pages open with 不安全 or 不安全——…属于高风险目的地 and close with 前往旅行需要格外谨慎 (PRK, PSE, RUS, SDN, SOM, SSD, SYR, TCD, UKR, VEN, YEM). The same pages' HERO says 不推荐前往, and their SUMMARY says most or all advisories say 避免一切旅行 (YEM: the 21 governments all advise avoiding all travel; RUS: 13 governments). The verdict tells a traveller both do not go and go with extra caution.
findings.expected: For a high-risk band with 不推荐前往 and avoid-all advisories, say 不建议前往 and drop the clause about extra caution while travelling.
findings.verification: opus: YEM, RUS and SYR say 不安全… but then 前往旅行需要格外谨慎. Their HERO says 不推荐前往, and the advisories are all or mostly 避免一切旅行 (YEM 21/21). The closing clause implies travel and understates the do-not-go message.

findings.quote: ReliefWeb（仅在灾害发生期间提供，因此不计入这四个来源）
findings.problem: '这四个来源' has no antecedent on the page. The HERO lists 4 government advisories, ReliefWeb and the World Bank, so a reader counts more than four sources while the same HERO says fewer than four. COK has the same wording.
findings.expected: Name the sources that count toward the four, or say 'not counted toward the four-source minimum'.
findings.verification: opus: The ASM HERO has 'ReliefWeb（仅在灾害发生期间提供，因此不计入这四个来源）'. The English is 'not counted toward the four' (the threshold), but 这四个来源 reads as 'these four sources', as if four sources existed. It sits right after '4个国家政府的旅行警告' and contradicts '来源不足四个'. Same text on COK, MNP, NCL, REU, TCA and GUM, so it is a template mistranslation.

findings.quote: O pilar mais forte de Brasil é saúde (6.5/10)
findings.problem: The overall score (TITLE 6.6/10) is above the strongest pillar (6.5/10). EST shows the same pattern (8.7/10 overall, strongest pillar 8.6/10). The composite is transformed (score = 1 + 9·c^0.96), so this can happen mathematically, but nothing on the page explains why a score sits above every bar it is built from.
findings.expected: Explain the transform on the page, or present the score on the same scale as the pillars.
findings.verification: opus: BRA.pt shows TITLE 6.6/10 and PILLAR BARS 5.7/6.1/6.2/6.3/6.5, so the score sits above every pillar. EST shows the same pattern (8.7 overall, pillars 8.3-8.6). latest.json has BRA pillar scores 0.57-0.65 displayed as 10*p, while the composite goes through 1+9*c^0.96, so the bars and the headline score use different scales.

findings.quote: Lo que sí tenemos Todavía ninguna fuente independiente cubre este destino.
findings.problem: The 'Lo que sí tenemos' (what we do have) item says no independent source covers the destination, and TITLE/DESCRIPTION/HERO still label the page 'Datos parciales' (partial data) although there is no data. Same on CXR (Isla de Navidad). FAQ Q3 adds the unsupported generalisation 'algo habitual en territorios muy pequeños o remotos'.
findings.expected: For zero-source pages drop the 'Lo que sí tenemos' heading and the 'Datos parciales' label (say that no data exists yet), and remove or source the generalisation.
findings.verification: opus: In the CCK and CXR HERO, the 'Lo que sí tenemos' heading is followed by 'Todavía ninguna fuente independiente cubre este destino', and the pages are labelled 'Datos parciales' with no data at all. Q1 also says to read the advisories below when none exist. The remote-territory remark is plausible, so it is not part of the defect. Grey 'partial data' pages are accepted by design, so this zero-data case is medium.

findings.quote: Os alertas de viagem de 14 governos ReliefWeb (apenas enquanto há um desastre em curso, por isso não conta entre as quatro)
findings.problem: The grey HERO lists 14 government advisories as what the site has, then says it has fewer than four independent sources. Without a stated counting rule (are advisories one source?), a reader counts more than four. The parenthetical 'por isso não conta entre as quatro' is also unclear.
findings.expected: State the counting rule, for example 'Alertas de 14 governos (contam como 1 fonte); ReliefWeb fora da contagem'.
findings.verification: opus: COK.pt HERO says a score needs four independent sources and that there are fewer than four. It then lists 'Os alertas de viagem de 14 governos' plus ReliefWeb, and only ReliefWeb is marked as not counting. Advisories don't count as a source in v10, but nothing says so, so a reader sees 14 items and gets confused.

findings.quote: anche il più debole, governance (8.0/10), rientra nella fascia di rischio basso
findings.problem: Overall, 8.0 and above is labelled 'rischio molto basso' (CZE 8.7, EST 8.7), yet pillar wording places CZE governance (8.0) and EST rischi naturali (8.3: 'rientra nella fascia di rischio basso', 'ben dentro la fascia di rischio basso') in the 'basso' band. 'a pesare sul punteggio sono' is also used for strong pillars: CAN 'governance (8.1/10)', AUS and DEU 'criminalità (8.2/10)', ESP 'governance (7.7/10)', FRA 'conflitto (7.5/10)'. That wording says they drag the score down.
findings.expected: Pillar band names use the same thresholds as the overall label; 'a pesare' only for pillars below the top band.
findings.verification: opus: The CZE FAQ really says governance 8.0 'rientra nella fascia di rischio basso' and later 'ben dentro la fascia di rischio basso', and EST says the same for 8.3. The same pages call the overall 8.7 'rischio molto basso', so pillar bands and overall bands disagree. The 'a pesare sul punteggio sono criminalità (8.2/10)' wording (DEU) and 'governance (8.1/10)' (CAN) are also confirmed: pillars in the top band are described as pulling the score down.

findings.quote: the lowest-rated is exposure to natural hazards: 1.6 out of 10 on the INFORM scale, where 10 is the highest exposure
findings.problem: The sentence calls natural hazards 'the lowest-rated' area and then gives '1.6 out of 10', which is on the INFORM scale where 10 is the worst. The bars read higher as safer. A reader can take 1.6 as a low rating, when it is the safest value on the page. Two scales are mixed in one clause.
findings.expected: Split it: 'Lowest-rated area: natural hazards (8.3/10). Exposure to natural hazards is low: 1.6 on the INFORM scale, where 10 is the highest exposure.'
