findings.verification: opus: The EST SUMMARY says 'All five areas score at least 7 out of 10; the lowest-rated is exposure to natural hazards: 1.6 out of 10', so two opposite 10-point scales sit in one sentence and the low hazard value reads as a bad rating. The same 'allGood' template appears on FIN (2.5) and GBR (3.5).

findings.quote: It combines 13 government travel advisories and 3 other public datasets
findings.problem: FSM is published as 'Generally safe' (7.2) with 55% data coverage. The page shows three feeds: advisories, INFORM and UCDP. The SUMMARY counts three other datasets, so four in all, which is the official-score floor (MIN_COVERAGE_SOURCES = 4 in /Users/riccardo/Developer/VibeCoding/Isitsafetotravel/.claude/worktrees/v10-integration/src/pipeline/scoring/coverage.ts; decideScoreStatus in /Users/riccardo/Developer/VibeCoding/Isitsafetotravel/.claude/worktrees/v10-integration/src/pipeline/scoring/status.ts). The third dataset is not on the page; by the code path it is most likely the World Bank feed, which has no FSM row. The danger guard does not apply (no level-4 advisory, UCDP deaths 0). The grey pages on this site say 'We publish a safety score only when at least four independent sources cover a place', so without the invisible feed FSM would fall under that rule and show as Partial data.
findings.expected: Show the feed that lifts FSM to four sources, or count only feeds with visible values. If FSM fails that rule, show it as Partial data like the other grey pages.
findings.verification: opus: In latest.json, FSM's sources are exactly advisories, inform, ucdp and worldbank, and it is 'scored'. Its crime pillar has dataCompleteness 0 and no World Bank indicator, so World Bank (population only) is the feed that lifts it to the four-source floor, and that feed adds nothing visible. FSM gets a score while showing only 3 real feeds.

findings.quote: 投票还不够（1/30 票，来自 0/3 个国家或地区）
findings.problem: One vote 'from 0 of 3 countries or regions' is contradictory: a vote exists but no country is recorded. The same count appears in JEY's HERO and COMMUNITY and in NLD's COMMUNITY.
findings.expected: Record the vote's country (or an 'unknown' bucket) so the country count matches the vote count.
findings.verification: opus: The JEY HERO/COMMUNITY and NLD COMMUNITY blocks both show 投票还不够（1/30 票，来自 0/3 个国家或地区）. A recorded vote with zero source countries is self-contradictory: a vote with a null country_iso is counted in the vote total but not in the country total.

findings.quote: une administration publique peu impartiale
findings.problem: The SUMMARY calls the weakest signal 'une administration publique peu impartiale' (little impartial public administration) and gives V-Dem's impartiality value as 0,98 on a scale of about -4 to +4, 'plus haut étant mieux'. On a scale centred on 0 with higher meaning better, 0,98 is above the midpoint, so the number does not support 'peu impartiale', and the midpoint is never stated. The signal is also written as a noun phrase rather than a signal name.
findings.expected: Give the value with its midpoint and drop 'peu impartiale' if it is above average, or name the signal that is actually weakest.
findings.verification: opus: The LTU.fr SUMMARY says 'le moins bien noté est une administration publique peu impartiale' with V-Dem at 0,98 on a −4..+4 scale where higher is better. latest.json shows vdem_gov_effectiveness raw 0.982 (normalized 0.64), which is above the midpoint. Calling it 'peu impartiale' misdescribes a merely relative weakness, and the sentence names a signal where the 'domaine' was announced.

findings.quote: Le point le plus faible est la faiblesse de la gouvernance
findings.problem: The MDV bars list 'Criminalité 5.1/10 *' (lower than 'Gouvernance 6.3/10') with an asterisk footnote saying a low-coverage pillar's contribution is 'réduite ou exclue'. The SUMMARY still calls governance the weakest point. The footnote is vague and is repeated inside the bar line on GRD, KIR, KNA, LCA, LIE, MDV and MHL. The phrase 'la faiblesse de la gouvernance' is a tautology, also used in HUN and MNE ('Le point le plus faible est la faiblesse de la gouvernance') and MLT ('le moins bien noté est la faiblesse de la gouvernance').
findings.expected: Say in plain words which pillar is excluded and why, and name the reported weakest pillar, for example 'La criminalité (5.1/10) n'est pas retenue faute de données suffisantes ; le point faible retenu est la gouvernance (6.3/10).' Remove the tautology.
findings.verification: opus: MDV.fr SUMMARY really says 'Le point le plus faible est la faiblesse de la gouvernance', while the first bar is 'Criminalité 5.1/10 *'. In latest.json, MDV's crime pillar has zero indicators (dataCompleteness 0), so 5.1 is a prior shown as if it were a measurement, and it is the lowest bar. The tautology 'le point le plus faible est la faiblesse de la gouvernance' also appears on CYP, CZE, HUN, MLT, MNE, POL, PRT and ROU.

findings.quote: 最薄弱的方面是治理薄弱：INFORM评分为5.8/10，10分最差（INFORM Risk 2026）。
findings.problem: The SUMMARY names governance as the weakest aspect, but PILLAR BARS on the same page shows 犯罪 5.1/10 (footnoted for low coverage) below 治理 6.3/10. FAQ 2 repeats the governance choice (最需要关注的领域是治理，得分为6.3/10) next to 没有任何单一因素构成突出风险.
findings.expected: Use one set of pillars: name crime (5.1, low coverage) as the weakest with its caveat, or say governance is weakest among fully covered pillars.
findings.verification: opus: MDV SUMMARY says 最薄弱的方面是治理薄弱 (INFORM 5.8), but PILLAR BARS lists 犯罪 5.1/10 (low-coverage asterisk) first and lower than 治理 6.3/10. FAQ 1 and FAQ 2 also skip crime. The page never explains that low-coverage crime is excluded from the weakest-pillar text.

findings.quote: even its weakest area, health, scores 7.6/10, well inside the low-risk band, and its five pillars range from 7.6/10 to 8.9/10
findings.problem: False on the page's own bars: governance is 5.4/10 and crime 5.7/10, so the weakest area is governance, not health, and the range runs 5.4 to 8.9. Governance at 5.4 falls in the 5 to 6 High caution band, so 'No pillar signals a significant risk' and the [B12] reassurance mislead a traveller. Q1 repeats the error: 'All five pillars score well for Nauru: even the weakest, health (7.6/10)'.
findings.expected: Name governance 5.4/10 as the weakest pillar with its band. Drop 'no pillar signals a significant risk' and 'all five pillars score well' while any pillar is below 7.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is verbatim in NRU FAQ Q2. 'Five pillars range from 7.6/10 to 8.9/10' is false against bars that show governance 5.4* and crime 5.7*. This is the same low-coverage exclusion as #1. Severity is lowered because both pillars rest on 25% coverage that is mostly the prior, so the main defect is the visible contradiction.

findings.quote: even the weakest, natural hazards (7.9/10), sits in the low-risk band
findings.problem: Bars show governance 5.4/10 and crime 5.7/10, both well below natural hazards 7.9/10. The FAQ then says 'No pillar signals a significant risk for Palau: even its weakest area, natural hazards, scores 7.9/10 ... range from 7.9/10 to 8.9/10'. Same template bug as NRU.
findings.expected: State governance 5.4/10 as the weakest pillar and its band. Remove the 'all five pillars score well' claim.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is verbatim in PLW FAQ Q1. The bars show governance 5.4* and crime 5.7*, both below natural hazards 7.9, and Q2 claims a range of 7.9 to 8.9. Same template bug as NRU.

findings.quote: Ja, sicher zu bereisen 9 8.5 von 10
findings.problem: The HERO prints an unlabelled integer before the score. For the same displayed 8.5, NZL and POL show '8' ('Ja, sicher zu bereisen 8 8.5 von 10') while PRT shows '9'. Other pages repeat the score the same way (e.g. 'Vorsicht geboten 7 6.8 von 10'). Readers see two numbers for one score, and the bare integer is never explained.
findings.expected: Drop the bare integer, or derive it from the displayed one-decimal score so that equal displayed scores give equal integers.
findings.verification: opus: PRT HERO 'Ja, sicher zu bereisen 9 8.5 von 10' and NZL/POL '... 8 8.5 von 10'. In latest.json, scoreDisplay is rounded from the raw score (PRT 8.537→9, NZL 8.496→8), while the label shows the rounded 8.5. Equal displayed scores therefore get different integers, and the hero shows two numbers for one score.

findings.quote: the score is pulled down by crime (6.3/10) and above all by conflict (3.0/10)
findings.problem: Governance 3.2/10, the second-lowest pillar, is left out. Crime 6.3/10 is above the 4.6 overall score, so it cannot be pulling the score down. The next answer repeats the error: 'Another area to watch is crime, at 6.3/10.'
findings.expected: Name governance 3.2/10 as the second drag and remove crime from the 'pulled down' list.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is verbatim in PSE FAQ Q1. Governance 3.2* is the second-lowest bar but is left out, while crime 6.3 is listed as pulling the score down. Q2 repeats 'Another area to watch is crime, at 6.3/10'. Same low-coverage exclusion.

findings.quote: Qatar est une destination considérée comme sûre
findings.problem: Reassurance contradicts the advisory tally. HERO says 'Généralement sûr' and FAQ Q1 says Qatar 'est une destination considérée comme sûre', but SUMMARY reports 11 of 23 governments 'déconseillent le voyage sauf raison impérative' and 1 'déconseille formellement tout voyage', and FAQ Q3 says the dominant advice is 'de reconsidérer tout voyage au Qatar'. A majority of issuers advising against non-essential travel is not compatible with 'généralement sûr' without qualification.
findings.expected: Qualify the reassurance (for example 'sûr pour la plupart des voyageurs, mais la majorité des gouvernements déconseillent le voyage non essentiel') or lower the verdict wording to match the advisory majority.
findings.verification: opus: QAT: HERO 'Généralement sûr' and FAQ 'Qatar est une destination considérée comme sûre', while SUMMARY gives 11 of 23 'déconseillent le voyage sauf raison impérative' plus 1 'déconseille formellement tout voyage' (12/23 at level 3 or above). FAQ Q3 says the dominant advice is to reconsider travel. Unqualified reassurance clashes with the page's own advisory majority. Q3 also says 'les avertissements les plus sévères ... ont été émis par Singapour' (plural, one issuer).

findings.quote: 卡塔尔被认为是一个安全的旅行目的地
findings.problem: QAT's FAQ calls the country a safe destination, then says mainstream advice is to reconsider travel. The SUMMARY has 11 governments at 重新考虑出行 and 1 at 避免一切旅行 out of 23, which is a majority. The same tension appears on SAU (对大多数旅行者而言相对安全, while 17 of 21 governments advise reconsidering or avoiding travel) and PAK (可以，但务必格外谨慎, while 16 of 24 advise reconsidering or avoiding).
findings.expected: Make the verdict wording match the advisory majority, or state that the score and the advisories are separate signals.
findings.verification: opus: QAT's FAQ says 卡塔尔被认为是一个安全的旅行目的地 (7.4, low risk) and then 主流建议是重新考虑前往. Its SUMMARY has 12 of 23 governments at reconsider or avoid. SAU says 相对安全 with 17 of 21 at reconsider or avoid. The verdict wording ignores the advisory majority.

findings.quote: the score is pulled down by governance (6.2/10) and above all by health (5.9/10)
findings.problem: PILLAR BARS shows crime 4.9/10 as the lowest pillar (asterisked for low coverage). The FAQ leaves it out, calls health 5.9 the 'above all' drag, and Q2 says health 'needs the most attention'. The low-coverage note is never explained in the FAQ.
findings.expected: Name crime 4.9/10 as the largest drag, flagged as low coverage, and explain how reduced-coverage pillars count.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is verbatim in STP FAQ Q1. Crime 4.9* is the lowest bar but is not mentioned. Health 5.9 is called the 'above all' drag and, in Q2, the area needing most attention. The low-coverage exclusion is never explained.

findings.quote: Non — Tchad est actuellement une destination à haut risque : en octobre 2026, le pays obtient 4.3/10 sur notre indice de sécurité, dans la catégorie « risque élevé », et tout voyage exige une grande prudence.
findings.problem: The FAQ wording 'tout voyage exige une grande prudence' understates the page's own SUMMARY, which says '8 déconseillent formellement tout voyage' and '10 déconseillent le voyage sauf raison impérative', and FAQ Q3 which says 'reconsidérer tout voyage au Tchad'. The same 'tout voyage exige une grande prudence' sentence is used on SYR, where 21 of 22 governments 'déconseillent formellement tout voyage'. For a 'Non' verdict this reads as a softer recommendation than the data.
findings.expected: Make the verdict sentence match the advisory mix, for example 'déconseillé pour la plupart des voyageurs' or 'la plupart des gouvernements déconseillent tout voyage'.
findings.verification: opus: The TCD quote is exact. On that page, 18 of 21 governments advise reconsidering or not travelling. SYR uses the same wording with 21 of 22 governments at 'déconseillent formellement tout voyage'. 'Tout voyage exige une grande prudence' is weaker than the advisory mix. The verdict 'Non' is still given, so this is medium rather than high.

findings.quote: 最需关注：冲突（6.3分）。
findings.problem: THA's description names conflict as the main concern (6.3), but the FAQ on the same page calls conflict the strongest pillar: 冲突（6.3/10）是泰国表现最强的支柱. The bars confirm conflict 6.3 is the highest value (治理 4.4 is the lowest). The SUMMARY also names armed conflict as the top concern. TUR has the same contradiction with a tie: DESCRIPTION 最需关注：冲突（6.7分）, while the FAQ says conflict is the strongest pillar, tied with 健康 6.7.
findings.expected: A pillar cannot be both the strongest and the main concern on one page. Choose the concern from the lowest-scoring pillar, or explain the indicator-level choice and drop the strongest-pillar sentence for that pillar.
findings.verification: opus: THA's DESCRIPTION and SUMMARY make conflict the top concern (6.3, 113 UCDP deaths), while the FAQ says 冲突（6.3/10）是泰国表现最强的支柱. TUR does the same: conflict 6.7 is tied for highest with 健康, yet it is the DESCRIPTION's 最需关注.

findings.quote: and above all by health (6.8/10)
findings.problem: PILLAR BARS shows governance 5.3/10 and crime 5.7/10, both asterisked for low coverage and both below health 6.8/10. The FAQ calls health the 'above all' drag, and Q2 says health 'needs the most attention', without mentioning the low-coverage pillars.
findings.expected: Mention governance 5.3 and crime 5.7 and say why they are excluded from the drag ranking.
findings.verification: opus: The phrase is verbatim in TON FAQ Q1. Governance 5.3* and crime 5.7* are both below health 6.8, but the FAQ names health as the main drag and the area needing most attention, without a word on the low-coverage pillars.

findings.quote: Tonga ne présente aucun facteur véritablement critique : le domaine qui demande le plus d'attention est le pilier santé, à 6.8/10.
findings.problem: Tonga's PILLAR BARS show 'Criminalité 5.7/10' and 'Gouvernance 5.3/10', both lower than santé 6.8, and the FAQ Q1 also says the score is pulled down 'surtout par santé (6.8/10)'. The two low pillars are marked as low coverage, but the page does not say the health pillar is the weakest one in the score.
findings.expected: Name criminalité or gouvernance as the lowest-scoring pillar, or explain on the page that these pillars are excluded from the score.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on TON. The bars show Gouvernance 5.3 and Criminalité 5.7, both low-coverage, yet the FAQ and DESCRIPTION name santé 6.8 as the weakest pillar. The page never says the two lower pillars are left out of these statements. This is the same mechanism as #3 (low-coverage pillars are shown but skipped in the text).

findings.quote: even the weakest, health (7.0/10), sits in the low-risk band
findings.problem: Bars show governance 4.7/10 (below 5, the High risk band) and crime 5.7/10. Q2 repeats 'no pillar signals a significant risk' with a range of 7.0 to 8.9. Both low pillars carry the low-coverage asterisk, which the FAQ never mentions.
findings.expected: Name governance 4.7/10 as the weakest pillar, explain the low coverage, and withdraw the 'no significant risk' sentence.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is verbatim in TUV FAQ Q1. The bars show governance 4.7* and crime 5.7*, and Q2 claims a range of 7.0 to 8.9 with 'no pillar signals a significant risk'. The FAQ never mentions the low coverage.

findings.quote: Lo que sí tenemos Todavía ninguna fuente independiente cubre este destino.
findings.problem: Under 'Lo que sí tenemos' (what we do have) the text says no independent source covers the place, while the TITLE and HERO still say 'Datos parciales', which implies some data exists.
findings.expected: Under a neutral heading, say 'Todavía no tenemos fuentes independientes para este destino', and use 'Sin datos suficientes' instead of 'Datos parciales'.
findings.verification: opus: UMI's HERO really does read 'Lo que sí tenemos Todavía ninguna fuente independiente cubre este destino.' and the page has no advisories at all, yet TITLE/HERO say 'Datos parciales'. The FAQ also says 'Lee los avisos gubernamentales más abajo' and asks what the advisories say, but none exist. The same zero-data template appears on CCK, CXR and NFK.

findings.quote: Im Gegensatz dazu kommt Kriminalität auf 5.0/10 — in diesem Bereich ist Afghanistan am stärksten.
findings.problem: On 'Nicht empfohlen' or 'hohes Risiko' pages the 'stärkste Säule' is still a weak score, and the text presents it as a strength. AFG: 5.0/10 for Kriminalität, overall 3.6. CAF: 'Naturgefahren auf 5.9/10 ... am stärksten' (overall 3.7). COD: 'Naturgefahren auf 5.4/10 ... am stärksten' (overall 3.8). The sentence also follows the governance boilerplate [B22] without connecting to it, so the flow is incoherent.
findings.expected: Describe the best pillar as the least weak one and state that it stays in the elevated-risk band. Do not call a 5.x pillar a strength.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on AFG.de, and the same pattern appears on CAF.de (Naturgefahren 5.9) and COD.de (Naturgefahren 5.4). The template calls a pillar of about 5/10 the country's strength ('am stärksten') on 'do not travel' pages. That is the generic 'strongest area' phrasing the blogger complained about, and for AFG it reads as if crime were not a concern. The German is also missing an article ('kommt Kriminalität auf' should read 'kommt der Bereich Kriminalität auf').

findings.quote: in diesem Bereich ist Haiti am stärksten.
findings.problem: A least-bad pillar is presented as a strength. HTI: „Die stärkste Säule von Haiti ist Naturgefahren (4.4/10)“ for a 3.7/10 country, plus „in diesem Bereich ist Haiti am stärksten“. Nine pages say 'stärkste Säule' for a pillar below 6.0: IRN Gesundheit 5.7 („in diesem Bereich ist Iran am stärksten“), LBN Gesundheit 5.7, MMR Kriminalität 5.6, MOZ Konflikt 5.5 (also its Hauptrisiko), NER Naturgefahren 5.5, NGA Kriminalität 5.5, IRQ Gesundheit 5.4, MLI Naturgefahren 4.9.
findings.expected: 'Die am wenigsten schwache Säule ist …', or no 'stärkste' sentence when the best pillar is below about 6/10. Never 'am stärksten' for a pillar that is itself a risk.
findings.verification: opus: HTI really says 'Die stärkste Säule von Haiti ist Naturgefahren (4.4/10)' and '…4/10 — in diesem Bereich ist Haiti am stärksten.' About 19 de pages call a pillar below 6/10 'stärkste Säule' (MLI 4.9, SOM 4.1, IRN 5.7, etc.). That presents a risk-level pillar as a strength, which is the exact pattern the blogger criticised.

findings.quote: No single factor stands out as critical for Angola: the area that needs the most attention is health, at 4.9/10.
findings.problem: On 47 of 63 scored pages the SUMMARY or DESCRIPTION names a main concern or risk, while the Q3 answer says no single factor stands out as critical. AGO: SUMMARY 'The main risk is poor access to health care' vs this FAQ line; BEN has the same pair. On AUT, CYP, CZE, DNK, FIN and GBR the FAQ says 'No pillar signals a significant risk' while DESCRIPTION still names a 'Top concern'.
findings.expected: One message per page: if a pillar is the main concern, Q3 should say so; if none stands out, SUMMARY and DESCRIPTION should not name a main concern.
findings.verification: opus: AGO Q2 opens with 'No single factor stands out as critical' even though governance (4.4) and health (4.9) are both below 5. COL (5.9, 'Only for experienced travelers', 612 conflict deaths) also gets this hedge. So it is a generic opener that softens real risks rather than a strict contradiction. 'Top concern' on CHE's 7.8 pillar is a much milder issue.

findings.quote: The main concern is poor public safety: the Global Peace Index rates safety and security at 2.37 on a scale from 1 (safest) to 5 (GPI 2026).
findings.problem: On the 1–5 scale (1 = safest, midpoint 3), values 2.37–2.64 sit in the safer half, yet 11 pages call them 'poor public safety' (BWA 2.37, GAB 2.62, CUB 2.64, BGD 2.58, and COG 2.92, ERI 3.19 with the same wording). Overall-GPI readings of 2.13–2.42 (BHR, BLR, BRA, BDI) are described as 'a climate of violence and insecurity'. Two alarm phrases applied to similar, relatively peaceful values.
findings.expected: Word a GPI reading by where it sits on the scale (e.g. 'relatively peaceful' or 'mid-range') and use consistent wording for similar values.
findings.verification: opus: Verified on BWA (2.37), KGZ (even 2.05), GAB, CUB, BGD: the SUMMARY always says 'The main concern is poor public safety' whatever the GPI value. BHR (2.13), BLR (2.22) and BRA (2.33) all say 'a climate of violence and insecurity'. Both phrases are fixed alarm labels attached to mid-scale or better-than-average readings, so a SUMMARY overstates the risk.

findings.quote: the strongest current warning — exercise increased caution — comes from United States and Canada.
findings.problem: On 7 pages (BHS, CHN, CRI, DOM, FRA, CIV, ATA) the 'strongest current warning' is the same level as the prevailing guidance, so the superlative adds nothing and reads as filler. The same sentence also misses 'the' before United States (see the article finding).
findings.expected: Drop the superlative when it repeats the prevailing level, e.g. 'Most governments advise increased caution.'
findings.verification: opus: FRA: '11 advise increased caution', yet the FAQ says 'the strongest current warning — exercise increased caution — comes from United States and Canada'. It names 2 of 11 governments as if they stood out, repeats the prevailing level, and drops 'the' before United States. The same template appears on BHS, CHN and ATA.

findings.quote: the lowest-rated is weak governance: 3.4 out of 10 on the INFORM scale
findings.problem: The template calls governance 'weak' whenever it is the lowest pillar, even at low risk values. CZE's Governance pillar is 8.0/10 and its INFORM value 3.4 is on a worst-is-10 scale, so calling it weak misreads the number. CYP has the same wording (Governance 7.2/10, INFORM 3.9).
findings.expected: Choose the adjective from the value band, not from the rank; a 3.4 on a worst-is-10 scale is low risk.
findings.verification: opus: CZE.en says 'the lowest-rated is weak governance: 3.4 out of 10 on the INFORM scale', but its Governance pillar is 8.0/10. CYP says the same with 3.9 (Governance 7.2/10). The adjective 'weak' is fixed regardless of the value, and on a scale where 10 is worst, 3.4 is a low risk.

findings.quote: El panorama general es tranquilizador: la mayoría de los gobiernos solo recomiendan precauciones normales para Isla Bouvet
findings.problem: On grey pages with a single advisory (BVT, ALA, ATF, GGY) the answer says 'la mayoría de los gobiernos' and 'El panorama general es tranquilizador'. One government cannot be a majority or a general picture, and these pages say their data is partial.
findings.expected: For one advisory, say that one government publishes it and give its level; drop the general reassurance and the majority wording.
findings.verification: opus: BVT, ALA, ATF and GGY each list exactly 1 advisory (e.g. Polonia Nivel 1), yet Q3 says 'El panorama general es tranquilizador: la mayoría de los gobiernos...'. 'Most governments' cannot be said of a single advisory.

findings.quote: En cambio, el pilar de riesgos naturales alcanza 4.4/10 y es el área más fuerte de Haití.
findings.problem: A 4.4/10 pillar on a page rated 'riesgo alto' (3.7/10 overall) is called 'el área más fuerte'. Same pattern: IRN ('el pilar de salud alcanza 5.7/10 y es el área más fuerte de Irán'), LBN (5.7), MLI (natural hazards 4.9), MMR (criminalidad 5.6), NER (natural hazards 5.5). The SUMMARY only calls a pillar a strength at 7.0/10 or above (country-summary.ts STRONG_PILLAR_MIN); the FAQ 'critical' copy has no such gate (country-faq-copy.ts:411).
findings.expected: Call a pillar a strength only at 7.0 or above, as the SUMMARY does; otherwise describe it as the least weak area of a high-risk profile.
findings.verification: opus: Quotes are on HTI (4.4), IRN (5.7) and MMR (5.6) es pages. Opening with 'En cambio' and calling a 4.4/10 pillar 'el área más fuerte' on a 3.7/10 page is the same generic strongest/weakest pattern the blogger complained about.

findings.quote: En cambio, el pilar de salud alcanza 4.1/10 y es el área más fuerte de Somalia.
findings.problem: Nine pages use 'En cambio, el pilar de X ... es el área más fuerte'. Five of them present a danger-zone pillar as a strength: SOM salud 4.1/10 (overall 3.8), SSD riesgos naturales 5.2/10 (overall 3.4), YEM riesgos naturales 5.1/10 (overall 3.4), SYR salud 5.5/10 (overall 3.7), SDN riesgos naturales 5.0/10 (overall 3.4). TCD 'Su pilar más fuerte es riesgos naturales, con 5.7/10' (overall 4.3) is the same problem. A least-bad pillar is framed as a positive contrast.
findings.expected: Say 'el pilar menos débil es salud (4.1/10), que sigue en la franja de riesgo alto', without 'En cambio' or 'área más fuerte'.
findings.verification: opus: SOM says 'En cambio, el pilar de salud alcanza 4.1/10 y es el área más fuerte' and SYR says 5.5; TCD says 'Su pilar más fuerte es riesgos naturales, con 5.7/10'. A high-risk pillar is framed as a positive contrast, which is the generic machine phrasing the blogger criticised.

findings.quote: Le tableau d'ensemble est rassurant : la plupart des gouvernements ne recommandent que des précautions normales pour Île Bouvet
findings.problem: BVT has no score ('Données partielles', 'Pas de score de sécurité officiel'), one advisory, and Bouvet Island is uninhabited, yet the FAQ calls the overall picture reassuring and speaks of 'la plupart des gouvernements' (one government). The same verdict appears on 16 partial pages with 1 to 17 advisories (e.g. GGY, FLK, FRO, GIB, ATF, ALA, CUW, ABW). ESH is the opposite case: 'La consigne dominante est de reconsidérer tout voyage au Sahara occidental' from 2 advisories on a no-score page. CCK and CXR, with zero advisories, add 'ce qui est courant pour les territoires très petits ou reculés', which also reads as reassurance.
findings.expected: On partial-data pages give the advisory count and say that no overall verdict is available. No 'rassurant' or 'consigne dominante' line may be generated from one or two advisories, and no generalisation about small territories should stand in for data.
findings.verification: opus: BVT has one advisory, from Poland, and no score, yet the FAQ says 'Le tableau d'ensemble est rassurant : la plupart des gouvernements…'. GGY says the same from a single advisory. The generalisation is drawn from one data point and the plural wording is wrong. ESH ('La consigne dominante…' from 2 advisories) is milder.

findings.quote: c'est le domaine où République centrafricaine est le plus solide
findings.problem: A least-bad pillar is presented as a strength on high-risk pages. CAF (overall 3.7/10, 'risque élevé') calls natural hazards at 5.9/10 the area where the country is most solid; COD (3.8/10) says the same at 5.4/10; BFA (4.1/10) at 6.1/10; AFG (3.6/10) at criminalité 5.0/10. 'Côté points forts' sentences do the same on BDI (overall 5.4, pillar 6.5), CMR (5.5, 6.3) and ETH (5.2, 6.1). The site itself treats 7/10 as the 'zone de faible risque', so 5 to 6/10 is not a strength.
findings.expected: Use 'point fort' only for pillars at or above 7/10 (the site's 'faible risque' zone). On high-risk pages say that no pillar is reassuring.
findings.verification: opus: CAF (pillars 2.1–5.9) says natural hazards at 5.9 is 'le domaine où République centrafricaine est le plus solide'. BDI says 'Côté points forts, le pilier risques naturels arrive en tête, à 6.5/10'. This is the 'strongest area' boilerplate the blogger criticised, applied to pillars below the site's own low-risk zone.

findings.quote: c'est le domaine où Haïti est le plus solide
findings.problem: On six 'risque élevé' pages (HTI, IRN, LBN, MLI, BIR, NER) answer 2 calls the best of the weak pillars a strength, right after 'point de vigilance majeur': HTI 'le pilier risques naturels atteint 4.4/10 : c'est le domaine où Haïti est le plus solide'; MLI 4.9/10; NER 5.5/10; BIR 5.6/10; LBN and IRN 5.7/10. A pillar at 4.4-5.7/10 is not a strength on a page whose overall band is 'risque élevé'.
findings.expected: Say 'le moins mauvais des cinq piliers (4.4/10), mais encore faible', or drop the strength sentence when the band is 'risque élevé'. Call a pillar 'solide' only above the band threshold.
findings.verification: opus: Verified quotes: HTI 'le pilier risques naturels atteint 4.4/10 : c'est le domaine où Haïti est le plus solide'. The same pattern appears on MLI (4.9), NER (5.5), LBN and IRN (santé 5.7). This is exactly the 'strongest area' machine sentence the blogger criticised, applied to a pillar that is itself weak; on Haiti the natural-hazards pillar is the 'most solid' despite the country's hurricane and earthquake exposure. BIR is not in this batch.

findings.quote: Le tableau d'ensemble est rassurant : la plupart des gouvernements ne recommandent que des précautions normales pour Géorgie du Sud
findings.problem: Partial-data pages (no score, 'Pas de score de sécurité officiel') still get a reassuring summary. SGS has 'un avis aux voyageurs officiel' (a single government) yet says 'la plupart des gouvernements' recommend normal precautions. SPM is the same. SMR (16 advisories, no breakdown) and SJM (2 advisories) are also called 'rassurant' with no score behind the claim. The reassurance contradicts the page's own 'Données partielles' message.
findings.expected: No 'rassurant' or 'la plupart des gouvernements' sentence on pages without a score. State the count and say that no overall assessment is published, e.g. 'Un seul gouvernement publie un avis : ...'.
findings.verification: opus: Narrowed. SGS and SPM each have exactly one advisory (Poland, level 1), yet the FAQ says 'la plupart des gouvernements', a plural majority claim built on a single source. 'Rassurant' alone is not wrong on SMR and SJM, where every listed advisory is level 1. The real defect is the count-blind majority wording on single-advisory pages.

findings.quote: c'est le domaine où Somalie est le plus solide.
findings.problem: A merely least-bad area is presented as a strength on high-risk pages. SOM: 'le pilier santé atteint 4.1/10 : c'est le domaine où Somalie est le plus solide'. SDN: 'le pilier risques naturels atteint 5.0/10 : c'est le domaine où Soudan est le plus solide'. SSD: 'Le pilier le plus solide de Soudan du Sud est risques naturels (5.2/10)'. SRB: 'Serbie ne présente aucun facteur véritablement critique' while its governance pillar is 4.5/10, below the 5/10 danger threshold.
findings.expected: Describe the best pillar relative to the others, not as a strength (e.g. 'le moins mauvais des cinq piliers, à 4.1/10, reste faible'). Don't use 'aucun facteur critique' when a pillar is under 5/10.
findings.verification: opus: Verbatim on the pages: SOM 'le pilier santé atteint 4.1/10 : c'est le domaine où Somalie est le plus solide', SDN 'risques naturels atteint 5.0/10 … le plus solide', SSD 'Le pilier le plus solide … risques naturels (5.2/10)'. SRB says 'aucun facteur véritablement critique' with Gouvernance 4.5/10, and SLE says the same with Santé 4.9/10. Both are below the danger threshold.

findings.quote: mentre a pesare sul punteggio sono governance (8.0/10) e, più di tutto, rischi naturali (4.4/10)
findings.problem: The driver sentence says 'a pesare sul punteggio sono' about the second-weakest pillar even when that pillar is a strength: governance 8.0 (JPN), rischi naturali 8.3 ('mentre a pesare sul punteggio sono rischi naturali (8.3/10)' in LIE), governance 8.2 (NLD). Readers are told an 8/10 pillar pulls the score down. Cause: the a1Drivers.normal copy in src/lib/country-faq-copy.ts inserts {second} with no score check.
findings.expected: When the second pillar is 7 or above, use a neutral clause, for example 'il punteggio è trainato soprattutto da X; Y resta solido (8.0/10)'.
findings.verification: opus: The quotes are present. JPN says 'a pesare sul punteggio sono governance (8.0/10)' and LIE says 'a pesare sul punteggio sono rischi naturali (8.3/10)'. Both describe a strong pillar (8/10 or higher) as one that drags the score down. This is generic machine phrasing.

findings.quote: Per contro, il pilastro rischi naturali ottiene 4.4/10 ed è l'area più solida di Haiti.
findings.problem: A least-bad area is presented as a strength even when the pillar is weak in absolute terms. Haiti's 'area più solida' is 4.4/10, on a 'Non raccomandato' page. Mali: 'Per contro, il pilastro rischi naturali ottiene 4.9/10 ed è l'area più solida di Mali'. Myanmar: 'il pilastro criminalità ottiene 5.6/10 ed è l'area più solida di Myanmar'. Iran: 'il pilastro salute ottiene 5.7/10 ed è l'area più solida di Iran'. The boilerplate 'Il suo punto di forza è il pilastro X' (B6/B17/B21) has the same problem. This is the failure mode the brief names.
findings.expected: When the best pillar is below about 6/10, or the verdict is high-risk or danger, say that no pillar is strong instead of calling it a point of strength or the most solid area.
findings.verification: opus: The HTI page says 'Per contro, il pilastro rischi naturali ottiene 4.4/10 ed è l'area più solida di Haiti' and FAQ A1 calls it 'Il pilastro più solido'. That page is rated 'Non raccomandato', and Haiti is in fact highly exposed to earthquakes and hurricanes. Mali (4.9) shows the same pattern. Calling a weak pillar a strength misleads readers.

findings.quote: Per contro, il pilastro salute ottiene 4.1/10 ed è l'area più solida di Somalia.
findings.problem: On six high-risk pages the FAQ calls the best pillar the 'area più solida' or 'punto di forza' even when its value is a high-risk value: SOM salute 4.1 (overall 3.8/10), SDN rischi naturali 5.0 (overall 3.4), SSD rischi naturali 5.2 (overall 3.4), SYR salute 5.5 (overall 3.7), YEM rischi naturali 5.1 (overall 3.4), and TCD 'Il suo punto di forza è il pilastro rischi naturali, con 5.7/10.' (overall 4.3). On a 'rischio alto' page this reads as reassurance.
findings.expected: Use neutral wording such as 'la voce meno critica', or drop the strength sentence when the best pillar is below about 6/10.
findings.verification: opus: Verified on SOM: 'Per contro, il pilastro salute ottiene 4.1/10 ed è l'area più solida di Somalia'. On TCD (4.3/10, Non raccomandato): 'Il suo punto di forza è il pilastro rischi naturali, con 5.7/10'. Calling a high-risk value a strength is the same generic 'strongest area' pattern the blogger criticised.

findings.quote: l'avviso più severo — usare maggiore prudenza — arriva da Stati Uniti e Canada
findings.problem: On 9 pages (PAN, PER, PRY, SLV, SWZ, TKM, TLS, UZB, XKX) the 'avviso più severo' is the same level as the prevalent advice ('usare maggiore prudenza'), so the superlative names the common level as the strictest and credits two named governments with it. QAT has a related problem: 'gli avvisi più severi — non viaggiare — sono stati emessi da Singapore' (one issuer, plural).
findings.expected: Name the strictest level actually used; if the top level is 'maggiore prudenza', say that no government advises against travel.
findings.verification: opus: The exact quote appears on SWZ.it and others. PAN.it says 'l'avviso più severo — usare maggiore prudenza — arriva da Stati Uniti e Australia' while its summary says 18 of 22 governments recommend that same level. The sentence credits two issuers with the strictest advice when it is in fact the prevailing level. QAT also uses plural 'avvisi più severi ... emessi' for one issuer (Singapore).

findings.quote: o pilar de riscos naturais obtém 4.4/10 e é a área mais forte de Haiti
findings.problem: On pages scored below 5 (risco alto, 'Não recomendado') the FAQ still calls the best pillar 'o pilar mais forte' or 'a área mais forte': 4.4/10 (HTI), 4.9/10 (MLI), 5.5/10 (NER), 5.7/10 (IRN and LBN). A reader takes a 4.4 out of 10 as a strength.
findings.expected: Describe it as the least weak area and say no pillar is strong. Drop the 'mais forte' label when the best pillar still sits in the high-risk band.
findings.verification: opus: HTI has 'Em contrapartida, o pilar de riscos naturais obtém 4.4/10 e é a área mais forte de Haiti', and MLI and NER have 'pilar mais forte ... riscos naturais (4.9/5.x)'. Every pillar on those pages is in the high-risk range, so presenting the best one as a strength is generic machine text and slightly misleading.

findings.quote: o alerta mais severo — redobrar a cautela — vem de Estados Unidos e Reino Unido
findings.problem: When the predominant advice is 'redobrar a cautela', the 'alerta mais severo' is the same level, so the clause adds nothing and reads as a tautology. PER has 2 'precauções normais' and 21 'cautela redobrada' and no higher level at all. The same clause appears on PAN, PRY, SLV, SWZ, TKM, TLS, UZB and XKX (9 pages in total).
findings.expected: 'O nível mais alto emitido é também redobrar a cautela, por Estados Unidos e Reino Unido', or drop the 'mais severo' clause when no government goes higher.
findings.verification: opus: PER.pt reads 'A orientação predominante é redobrar a cautela ao visitar o Peru; o alerta mais severo — redobrar a cautela — vem de Estados Unidos e Reino Unido.' with 21 of 23 governments at caution, and PAN reads the same way. The clause is tautological and wrongly singles out two governments as the strictest when most say the same thing. 'De Estados Unidos' also lacks its article ('dos'). 24 pt pages print 'mais severo — redobrar a cautela'.

findings.quote: the lowest-rated is weak public administration: V-Dem rates the impartiality of public administration at 0.98 on a scale of about −4 to +4, where higher is better
findings.problem: The sentence calls the area 'weak' while quoting a positive value on a scale centred on zero where higher is better, so 0.98 is above the midpoint. The wording contradicts the number it cites. Governance is 7.4/10 here, and the sentence is describing the lowest of five bars, all at 7 or more.
findings.expected: Describe the lowest-rated factor neutrally, for example 'lowest-rated factor: impartiality of public administration (0.98)', and do not call a positive value weak.
findings.verification: opus: The LTU summary quote is exact. It calls 0.98 on a -4 to +4 scale, where higher is better, 'weak public administration', inside an 'all five areas at least 7' sentence for a country ranked 15th. The fixed negative driver label contradicts the value it cites. This is the generic machine-sentence pattern the blogger criticised.

findings.quote: Non — Palestine est actuellement une destination à haut risque : en octobre 2026, le pays obtient 4.6/10 sur notre indice de sécurité, dans la catégorie « risque élevé », et tout voyage exige une grande prudence.
findings.problem: The sentence understates the page's own advisory picture. SUMMARY says 11 of 17 governments 'déconseillent formellement tout voyage' and 2 more 'déconseillent le voyage sauf raison impérative', and FAQ Q3 says most governments 'déconseillent désormais tout voyage'. 'tout voyage exige une grande prudence' sounds like a generic caution, not the 'ne pas voyager' majority the page reports.
findings.expected: State the majority advice directly ('la majorité des gouvernements déconseillent tout voyage') in the Q1 answer, or quote the advisory counts.
findings.verification: opus: The page is PSE, not PAL; the quote is verbatim in its FAQ Q1. SUMMARY gives 11 of 17 'déconseillent formellement tout voyage', 14 505 conflict deaths in 2025, and Conflit 3.0/10. The high-risk template's 'tout voyage exige une grande prudence' understates a do-not-travel majority, though the answer does start with 'Non'.

findings.quote: Crime 4.9/10
findings.problem: CPV, COM and BRN show a Crime pillar (4.9/10, 4.8/10 and 5.5/10) with the low-coverage asterisk, but their INDICATORS tables contain no crime row at all (no GPI safety, no homicide rate). These numbers cannot be traced to any evidence shown on the page. For BRN this is implausible, since Brunei is a low-crime state. The BRN summary also counts 3 datasets while its table shows 2, so a hidden source may be behind the pillar.
findings.expected: Show Crime as partial data when no crime indicator exists, or display the source row that feeds it.
findings.verification: opus: In latest.json BRN's crime pillar has indicators [] and dataCompleteness 0, yet it shows 0.546 (5.5/10) as the lowest bar. CPV (4.9) and COM (4.8) also have no crime row. The bar shows a value that comes only from the prior as if it were measured. For Brunei it is implausible: lower than Malaysia (7.8) and Singapore (8.6) in its own comparison table.

findings.quote: Health 4.6/10
findings.problem: Uncertain whether intended shrinkage or a bug. The health pillar sits well above what its two INFORM health rows imply, and the gap is largest where health is worst: CIV shows 4.6 while its rows (access 7.1, epidemic 7.7, both higher-is-worse) imply about 2.6; CAF 3.4 vs about 1.4; COD 3.9 vs about 2.05; CMR 4.7 vs about 2.85; COG 4.9 vs about 3.05. The gap shrinks to roughly zero where health is good (CHE, CZE, DNK).
findings.expected: Either show on the page which pillar values are prior-driven, or align the pillar with the displayed evidence. Formula evaluation should test this directly.
findings.verification: opus: In latest.json, CIV health has fully covered indicators normalized to 0.29 and 0.23, yet the pillar is 0.462. For CAF they are 0.08 and 0.20 with a pillar of 0.341; for COD 0.23 and 0.18 with 0.39. On the high end, CHE (0.97 and 0.78) gets 0.883. So even at 100% coverage the shrinkage lifts the worst health pillars by about 2 points, with an implied prior of about 0.75-0.87. That runs against the 'conservative prior' the methodology claims.

findings.quote: PILLAR BARS: Governance 3.5/10 | Health 4.6/10 | Crime 5.5/10 | Natural hazards 6.5/10 | Conflict 7.6/10
findings.problem: On high-risk pages the Health bar sits 1 to 2 points above what its own listed inputs give on the safety scale, and the low-risk pages match. LBR: Health 4.6, but its only two inputs (INFORM access 7.5 and epidemic 7.5 risk) average 2.5. Same pattern: MDG 4.6 vs 2.6, MWI 5.3 vs 3.7, MRT 5.0 vs 3.6, MOZ 4.9 vs 3.2, MLI 4.5 vs 3.2, MMR 5.0 vs 3.8. LTU, LVA, LUX and LIE match within 0.2, and LBY matches exactly (6.6 vs 6.6). Natural hazards goes the same way on MEX: 4.8 against 3.5 from its exposure input alone, before the two GDACS alerts. If the bar is a shrink toward a prior that weighs as one input, the implied prior is roughly 7 to 9 (my arithmetic). That does not fit a conservative prior (CLAUDE.md: 'missing data collapses to the prior, never inflates'). Unless an unlisted input exists, the cause is uncertain.
findings.expected: List every input that feeds the Health and Natural hazards bars. Check the prior used for high-risk countries; a bar should not sit above its inputs where the inputs say high risk.
findings.verification: opus: The symptom is real: LBR health inputs are normalised 0.25 and 0.25, yet the pillar is 0.459. The cause is not the prior (muBase 0.45, Africa offset -0.05). It is the v10 pillarCalibration for health in weights.json (alpha 0.1617, beta 0.9136). That offset lifts every low health value by about 1.5 points, so the worst-health countries show a Health bar well above what their inputs say.

findings.quote: 是，可以安全出行 8 8.5 满分 10 安全评分
findings.problem: The HERO integer badge disagrees with the displayed decimal. NZL and POL show 8 next to 8.5, but PRT shows 9 next to 8.5. SUR shows 7 next to 7.5 and TJK shows 6 next to 6.5, where ordinary half-up rounding gives 8 and 7. The badge looks rounded from an unrounded score while the decimal is rounded to one place, so the same displayed value gets different badges.
findings.expected: Derive both numbers from the same displayed value with one rounding rule, or drop the badge.
findings.verification: opus: latest.json gives NZL 8.4956 with scoreDisplay 8 and PRT 8.5367 with scoreDisplay 9, yet both show the decimal 8.5. SUR is 7.498 (shows 7 / 7.5) and TJK 6.456 (shows 6 / 6.5). The badge is rounded from the raw score and the decimal separately, so the same 8.5 gets badges of 8 and 9.

findings.quote: CPV | Cabo Verde | 6.9 | rank 96 | moderate | conf=8.2 crim=4.9 heal=6.4 gove=6.4 envi=7.7 | L1x10 L2x8 | homicide: missing
findings.problem: Cabo Verde is a widely cited low-crime, politically stable island destination, with 10 of 18 advisories at Level 1 and no Level 3 or 4 advisories. Its crime pillar (4.9) is the lowest-possible-looking value and sits well below Ghana's 7.4 and Mauritius's 7.4. The homicide rate is missing, so the crime pillar falls back to the conservative prior instead of reflecting the country's known safety. The result is a 'moderate' band for a place that most travellers would expect in the 'good' band alongside Botswana (7.5) and Namibia (7.3). Missing data is damping a well-known safe destination.
findings.expected: Cabo Verde should reach the 'good' band (7.0 or above), in line with its advisory profile and conflict and environment pillars.
findings.verification: opus: The row is confirmed: crime pillar 4.9 with no homicide figure. Sao Tome has the identical 4.9, so the pillar is the conservative prior, not a measurement. Cabo Verde has no Level 3 or 4 advisories (L1x10, L2x8; the US rates it Level 1) and is a stable, low-conflict island destination. Experts would rate it at least on par with Namibia (7.3) and Botswana (7.5), so a 7.0 floor is defensible. The cause is the missing crime/homicide input collapsing to the prior.

findings.quote: CUB Cuba 6.2 (moderate, gove=3.2, heal=7.5, advisories L1x2 L2x2 L3x13 L4x2); compare MEX Mexico 6.0 (advisories L2x21 L3x1)
findings.problem: Cuba is rated 6.2, above Mexico at 6.0, even though 15 of its 19 government advisories are L3 (reconsider travel) or L4 (do not travel), while Mexico has 1 L3 out of 22 and no L4. Most governments are telling travellers to reconsider going to Cuba, so the advisory consensus should pull Cuba below Mexico, not above it. The health pillar of 7.5 also looks high for a country with ongoing shortages of medicine and power outages.
findings.expected: Cuba should sit clearly below Mexico, at or under about 5.8, consistent with majority L3/L4 advisories. The current score is 0.4 above that bound.
findings.verification: opus: latest.json shows 13 of 19 sources at L3 nationwide ('avoid non-essential travel': UK, CA, AU, DE, NL, NZ, IE, BE, CH, AT, FR, TW, HU) and 2 at L4 (PL, CZ), reflecting Cuba's 2026 fuel, power and medicine collapse. A 'moderate' score of 6.18 with a 7.5 health pillar contradicts that consensus; Venezuela, with a similar advisory profile, is at 4.8. Comparing Cuba with Mexico is debatable because of Mexico's violent crime, so I keep only an absolute bound, loosened from 5.8 to 6.0 (out of the moderate band) for margin.

findings.quote: DOM | Dominican Republic | 6.8 | rank 99 | moderate (vs JAM | Jamaica | 6.8 | rank 105 | moderate)
findings.problem: The two are tied at 6.8, yet Jamaica's homicide rate is 49.4 per 100k (2023) against 10.9 for the Dominican Republic, about four and a half times higher. Jamaica also has the lower crime pillar (5.0 against 6.6) and three Level 3 advisories against none for the Dominican Republic. A traveller comparing the two on violent crime would expect the Dominican Republic to rank clearly higher.
findings.expected: The Dominican Republic should score clearly above Jamaica, by roughly 0.3 points or more.
findings.verification: opus: Rows checked: both 6.8. JAM: homicide 49.4 (2023), crime 5.0, one L3 plus 16 L2. DOM: homicide 10.9, crime 6.6, no L3. Jamaica's homicide rate fell in 2024-25 but is still well above the Dominican Republic's, and the US keeps Jamaica at Level 3 against Level 2 for the DR. The tie comes from Jamaica's better governance and environment pillars offsetting a much worse violent-crime picture, and the ordering DOM > JAM is robust.

findings.quote: IDN | Indonesia | 6.3 | rank 134 | moderate (vs ZAF | South Africa | 6.3 | rank 133 | moderate)
findings.problem: The two are tied at 6.3. South Africa's homicide rate is 43.7 per 100k (2022) against Indonesia's 0.3 (2022), its crime pillar is the lowest in this batch (4.5 against Indonesia's 7.6), and it carries three Level 3 advisories against none for Indonesia. The Indonesia rating is driven down by governance and natural hazards, while violent crime, the main risk for most travellers to South Africa, is far worse there. Most experts would rank Indonesia clearly safer for a typical tourist.
findings.expected: Indonesia should score clearly above South Africa, by roughly 0.3 points or more.
findings.verification: opus: Rows checked: both 6.3. ZAF: homicide 43.7, crime 4.5, 3x L3. IDN: homicide 0.3, crime 7.6, no L3 (L2x19). The tie comes from Indonesia's low governance (3.8), hazard (4.2) and health (5.3) pillars. For a typical tourist (Bali, Java), Indonesia is widely regarded as safer than South Africa, where violent crime (carjacking, armed robbery, express kidnapping) is the dominant risk. GPI and advisories agree, so the ordering IDN > ZAF holds with a margin despite Indonesia's terrorism and disaster exposure.

findings.quote: JPN | Japan | 8.1 | rank 33 | excellent (vs ITA | Italy | 8.2 | rank 29 | excellent)
findings.problem: Japan is rated just below Italy. Japan has a homicide rate of 0.2 per 100k (2023) against Italy's 0.6, and a crime pillar of 8.7 against 8.3. Japan's lower overall score comes almost entirely from natural hazards (4.4, earthquakes and typhoons against Italy's 6.1). Most travel-safety experts would rank Japan as the safer destination for a traveller, and the gap of 0.1 is within noise.
findings.expected: Japan should score above Italy, since its crime and conflict advantages are large and its hazard exposure is shared with Italy in part.
findings.verification: opus: Rows checked: JPN 8.1 (crime 8.7, conflict 8.6, homicide 0.2, envi 4.4) vs ITA 8.2 (crime 8.3, homicide 0.6, envi 6.1). Japan has lower homicide and far less pickpocketing and petty crime, ranks above Italy in the GPI and in essentially every traveller-safety ranking, and has excellent disaster preparedness. Japan ranking below Italy comes only from the hazard pillar, which weighs exposure without preparedness, and almost no expert would accept that ordering.

findings.quote: PNG | Papua New Guinea | 6.2 | 141 | moderate | conf=7.2 crim=6.2 heal=4.9 gove=4.3 envi=4.6 | L2x14 L3x5 L4x1 | - | 0 (2025)
findings.problem: PNG sits in the moderate band (6-7), but the row's own advisory evidence is the weakest in the region: 6 of 20 government advisories are L3 or L4 (30%), against 1 of 20 for Solomon Islands. Its health (4.9), governance (4.3) and natural-hazard (4.6) pillars are among the lowest in the batch. Widely known risks (Port Moresby robbery and carjacking, Highlands tribal fighting, Bougainville instability) are commonly treated as high-caution, not moderate. The homicide field is empty, so the crime pillar cannot be checked against data here. The error is the band, not the ordering.
findings.expected: A score in the high-caution band (5-6), i.e. at or below about 6.0. Its advisory mix and pillar profile put it below the Solomon Islands and the small Pacific states, but the gap is a band-level judgement, so the bound is kept loose.
findings.verification: opus: The table row is right: PNG scores 6.2 (moderate), with L2x14 L3x5 L4x1 and the weakest health, governance and hazard pillars in the batch. latest.json shows US L3 (Reconsider Travel) and Canada L3 (Avoid non-essential travel). Port Moresby's violent crime, tribal fighting in the Highlands, weak medical care and International SOS-style 'high' security and medical ratings put PNG in high caution by any reasonable traveller standard. Its crime pillar (6.2, no homicide data) is also oddly higher than the data-poor Pacific states, so a 6.0 band-edge bound is defensible.

findings.quote: Exercise caution 7 6.9 out of 10 Safety Score
findings.problem: Trinidad and Tobago's 6.9 ties Vietnam's 6.9 on the page (T&T ranks 93rd, Vietnam 92nd). T&T has 40.4 homicides per 100,000 (2022), a crime pillar of 5.3/10 and four governments at reconsider-travel (US, Poland, Spain, Taiwan). Vietnam has a crime pillar of 7.0/10, no reconsider-travel advisory and 12 governments at normal precautions. The order holds only by a rounding-level margin.
findings.expected: Trinidad and Tobago clearly below Vietnam, by more than rounding.
findings.verification: opus: TTO scores 6.919 and VNM 6.924 (both shown as 6.9). TTO has 40.4 homicides per 100k, a crime pillar of 5.3 and 4 reconsider-travel advisories, against none for VNM. A traveller would see these as equally safe, which is implausible. The ordering constraint is robust.

findings.quote: Austrian Federal Ministry (BMEIA): Level 1 (Sichere Lage)
findings.problem: A country's own government is listed as one of the advisory issuers for that same country. On AUT, the Austrian ministry is counted in 'Of the 22 governments that publish a travel advisory for Austria'. On ARG, 'Argentina Ministry of Foreign Affairs: Level 2 (Precaucion)' is counted as an advisory for Argentina. A home ministry's advice is aimed at its own nationals travelling abroad, so these entries look like a mapping artefact. They inflate the advisory counts and feed the advisory consensus that enters the score. Probably the same mapping affects other home-country entries outside this batch.
findings.expected: Exclude the issuer whose country equals the page's country (AUT, ARG) from the advisory list, counts and consensus. Check the mapping on other pages.
findings.verification: opus: AUT lists 'Austrian Federal Ministry (BMEIA): Level 1 (Sichere Lage)', from bmeia.gv.at/.../land/oesterreich. ARG lists 'Argentina Ministry of Foreign Affairs: Level 2 (Precaucion)', from the cancilleria alerts page. Both count toward 'Of the 22 governments...' and the advisory consensus. A home ministry does not issue a travel advisory for its own country, so these are parser artefacts.

findings.quote: Crime 5.7/10 * When a pillar has low data coverage, its contribution to the overall score is reduced or excluded.
findings.problem: Nauru (NRU) and Palau (PLW) both show a Crime pillar of 5.7/10, yet neither INDICATORS table has any crime row (no GPI safety, no World Bank homicide). The figure is the prior, not evidence; the asterisk only says its weight is reduced. Palau's advisories are almost all normal (15 of 17 at Level 1), so a 5.7 crime score is hard to reconcile with the page's own evidence.
findings.expected: Show 'no crime data' rather than a number when a pillar has no indicators, and keep such a pillar out of the headline.
findings.verification: opus: In latest.json the NRU crime pillar has indicators: [] and dataCompleteness 0, so the score 0.5716 (shown as 5.7/10) is purely the prior. PLW is the same: no crime row on either page. The page still prints a number as if it were measured, with only a generic asterisk.

findings.quote: Crime 4.9/10 *
findings.problem: The Crime bar on STP (4.9/10, the page's lowest pillar) has no crime indicator behind it: INDICATORS lists only Health, Governance, Natural hazards and Conflict rows. SLB shows Crime 5.5/10 * with the same gap. The asterisk says only that low-coverage pillars are reduced or excluded; it does not say the number is a fallback. CLAUDE.md says missing data collapses to a prior, so these bars are probably that prior shown as a measured score. Examples: STP, SLB.
findings.expected: Show the pillar as 'no data' (or label the number as an estimate) and keep it out of the weakest-area ranking.
findings.verification: opus: In latest.json the STP crime pillar has 0 indicators and score 0.494, and SLB crime has 0 indicators and 0.546. These are the prior, but the page shows them as 'Crime 4.9/10 *' and 'Crime 5.5/10 *' like measured values. STP's crime bar is also its lowest pillar. The asterisk note does not say the value is an estimate.

findings.quote: UK FCDO: Level 3 (Advise against all but essential travel)
findings.problem: The UK entry is Level 3 on SDN, SOM and TCD. GOV.UK (fetched) says FCDO 'advises against all travel to Sudan', except Hala'ib and Bir Tawil, which get 'all but essential'. For Somalia it says 'advises against all travel to Somalia, including Somaliland, except for the regions of Awdal, Maroodijeh, and Sahil' (fetched). Chad is only partly wrong: the rest of the country including N'Djamena is 'all but essential', but the north, Lake Chad and border areas are 'all travel' (search extract only). All three banners read 'advises against all travel to parts of [country]', so the mapping seems to read 'parts of' as Level 3. Effects: SDN's '2 advise reconsidering travel' should be 1 and '18 advise against all travel' should be 19; SOM's '3 advise reconsidering travel' should be 2 and '16' should be 17.
findings.expected: Map each UK entry to the strictest level that covers most of the country (Level 4 for SDN and SOM), or show the regional split. Re-check every FCDO 'parts of' banner in the mapping.
findings.verification: opus: In advisories.ts, UK_ALERT_LEVEL maps 'avoid_all_travel_to_parts' to 3, and UK_LEVEL_TEXT[3] is 'Advise against all but essential travel'. For Sudan and Somalia the FCDO advises against all travel to nearly the whole country, so the label and level are wrong and the advisory counts are understated. For Chad, Level 3 is defensible.

findings.problem: The crime value is 5.7 to the decimal for Samoa, Tonga and Vanuatu (FJI table) and for Palau, Micronesia, Nauru and Kiribati (FSM table). Marshall Islands is 5.8. Fiji itself has crime 7.9. Identical values across seven unrelated states look like a fallback to the prior, not measured values. FSM's crime bar is already flagged as low data coverage. This is inferred from the batch text only and should be checked against the data.
findings.expected: Measured, distinct crime values for each state, or the crime pillar shown as low-coverage and excluded from the comparison.
findings.verification: opus: latest.json shows crime dataCompleteness 0 with no indicators for WSM, TON, VUT, PLW, FSM, NRU, KIR and MHL (scores 0.567-0.579, so prior-only, about 5.7). FJI has crime 0.79 from World Bank homicide (completeness 0.5). The FJI comparison table puts prior-only 5.7 values next to Fiji's measured 7.9 with no low-coverage marker, which suggests Fiji is much safer from crime than its neighbours without data to back it.

findings.quote: Crime 5.7/10 * When a pillar has low data coverage
findings.problem: The Crime bar reads 5.7/10, but FSM has no crime input on the page (no GPI row, no homicide row). In the shrinkage step (/Users/riccardo/Developer/VibeCoding/Isitsafetotravel/.claude/worktrees/v10-integration/src/pipeline/scoring/engine.ts, header comment: p_hat = (n*p + K*mu)/(n+K)) a pillar with no data takes the prior mu, so 5.7 is a prior, not a measurement. The footnote only says the pillar's contribution is 'reduced or excluded'. The number is also well below Conflict 8.9/10 even though 12 of 13 advisories are Level 1, so it does not come from the page's own evidence.
findings.expected: Show Crime as no data (grey) instead of a number, or label the value as a regional estimate with its source. Do not present a prior as a pillar score.
findings.verification: opus: In latest.json, FSM crime has score 0.567, dataCompleteness 0 and no indicators, so 5.7/10 is the shrinkage prior. The page shows it as a numbered bar with only a generic 'reduced or excluded' footnote.

findings.quote: French Ministry of Foreign Affairs: Level 2 (Vigilance renforcee)
findings.problem: Uncertain. 20 of the 22 advisories for Iraq are Level 3 or 4, yet France is shown at Level 2. In this batch France's 'Formellement deconseille' is mapped to Level 4 (HTI, IRN), and my understanding is that the French advice for most of Iraq has been 'formellement deconseille' for years. Check the live Quai d'Orsay page; a correction would move Iraq's 'increased caution' count from 2 to 1.
findings.expected: Verify the French level for Iraq and correct it if the official advice is Level 4.
findings.verification: opus: I fetched the live diplomatie.gouv.fr Iraq page (zones updated 01/07/2026). It has only red zones ('formellement déconseillé') and orange zones ('déconseillé sauf raison impérative', which covers Baghdad, Basra, Erbil and the rest of Kurdistan). No zone is 'vigilance renforcée', so Level 2 is a parser error from extractFrTerritoryLevel. The correct level is at least 3, so the 'increased caution' count for IRQ should drop from 2 to 1.

findings.quote: Crime 5.7/10 * When a pillar has low data coverage
findings.problem: KIR shows Crime 5.7/10, but its INDICATORS table has no crime row (no GPI safety-and-security, no homicide rate); it lists only INFORM governance, health and natural hazards, ReliefWeb and UCDP. The number is therefore the model's prior, which the formula uses when data are missing, not a measurement. The footnote about low coverage is small, and the page is at 55% coverage, yet the bar reads like a measured pillar.
findings.expected: Show 'no data' or omit the bar for any pillar with no supporting indicator, rather than displaying the prior as a score.
findings.verification: opus: In latest.json the KIR crime pillar has dataCompleteness 0 and no indicators, yet the bar shows Crime 5.7/10. Only a generic footnote marks it, so the prior is displayed as if it were a measured pillar score.

findings.quote: Am meisten Aufmerksamkeit verdient die Gewaltkriminalität: 5,1 Tötungsdelikte je 100.000 Einwohner (Weltbank, 2021).
findings.problem: A 2021 World Bank homicide figure, five years old on a 2026 page, is the basis of a present-tense 'Am meisten Aufmerksamkeit verdient …' claim. The year is shown, so it is not hidden, but the claim reads as current. LUX repeats the pattern with 2022 („am niedrigsten bewertet ist die Gewaltkriminalität: 1,5 … (Weltbank, 2022)“). LIE's FAQ2 cites 'Mordrate (Weltbank)' without the year.
findings.expected: Add the data age to the claim ('zuletzt erhobene Daten: 2021') or prefer a newer indicator when one exists. Keep the year in every mention of that indicator.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on LIE. The year is shown and the indicator row discloses the World Bank lag, so staleness alone is weak. The real problem is different: a single 2021 rate of 5.1/100k in a country of about 40k people (about 2 homicides, i.e. statistical noise) is headlined as the main concern. It also makes Kriminalität (6.6) the weakest pillar, with 'erhöhte Wachsamkeit' advice, for one of Europe's safest places. Recategorised as an implausible value.

findings.quote: La principal preocupación es la delincuencia violenta: 5,1 homicidios por cada 100.000 habitantes (Banco Mundial, 2021).
findings.problem: The present-tense 'La principal preocupación' rests on World Bank 2021 data. Other pages quote 2023 for the same indicator (6 pages), and LUX uses 2022 in the same position ('la peor valorada es la delincuencia violenta: 1,5 homicidios por cada 100.000 habitantes (Banco Mundial, 2022)'). The year is printed, so this is data vintage rather than a false date, but the sentence presents it as current.
findings.expected: Use the latest World Bank year per country, or add 'último dato disponible' next to the year.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is in the LIE SUMMARY, and the data has wb_homicide 5.12 with year 2021. The bigger problem is not the vintage. For Liechtenstein (~40k people, about 2 homicides), the formula itself damps this rate as noise, yet the SUMMARY makes 'delincuencia violenta' the 'principal preocupación' of an 8.2/10 'riesgo muy bajo' country, using data from five years ago.

findings.quote: 5,1 homicides pour 100 000 habitants (Banque mondiale, 2021)
findings.problem: The SUMMARY presents a 2021 homicide figure as the current 'principal point de vigilance' on a page dated 15 octobre 2026. The year is printed, but nothing says the figure is five years old or that newer data is missing (other pages cite 2023).
findings.expected: Flag the year as the last available figure in the sentence ('dernière donnée disponible : 2021'), or use a more recent source.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on LIE.fr's SUMMARY, and latest.json gives wb_homicide 5.12, year 2021, as the only crime indicator. The year is printed, so staleness alone would be minor. The real problem is that for a population of about 39k, 5.1 per 100k means 1-2 homicides, which is statistical noise that the formula itself damps. The SUMMARY still presents it as the main concern of a very safe country.

findings.quote: PILLAR BARS: Crime 5.1/10 * When a pillar has low data coverage, its contribution to the overall score is reduced or excluded.
findings.problem: The Crime bar is a number, but the Maldives page lists no crime input: no Global Peace Index safety row and no World Bank homicide row (its indicators are V-Dem, INFORM and UCDP only). MHL shows the same (Crime 5.8/10 with only INFORM, ReliefWeb, GDACS and UCDP rows). The value is therefore a prior displayed as if measured. For the Maldives it is the lowest bar, yet the summary calls governance (6.3) the weakest area. The asterisk says the bar's weight is reduced; it does not say there is no evidence behind the number.
findings.expected: Show 'no crime data' instead of a numeric crime bar, or label the value as a prior. Keep the SUMMARY consistent with the bars.
findings.verification: opus: In latest.json the MDV crime pillar has dataCompleteness 0 and no indicators, so the 5.1 bar is just the shrinkage prior (0.511). MHL is the same (crime 0.579, no inputs). The page shows the number as if measured, with only a 'low data coverage' asterisk. That asterisk is also inaccurate: a pillar with n=0 still enters the geometric mean at full weight, carrying the prior.

findings.quote: Global Peace Index, militarisation | 2.70
findings.problem: A traveller cannot act on a country's militarisation (military spending and arms-trade measures), yet it is listed as a Conflict-pillar indicator on every full-score page (AFG 2.70, AUS 1.70, AUT 1.34). Other structural rows have the same problem: 'Governance (INFORM) | 8.7 / 10' on AFG and 'Impartial public administration (V-Dem) | 2.15' on AUT. These feed the scores yet are shown to readers as if they explained the risk.
findings.expected: Show only traveller-actionable indicators as drivers (crime, road, health or hazard incidents, detention or consular risk). Keep structural measures in the methodology or label them as context.
findings.verification: opus: 'Global Peace Index, militarisation | 2.70' is on AFG, and the row appears on every scored page (e.g. AUT, ARE), shown as a Conflict-pillar indicator and weighted 11.25% in the formula. Military spending, armed-forces size and arms trade say nothing a traveller can act on. This is the same kind of irrelevant indicator the blogger criticised.

findings.quote: Impartial public administration (V-Dem) | 3.99
findings.problem: Travellers cannot act on V-Dem 'impartial public administration' or GPI 'militarisation'. Both appear on nearly every page, for example DEU (3.99 and 2.08) and CHE (3.58 and 1.56). The INFORM Governance rows and V-Dem political corruption rows are similar background indicators, not traveller-facing risks.
findings.expected: Remove these rows from display and from the traveller-risk pillars, or label them clearly as background context.
findings.verification: opus: The rows exist exactly as quoted: DEU 'Impartial public administration (V-Dem) | 3.99' and 'GPI militarisation 2.08', CHE 3.58 and 1.56. GPI militarisation (military spending, arms exports, nuclear capability) has no bearing on a traveller's safety, yet it feeds the conflict pillar. The V-Dem administration row is more defensible as a proxy for police and court reliability. It is the same class of problem as the blogger's complaint.

findings.quote: Global Peace Index, militarisation | 3.92
findings.problem: GPI militarisation is a national military-capacity measure (spending, armed-forces size, arms trade). It is listed as a traveller-facing indicator on 24 of the 26 scored pages (all except KIR and KNA), and the formula gives it 11.25% of the conflict pillar (CLAUDE.md). A traveller cannot act on it and it does not describe a risk met on the ground. Examples: ISR 3.92, KOR 2.23, IRQ 2.18. It is the same kind of input the blogger objected to, namely indicators irrelevant to travellers.
findings.expected: Drop militarisation from the displayed traveller indicators and test the conflict pillar without it; keep GPI overall, UCDP deaths and the advisory consensus.
findings.verification: opus: The row appears on the ISR page (3.92) and the KOR page (2.23). The code itself excludes gpi_militarisation as a driver because it is 'not something a traveller meets' (indicator-display.ts), yet it is shown and scored. The ISR FAQ even names militarisation as the lowest-scoring signal. This is the same class of problem as the blogger's irrelevant-indicator complaint.

findings.quote: - Conflict | Global Peace Index, militarisation | 1.71 | GPI scale 1–5, lower is better | GPI 2026 | 2026
findings.problem: A traveller cannot act on the GPI militarisation index, which measures a country's military capacity and spending rather than risk to a visitor. It appears on 19 pages and carries 11.25% of the Conflict bar. The V-Dem 'Impartial public administration' row (22 pages, e.g. LBR −0.06, LTU 0.98, MDV 2.00) is in the same class: a civil-service quality score, not something a visitor can use. These are the kind of rows the blogger objected to (air pollution, child mortality).
findings.expected: Drop militarisation from the displayed indicators, and drop or relabel the impartial-administration row as background. If either stays in the formula, say why on the page.
findings.verification: opus: The GPI militarisation row appears on many pages (LBR 1.71, LBY 2.09, MWI 1.93, LTU 1.96). It measures military spending, personnel and weapons capacity, not risk to a visitor, yet it feeds the Conflict bar. The V-Dem impartial administration row (LBR -0.06, LTU 0.98, MDV 2.00) is governance background in the same class.

findings.quote: The main concern is the spread of epidemics: 5.9 out of 10 on the INFORM scale
findings.problem: The headline 'main concern' is INFORM's country-level epidemic-risk score (MYS 5.9, OMN 4.7, PRY 5.8). It is a structural index of outbreak preparedness, not a traveller-facing hazard, yet the sentence presents it as what a visitor should worry about most. It is picked only because it is the lowest-rated line inside the Health pillar (selectPillarDriver in src/lib/indicator-display.ts). On Oman the same 4.7 also appears as natural-hazard exposure, which the summary does not mention. Arguable; flagged for relevance.
findings.expected: Headline a traveller-relevant risk (for example dengue advice, road safety or hazard alerts) and present INFORM epidemic risk as background.
findings.verification: opus: MYS, OMN and PRY headline INFORM epidemic risk (5.9, 4.7, 5.8) as 'the main concern'. On OMN this is misleading: 9 of 22 governments advise reconsidering travel and the Natural hazards pillar (5.1) is lower than Health (6.9), yet the headline is a structural epidemic index. For MYS (dengue) it is more defensible.

findings.quote: Global Peace Index, militarisation | 2.10
findings.problem: GPI militarisation (military spending, arms trade, armed forces) is listed as a Conflict input on 20 of the 24 scored pages. A traveller cannot act on a country's militarisation, and it does not measure the risk to a visitor. It also pushes in odd directions: SGP (2.10) and SWE (2.12) have higher militarisation than THA (1.56), which lowers their Conflict scores even though both are among the safest places on the list. CLAUDE.md documents militarisation at 11.25% of Conflict under v9.1; check whether v10 keeps it. Examples: SGP, SWE, THA.
findings.expected: Drop GPI militarisation from the traveller-safety composite, or document why it is a risk proxy for visitors. Conflict should rest on violence and advisories.
findings.verification: opus: Every scored page with GPI lists 'Global Peace Index, militarisation' under Conflict. SGP shows 2.10 and SWE 2.12, against THA's 1.56. This lowers the Conflict pillar of very safe places on the basis of military spending and arms trade, which do not measure risk to visitors. It is the same 'irrelevant indicator' kind the blogger criticised.

findings.quote: Global Peace Index, militarisation | 3.09
findings.problem: Militarisation (military spending, personnel, arms trade) is not something a visitor can act on, and the codebase already treats it that way: indicator-display.ts sets NOT_A_TRAVEL_DRIVER = {gpi_militarisation}, so it is never the summary's driver. It still scores inside the Conflict pillar at 11.25% (weights.json). For USA, militarisation (3.09 raw, 4.8/10 normalised) is the weakest of its three conflict inputs, so a large military power is marked down for its footprint while its UCDP conflict deaths are 0.
findings.expected: Remove militarisation from the Conflict pillar or re-weight it and re-normalise; if kept, document why it is a traveller risk. Keep it out of the traveller-facing indicator table.
findings.verification: opus: The USA page lists 'Global Peace Index, militarisation | 3.09' inside the Conflict pillar (7.4). Military spending and arms exports are not a traveller risk, which the codebase itself admits by excluding it as a driver, yet it still weighs in the score and appears in the table. This is the kind of irrelevant-indicator complaint the blogger made.

findings.quote: The main concern is poor public safety: the Global Peace Index rates safety and security at 2.62
findings.problem: Nicaragua's summary names poor public safety as the main concern, while the PILLAR BARS directly under it show Governance 1.7/10, the lowest pillar by far (V-Dem rule of law 0.01, impartial public administration -3.55). Governance is excluded from the driver by design (DIRECT_RISK_PILLARS in src/lib/country-summary.ts), so the headline never mentions it. The same pattern appears on North Korea (Governance 2.4/10, while the 'main risk' is conflict at 4.8/10) and Peru (Governance 4.8/10, while the 'main concern' is crime at 6.5/10).
findings.expected: Decide explicitly whether a pillar at 1 to 4 out of 10 may stay out of the headline; if not, add a governance sentence when governance is below about 4/10.
findings.verification: opus: NIC's summary names poor public safety (Crime 6.3/10) as the main concern, while the pillar bars directly under it show Governance 1.7/10, which is never mentioned. PRK (Governance 2.4) and PER (Governance 4.8) follow the same pattern. Governance is left out by design. For NIC, though, arbitrary detention is a real traveller risk, so leaving out a 1.7 pillar is misleading by omission rather than a hard contradiction.

findings.quote: 目前最严厉的警告——重新考虑出行——来自美国和加拿大。
findings.problem: The strictest-tier issuers are given as two names although the SUMMARY counts more at that tier (OMN: 9 governments at 重新考虑出行). TCD (8 at avoid, named US and Australia), VEN (6, named Canada and Australia) and PAN (18 at 提高警惕, named US and Australia) read as though these were the only issuers.
findings.expected: Give the count and the names, for example 目前有9个政府建议重新考虑出行，包括美国和加拿大.
findings.verification: opus: OMN.zh: 9 governments at reconsider, yet the page says 目前最严厉的警告——重新考虑出行——来自美国和加拿大. VEN: 6 at avoid, named only as 由加拿大和澳大利亚发布. PAN: 18 at 提高警惕, two named. With no 等 or count, these read as complete lists, unlike the PRK template that says 等国. The English text has the same problem.

findings.quote: É seguro viajar para o Congo? 5.6/10 (2026)
findings.problem: COG is the Republic of the Congo, but TITLE, H1, HERO and SUMMARY all say 'o Congo', while the DRC page is titled 'República Democrática do Congo' (3.8/10). Side by side, a traveller can read the wrong country's score. 'Congo' alone is ambiguous in Portuguese.
findings.expected: 'República do Congo' in TITLE, H1, HERO and SUMMARY, with the DRC keeping 'República Democrática do Congo'.
findings.verification: opus: COG pt TITLE and H1 say 'o Congo', while COD is 'República Democrática do Congo'. The de and zh pages disambiguate ('Kongo-Brazzaville', '刚果（布）'). 'Congo' is the ISO short name, so this is ambiguity, not an error.

findings.quote: The main concern is armed conflict: 144 people were killed in armed conflict in 2025 (UCDP)
findings.problem: The headline risk is armed conflict (144 deaths), yet on the same page Natural hazards is 3.8/10, the second-lowest pillar (Conflict is 6.1/10), with INFORM natural hazard exposure at 8.2/10 and 8 orange or red GDACS alerts. For a traveller to the Philippines typhoon and earthquake risk is the one the summary should name. The driver rule (selectDriverPillar in src/lib/country-summary.ts) ranks pillars by weight times log-shortfall; natural hazards carries only 10% weight against conflict's 30%, so conflict wins. PAK has the same effect: natural hazards 3.4/10 is never mentioned.
findings.expected: Name the pillar that is actually lowest for a traveller, or change the driver rule so a 3.8/10 hazard pillar with active alerts can be the headline; mention active GDACS alerts when present.
findings.verification: opus: The PHL summary names armed conflict (Conflict pillar 6.1/10) as the main concern. The same page shows Natural hazards at 3.8/10, with INFORM exposure 8.2/10, 8 orange/red GDACS alerts and 2 ReliefWeb disasters, and the summary never mentions hazards. Conflict in Mindanao is a real risk, so naming it is defensible. Leaving out a far lower pillar with active alerts is still a real gap caused by the weight-based driver rule.

findings.quote: Serbia 7.7 ; Moldova 7.6 ; Bosnia and Herzegovina 7.6
findings.problem: Albania's 'In the same region' list includes Moldova, which is in Eastern Europe and not in the Balkans. Serbia and Bosnia fit, but Moldova is a weak match.
findings.expected: Keep the 'same region' list to Balkan or Southern European countries for Albania.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on ALB.en. Moldova appears because regions.ts puts all of Europe in one bucket and orders it by closest score. It is a weak Balkan peer and has the same root cause as #4.

findings.quote: Its best-rated area is conflict (8.3/10).
findings.problem: When two pillars share the displayed top value, the page still names one as uniquely best.
