GRC: SUMMARY says 'Its best-rated area is conflict (8.3/10)' while PILLAR BARS show Health 8.3/10 and Conflict 8.3/10. HRV: FAQ 1 says 'health (8.7/10) is Croatia's strongest pillar' while Conflict is also 8.7/10. KWT: SUMMARY says 'Its best-rated area is health (7.0/10)' with Crime 7.0/10 on the bars. KEN: FAQ 1 says 'crime (6.1/10) is Kenya's strongest pillar' with Natural hazards 6.1/10 on the bars.
findings.expected: Name both pillars when they tie (for example 'Health and conflict are tied at 8.3/10'), or use an explicit, visible tie-break rule.
findings.verification: opus: Verified on the pages: GRC SUMMARY 'Its best-rated area is conflict (8.3/10)' with bars Health 8.3 | Conflict 8.3; HRV FAQ 'health (8.7/10) is Croatia's strongest pillar' with Conflict 8.7; KWT 'best-rated area is health (7.0/10)' with Crime 7.0; KEN FAQ 'crime (6.1/10) is Kenya's strongest pillar' with Natural hazards 6.1. The underlying values probably differ in the second decimal, but at the displayed precision the pages name one pillar as uniquely best when two are tied. Not misleading for safety, so the severity is lowered to low.

findings.problem: When a page has fewer than three real neighbours, the table is filled with the nearest scored countries within NEARBY_MAX_KM = 2,000 km of one point per country (src/lib/comparisons.ts, points in src/data/country-coords.json), so 'nearby' includes places 1,200 to 1,950 km away. Approximate distances from those points: VUT lists Nauru (~1,790 km) and Tuvalu (~1,490 km); TON lists Vanuatu (~1,860 km) and Tuvalu (~1,650 km); SLB lists Micronesia (~1,830 km); TLS lists Brunei (~1,935 km); SGP lists Brunei (~1,245 km) and Cambodia (~1,250 km); URY lists Chile (~1,400 km); PRT lists Algeria (~1,520 km) and France (~1,295 km); REU (grey) lists Seychelles (~1,590 km) and Comoros (~1,600 km). Timor-Leste has no Australia entry at all: Australia appears only as 'nearby' at ~1,940 km because its point is the national centre, while Darwin is about 700 km from Dili. The 'nearby' label does not mean close.
findings.expected: Tag as 'nearby' only countries within roughly 1,000 km, or show no fill and say there are no close neighbours. Measure distance from the nearest border or coast rather than one national point. Add real maritime neighbours for island states (Timor-Leste and Australia at minimum).
findings.verification: opus: I recomputed the distances from country-coords.json and they match the claims: VUT-NRU 1794, TON-VUT 1861, TLS-BRN 1935, TLS-AUS 1941, PRT-DZA 1518 km. TLS has only ['IDN'] in borderMap, so Australia, its real maritime neighbour across the Timor Sea, shows only as a borderline 'nearby'. In the open Pacific ~1,800 km is arguably close, so the main real defect is the missing maritime neighbours, not the label.

findings.problem: 40 borderMap pairs are one-sided (A lists B, B does not list A); 22 involve batch countries. Effect: a page names a country whose own page never names it back. In this batch, Palau lists the Philippines (the Palau table shows Philippines 6.1) but the Philippines table does not show Palau; Singapore lists Indonesia; Tuvalu lists Fiji and Kiribati; the Philippines lists Indonesia and Malaysia; Seychelles lists Madagascar and Mauritius; New Zealand lists Fiji (see the NZL and SYC findings).
findings.expected: Derive the reverse entries automatically, or enforce symmetry in a unit test, and keep one-sided entries only when deliberate and documented.
findings.verification: opus: A script over borderMap finds exactly 40 one-sided pairs (e.g. PLW->PHL, SGP->IDN, PHL->IDN/MYS, TUV->FJI/KIR). The PHL table (Taiwan, Malaysia, Indonesia) has no Palau, and the IDN table has no Singapore or Philippines. Some asymmetry is deliberate (HKG/MAC->CHN), so this is a low-severity consistency issue.

findings.quote: Liechtenstein nearby | 8.2 | 9.0 | 6.6 | 9.3 | 7.2 | 8.3
findings.problem: The 'nearby' tag is applied to countries hundreds of km away, so the tag does not mean close. Andorra (AND): Liechtenstein is roughly 800 km away and Switzerland roughly 550 km, both tagged nearby. Bonaire (BES): Grenada, Trinidad and Tobago and Saint Vincent are each roughly 700-800 km away. Anguilla (AIA): Saint Lucia is roughly 500 km away. American Samoa (ASM): Tuvalu is roughly 1,200+ km away and Tonga roughly 1,000 km. These are rough great-circle estimates from geography knowledge.
findings.expected: Reserve the 'nearby' tag for countries that are close, or drop the far ones from the table, so that 'nearby' is never applied to places ~500 km or more away.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on AND.en. Fillers get the 'nearby' tag at any centroid distance up to NEARBY_MAX_KM=2000. Computed distances: AND-LIE 810 km, AND-CHE 707 km, AIA-LCA 532 km, ASM-TON 823 km, ASM-TUV 1446 km, BES-GRD 710 km. They are the nearest data-sufficient places, so the selection is defensible, but the 'nearby' label overstates closeness. This is a labelling issue that does not affect a safety decision.

findings.problem: The 'nearby' tag is applied to distant countries. Sweden is about 2,000 km from Iceland (ISL). The Netherlands and Belgium are roughly 750-800 km from Ireland (IRL, 'Netherlands nearby'). The Dominican Republic is about 700 km from Jamaica (JAM). The tags are also inconsistent: Haiti (about 475 km from Jamaica, the closer place) carries no tag while the Dominican Republic does. The tag rule appears to be continent-wide or loose rather than distance-based.
findings.expected: 'nearby' only for places close by land or short sea crossing, applied with one consistent rule (for example a distance threshold), and closer places should not be left untagged while farther ones are tagged.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on ISL.en.txt. Sweden tagged 'nearby' to Iceland (about 2,000 km) is a stretch, and Denmark, which really neighbours Iceland through the Faroes and Greenland, is missing. Belgium and the Netherlands as 'nearby' to Ireland are loose too. The Haiti point is a misreading: untagged rows (Haiti, Cuba, UK, Norway) are declared neighbours and 'nearby' marks filler rows, so that part is not inconsistent.

findings.quote: la peor valorada es la exposición a peligros naturales: 2,5 sobre 10 en la escala de INFORM, donde 10 es la exposición máxima
findings.problem: The sentence calls natural hazards the worst-rated area and then gives a low figure (2,5) on an exposure scale where 10 is maximum. Read naturally, '2,5 sobre 10' is bad, but it means low exposure, and the pillar itself is 7.7/10 (top band). Same construction on BEL (3,4), CHE (2,3), DNK (2,2), EST (1,6), FIN (2,5), GBR (3,5).
findings.expected: State low exposure explicitly ('exposición baja: 2,5 sobre 10, donde 10 es la exposición máxima') or give the pillar score for 'peor valorada'.
findings.verification: opus: AUT SUMMARY reads 'la peor valorada es la exposición a peligros naturales: 2,5 sobre 10 en la escala de INFORM, donde 10 es la exposición máxima'. The direction of the scale is stated, so the sentence is not false, but a low-is-good figure next to /10 pillar scores where high is good is confusing. Style-level only.

findings.quote: se ve lastrada por criminalidad (6.6/10) y, sobre todo, por salud (6.6/10)
findings.problem: Two pillars with identical scores are ranked ('y, sobre todo'). BWA: criminalidad and salud are both 6.6/10, yet DESCRIPTION and Q2 name criminalidad as the area needing most attention without mentioning the tie. CPV: 'se ve lastrada por salud (6.4/10) y, sobre todo, por gobernanza (6.4/10)' while DESCRIPTION says 'Mayor riesgo: salud (6.4)'.
findings.expected: Say 'a la par' or 'empatan' for ties and state which rule picks the main risk.
findings.verification: opus: The BWA text is exact: 'se ve lastrada por criminalidad (6.6/10) y, sobre todo, por salud (6.6/10)', while DESCRIPTION and Q2 name criminalidad. CPV likewise ranks salud 6.4 and gobernanza 6.4 with 'sobre todo' but names salud in DESCRIPTION. Ties are ranked arbitrarily and inconsistently.

findings.quote: la peor valorada es la exposición a peligros naturales: 2,5 sobre 10 en la escala de INFORM, donde 10 es la exposición máxima
findings.problem: The SUMMARY calls the weakest area 'la peor valorada' or the 'principal preocupación' and then quotes a sub-indicator where 10 is maximum exposure, so the figure shown is the low-risk end. ISL 2,5 (its natural-hazards bar is 7.7/10), IRL 2,3, NOR 2,8, LVA 2,4, MDA 3,4 ('principal preocupación'), MNG 3,3. LUX calls 'la delincuencia violenta: 1,5 homicidios por cada 100.000 habitantes' the worst area, a very low rate. A reader sees the 'worst' label next to the best-looking number.
findings.expected: Give the sub-indicator in the pillar's direction ('exposición baja: 2,5 sobre 10') or drop the figure.
findings.verification: opus: ISL 'la peor valorada es la exposición a peligros naturales: 2,5 sobre 10 ... donde 10 es la exposición máxima' and LUX '1,5 homicidios' sit after 'al menos un 7', so the worst-area label is relative and the scale is stated. This is confusing but not false, so the severity is low.

findings.quote: a mais baixa é a exposição a riscos naturais: 2,3 de 10 na escala do INFORM, sendo 10 a exposição mais alta
findings.problem: On the pages with 'As cinco áreas têm pelo menos 7 de 10; a mais baixa é…' the lowest pillar (IRL riscos naturais 7,8/10) is followed by an INFORM exposure figure (2,3 'de 10', where 10 is the highest exposure). A reader sees 'a mais baixa … 2,3' and reads the weakest area as a low number, while 2,3 means low exposure. ISL (2,5), LVA (2,4), NOR (2,8) do the same. LUX does it with 'a mais baixa é a criminalidade violenta: 1,5 homicídios por 100 mil habitantes'.
findings.expected: Give the pillar score with the name ('a área mais fraca é riscos naturais, 7,8/10') and quote the INFORM value with its direction ('exposição baixa: 2,3 de 10, onde 10 é a mais alta').
findings.verification: opus: IRL: 'a mais baixa é a exposição a riscos naturais: 2,3 de 10 na escala do INFORM, sendo 10 a exposição mais alta'. LUX: 'a mais baixa é a criminalidade violenta: 1,5 homicídios'. The scale direction is stated, so this is not strictly wrong, but 'a mais baixa' next to a low raw value without the pillar score (7.8/10) is ambiguous. This is a style/clarity issue only.

findings.quote: 其中以健康（8.8/10）表现最为突出。
findings.problem: On FIN, crime, conflict and health all read 8.8/10, so health is not the single most outstanding pillar. DNK (governance = health 8.8), EST (conflict = health 8.6) and CZE (conflict = health 8.8) have the same tie. The FAQ's strongest-pillar slot in src/lib/seo.ts does not apply the near-tie check that src/lib/pillar-extremes.ts provides.
findings.expected: Name the tie (e.g. '健康与犯罪、冲突并列最高，均为8.8/10') or drop the superlative when pillars tie.
findings.verification: opus: FIN's PILLAR BARS show 犯罪 8.8, 冲突 8.8 and 健康 8.8, yet the FAQ says '其中以健康（8.8/10）表现最为突出'. DNK (治理 = 健康 8.8), EST (冲突 = 健康 8.6) and CZE (健康 = 冲突 8.8, which the FAQ names as 冲突) show the same displayed tie. The superlative picks one pillar out of a tie.

findings.quote: Sierra Leone nearby | 6.6 | 7.8 | 5.9 | 4.9 | 5.0 | 6.6
findings.problem: Sierra Leone (roughly 1,300 km from Cabo Verde) is tagged 'nearby'. Gambia, untagged in the same header (neighbouring and nearby), is not a neighbour. Mauritania (roughly 800 km, score 5.7, shown on the COG page as 'Mauritania 5.7') is closer than Sierra Leone and is missing from the table.
findings.expected: Include Mauritania as the nearest mainland state. Remove the nearby tag from Sierra Leone and remove Gambia from the neighbour rows.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is exact. Sierra Leone (about 1,300 km in reality, centroid 1471) is tagged nearby, while Mauritania (scored 5.7, closer to the Cabo Verde islands in reality) misses by centroid (1483 km). The claim about Gambia is wrong: borderMap lists CPV:[SEN, GMB] as maritime neighbours, and Gambia is about as close as Senegal, so Gambia should stay. Low-severity selection quirk.

findings.problem: Christmas Island is in the Indian Ocean, a few hundred km from Java. Brunei (roughly 2,000 km), Singapore (roughly 1,300 km) and Malaysia (roughly 1,500 km) are all tagged 'nearby'. The only truly close state, Indonesia (roughly 400 km, score 6.3), is the lowest row in the table. The 'nearby' tag gives proximity that the reader will take as meaningful.
findings.expected: Tag 'nearby' only for states within a plausible travel distance, or drop distant states from the table. Keep Indonesia as the primary neighbour.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is exact. CXR (grey) gets 4 fillers by centroid: Singapore 1327, Malaysia 1629, Indonesia 1660 and Brunei 1929 km. All are under the 2000 km cap, but Brunei is about 2,000 km away. Java is only about 350 km away, yet Indonesia's centroid puts it third. Australia, the sovereign state, is excluded (centroid 3306 km). Indonesia is last only because rows are sorted by score, which is by design. Minor problem on a grey page.

findings.problem: Belgium and the Netherlands are roughly 700 km away across the North Sea, yet they carry the same 'nearby' tag as Ireland, which is close. The same looseness appears on HKG ('- Laos nearby', a landlocked country about 1,300 km away) and IOT ('- Sri Lanka nearby', about 1,800 km away).
findings.expected: Reserve 'nearby' for places within a short distance, or use a distance threshold so that Belgium, the Netherlands, Laos and Sri Lanka are not tagged as nearby.
findings.verification: opus: All the quoted rows are on the pages: Belgium/Netherlands on IMN, Laos on HKG and Sri Lanka on IOT. NEARBY_MAX_KM=2000 in comparisons.ts lets places 700-1,800 km away carry the same 'nearby' tag as Ireland or the UK. For isolated territories these are the closest scored places, so this is loose labelling rather than wrong data.

findings.problem: Iran is absent from Kuwait's neighbour table, though it is the Gulf's northern shore and across the water from Kuwait (Bushehr is roughly 280 km away). Qatar, roughly 580 km away, is tagged 'nearby' instead. Iran has an official score (3.9 on the IRN page) and appears in the Iraq table.
findings.expected: Iran included as a Gulf neighbour with its official score, or the 'nearby' tagging reviewed for Qatar.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on KWT.en.txt. Kuwait's table has Qatar and Bahrain as 'nearby' plus Saudi Arabia and Iraq, but no Iran. Iran's Khuzestan coast is less than about 100-150 km from Kuwait across the northern Gulf, much closer than Qatar (about 550 km), and Iran (3.9) is in the Iraq table. Omitting a nearby high-risk country makes the regional picture look rosier.

findings.quote: North Korea nearby | 4.8 | 4.8 | 4.8 | 7.7 | 2.4 | 4.7
findings.problem: North Korea shares no border with Mongolia (China lies between them, and the distance is well over 1,000 km) yet is tagged 'nearby'. Kazakhstan, a real land neighbour of Mongolia with an official score (7.3, shown on this same page under 'In the same region'), is missing from the table.
findings.expected: Kazakhstan should be in the neighbours table. North Korea should be dropped, or at least not tagged 'nearby' next to a missing land neighbour.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on MNG.en. The finding is right that North Korea is tagged 'nearby' while Kazakhstan (7.3, data-sufficient, about 37 km from Mongolia at the closest point) is left out. But it wrongly calls Kazakhstan a land neighbour: Mongolia borders only Russia and China. The cause is centroid distance: North Korea is about 1,900 km away and Kazakhstan about 2,790 km, which is over the 2,000 km NEARBY_MAX_KM limit. The fix is a proximity override or edge-to-edge distance, not a new border.

findings.problem: Malawi is a landlocked country roughly 1,200 km from Mayotte, and Seychelles (also tagged 'nearby', quoted as 'Seychelles nearby | 7.8 | 8.5 | 6.4 | 7.9 | 7.9 | 7.3') is roughly 1,400 km away. Mozambique, about 500 km away across the Mozambique Channel and scored 5.5 on the Mozambique page, is absent. A traveller would find Malawi and Seychelles odd as Mayotte's 'nearby' comparisons.
findings.expected: Mozambique should be in the 'nearby' rows. Malawi and Seychelles should be dropped, or the 'nearby' set should be built from actual proximity.
findings.verification: opus: The quotes are on MYT.en. By centroid distance Malawi (about 1,207 km) beats Mozambique (about 1,282 km), so landlocked Malawi is shown while Mozambique, which lies between it and Mayotte across the Channel (about 500 km away), is left out. The Seychelles distance claim is overstated, because its Aldabra group lies about 400 km from Mayotte. Mayotte is also a grey page, so finding #0 covers whether the table should exist at all. A borderMap entry (MYT: COM, MDG, MOZ), like the existing ALA one, would fix the selection.

findings.problem: Norfolk Island is an Australian external territory, and Australia (scored on the site, e.g. 'Australia 8.5' on the Netherlands similar-risk list) is absent from its table. Tonga, roughly 1,900 km away, and Fiji, roughly 1,600 km away, are tagged 'nearby' instead. The administering state is the most relevant comparison and is missing.
findings.expected: Australia should be in the table. The 'nearby' tag should be limited to the closest states.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on NFK.en. Australia, the administering state, is missing because its centroid is about 3,480 km away, beyond NEARBY_MAX_KM, while Tonga (about 1,970 km) and Fiji (about 1,600 km) get in. Norfolk is a grey page (see #0). If the table is kept, it needs a borderMap entry like ALA's (NFK: AUS, NZL, NCL).

findings.problem: UMI has no borderMap entry and one point, Wake Island (19.3, 166.63). Kiribati (score 7.1), whose Line and Phoenix islands lie several hundred km from Jarvis, Palmyra and Kingman, is 2,102 km from that point (Kiribati's point is Tarawa) and falls outside the 2,000 km cut. The table instead lists Micronesia (~1,650 km from Wake) and the Marshall Islands (~1,090 km). The grey-table problem applies here too.
findings.expected: Give UMI explicit maritime neighbours (KIR, plus MHL and FSM for Wake), or describe the territory by its island groups rather than one point; or drop the table on this grey page.
findings.verification: opus: The UMI page shows Marshall Islands and Micronesia as nearby. UMI's single point is Wake Island, and Kiribati is 2,102 km from it, just over the cut, although Jarvis, Palmyra and Kingman sit next to Kiribati's Line Islands. Minor because this is a grey page.

findings.quote: auf einer Skala von 1 (am friedlichsten) bis 5 (GPI 2026)
findings.problem: The source tag sits on the scale end, so the sentence reads as if the scale ends at 'GPI 2026' (AFG, BDI, BGD, GAB). The same indicator is called 'gesellschaftliche Sicherheit (Global Peace Index)' in FAQs (DOM, ECU) and 'öffentliche Sicherheit' in SUMMARY. Two terms for one indicator.
findings.expected: Write '... mit 3,11 auf einer Skala von 1 (am friedlichsten) bis 5; Quelle: Global Peace Index 2026', and use one term throughout.
findings.verification: opus: 'bis 5 (GPI 2026)' is on AFG, BGD and DOM. Attaching the source to the scale end is slightly awkward but understandable. The terminology point is real: the GPI Safety & Security indicator is called 'öffentliche Sicherheit' in the SUMMARY and 'gesellschaftliche Sicherheit (Global Peace Index)' in the FAQ. This is a minor inconsistency.

findings.quote: TITLE: Ist Afghanistan sicher? Score 3.6/10 (2026)
findings.problem: English 'Score' in the title of all 63 scored pages in this batch (e.g. 'Score 6.4/10'). A German title would use 'Sicherheitswert' or just the number.
findings.expected: 'Ist Afghanistan sicher? Sicherheitswert 3.6/10 (2026)'.
findings.verification: opus: AFG.de and DEU.de titles read 'Ist X sicher? Score N/10 (2026)'. 'Score' is an accepted anglicism in German, but the rest of the page consistently says 'Sicherheitsbewertung', so the title is inconsistent with it. This is a style issue only.

findings.quote: und ist als hohe Vorsicht geboten eingestuft
findings.problem: 'als … eingestuft' needs a noun, but the template inserts the band phrase 'hohe Vorsicht geboten' bare (GIN, KHM, MOZ, MRT, NIC). Native phrasing would be 'und fällt in die Stufe „hohe Vorsicht geboten“'.
findings.expected: '…und fällt in die Stufe „hohe Vorsicht geboten“.'
findings.verification: opus: The template high_caution in src/lib/country-faq-copy.ts produces 'und ist als hohe Vorsicht geboten eingestuft' (e.g. GIN FAQ1). That is ungrammatical German, because 'als … eingestuft' needs a noun phrase. The other bands work because their labels are nouns ('als mittleres Risiko eingestuft').

findings.quote: statt geschätzt zu werden
findings.problem: Boilerplate (192 pages) says the value approaches a regional prior 'statt geschätzt zu werden' (instead of being estimated), but shrinkage is itself an estimate, so the phrase misdescribes the method. Boilerplate B8 also switches terms: 'einen Ort abdecken' versus 'ein Reiseziel abdecken' in HERO and SUMMARY.
findings.expected: '…nähert sich der Wert eines Landes einem vorsichtigen regionalen Richtwert an, wenn die Daten spärlich oder veraltet sind…'; in B8 'ein Reiseziel abdecken'.
findings.verification: opus: B3 'statt geschätzt zu werden' mistranslates the English source 'instead of guessing' (ui.ts methodology). In German it reads as 'instead of being estimated', which misdescribes shrinkage, itself an estimate. Better: 'statt auf Vermutungen zu beruhen'. The Ort/Reiseziel inconsistency in B8 is trivial.

findings.quote: Das Gesamtbild ist beruhigend: Die meisten Regierungen empfehlen für Pitcairninseln nur normale Vorsicht
findings.problem: 16 of the 18 grey pages (no score, 'Unvollständige Datenlage', 'Wir veröffentlichen eine Sicherheitsbewertung nur, wenn …') carry the same reassurance verdict: PCN (2 advisories), PRI (8), REU (5), VAT (6), SGS (1), among others. The batch gives no advisory levels for grey places, so the verdict has no stated basis and sits next to the page's own 'keine offizielle Sicherheitsbewertung'. On the three grey pages with a single advisory (SGS, SHN, SPM) the text says 'Die meisten Regierungen empfehlen' about one government. The zero-advisory page UMI gets a different, accurate sentence ('veröffentlicht keine Regierung … einen Reisehinweis'), so the template is inconsistent.
findings.expected: No 'beruhigend' verdict on grey pages. For one advisory, say that one government publishes an advisory and print its level; for none, use the UMI wording; for several, print the counts only.
findings.verification: opus: Only partly right. Grey pages do list advisory levels (PCN shows 2x Stufe 1), so the reassurance has a basis, and showing advisories on grey pages is accepted. What is real: with exactly one advisory (SGS, SHN, SPM, ALA, IMN, JEY...) the text still says 'Die meisten Regierungen empfehlen ... und keine stuft es ...' about a single government. Kept at low severity, as a count/wording template bug only.

findings.quote: Ist Nepal sicher? Score 6.8/10 (2026)
findings.problem: English 'Score' sits in the TITLE of all 64 scored pages (for example 'Ist Nepal sicher? Score 6.8/10 (2026)'). It is untranslated English in a German title and reads like machine output. DESCRIPTION and HERO on the same page do not use it.
findings.expected: 'Ist Nepal sicher? 6.8/10 (2026)' or 'Ist Nepal sicher? Sicherheitsbewertung 6.8/10 (2026)'.
findings.verification: opus: NPL.de TITLE reads 'Ist Nepal sicher? Score 6.8/10 (2026)'; the template in src/pages/de/land/[slug].astro:42 hardcodes the English 'Score' for every scored de page. 'Score' is an anglicism German readers will understand, but the DESCRIPTION uses 'Sicherheit 6.8/10', so this is inconsistent and reads as untranslated. It is a style problem.

findings.quote: Kostenloser Wert aus 30+ öffentlichen Quellen
findings.problem: Machine-style phrasing in the DESCRIPTION template (52 pages): 'Kostenloser Wert' (a native would write 'kostenlose Bewertung'). Boilerplate [B2] keeps the English term '(Bayesian Shrinkage)' inside German text; [B3] 'statt geschätzt zu werden' is unclear; [B14] 'allgemeine Friedfertigkeit (Global Peace Index)' is an odd rendering of peacefulness, and it recurs in many FAQ answers. The V-Dem label 'unparteiische öffentliche Verwaltung' (ROU, SVK) should read 'Unparteilichkeit der öffentlichen Verwaltung'. The GPI sentences tag '(GPI 2026)' inside the sentence, and pages mix comma decimals ('2,44', '4,1 von 10') with dot scores ('6.8/10').
findings.expected: 'Kostenlose Bewertung aus 30+ öffentlichen Quellen'; 'Bayes-Schrumpfung' or a German gloss; 'allgemeine Friedlichkeit'; 'Unparteilichkeit der öffentlichen Verwaltung'; cite the GPI edition in brackets after the sentence.
findings.verification: opus: The NPL DESCRIPTION has 'Kostenloser Wert aus 30+ öffentlichen Quellen, täglich neu berechnet'. 'Wert' (value) is unidiomatic here; 'kostenlose Bewertung' would be natural. Boilerplate B2 keeps the English '(Bayesian Shrinkage)', and 'Friedfertigkeit' is an odd rendering of peacefulness. All of these are style problems.

findings.quote: statistical detail. conflict (8.7/10) is Australia's strongest pillar
findings.problem: The thin-data boilerplate is glued in front of the pillar sentence, which then starts in lowercase. This happens in 53 FAQ answers (e.g. 'statistical detail. crime (5.0/10) is Afghanistan's strongest pillar' on AFG). The boilerplate is also inserted on pages with 100% data coverage (AUS, ALB, ARE, CAN), where it implies thin data that is not there.
findings.expected: Capitalise the pillar name after the sentence break, and show the thin-data sentence only when coverage is below full.
findings.verification: opus: The text 'statistical detail. crime (5.0/10) is Afghanistan's strongest pillar' appears on AFG and GAB, and the lowercase sentence start shows up across 166 en pages. The second claim is wrong: the thin-data sentence is general methodology and does not say this country has thin data.

findings.quote: has been issued by United States and United Kingdom, among others
findings.problem: The article is missing before 'United States', 'United Kingdom' and 'Netherlands' in 19 advisory answers (e.g. AFG 'issued by United States', BHR 'issued by Netherlands and Poland', DZA 'from United Kingdom and Austria'; also ATA, BHS, CHN, CRI, DOM, FRA 'comes from United States and Canada'). The possessives 'the United Arab Emirates's strongest pillar' (ARE) and 'the Bahamas's strongest pillar' (BHS) also read awkwardly.
findings.expected: 'the United States', 'the United Kingdom', 'the Netherlands'; prefer 'the UAE's' and 'the Bahamas''.
findings.verification: opus: AFG and BLR read 'has been issued by United States and United Kingdom, among others', and BHR reads 'issued by Netherlands and Poland'. The article 'the' is missing, which a native speaker notices at once. 'the Bahamas's' is acceptable English.

findings.quote: As of October 2026, the Aland Islands has one government travel advisory on record. The overall picture is reassuring: most governments advise only normal precautions for the Aland Islands
findings.problem: Partial-data pages (no score) still get a verdict. 'Most governments' is used when there is one government (ALA, and the same template on GGY 'has one government travel advisory' and ATF and BVT). Across 16 of the 20 partial pages the picture is called 'reassuring' although the same page says no safety score can be given.
findings.expected: No verdict wording on pages without a score; with one government say '1 government advises normal precautions'.
findings.verification: opus: ALA FAQ says 'has one government travel advisory on record. The overall picture is reassuring: most governments advise only normal precautions', so 'most governments' is used for a single advisory. On ABW (7 of 8 at normal precautions) 'reassuring' is accurate, so that part of the claim does not hold.

findings.quote: This pillar reflects violent crime, theft and organized criminal activity
findings.problem: Spelling is mixed: boilerplate [B8] uses American 'organized', the FAQ uses British 'militarisation' (BHR, BLR), and the COMPARISON HEADING uses 'neighbouring' (e.g. ABW), while 'travelers' is American.
findings.expected: One spelling convention (en-GB or en-US) across boilerplate and page text.
findings.verification: opus: The English pages mix spellings: 'organized' and 'travelers' (US) next to 'neighbouring' (ABW comparison heading) and 'militarisation' in our own sentence on BHR ('militarisation (Global Peace Index)'). Style-level.

findings.quote: COMMUNITY: Community Sentiment Community Not enough votes yet
findings.problem: The widget label repeats 'Community' on every page. CHN shows 'Community Sentiment Community Community rating 7.3/10' with a doubled word.
findings.expected: A single heading followed by the status text.
findings.verification: opus: In SentimentPillar.astro the H2 'Community Sentiment' is followed by a pill badge whose text is also 'Community' (sentiment.badge), and on active pages by the row label 'Community rating'. ABW and CHN show the redundant label. It is a UI pill rather than a literally doubled word, so low.

findings.quote: TITLE: Is the Cayman Islands Safe?
findings.problem: Plural place names take plural agreement. 'Is the Cayman Islands Safe?' should read 'Are the Cayman Islands safe?', and the Q3 answer 'the Cayman Islands has 8 government travel advisories' should use 'have'. The same verb error appears in COK ('the Cook Islands has 14'), FRO ('the Faroe Islands has 3'), FLK ('the Falkland Islands has 2'), ALA ('the Aland Islands has one') and BES ('Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba has 3').
findings.expected: 'Are the Cayman Islands safe?' and 'have' with these plural names, or rephrase so the verb is not needed.
findings.verification: opus: Verified in the CYM, COK and FRO TITLEs ('Is the Cayman Islands Safe?') and the Q3 texts ('the Cook Islands has 14', 'the Faroe Islands has 3'). Singular agreement is defensible for a political unit (as with the Netherlands or the Philippines), but 'Are the Cayman/Faroe Islands safe?' is the natural native phrasing and the usual search query. Low.

findings.quote: conflict (7.1/10) is Guinea's strongest pillar
findings.problem: On 58 full-score pages the FAQ 1 answer, after the boilerplate sentence ending 'full statistical detail.', starts a sentence with a lowercase pillar name ('conflict', 'health', 'crime' or 'natural hazards'). A native editor would flag each one as a fragment.
findings.expected: Capitalise the pillar name ('Conflict (7.1/10) is Guinea's strongest pillar, while ...') or join it to the preceding sentence.
findings.verification: opus: GIN FAQ1 has '...full statistical detail. conflict (7.1/10) is Guinea's strongest pillar'. The 'normal' template (country-faq-copy.ts:292) opens the sentence with {strongest}, a lowercase pillar label, so on many pages a sentence starts in lowercase. It is a visible grammar error but does not mislead.

findings.quote: rated as high caution and ranking 159th
findings.problem: The same band label is lowercase in SUMMARY and capitalised in FAQ on the same page ('rated as high caution' versus 'classified as High caution.'), and FAQ capitalises band names mid-sentence ('classified as Very low risk'). Spelling mixes UK and US conventions: 'organized criminal activity' (boilerplate B8) and 'traveling'/'travelers' sit beside 'neighbouring', and 'militarisation (Global Peace Index)' appears on ISR, JOR, KWT and LBY.
findings.expected: One convention: band names in lowercase running prose ('classified as very low risk'), and one spelling family throughout (UK: 'organised', 'travellers', 'militarisation'; or US throughout).
findings.verification: opus: GIN SUMMARY 'rated as high caution' versus FAQ 'classified as High caution' (also BDI, BLR, COG), and FAQ 'classified as Very low risk' mid-sentence. Spelling mix verified across en pages: US 'travelers' and 'traveling' (192 pages) and 'organized' (50) next to UK 'neighbouring' (239). 'Militarisation' is GPI's own indicator name and is acceptable, but the travelers/neighbouring mix is real.

findings.quote: COMMUNITY: Community Sentiment Community Not enough votes yet
findings.problem: The community block repeats its label ('Community Sentiment Community Not enough votes yet') on every full-score page. The related headings read 'Related Countries > In the same region' and 'Related Countries > Countries with a similar risk profile': the '>' separator and the repeated noun look like breadcrumb text leaking into headings.
findings.expected: One label ('Community sentiment'), and plain headings such as 'Countries in the same region' and 'Countries with a similar risk profile'.
findings.verification: opus: Only partly valid. The community block really renders an h2 'Community Sentiment' with a 'Community' badge next to it (SentimentPillar.astro, the sentiment.badge key), which is redundant. The 'Related Countries > In the same region' text is NOT on the page: the '>' is the audit extractor's h2 > h3 notation (extract-page-facts.ts line 132), so that half of the finding is rejected.

findings.quote: the United States's strongest pillar
findings.problem: Possessives with country names are awkward and inconsistent: 'the Philippines's strongest pillar' (PHL), 'the Solomon Islands's' (SLB), 'the Seychelles's' (SYC), 'Saint Vincent and the Grenadines's' (VCT). The construction reads awkwardly.
findings.expected: 'the strongest pillar in the United States' or a rewritten sentence that avoids the possessive.
findings.verification: opus: Found 'the United States's strongest pillar' (USA), 'the Philippines's' (PHL), 'the Solomon Islands's' (SLB) and 'Grenadines's' (VCT). Standard English uses a bare apostrophe for plural-form names (the United States', the Philippines'). This is a style issue.

findings.quote: organized criminal activity
findings.problem: Mixed spelling in the en text: US 'organized' (B8), 'travelers' (community text) and 'militarisation' (GPI sentences), against UK 'neighbouring' in the COMPARISON HEADING on most pages.
findings.expected: Use one English variety throughout. The majority of the text is US ('travelers', 'organized'), so 'neighboring' and 'militarization' would match.
findings.verification: opus: Across en pages: 'neighbouring' on 239 and 'militarisation' on 162 (UK spelling), against 'travelers' on 192 and 'organized' on 50 (US spelling). There are no pages with the opposite variants, so the mix is systematic. Style only.

findings.quote: Is It Safe to Travel to Reunion Right Now?
findings.problem: English names drop diacritics: 'Reunion' (should be Réunion; the REU H1, and its grey table row 'Reunion | Partial data'), 'Sao Tome and Principe' (the STP H1, and the 'Sao Tome and Principe 6.8' entry in ZMB's related list; should be São Tomé and Príncipe), and 'Cote d'Ivoire 6.4' in SLE's related list (should be Côte d'Ivoire). Only 'Aland Islands' is an accepted name issue.
findings.expected: Use the standard English names with diacritics in the name source, then regenerate the pages and related lists.
findings.verification: opus: The REU H1 reads 'Reunion' and SLE's related list has 'Cote d'Ivoire'; standard English (ISO 3166) is 'Réunion' and 'Côte d'Ivoire'. The STP part is wrong: 'Sao Tome and Principe' without accents is the official UN/ISO English short name. Style only.

findings.quote: on a scale from 1 (most peaceful) to 5 (GPI 2026)
findings.problem: The source tag '(GPI 2026)' follows the top of the scale, so the sentence reads as if '5' were a GPI 2026 label. This recurs in every SUMMARY that quotes the Global Peace Index (AFG, ARG, BDI, BGD, BHR, BLR).
findings.expected: Attribute the source after the score, for example 'The Global Peace Index (GPI 2026) scores the country 3.11, on a scale from 1 (most peaceful) to 5.'
findings.verification: opus: AFG, BDI, BHR and BLR all have '...on a scale from 1 (most peaceful) to 5 (GPI 2026)'. The source tag sits where the label of the scale's upper end would go, so '5' reads as if it were labelled 'GPI 2026'. The meaning is still clear, so this is low severity.

findings.quote: on a scale from 1 (safest) to 5 (GPI 2026)
findings.problem: The GPI sentence attaches the source year to the top of the scale, so 'on a scale from 1 (safest) to 5 (GPI 2026)' reads as if 5 were GPI 2026. The scale label also varies: GUY and KGZ say '1 (safest)', while ISR, JOR, KEN, KWT and IRQ say '1 (most peaceful)'. Seven pages use this sentence.
findings.expected: Write the GPI value with its source and one scale label on every page, e.g. 'GPI 2026: 2.70, on a scale from 1 (most peaceful) to 5 (least peaceful)'.
findings.verification: opus: GUY reads 'rates safety and security at 2.70 on a scale from 1 (safest) to 5 (GPI 2026)'. The source parenthesis sits where a scale-end label belongs, so it reads as if 5 meant 'GPI 2026'. The 'safest' vs 'most peaceful' wording is not a problem: it is correct per indicator (safety and security vs overall).

findings.quote: on a scale from 1 (safest) to 5 (GPI 2026)
findings.problem: On 7 pages (RWA, SAU, SEN, SLV, SSD, SWZ, TCD) the source tag '(GPI 2026)' sits inside the scale description, so the 5 at the end of the range reads as if it were labelled 'GPI 2026'. The source belongs after the sentence.
findings.expected: Keep the scale as 'on a scale from 1 (safest) to 5' and put the source at the end of the sentence.
findings.verification: opus: The batch contains 'on a scale from 1 (safest) to 5 (GPI 2026)' (RWA, SEN, SLV, SWZ) and 'from 1 (most peaceful) to 5 (GPI 2026)' (SAU, SSD, TCD). The source tag reads as the label of the scale's endpoint.

findings.quote: ¿Es seguro viajar a Benin? 6.1/10 (2026)
findings.problem: English spellings in Spanish text: 'Benin' (BEN, 16 occurrences incl. TITLE/H1/DESCRIPTION) should be 'Benín'; 'Brunei' (BRN, 16) should be 'Brunéi'; 'Islas Aland' (ALA, 11) should be 'Islas Åland'. The Åland item is the Spanish name, not the already-accepted English 'Aland Islands'. COG's TITLE 'Congo' is ambiguous next to COD's 'República Democrática del Congo'; use 'República del Congo'.
findings.expected: Spanish country names with diacritics, and an unambiguous name for the Republic of the Congo.
findings.verification: opus: BEN.es TITLE/DESCRIPTION use 'Benin' (14 times, never 'Benín') and BRN.es uses 'Brunei'. RAE/Fundéu forms are 'Benín' and 'Brunéi', and 'Islas Åland' is the ISO Spanish form. The Congo part does not hold: 'Congo' is the standard Spanish (UN/RAE) short name for COG and is not a defect.

findings.quote: También merece atención criminalidad, con 4.5/10.
findings.problem: Pillar names used as bare nouns where Spanish normally takes an article: B6 'Su pilar más fuerte es conflicto', B17 'Su pilar más fuerte es salud', B22 'También merece atención gobernanza', BFA 'También merece atención criminalidad', BHS 'La señal principal detrás de esto es tasa de homicidios'. 'Señal' for indicator is a calque, and 'Las señales con la puntuación más baja' reads as machine translation.
findings.expected: Add the article ('es el conflicto', 'merece atención la gobernanza') and use 'indicador' instead of 'señal'.
findings.verification: opus: BFA has 'También merece atención criminalidad, con 4.5/10' and BHS has 'La señal principal detrás de esto es tasa de homicidios'. Templates B6, B17, B18 and B22 drop the article that Spanish requires for these postverbal subjects or predicates ('la criminalidad', 'la tasa de homicidios', 'el conflicto'). The text reads ungrammatical or machine-made. 'señal' for indicator is a minor calque.

findings.quote: con corrección por incertidumbre (Bayesian shrinkage)
findings.problem: English term left in the Spanish formula sentence that opens the FAQ on 192 pages (source: src/lib/country-faq-copy.ts:405). The rest of the sentence is translated.
findings.expected: A Spanish gloss, e.g. '(encogimiento bayesiano)', or drop the parenthesis.
findings.verification: opus: 'con corrección por incertidumbre (Bayesian shrinkage)' appears in the es FAQ A1 (HTI, LUX, IDN). The English term is left untranslated inside an otherwise Spanish sentence.

findings.quote: la puntuación global de Haití se empuja marcadamente hacia el extremo bajo
findings.problem: Calque of English 'pushes the score toward the low end'. A native would write 'la baja mucho' or 'la sitúa muy cerca del mínimo'. The same sentence also explains a methodology effect ('Estas advertencias son lo bastante graves como para pesar mucho en nuestro índice') inside a traveller FAQ. Seen on HTI, IRN, IRQ, LBN, LBY, MLI, MMR and NER.
findings.expected: Plain Spanish ('la baja mucho'); move the methodology explanation to the methodology page.
findings.verification: opus: HTI A3 contains 'la puntuación global de Haití se empuja marcadamente hacia el extremo bajo'. That is an awkward calque, though still understandable. The methodology aside itself is accepted boilerplate, so only the phrasing counts.

findings.quote: La principal preocupación en Haití es conflicto, con 3.2/10.
findings.problem: Pillar names are used bare after 'es' in FAQ answers ('es conflicto', 'es salud', 'es criminalidad', 'es riesgos naturales'), which reads like a label. A native would write 'es el conflicto' or 'es la salud'. The SUMMARY uses 'la de conflictos', so the surfaces differ. Seen on HTI and GRC ('El pilar más fuerte de Grecia es conflicto (8.3/10)').
findings.expected: Add the article in the es pillar-name forms used in predicate position.
findings.verification: opus: HTI reads 'La principal preocupación en Haití es conflicto, con 3.2/10' and GRC reads 'El pilar más fuerte de Grecia es conflicto (8.3/10)'. A native speaker would put the article in ('es el conflicto'), so the bare noun reads like a label.

findings.quote: (Bayesian shrinkage)
findings.problem: Methodology sentence B1, shown on 192 pages, keeps English '(Bayesian shrinkage)' inside Spanish text. B3's 'consenso calibrado' is a literal calque of 'calibrated consensus'. Both read as machine translation.
findings.expected: 'con ajuste bayesiano por incertidumbre' (or drop the parenthesis), and 'un consenso ajustado de los avisos de viaje gubernamentales' in B3.
findings.verification: opus: B1 (192 pages) does read 'con corrección por incertidumbre (Bayesian shrinkage)', an untranslated English term inside Spanish text. 'consenso calibrado' in B3 is understandable Spanish and only a weak point.

findings.quote: Las señales con la puntuación más baja en este ámbito son muertes por conflicto (UCDP) y paz general (Global Peace Index).
findings.problem: 'señal(es)' used for indicators appears about 25 times ('La señal principal detrás de esto es...', 'Las señales con la puntuación más baja...'), a calque of English 'signals'. 'Global Peace Index' stays in English in about 43 places, where Spanish text normally says 'Índice Global de Paz (GPI)'. Some sentences repeat the same source twice ('paz general (Global Peace Index) y militarización (Global Peace Index)').
findings.expected: 'Los indicadores con peor puntuación en este ámbito son...', and 'Índice Global de Paz (GPI)' at first mention.
findings.verification: opus: The B13/B16/B18/B19/B21 templates use 'señal(es)' for indicators, a calque of 'signals'. 11 pages say 'paz general (Global Peace Index) y militarización (Global Peace Index)', naming the same source twice in English. The text is readable, but it reads as machine-made, which is the blogger's complaint.

findings.quote: la puntuación global de Rusia se empuja marcadamente hacia el extremo bajo
findings.problem: On 9 very-low pages (PRK, PSE, RUS, SDN, SOM, SSD, SYR, UKR, YEM) the advisory paragraph says 'Estas advertencias son lo bastante graves como para pesar mucho en nuestro índice' and 'se empuja marcadamente hacia el extremo bajo'. Both are literal translations, the second is hard to read, and 'nuestro índice' is meta language inside a traveller answer.
findings.expected: 'la puntuación global de Rusia baja de forma notable, además de lo que ya indiquen sus otros pilares'.
findings.verification: opus: Checked RUS and SYR: both have 'la puntuación global de Rusia/Siria se empuja marcadamente hacia el extremo bajo', an awkward literal calque in the FAQ answer, along with the meta phrase 'pesar mucho en nuestro índice'.

findings.quote: Sentimiento de la comunidad Comunidad Aún no hay suficientes votos
findings.problem: Every page's community block reads 'Sentimiento de la comunidad Comunidad', with the same word twice in a row, which reads as a duplicated heading.
findings.expected: Drop the second 'Comunidad', or make the badge a label that does not repeat the heading.
findings.verification: opus: All 248 es pages show 'Sentimiento de la comunidad Comunidad': the heading is followed by a badge with the same word. It is visually redundant, a UI label issue only.

findings.quote: Su pilar más fuerte es conflicto, con #/#.
findings.problem: Boilerplate B6 and B22 ('También merece atención gobernanza, con #/#.') use pillar names as bare nouns with no article, a telegraphic label style. The FAQ repeats it ('El pilar más fuerte de X es conflicto (7.5/10)').
findings.expected: 'Su pilar más fuerte es el de conflicto' and 'También merece atención la gobernanza'.
findings.verification: opus: The B6/B17/B20/B22 templates use bare pillar nouns ('Su pilar más fuerte es conflicto, con', 'También merece atención gobernanza'). Spanish needs an article here ('el de conflicto', 'la gobernanza'), and the wording also clashes with B1's 'conflictos'.

findings.quote: (Bayesian shrinkage)
findings.problem: English term left untranslated in the French methodology sentence [B1], which the batch header says appears on 192 pages: 'corrigée pour l'incertitude (Bayesian shrinkage)'.
findings.expected: 'corrigée pour l'incertitude (lissage bayésien)', or gloss the English term once in French.
findings.verification: opus: [B1] on 192 fr pages leaves the English term '(Bayesian shrinkage)' untranslated, as the it and es a1Formula do. The methodology text itself is accepted; this is only a missing translation.

findings.quote: le Global Peace Index attribue au pays la note de 3,11 sur une échelle de 1 (le plus pacifique) à 5 (GPI 2026)
findings.problem: The top of the scale has no description, and the parenthesis '(GPI 2026)' is attached to the 5, so it reads as if 5 were the GPI 2026 value. The same shape appears in BHR, BRA, BGD and many other SUMMARY lines.
findings.expected: 'sur une échelle de 1 (le plus pacifique) à 5 (le moins pacifique), selon le Global Peace Index 2026'.
findings.verification: opus: The AFG, BDI and BHR SUMMARY lines read 'sur une échelle de 1 (le plus pacifique) à 5 (GPI 2026)'. The upper end has no description, and '(GPI 2026)' looks like a gloss on 5. ARG and COG use the same shape ('1 (la plus sûre) à 5 (GPI 2026)'). It is ambiguous rather than false.

findings.quote: (Bayesian shrinkage)
findings.problem: B1 leaves English inside the French methodology sentence. B4 'un consensus calibré des avis de voyage gouvernementaux' reads as a literal translation of 'calibrated consensus'. B7 'Restez attentif aux risques spécifiques détaillés plus bas.' is generic filler on 64 pages that names no risk. Low severity: these are methodology lines and filler, not safety claims.
findings.expected: A French term (for example 'pondération bayésienne'); 'un consensus pondéré des avis de voyage gouvernementaux'; B7 replaced by a concrete pointer to the lowest-weighted pillar or the main advisory.
findings.verification: opus: B1 on 192 fr pages contains the English '(Bayesian shrinkage)' in a French sentence, and B7 is generic filler that names no risk. 'consensus calibré' is acceptable French, so that part is rejected. Low severity, since this is methodology and filler text.

findings.quote: Voyager au Nepal : est-ce sûr ? 6.8/10 (2026)
findings.problem: Minor French spelling/terminology. 'Nepal' is the English form; French is 'Népal' (NPL TITLE, H1, FAQ). The boilerplate B1 also keeps the English '(Bayesian shrinkage)' and B14 says 'morts liées aux conflits (UCDP)' where 'décès liés aux conflits' is the natural term.
findings.expected: 'Voyager au Népal' ; 'Népal : est-ce sûr...' ; 'décès liés aux conflits' ; replace '(Bayesian shrinkage)' with a French term such as '(réduction bayésienne)'.
findings.verification: opus: Verified that the French NPL TITLE, H1, SUMMARY and FAQ use the English 'Nepal' instead of 'Népal'. The boilerplate B1 keeps the English '(Bayesian shrinkage)' in French text. 'morts liées aux conflits' is acceptable French, so that part is only a preference. The country-name error is in TITLE/H1 but minor.

findings.quote: per Germania e nessuno lo colloca oltre un avviso di basso livello.
findings.problem: The masculine pronoun 'lo' is used for feminine country names: Germania should be 'la colloca'. Same on ESP ('per Spagna e nessuno lo colloca'), CHE ('per Svizzera'), CZE ('per Repubblica Ceca'), DNK ('per Danimarca'), FIN ('per Finlandia'), EST ('per Estonia'), BIH ('per Bosnia ed Erzegovina') and GIB ('per Gibilterra'). At least nine pages.
findings.expected: Pronoun agrees with the gender of the country name ('la' for feminine names).
findings.verification: opus: Found 'per Germania e nessuno lo colloca' and the same on ESP, CHE, CZE, DNK, FIN, EST and GIB. The masculine 'lo' does not agree with the feminine names. It overlaps with the missing-article problem in #9, so low.

findings.quote: il suo contributo allo score complessivo è ridotto o escluso
findings.problem: Untranslated English 'score' in an Italian footnote, on 8 pages (ATG, BHS, BLZ, BRN twice, COM, CPV, DMA, FSM twice).
findings.expected: 'punteggio complessivo'.
findings.verification: opus: The footnote 'il suo contributo allo score complessivo è ridotto o escluso' appears on ATG, BHS, BLZ, BRN (x2), COM, CPV, DMA and FSM (x2). Everywhere else the it copy uses 'punteggio', so the English 'score' is inconsistent. It is a style-level anglicism.

findings.quote: il Global Peace Index assegna al paese 3,11 su una scala da 1 (massima pace) a 5 (GPI 2026)
findings.problem: The edition label sits after the scale's end point, so it reads as if the scale ends at 'GPI 2026'. Same wording in every GPI-based SUMMARY (e.g. ARG, BGD, BDI, CUB).
findings.expected: Put the source and scale apart, e.g. '... su una scala da 1 (massima pace) a 5 (indice GPI 2026)'.
findings.verification: opus: Every GPI summary reads 'su una scala da 1 (massima pace) a 5 (GPI 2026)' (AFG, BHR, BRA, ...). The parallel parentheses make '(GPI 2026)' read as the label for endpoint 5, and the actual label for 5 (least peaceful) is missing. This is a minor wording ambiguity.

findings.quote: il suo contributo allo score complessivo è ridotto o escluso
findings.problem: English 'score' sits in the asterisk footnote on pages with low-coverage pillars (KIR, MHL, MDV, KNA, LCA, LIE). The formula boilerplate keeps '(Bayesian shrinkage)' in English as well.
findings.expected: Use 'punteggio complessivo' in the footnote, and an Italian gloss such as 'stima bayesiana' in the boilerplate.
findings.verification: opus: KIR.it has 'il suo contributo allo score complessivo è ridotto o escluso', while every other place on the site says 'punteggio'. This is an inconsistent anglicism. '(Bayesian shrinkage)' as a technical term in parentheses is acceptable. Style only.

findings.quote: Sentiment della community Community Non ci sono ancora abbastanza voti
findings.problem: The heading and the label both say 'community' on every page. Related slips: 'Il punto più debole è la debolezza della governance' (HUN, MNE, MDV) and 'la più bassa riguarda la debolezza della governance' (MLT) repeat the same word; 'Saint Kitts e Nevis e nessuno lo colloca' (KNA) stacks two 'e'.
findings.expected: Drop the duplicate label. Write 'Il punto più debole è la governance'. Split the KNA sentence with a comma or a new clause.
findings.verification: opus: 'Sentiment della community Community' (heading plus badge), 'Il punto più debole è la debolezza della governance' (HUN) and 'Saint Kitts e Nevis e nessuno lo colloca' (KNA) are all on the pages. These are minor style slips. A worse one in the same template went unreported: 'nessuno lo colloca' is fixed in the masculine, so feminine countries read wrongly (Croazia, Ungheria, Malta should take 'la').

findings.quote: Il rischio principale è lo scarso accesso alle cure mediche: 8,1 su 10
findings.problem: The sentence mixes an Italian decimal comma (INFORM '8,1 su 10') with dot-decimal scores ('5.7/10'). The COMMUNITY text uses '±1,0 punti'. Large counts drop the thousands separator while '100.000' keeps it: '2428 persone uccise' (HTI), '1243 persone' (IRN), '2615 persone' (NGA). The DESCRIPTION also writes the pillar as '(4.2)' with no '/10', unlike every other score. The dot convention for scores is accepted; these other numbers are inconsistent with it.
findings.expected: One Italian convention within a sentence and across the page: 2.428 / 1.243 / 2.615 for counts, and a single decimal symbol for the page's numbers.
findings.verification: opus: Counts drop the Italian thousands separator ('2428 persone uccise' HTI, '1243 persone' IRN) while '100.000 abitanti' keeps it on the same page. The decimal comma in INFORM values next to dot-decimal scores follows from the accepted dot convention, so only the thousands separators are a real defect.

findings.quote: il suo contributo allo score complessivo è ridotto o escluso
findings.problem: The asterisk footnote on 11 pages (e.g. NRU, PLW, TUV, WSM, VUT, TWN, PSE) uses the English noun 'score' inside an Italian sentence.
findings.expected: 'il suo contributo al punteggio complessivo è ridotto o escluso'.
findings.verification: opus: ui.ts it 'country.pillar_low_coverage_note' reads 'il suo contributo allo score complessivo è ridotto o escluso' (seen on NRU and TWN). Every other Italian string uses 'punteggio', so the anglicism is inconsistent. This is a style issue only.

findings.quote: Il punto più debole è la debolezza della governance
findings.problem: ROU repeats 'debolezza' in one clause ('Il punto più debole è la debolezza della governance'); POL and PRT say the same with 'la più bassa riguarda la debolezza della governance'.
findings.expected: 'Il punto più debole è la governance'.
findings.verification: opus: ROU.it, HUN.it, MNE.it and MDV.it all contain 'Il punto più debole è la debolezza della governance', a redundant debole/debolezza repetition. 'la più bassa riguarda la debolezza della governance' (POL, PRT) is acceptable Italian, so only the 'punto più debole' variant needs a different noun phrase.

findings.quote: Sim, mas apenas com cautela real — Burundi apresenta um risco considerável
findings.problem: 'cautela real' is an unnatural literal rendering of an English phrase. The same wording appears on BDI, BLR, CMR, COG, COL, ECU, ERI and ETH.
findings.expected: 'Sim, mas só com muita cautela' or similar wording a native would use.
findings.verification: opus: 'Sim, mas apenas com cautela real' appears on 15 pt pages (e.g. BDI, ECU, ETH). It is an awkward calque of 'real caution'; a native would write 'com muita cautela' or 'com bastante cautela'. Understandable, but it reads as machine-translated.

findings.quote: Sentimento da comunidade Comunidade
findings.problem: Every page's community block repeats the word: the heading 'Sentimento da comunidade' is followed by the card label 'Comunidade'.
findings.expected: Keep one label (the heading alone, or the card label alone).
findings.verification: opus: All 248 pt pages contain 'Sentimento da comunidade Comunidade'. SentimentPillar.astro renders the h2 'country.pillar.sentiment' next to a visible pill badge 'sentiment.badge' ('Comunidade'), so the word visibly repeats. The same pattern exists in the other locales.

findings.quote: por isso não conta entre as quatro
findings.problem: On GUM, MNP and NCL the HERO source list says a disaster feed 'não conta entre as quatro'. 'As quatro' refers to the four-source threshold stated elsewhere, so it is unclear to a traveller.
findings.expected: Rephrase, e.g. '(só aparece durante um desastre em curso e não entra na contagem das quatro fontes)', with the threshold explained once.
findings.verification: opus: GUM.pt HERO lists 'alertas de desastres do GDACS (apenas enquanto há um desastre em curso, por isso não conta entre as quatro)'. The earlier 'pelo menos quatro fontes' gives the reference, but 'não conta entre as quatro' is elliptical and odd when the place has fewer than four sources. 'não entra na contagem das quatro fontes' would be clear. Minor wording.

findings.quote: a pontuação geral de Sudão é fortemente puxada para o lado mais baixo
findings.problem: One methodology sentence repeats on 9 pages (e.g. SDN, SOM; also PRK, PSE, RUS, SSD, SYR, UKR, YEM): 'Esses alertas são graves o suficiente para pesar fortemente em nosso índice: quando a maioria dos governos emite um aviso de não viajar, a pontuação geral de X é fortemente puxada para o lado mais baixo, além do que já indicam seus outros pilares.' It reads as machine translation ('pesar fortemente', 'o lado mais baixo') and drops the article ('de Sudão').
findings.expected: Plain pt, e.g. 'Quando a maioria dos governos desaconselha a viagem, a pontuação geral fica bem abaixo do que indicam os pilares sozinhos', with the article ('do Sudão').
findings.verification: opus: The a3Cap template in src/lib/country-faq-copy.ts uses {name} instead of the article-aware form. This produces 'a pontuação geral de Sudão/Afeganistão/Iêmen/Irã/Iraque/Haiti/Mali/Níger...' on 21 pt pages, where pt needs 'do Sudão', 'do Afeganistão' and so on. The 'machine translation' wording complaint is weaker, but the missing article is a real grammar error.

findings.quote: o Global Peace Index avalia a segurança e proteção em 2,44 em uma escala de 1 (mais seguro) a 5 (GPI 2026)
findings.problem: Template sentence on about 21 pages (e.g. NPL, PAN, SEN). 'avalia … em 2,44' is a calque, and the source tag '(GPI 2026)' sits after the scale's maximum '5', so it reads as part of the scale. Its variant 'dá ao país … em uma escala de 1 (mais pacífico) a 5 (GPI 2026)' appears on 7 more pages.
findings.expected: 'o Global Peace Index dá ao país 2,44 numa escala de 1 (mais seguro) a 5 (fonte: GPI 2026)'.
findings.verification: opus: NPL.pt summary reads 'o Global Peace Index avalia a segurança e proteção em 2,44 em uma escala de 1 (mais seguro) a 5 (GPI 2026)', on 32 pt pages. The scale's upper end has no label, so '(GPI 2026)' reads as the label of 5. 'Avalia … em' is acceptable pt, so the issue is the misplaced source tag.

findings.quote: 这还是在其他支柱已有表现的基础之上。
findings.problem: A calque of an English clause ('on top of what the other pillars already show'), unreadable in Chinese. The clause before it, '这些警告严重到足以在我们的指数中占据很大权重', is also machine-style. Found on AFG, BFA, BLR and CAF (avoid-all pages). Cause: zh a3Cap in src/lib/country-faq-copy.ts (about line 600).
findings.expected: e.g. '当多数政府发布切勿前往的警告时，总分会被进一步下调，下调幅度随警告数量增加。'
findings.verification: opus: zh a3Cap ('…这还是在其他支柱已有表现的基础之上。') is a literal calque of 'on top of whatever its other pillars show'. It is awkward and unclear to a native reader. It appears on 21 zh pages (AFG among them).

findings.quote: 当某个支柱的数据覆盖率较低时,其对总体评分的贡献会被减少或排除.
findings.problem: ASCII comma and full stop inside Chinese text, plus an inline '*' after the pillar value (src/i18n/ui.ts key country.pillar_low_coverage_note). Seen on ATG, BHS, BLZ, BRN, COM, CPV, DMA and FSM.
findings.expected: Full-width punctuation, shown as a footnote under the bars rather than inline.
findings.verification: opus: The ATG PILLAR BARS show '治理 5.7/10 * 当某个支柱的数据覆盖率较低时,其对总体评分的贡献会被减少或排除.', with an ASCII comma and full stop inside Chinese text. It comes from a single i18n template.

findings.quote: 风险等级为风险极低
findings.problem: Doubles 风险 ('risk level is risk, very low'). Appears on 15 pages (AUS, AUT, BEL, BGR, CAN, CHE, CYP, CZE, DEU, DNK, ESP, EST, FIN, FRA, GBR).
findings.expected: 风险等级为极低, or the band label on its own.
findings.verification: opus: DEU's SUMMARY has '风险等级为风险极低', which repeats 风险 awkwardly. It is on about 38 zh pages in the excellent band and comes from the band label being inserted into 风险等级为{band}.

findings.quote: 其得分为 8.5/10
findings.problem: A stray space between 为 and the number, on about 24 pages. The other FAQ verdict variants have no space ('其在我们的安全指数中得分为{score}/10'), so spacing is inconsistent. Source: src/lib/country-faq-copy.ts zh a1Verdict.excellent.
findings.expected: 其得分为8.5/10 with no space, matching the other variants.
findings.verification: opus: DEU's FAQ has '其得分为 8.5/10' (with a space) while other variants on other pages have '得分为6.4/10' (no space). The spacing is inconsistent across templates (B6 also uses a space), so this is purely typographic.

findings.quote: 这些警告严重到足以在我们的指数中占据很大权重：当多数政府发布切勿前往的警告时，海地的总分会被明显拉低，这还是在其他支柱已有表现的基础之上。
findings.problem: A machine-like paragraph in FAQ 3 of the 8 pages where most governments advise avoiding all travel (HTI, IRN, IRQ, LBN, LBY, MLI, MMR, NER). Phrases such as 严重到足以…占据很大权重 and 这还是在其他支柱已有表现的基础之上 are not idiomatic, and the paragraph explains the score mechanism rather than the advice.
findings.expected: One plain sentence, e.g. 多数政府建议避免前往，这一结论已计入评分并拉低了总分; or remove it.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is in HTI FAQ 3, and the same template text appears on 21 zh pages (AFG, HTI, IRN, SYR, YEM...), not 8. 严重到足以…占据很大权重 and 这还是在其他支柱已有表现的基础之上 are translationese and the second clause is unclear to a native reader. The meaning is still recoverable, so this is a wording problem, not misleading content.

findings.quote: 目前最严厉的警告——提高警惕——来自美国和加拿大。
findings.problem: On 7 pages (IDN, KGZ, LKA, MDV, MYS; grey HKG, NCL) the strictest warning is the same level as the mainstream advice. IDN says 主流建议是前往印度尼西亚时提高警惕 (19 of 21 governments) and then 目前最严厉的警告——提高警惕. A superlative that names the majority level tells the reader nothing and reads as a contradiction.
findings.expected: Say the highest level issued is 提高警惕, or name the tier that is actually strictest; drop the superlative when it equals the majority level.
findings.verification: opus: IDN and KGZ FAQ 3 both say 主流建议是…提高警惕；目前最严厉的警告——提高警惕——来自…. Calling the majority level the 'strictest' is redundant and reads oddly. It is not misleading, because no stricter tier was issued.

findings.quote: 最薄弱的方面是治理薄弱
findings.problem: 薄弱 is used twice in one clause on HUN, MNE and MDV (最薄弱的方面是治理薄弱), and MLT has 其中评分最低的是治理薄弱. The word names the subject and then repeats it as its property.
findings.expected: 最薄弱的方面是治理 (or 治理方面最薄弱).
findings.verification: opus: HUN and MNE SUMMARY have 最薄弱的方面是治理薄弱, and MLT has 其中评分最低的是治理薄弱. Inserting the negative label '治理薄弱' into the 'weakest aspect is X' frame duplicates 薄弱 and reads as a machine join.

findings.quote: 各国政府的旅行警告对 几内亚 有何评价？
findings.problem: Template-wide on all 83 pages: FAQ 3 puts spaces around the place name (对 几内亚 有何评价), FAQ 1 writes 2026 年 with a space while SUMMARY writes 2026年, and running text uses 30+个 with a plus sign.
findings.expected: Remove the inserted spaces, write 2026年 everywhere, and write 30多个 or the exact count.
findings.verification: opus: GIN FAQ has 各国政府的旅行警告对 几内亚 有何评价？ with spaces around the name (template-wide). FAQ question 2026 年前往… has a space while SUMMARY writes 2026年. 30+个 is informal but common, so it is minor. All of these are spacing and typography only.

findings.quote: 多数政府对南乔治亚和南桑威奇群岛仅建议采取正常预防措施
findings.problem: The FAQ on 16 unscored pages (PCN, PRI, PYF, REU, SGS, SHN, SJM, SMR, SPM, SXM, TCA, TKL, VAT, VGB, VIR, WLF) gives a reassurance verdict (总体情况令人安心) about advisories, although the page gives no safety score. SGS, SHN and SPM each report exactly one advisory, yet say 多数政府 (most governments), which cannot describe one government.
findings.expected: On unscored pages, drop the reassurance sentence. For a single advisory, state that single level instead of using 多数政府.
findings.verification: opus: SGS, SHN and SPM each list one advisory (Poland, level 1) but say 多数政府…仅建议采取正常预防措施. 'Most governments' cannot describe a single government. Calling the advisories reassuring on an unscored page is accurate, since the only advisory is level 1, so only the count wording is wrong.

findings.quote: 风险等级为风险极低
findings.problem: Doubled 风险 on 8 pages (NZL, POL, PRT, SGP, SVK, SVN, SWE, ROU): 风险等级为风险极低.
findings.expected: 风险等级为极低, or 属于风险极低等级.
findings.verification: opus: The SUMMARY template produces 风险等级为风险极低 on 39 zh pages (for example NZL, SVK). On 15 more pages it produces 风险等级为高度谨慎, a band name rather than a risk level. Both are awkward template output.

findings.quote: 当某个支柱的数据覆盖率较低时,其对总体评分的贡献会被减少或排除.
findings.problem: The coverage footnote on 11 pages (NRU, PLW, PSE, SLB, STP, TON, TUV, TWN, VCT, VUT, WSM) uses ASCII comma and full stop inside Chinese text and sits inside the pillar list. Question headings also have stray spaces, for example 各国政府的旅行警告对 尼泊尔 有何评价？ and 2026 年前往….
findings.expected: Use full-width ，and 。 with no spaces, and put the footnote on its own line below the bars.
findings.verification: opus: The coverage footnote uses an ASCII comma and full stop on 26 zh pages (for example TWN). FAQ headings put spaces around Chinese names (对 尼泊尔 有何评价). Typography only.

findings.quote: 请在出行前查阅你所在国家政府的最新指引。
findings.problem: Uses 你 where the rest of the site uses 您 (e.g. '投出您的一票' on the same page). CXR shares the same template. The sentence before it, '这在面积很小或偏远的地区很常见', is an unsourced generalization that says nothing specific about Cocos Islands.
findings.expected: '请在出行前查阅您所在国家政府的最新指引。' and drop or source the generalization.
findings.verification: opus: CCK's FAQ has '请在出行前查阅你所在国家政府的最新指引。' while the same page uses 您 elsewhere (投出您的一票, 您去过…). The same template is on CXR, NFK and UMI. The 'small or remote places' remark is a reasonable explanation, not a defect, so only the 你/您 inconsistency stands.

findings.quote: Voyager au Congo : est-ce sûr ? 5.6/10 (2026)
findings.problem: 'Congo' alone is ambiguous in French: it could mean the Republic of the Congo (this page) or the DR Congo, which has its own page 'Voyager en République démocratique du Congo'. The H1 ('Congo : est-ce sûr…') and the FAQ repeat the short name.
findings.expected: 'Voyager en République du Congo : est-ce sûr ? 5.6/10 (2026)' in TITLE, H1 and FAQ.
findings.verification: opus: The COG TITLE, H1 and SUMMARY say 'Congo' / 'au Congo'. 'Congo' is the official ISO short name, and the DRC page says 'République démocratique du Congo' in full, so the text is not wrong. Still, the two scores differ a lot (5.6 vs 3.8), so 'République du Congo' (or 'Congo-Brazzaville') would avoid confusion in a safety context.

findings.quote: É seguro viajar para as Ilhas Faroe? Dados parciais (2026)
findings.problem: 'Faroe' is the English spelling; the usual Portuguese form is Feroé (with accent). It is used in TITLE, H1, DESCRIPTION, HERO, COMMUNITY and FAQ.
findings.expected: 'Ilhas Feroé' throughout.
findings.verification: opus: FRO.pt uses 'Ilhas Faroe' (10 times). That is the English spelling; standard Portuguese is 'Ilhas Feroé', with 'Faroé' as a variant. Minor localisation issue.

findings.quote: em 2,70 em uma escala de 1 (mais seguro) a 5 (GPI 2026)
findings.problem: The source tag '(GPI 2026)' follows the scale's end-point '5' and reads as part of the scale. The figure uses a decimal comma ('2,70') while the scores on the same page use a dot.
findings.expected: Put the source tag after the value, e.g. '2,70 (GPI 2026), em que 1 = mais seguro e 5 = menos seguro'.
findings.verification: opus: GUY.pt SUMMARY: 'avalia a segurança e proteção em 2,70 em uma escala de 1 (mais seguro) a 5 (GPI 2026)'. '(GPI 2026)' attaches to the end-point 5, and that end is not labelled 'menos seguro'. The decimal comma on an indicator value is correct pt formatting and not a defect (only scores use the accepted dot). This is a template issue, not specific to GUY.

findings.quote: conflict (8.1/10) is the Maldives's strongest pillar
findings.problem: 'Maldives's' and 'Netherlands's' are non-standard possessives for these plural-form country names (NLD has the same error: 'health (8.7/10) is the Netherlands's strongest pillar'). Native style is 'the Maldives' and 'the Netherlands'', or a rephrase such as 'the strongest pillar in the Maldives'.
findings.expected: 'conflict (8.1/10) is the strongest pillar in the Maldives, while ...' (and the equivalent for the Netherlands).
findings.verification: opus: MDV FAQ 'conflict (8.1/10) is the Maldives's strongest pillar' and NLD 'the Netherlands's strongest pillar' are on the pages. Names that are plural in form take only the apostrophe ('the Netherlands'', 'the Maldives''). The same error appears for the United States, the Philippines, the Bahamas, Solomon Islands, United Arab Emirates, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Seychelles and Comoros. Barbados's, Belarus's, Honduras's and Laos's are acceptable.

findings.quote: 请在出行前查阅你所在国家政府的最新指引。
findings.problem: This FAQ switches to 你 while every other page addresses the reader as 您 (e.g. 投出您的一票, 您去过诺福克岛吗？). The same answer asserts without a source that missing advisories are 这在面积很小或偏远的地区很常见, a generic claim the page does not support.
findings.expected: Use 您 throughout; drop the unsourced generalisation or cite its basis.
findings.verification: opus: 请在出行前查阅你所在国家政府的最新指引 appears in the no-advisory FAQ on NFK, CCK, CXR and UMI, while the rest of the site uses 您. The 'common for small or remote places' remark is a reasonable generic statement and not an error. Only the register switch is real.

findings.quote: ist als hohe Vorsicht geboten eingestuft
findings.problem: A band label is used as a noun phrase ('als hohe Vorsicht geboten eingestuft'). The same wording appears on UGA. It reads awkwardly, and the DESCRIPTION already uses the label in brackets.
findings.expected: 'ist in die Stufe „hohe Vorsicht geboten“ eingestuft.'
findings.verification: opus: PAK and UGA both contain 'ist als hohe Vorsicht geboten eingestuft'. The band label is a sentence fragment ('Vorsicht geboten') used as a classification noun, which is ungrammatical. The label needs quotes or a noun form, e.g. 'in die Stufe „hohe Vorsicht geboten“ eingestuft'.

findings.quote: El punto más débil es la debilidad de la gobernanza
findings.problem: The sentence repeats the same word ('punto más débil ... debilidad') and reads as clumsy.
findings.expected: 'La gobernanza es el punto más débil: 4,9 sobre 10 ...'.
findings.verification: opus: The ROU SUMMARY contains 'punto más débil es la debilidad de la gobernanza: 4,9 sobre 10'. The repetition is clumsy, and it comes from a template, so it hits any page where INFORM governance is the weakest indicator.

findings.quote: o que é comum em territórios muito pequenos ou remotos
findings.problem: Unsupported generalisation: nothing in the page's data supports 'é comum em territórios muito pequenos ou remotos'; it explains an empty advisory list with a claim the page does not back. The same answer writes 'publica um aviso de viagem para Ilhas Menores Distantes dos Estados Unidos' without the article ('para as Ilhas…').
findings.expected: State only what the dataset holds, e.g. 'Nenhum governo do nosso conjunto de dados publica um aviso de viagem para este território.'
findings.verification: opus: UMI.pt reads 'nenhum governo do nosso conjunto de dados publica um aviso de viagem para Ilhas Menores Distantes dos Estados Unidos, o que é comum em territórios muito pequenos ou remotos.' The generalisation is true for UMI, but the a3None/a3NoneGrey template uses bare {name}, so the article is missing ('para as Ilhas…'). The real defect is the grammar, not the claim.

findings.quote: 请在出行前查阅你所在国家政府的最新指引
findings.problem: The only page that uses 你 (informal you); every other page uses 您. The same answer says 这在面积很小或偏远的地区很常见, an unsourced generalisation stated as fact.
findings.expected: 请在出行前查阅您所在国家政府的最新指引. Drop the generalisation, or state only what the dataset shows.
findings.verification: opus: The informal 你所在国家 appears in the zero-advisory FAQ template on CCK, CXR, NFK and UMI, so on 4 pages, not one; every other page uses 您. The 'common in small or remote places' remark is a harmless generalisation, so only the register mismatch counts.

findings.quote: Les 22 gouvernements qui publient des conseils aux voyageurs se rendant en Afghanistan déconseillent formellement tout voyage.
findings.problem: The SUMMARY says all 22 governments formally advise against all travel; the FAQ on the same page says 'La plupart des gouvernements déconseillent désormais tout voyage en Afghanistan'. Same data, different quantifier, and no breakdown is given to settle it.
findings.expected: Use the same quantifier in both lines (e.g. '22 sur 22' or 'la plupart') and state the breakdown once.
findings.verification: opus: In latest.json all 22 AFG advisories are level 4. The SUMMARY says all 22 advise against travel, but the FAQ template says 'La plupart des gouvernements' (most). The FAQ understates a unanimous consensus. It also has article errors ('pour Afghanistan', 'de Afghanistan').

findings.quote: Tutti i 22 governi che pubblicano avvisi per chi viaggia in Afghanistan sconsigliano qualsiasi viaggio.
findings.problem: The SUMMARY says all 22 governments advise against any travel. FAQ Q3 on the same page says 'La maggior parte dei governi sconsiglia ormai del tutto i viaggi in Afghanistan' and names only the US and UK 'tra gli altri'. Two different quantifiers for the same count, and the FAQ softens the SUMMARY.
findings.expected: One count with the same wording in SUMMARY and FAQ.
findings.verification: opus: The AFG SUMMARY says 'Tutti i 22 governi … sconsigliano qualsiasi viaggio', and FAQ Q3 says 'La maggior parte dei governi sconsiglia ormai del tutto…'. That is not strictly false, but it understates a unanimous count, and the wording comes from a template. Low severity.

findings.quote: und Reisen dorthin erfordern erhebliche Vorsicht
findings.problem: FAQ1 answers 'Nein' and then softens: „Reisen dorthin erfordern erhebliche Vorsicht“ (HTI). The same pages show that most governments say not to travel at all: HTI 20 of 23 'von allen Reisen ab' (FAQ3: „Die meisten Regierungen raten inzwischen von jeder Reise nach Haiti ab“); IRN 23 of 24; MLI 20 of 21; NER 18 of 21; LBY 17 of 21; LBN 17 of 23; IRQ 16 of 22; MMR 12 of 22. The softer phrase understates what the advisories say (same sentence on NGA, where 14 of 21 say reconsider).
findings.expected: When most advisories say do not travel, FAQ1 should say so, e.g. 'Nein — die meisten Regierungen raten von jeder Reise ab.' Keep 'erhebliche Vorsicht' only where the advisories themselves call for caution.
findings.verification: opus: HTI and IRN FAQ1 end with 'Reisen dorthin erfordern erhebliche Vorsicht' while 20/23 and 23/24 advisories say do not travel. FAQ1 does say 'Nein — … Hochrisiko', and FAQ3 states the do-not-travel majority, so this is an understatement rather than a contradiction.

findings.quote: Nur für erfahrene Reisende
findings.problem: On the 5–6 band the HERO verdict is „Nur für erfahrene Reisende“ (GIN 5.7, KHM 5.9, MOZ 5.5, MRT 5.7, NIC 5.9), but the SUMMARY of the same page classifies the place as „hohe Vorsicht geboten“ and FAQ1 says „Ja, aber nur mit wirklicher Vorsicht“. Two scales run on one page (Nicht empfohlen / Nur für erfahrene Reisende / Vorsicht geboten vs hohes Risiko / hohe Vorsicht geboten / mittleres Risiko) and they do not map one to one.
findings.expected: One band label per page, identical in HERO, SUMMARY and FAQ1 (e.g. 'hohe Vorsicht geboten'), or an explicit sentence explaining what 'Nur für erfahrene Reisende' means for that band.
findings.verification: opus: The 15 de pages in the 5–6 band do show HERO 'Nur für erfahrene Reisende' and SUMMARY 'Einstufung: hohe Vorsicht geboten' (e.g. GIN). The reviewer's 'do not map one to one' claim is wrong: across all de pages each hero label maps to exactly one summary label. Still, two vocabularies run on one page and they overlap in a confusing way. The hero label for the 6–7 band is 'Vorsicht geboten', while the summary label for the 5–6 band is 'hohe Vorsicht geboten'. The FAQ answer 'Ja … Die meisten Reisen verlaufen gut' also sits awkwardly next to 'Nur für erfahrene Reisende'.

findings.quote: am niedrigsten bewertet ist die Gefährdung durch Naturgefahren: 2,3 von 10 auf der INFORM-Skala
findings.problem: 'am niedrigsten bewertet' marks the weakest pillar, but the figure attached is a hazard index where 10 is the worst, so 2,3 is a low and good value. IRL reads as both weakest and very low-risk. LUX does the same with „am niedrigsten bewertet ist die Gewaltkriminalität: 1,5 Tötungsdelikte je 100.000 Einwohner“. A reader cannot tell whether the lowest rating is a weakness.
findings.expected: Give the pillar score first ('schwächste Säule: Naturgefahren 7.8/10') and state the indicator's direction beside its value ('Gefährdung 2,3 von 10; niedrig ist gut').
findings.verification: opus: IRL SUMMARY: 'am niedrigsten bewertet ist die Gefährdung durch Naturgefahren: 2,3 von 10 auf der INFORM-Skala, wobei 10 die höchste Gefährdung bedeutet'. The direction is stated, so the reviewer overstates the problem. Even so, 'am niedrigsten bewertet' (the weakest pillar) attached to a good-looking low hazard value reads muddled, and the same goes for LUX '1,5 Tötungsdelikte'. Minor wording issue.

findings.quote: Am besten bewertet ist der Bereich Konflikt (8.3/10).
findings.problem: Ties are presented as one strongest pillar. GRC: PILLAR BARS show Gesundheit 8.3/10 and Konflikt 8.3/10, but SUMMARY and FAQ1 name only Konflikt. HRV: „Die stärkste Säule von Kroatien ist Gesundheit (8.7/10)“ with Konflikt also at 8.7. KWT: „Am besten bewertet ist der Bereich Gesundheit (7.0/10)“ with Kriminalität also at 7.0. KEN: „Die stärkste Säule von Kenia ist Kriminalität (6.1/10)“ with Naturgefahren at 6.1. IRN: „vor allem Regierungsführung (3.1/10)“ with Naturgefahren also at 3.1.
findings.expected: Name both pillars in a tie ('Konflikt und Gesundheit, je 8.3/10') or use tie-aware wording. Use 'vor allem' only for a strictly lower value.
findings.verification: opus: Verified on the pages. GRC bars show Gesundheit 8.3 and Konflikt 8.3, yet only Konflikt is named. HRV has Konflikt and Gesundheit at 8.7 with only Gesundheit named, KEN has Naturgefahren and Kriminalität at 6.1, and IRN has Regierungsführung and Naturgefahren at 3.1 with 'vor allem Regierungsführung'. The underlying unrounded values probably differ, but at display precision the reader sees an unexplained tie. Minor.

findings.quote: the score is pulled down by crime (6.6/10) and above all by health (6.6/10)
findings.problem: Ties are ranked as if one were bigger: BWA crime 6.6 and health 6.6 ('above all by health'), CPV health 6.4 and governance 6.4 ('above all by governance (6.4/10)'). CZE says conflict (8.8/10) is 'leading' while health is also 8.8.
findings.expected: Use 'tied' wording or one fixed tie-break rule.
findings.verification: opus: BWA shows Health 6.6 and Crime 6.6 but the text says 'above all by health (6.6/10)'. The underlying values do differ (0.656 vs 0.664), so the order is right, but at the displayed precision the 'above all' reads as an unexplained tie-break. Style-level.

findings.quote: No single factor stands out as critical for Croatia: the area that needs the most attention is natural hazards, at 6.5/10.
