findings.problem: SUMMARY names a 'main concern' or 'main risk' (HRV: 'The main concern is exposure to natural hazards: 4.4 out of 10 on the INFORM scale'), and FAQ 2 then says 'No single factor stands out as critical' (51 pages use this sentence). The page names and denies a main risk in the same breath. Separately, IRL, ISL, LTU, LUX, LVA, MHL, MLT and NOR label a pillar 'Top concern' in DESCRIPTION (IRL: 'Top concern: natural hazards (7.8).') while FAQ 2 says 'No pillar signals a significant risk'.
findings.expected: One framing per page: if a pillar is the main concern, FAQ 2 says so; if no pillar signals a significant risk, no 'Top concern' or 'main concern' label is shown.
findings.verification: opus: The HRV pair ('main concern' plus 'No single factor stands out as critical... needs the most attention') is not a real contradiction, since a main concern need not be critical. The IRL/ISL case holds: DESCRIPTION says 'Top concern: natural hazards (7.8)' while FAQ2 says 'No pillar signals a significant risk'. The meta-description template has no all-good frame. This is a framing mismatch, not misleading.

findings.quote: Travel advisories from 10 governments
findings.problem: Partial-data HERO boxes say 'Travel advisories from 10 governments' and, in the same box, 'Fewer than four cover Guadeloupe.' The four-source floor counts feeds, and all advisories count as a single feed (/Users/riccardo/Developer/VibeCoding/Isitsafetotravel/.claude/worktrees/v10-integration/src/pipeline/scoring/coverage.ts; engine.ts keeps one 'advisories' entry), so the rule is applied correctly, but the copy never says so. A reader counts governments and sees a contradiction. The same clash appears on FRO ('Travel advisories from 3 governments World Bank' with 'Fewer than four cover the Faroe Islands.'), GUF (9 governments), GRL (7 governments, UCDP, World Bank) and GIB (4 governments, World Bank).
findings.expected: Use one unit in both sentences, e.g. 'advisories from 10 governments (1 source)' and 'fewer than four sources', or count each government as a source.
findings.verification: opus: The GLP HERO says 'at least four independent sources ... Fewer than four cover Guadeloupe. What we do have Travel advisories from 10 governments'. The same appears on GUF (9), GRL (7), GIB (4) and FRO (3). Advisories count as one source, but the copy never says so, so a reader counting governments sees a clash.

findings.quote: the lowest-rated is exposure to natural hazards: 2.3 out of 10
findings.problem: The SUMMARY mixes two scales in one sentence. The pillar bars use 10 = safest (IRL 'Natural hazards 7.8/10'), while the quoted INFORM indicator uses 10 = highest exposure (IRL 2.3). A low, good exposure number therefore sits beside 'lowest-rated' and reads as a weakness. The same mix appears in ISL ('2.5 out of 10') and in HUN ('weakest area is weak governance: 5.0 out of 10 ... where 10 is the worst', beside 'Governance 5.5/10').
findings.expected: Quote the pillar score in the bar's direction and state the indicator separately, e.g. 'Natural hazards is the weakest area at 7.8/10, because exposure is low (2.3/10).'
findings.verification: opus: IRL and ISL say 'All five areas score at least 7 out of 10; the lowest-rated is exposure to natural hazards: 2.3 out of 10' in one sentence. The inverted INFORM scale is explained, but the two 'out of 10' figures still clash. HUN's 'The weakest area is weak governance: 5.0 out of 10 … where 10 is the worst' sits beside a 5.5/10 bar and says 'weak' twice.

findings.quote: The main risk is poor access to health care: 7.5 out of 10 on the INFORM scale
findings.problem: The 'main risk / main concern / weakest area' sentence names a pillar that is not the lowest bar on 16 of the 25 pages that carry one (LBR, LBY, LKA, LSO, MAR, MDA, MDG, MDV, MEX, MHL, MMR, MNG, MOZ, MRT, MUS, MWI). On 15 of those 16 the lowest bar is Governance, which the sentence never names. LBR: Governance 3.5 is lowest, the summary names Health (4.6). MDG: Governance 2.7 is lowest, the summary names Health. MNG: Governance 4.5 is lowest; the summary names natural hazards and calls INFORM exposure of 3.3/10 the main concern. MOZ is the sharpest case: 'The main concern is armed conflict', but Conflict (5.5) is the highest of its five bars and Governance (3.4) the lowest.
findings.expected: Build the headline risk from the same ranking the bars display: name the lowest-rated pillar, including Governance, and never call the best-rated pillar a main concern.
findings.verification: opus: Quotes are on the pages (LBR names health 4.6 while Governance 3.5 is the lowest bar; MOZ calls conflict, its highest bar at 5.5, the main concern). Leaving governance out is deliberate: selectDriverPillar in src/lib/country-summary.ts picks among the direct-risk pillars by weighted drag, after the blogger objected to 'biggest concern is governance'. So 'always name the lowest bar' is not the right fix. What remains is a visible inconsistency: nothing says the ranking is about traveller risk, and MOZ calls its best-rated bar the main concern.

findings.quote: the lowest-rated is weak governance: 4.2 out of 10 on the INFORM scale
findings.problem: In the same sentence as 'All five areas score at least 7 out of 10', governance is 7.3/10 on Poland (POL) and 7.2/10 on Portugal (PRT). 'weak governance' is the fixed topic text (src/i18n/indicator-copy.ts, topics.inform_governance) and is used even above 7/10, while the V-Dem rule of law rows are 0.88 and 0.89. Norway (NOR) has the same frame: 'the lowest-rated is exposure to natural hazards: 2.8 out of 10', where 2.8 is a low risk, not a weakness.
findings.expected: In the all-good frame use neutral wording, and reserve 'weak' for pillars below 5/10.
findings.verification: opus: The POL and PRT summaries say 'All five areas score at least 7' and then 'the lowest-rated is weak governance: 4.2 / 3.8 out of 10 on the INFORM scale', while their Governance pillars are 7.3 and 7.2. The fixed label 'weak governance' contradicts the positive frame. NOR's 'exposure to natural hazards' wording is neutral and is not a problem.

findings.quote: It combines 17 government travel advisories and 3 other public datasets
findings.problem: The dataset count does not match the INDICATORS table. Nauru shows 2 datasets (INFORM, UCDP) but says 3; Palau shows 3 (INFORM, ReliefWeb, UCDP) but says 4; North Korea shows 4 (V-Dem, INFORM, GPI, UCDP) but says 5; Niger shows 5 but says 6; Nepal shows 6 but says 7. Likely cause: the count (src/lib/provenance-copy.ts, from country.sources) comes from buildSourcesForCountry in src/pipeline/scoring/engine.ts, which counts a feed when any raw row exists for the country, including rows that never appear on the page.
findings.expected: Count only feeds that are displayed and feed the score, or disclose the hidden feed.
findings.verification: opus: The NRU sources in latest.json are advisories, inform, ucdp and worldbank, so the page counts 3 datasets. The NRU page shows only INFORM and UCDP rows: no World Bank row, and the crime indicators are empty. The 'other public datasets' count includes feeds that never appear on the page or feed the score.

findings.quote: It combines 17 government travel advisories and 4 other public datasets
findings.problem: The dataset count in the SUMMARY is higher than the sources shown in INDICATORS on 13 of the 24 scored pages. STP says 4 other datasets but shows 3 (V-Dem, INFORM, UCDP). SLE says 6 and shows 5; TGO says 5 and shows 4. The page does not explain the gap.
findings.expected: Count only the datasets whose values are displayed, or show the missing dataset as 'no data'.
findings.verification: opus: STP says '17 government travel advisories and 4 other public datasets' but its INDICATORS show only INFORM, V-Dem and UCDP (3). SLE says 6 but shows INFORM, V-Dem, GPI, ReliefWeb and UCDP (5). The count includes a source that has no displayed row.

findings.quote: The main concern is poor access to health care: 6.4 out of 10 on the INFORM scale
findings.problem: The named concern follows a design rule, not the lowest bar. country-summary.ts selectDriverPillar() looks only at direct-risk pillars (conflict, crime, health, natural hazards), skips governance unless every direct-risk pillar is 7.0+, skips pillars below 0.30 coverage, and ranks by weight times -ln(score). Result: 16 of the 22 SUMMARY blocks that name a main concern name a pillar that is not the lowest visible bar. Governance is the lowest visible bar on 13 pages (e.g. TJK 2.3, TKM 2.3, UZB 3.4, YEM 1.5, VEN 1.5) and no summary mentions it. ZWE names health access (6.4) while its governance bar is 3.0/10, and governance is also the highest INFORM risk on that page (7.4). USA names crime (6.9) over natural hazards (5.4) because crime carries 25% weight against 10%.
findings.expected: Mention the weakest bar as context (for example 'Governance is the weakest bar at 3.0/10, but it is not a direct travel risk'), or state the selection rule on the page, so the summary does not look like it contradicts the bars.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on ZWE: the summary names health access (6.4) as the main concern while the Governance bar of 3.0 is the lowest. USA names crime (6.9) while Natural hazards is 5.4. Leaving governance out is a deliberate design choice, so this is only a readability mismatch between summary and bars, not misleading. The '16 of 22' count was not verified.

findings.quote: It combines 21 government travel advisories and 6 other public datasets
findings.problem: The count is every entry in the country's sources list except advisories (provenance-copy.ts getProvenanceCounts), so a feed that gave no visible value is still counted. TJK's sources include worldbank, but its crime pillar is GPI-only and no homicide row appears; the table shows 5 distinct datasets against the claimed 6. Same on ZMB (6 claimed, 5 shown), TON (4 vs 3) and nine other scored pages in this batch (TKM, TLS, TUN, TUV, TZA, VNM, VUT, WSM, YEM).
findings.expected: Count only feeds that contributed a visible value, or show the missing World Bank row as 'no value'.
findings.verification: opus: TJK's sources in latest.json include worldbank, but the page has no World Bank row; it shows 5 distinct datasets (V-Dem, INFORM, ReliefWeb, GPI, UCDP) against the claimed '6 other public datasets'. The count includes feeds that contributed nothing visible. Examples: TJK, ZMB.

findings.quote: Fewer than four cover Wallis and Futuna.
findings.problem: Partial-data copy: the box lists advisories ('Travel advisories from 4 governments') and then says 'Fewer than four cover Wallis and Futuna.' A reader counts four sources. The four-source rule appears to exclude advisories, but the page does not say so. Same pattern on VAT (6 governments, 'Fewer than four cover Vatican City.') and XKX (18 governments, 'Fewer than four cover Kosovo.'). VGB, VIR and XKX also list 'World Bank' under 'What we do have' with no value shown.
findings.expected: Say 'at least four independent datasets (advisories are not counted)', and drop bare source names that show no value.
findings.verification: opus: The WLF hero lists 'Travel advisories from 4 governments' and then says 'Fewer than four cover Wallis and Futuna.' XKX lists 18 governments plus a bare 'World Bank' with no value. The page does not say that advisories are excluded from the four-source rule, so a reader sees a contradiction. Examples: WLF, VAT, XKX.

findings.quote: incluso el más débil, riesgos naturales (8.3/10), se sitúa en la franja de riesgo bajo
findings.problem: The totals scale puts 8.0 and above in 'riesgo muy bajo' (EST TITLE: 8.7/10 'riesgo muy bajo'), yet the pillar text calls the 8.3 pillar 'franja de riesgo bajo'. CZE does the same with gobernanza 8.0/10 ('claramente dentro de la franja de riesgo bajo').
findings.expected: One band vocabulary for pillars and totals: pillars at 8.0 or above are in the 'riesgo muy bajo' band.
findings.verification: opus: Pillars use a separate band vocabulary: every pillar at 8.0 or above is labelled 'Bajo' (EST and CZE indicator tables), while totals at 8.0 or above are 'riesgo muy bajo'. The reviewer misquoted EST's TITLE, which carries no band text. The pillar sentence is consistent with the pillar scale, so this is only a vocabulary mismatch.

findings.quote: Puntuación gratuita de 30+ fuentes públicas, recalculada a diario.
findings.problem: 63 of 65 scored DESCRIPTIONs promise '30+ fuentes públicas', but the same page's SUMMARY counts the sources behind that country's score: GIN 20 advisories + 5 datasets = 25; GRD 19 + 3 = 22; HTI 23 + 6 = 29. The '30+' is the site-wide total (SOURCE_COUNT_DISPLAY, src/lib/seo.ts:313; src/lib/site-stats.ts:44-47 and 120), not this country's count, so it reads as a claim about the score.
findings.expected: Use the page's own count in the DESCRIPTION, or say 'más de 30 fuentes en todo el sitio'.
findings.verification: opus: The '30+ fuentes públicas' DESCRIPTION appears 63 times in the batch, while the page SUMMARY counts 20 advisories + 5 datasets for GIN. It reads as a per-score claim. This is a mild overstatement.

findings.field: HERO verdict vs FAQ A1 verdict
findings.quote: Solo para viajeros expertos
findings.problem: On five pages in the 5.0-5.99 band the HERO verdict says 'Solo para viajeros expertos' (only for experienced travellers) while FAQ A1 says 'Sí, pero solo con verdadera precaución' (yes, with real caution). That is two verdict strengths on one page (GIN 5.7, KHM 5.9, MOZ 5.5, MRT 5.7, NIC 5.9).
findings.expected: One verdict phrase for both places.
findings.verification: opus: GIN, KHM and MOZ carry both the HERO 'Solo para viajeros expertos' and the FAQ A1 'Sí, pero solo con verdadera precaución'. These are two different verdict strengths for the same band. The gap is mild but real.

findings.quote: Puntuación gratuita de 30+ fuentes públicas, recalculada a diario.
findings.problem: The DESCRIPTION of 62 scored pages promises '30+ fuentes públicas', but the same page's SUMMARY counts the sources it combines, and 61 of 64 scored pages total fewer than 30 (range 17 to 31). Example NRU: DESCRIPTION '30+', SUMMARY '17 avisos de viaje gubernamentales y otros 3 conjuntos de datos públicos' (20 in total). If 30+ is meant as a site-wide total, the page does not say so.
findings.expected: Show the page's own source count, or write 'más de 30 fuentes en total' and make clear that it is a site-wide figure.
findings.verification: opus: VEN DESCRIPTION says '30+ fuentes públicas' while its SUMMARY says '20 avisos... y otros 7 conjuntos de datos' (27 in total). NRU totals 20. This page-level meta snippet overstates the page's own source count.

findings.quote: Score gratuit issu de 30+ sources publiques, recalculé chaque jour.
findings.problem: The DESCRIPTION meta claims '30+ sources' on pages where the SUMMARY and the methodology sentence give fewer sources. SWZ says 'Le score combine 19 avis aux voyageurs officiels et 5 autres jeux de données publics' (24 sources), SWE gives 20 + 5 = 25, TCD gives 21 + 6 = 27. The number disagrees within the same page.
findings.expected: Use the same source count in the DESCRIPTION and SUMMARY, or drop the '30+' number from the DESCRIPTION.
findings.verification: opus: The DESCRIPTION on SWZ and TCD says 'issu de 30+ sources publiques', while the SUMMARY counts 19+5=24 and 21+6=27. SWE is a wrong example: its DESCRIPTION is shorter and does not contain '30+'. The count still disagrees within the same page on most pages. It probably means the site-wide catalogue, but it reads as this country's count.

findings.quote: Punteggio gratuito da 30+ fonti pubbliche, ricalcolato ogni giorno.
findings.problem: The '30+' figure is a site-wide constant (SOURCE_COUNT_DISPLAY in src/lib/seo.ts, used in the Italian meta description), while the same page's SUMMARY states how many sources the score combines. GMB: 17 advisories + 5 datasets = 22; GIN: 20 + 5 = 25; GRD: 19 + 3 = 22; HTI: 23 + 6 = 29. Only India (24 + 7 = 31) reaches 30 among the pages with this sentence. DESCRIPTION and SUMMARY disagree on the number of sources.
findings.expected: Print the page's own count (N advisories + M datasets) in the DESCRIPTION, or keep the site-wide figure only in methodology or about text.
findings.verification: opus: GIN DESCRIPTION says 'Punteggio gratuito da 30+ fonti pubbliche', but its SUMMARY says the score combines 20 advisories plus 5 datasets (25). GMB has 22 and HTI has 29. The site-wide constant reads as a per-page claim. This is only a number mismatch in the meta snippet, so severity is low.

findings.quote: Tutti i 19 governi che pubblicano avvisi per chi viaggia in Croazia raccomandano le normali precauzioni.
findings.problem: On the same page the FAQ says 'la maggior parte dei governi raccomanda solo precauzioni normali'. Where every government agrees (HRV 19/19, HUN 18/18, LIE 18/18, MLT 20/20), the FAQ's 'la maggior parte' understates the figure, so the two quantifiers disagree on the page.
findings.expected: Use 'tutti' in both places when the count is complete, and 'la maggior parte' only when the share is below 100%.
findings.verification: opus: HRV, HUN and MLT each say 'Tutti i N governi ... raccomandano le normali precauzioni', and the FAQ on the same pages says 'la maggior parte dei governi raccomanda solo precauzioni normali'. The FAQ template does not switch to 'tutti' when the share is 100%.

findings.quote: Pontuação gratuita de 30+ fontes públicas, recalculada diariamente.
findings.problem: Every scored DESCRIPTION promises '30+ fontes públicas'. The same page's SUMMARY counts the sources the score combines: GIN '20 avisos de viagem governamentais e outros 5 conjuntos de dados públicos' = 25. The SUMMARY totals are 18–29 on 64 of 65 scored pages (IND reaches 31). If 30+ is a platform-wide figure, the DESCRIPTION does not say so.
findings.expected: Use the page's own count in DESCRIPTION (e.g. '25 fontes'), or label the 30+ figure as the platform total.
findings.verification: opus: 'Pontuação gratuita de 30+ fontes públicas' appears in the DESCRIPTION of 183 pt pages. On the same pages the SUMMARY gives a smaller count, e.g. GIN 20+5=25 and MOZ 20+7=27, so the page-level claim is inaccurate unless it is labelled as the platform total.

findings.quote: 最高级别的警告——切勿前往——已由美国和英国等国发布。
findings.problem: On 15 pages the top advisory level is called 切勿前往 in the FAQ (src/lib/country-faq-copy.ts advisory level words, about line 262) but 避免一切旅行 in the SUMMARY (src/i18n/country-summary-copy.ts about line 234). BFA: SUMMARY '14个建议避免一切旅行' vs FAQ '切勿前往'. BHR: SUMMARY '4个建议避免一切旅行' vs FAQ '最严厉的警告——切勿前往——由荷兰和波兰发布'. The site's advisory glossary uses '4 级 — 切勿前往' (src/i18n/government-advisories-copy.ts about line 419), so the SUMMARY label is the outlier. Readers can take them as two different levels.
findings.expected: One Chinese label for level 4 across SUMMARY, FAQ, hub pages and glossary, matching the advisory glossary (切勿前往).
findings.verification: opus: Level 4 is '建议避免一切旅行' in country-summary-copy.ts:234 but '切勿前往' in country-faq-copy.ts:262 and in the glossary (government-advisories-copy.ts:419). Both show on the same AFG page. This is a terminology inconsistency; the terms are near-synonyms, so the risk of confusion is minor.

findings.quote: 没有任何一国将其提升至低级别以上的警告。
findings.problem: Read naturally ('低级别' = normal precautions), this clause contradicts the SUMMARY on 26 scored pages that list 1-8 governments advising 提高警惕 (BEL 8, ALB 8, CPV 8, ARG 7, GAB 7, BWA 7 and others). If 低级别 means caution, the term is never defined. The sentence is ambiguous on every page that uses it, and it is the same template as the GAB/BWA finding.
findings.expected: Name the levels explicitly, e.g. '没有任何一国建议重新考虑或避免前往', and only when the counts support it.
findings.verification: opus: The clause appears on BRN (2 caution) and BWA (7 caution + 1 reconsider). The template never checks the max level, and '低级别' is undefined, so with visible '等级 2' cards it reads as false. The clearly false level 3/4 case is #0; this is the residual ambiguity for level-2-only pages.

findings.quote: tiré vers le bas par criminalité (6.6/10) et surtout par santé (6.6/10)
findings.problem: Two pillars with the same value are ordered with 'et surtout', which implies a larger drag for santé. CPV has the same problem ('par santé (6.4/10) et surtout par gouvernance (6.4/10)').
findings.expected: '… tiré vers le bas à égalité par criminalité et santé (6.6/10)'.
findings.verification: opus: BWA shows 'criminalité (6.6/10) et surtout par santé (6.6/10)' and CPV shows 'santé (6.4/10) et surtout par gouvernance (6.4/10)'. In the data BWA is crime 0.664 vs health 0.656 and CPV is health 0.642 vs governance 0.640, so the order is right. But the displayed values are equal, so 'surtout' (above all) reads as a contradiction.

findings.quote: A pontuação combina 20 avisos de viagem governamentais e outros 7 conjuntos de dados públicos
findings.problem: The COMMUNITY block adds a community adjustment ('Pontuação dos dados 6.7', 'Ajuste da comunidade +0.4', 'Pontuação de segurança 7.1/10'), but the methodology sentence says the score combines advisories and public datasets only.
findings.expected: Mention the community adjustment in the methodology sentence wherever it is applied.
findings.verification: opus: CHN.pt SUMMARY says the score combines 20 advisories and 7 public datasets. The COMMUNITY block shows 'Pontuação dos dados 6.7 Ajuste da comunidade +0.4 Pontuação de segurança 7.1/10'. The methodology sentence leaves out the community adjustment that was actually applied.

findings.quote: Non ci sono ancora abbastanza voti (1/30 voti, 0/3 paesi di provenienza)
findings.problem: One vote cannot come from zero countries of origin. The HERO shows the same '1/30 voti, 0/3 paesi di provenienza' pair. Other grey pages with votes show at least one country (ABW: 2/30 voti, 2/3 paesi).
findings.expected: At least one country of origin whenever there is at least one vote.
findings.verification: opus: The GGY page shows '1/30 voti, 0/3 paesi di provenienza', and latest.json has votes:1, origins:0 for GGY. The vote probably came from an unknown origin country, but the visible text contradicts itself. It has no effect on safety.

findings.quote: Comunidade Ainda não há votos suficientes (1/30 votos, 0/3 países de origem)
findings.problem: One vote cannot come from zero countries of origin; pages with one vote show 1/3 countries. The same figures appear in HERO and COMMUNITY.
findings.expected: 1/3, or an explanation when the origin is unknown.
findings.verification: opus: GGY.pt HERO and COMMUNITY show '(1/30 votos, 0/3 países de origem)'. latest.json has GGY community votes=1, origins=0, so the vote apparently has an unknown or excluded origin. Other one-vote pages (BRA, ARG, BHR) show 1/3. A reader sees a contradiction and no explanation is given.

findings.quote: 仅限经验丰富的旅行者
findings.problem: On the 5 to 6 band pages (GIN, KHM, MOZ, MRT, NIC) the HERO verdict 仅限经验丰富的旅行者 (only for experienced travellers) is stricter than FAQ 1's opening 可以 (GIN: 可以，但务必格外谨慎). Travellers get two different verdicts to the same question. The band label itself matches the score.
findings.expected: Use one verdict for the 5 to 6 band in both HERO and FAQ 1.
findings.verification: opus: GIN HERO shows 仅限经验丰富的旅行者, while FAQ 1 opens 可以，但务必格外谨慎…多数行程能够顺利完成 and names the band 高度谨慎. The hero badge is noticeably more restrictive than the FAQ's 'yes, most trips go fine'. This is a tone mismatch across the 5–6 band template rather than a hard contradiction.

findings.quote: Community Not enough votes yet (1/30 votes, 0/3 countries of origin)
findings.problem: One vote is shown against zero countries of origin. That cannot be right if every vote records a country, and every other one-vote page shows at least 1/3 countries. NLD shows the same line ('1/30 votes, 0/3 countries of origin').
findings.expected: Count the countries of origin of the votes received, or explain that a vote with no country code is counted in the total but not in the country count.
findings.verification: opus: JEY and NLD both show '1/30 votes, 0/3 countries of origin'. Across en pages, 6 places show 1 vote with 0 countries, against 69 that show 1 vote with 1 country. A vote apparently counts in the total without a country_iso (probably null from request.cf.country), and the display does not explain it.

findings.field: FAQ A1 and A2 band wording
findings.quote: incluso el más débil, criminalidad (8.0/10), se sitúa en la franja de riesgo bajo
findings.problem: The same displayed 8.0/10 is 'riesgo muy bajo' on an overall score (GRC: 'Grecia: seguridad 8.0/10 (riesgo muy bajo)') but 'franja de riesgo bajo' for a pillar here, and FAQ A2 repeats 'claramente dentro de la franja de riesgo bajo' for the same 8.0 value. The 'allStrong' copy hardcodes 'franja de riesgo bajo' (country-faq-copy.ts:408) for any weakest pillar at 7.0 or above, so values of 8.0 and above get the wrong label. Probably a rounding boundary at 8.0.
findings.expected: Derive the band word from the value for pillars too, so 8.0 and above read 'riesgo muy bajo', or avoid band words for pillars.
findings.verification: opus: LUX FAQ reads 'incluso el más débil, criminalidad (8.0/10), se sitúa en la franja de riesgo bajo' and 'obtiene 8.0/10, claramente dentro de la franja de riesgo bajo'. The site labels an 8.0 overall as 'riesgo muy bajo' (GRC), so the band word for the same value is inconsistent. This is a minor wording issue.

findings.quote: anche il più debole, criminalità (8.0/10), rientra nella fascia di rischio basso
findings.problem: 8.0 is labelled 'rischio molto basso' elsewhere on the site (GRC DESCRIPTION: 'Grecia: sicurezza 8.0/10 (rischio molto basso).'), but LUX calls the same 8.0 'fascia di rischio basso' in both FAQ answers (the second says 'ben dentro la fascia di rischio basso'). The allStrong and strong copy in src/lib/country-faq-copy.ts hard-codes 'fascia di rischio basso' whatever the weakest pillar's band is.
findings.expected: Derive the band word from the score ('fascia di rischio molto basso' at 8.0 and above), or use a band-neutral phrase.
findings.verification: opus: LUX FAQ says criminalità 8.0 'rientra nella fascia di rischio basso'. GRC DESCRIPTION calls 8.0 'rischio molto basso'. The band word is hard-coded instead of taken from the score. The mismatch is minor and the statement is not unsafe, so severity is low.

findings.quote: Aucune source indépendante ne couvre encore cette destination.
findings.problem: TITLE ('Voyager en Île Norfolk : est-ce sûr ? Données partielles (2026)'), DESCRIPTION and HERO say 'Données partielles' ('moins de quatre sources indépendantes'). The HERO's 'Ce dont nous disposons' block, however, says 'Aucune source indépendante ne couvre encore cette destination', which is zero sources. Zero sources means no data, not partial data. The Q3 answer (no government publishes an advisory) matches zero data.
findings.expected: A 'no data' label for zero-source places (for example 'Aucune donnée disponible'), keeping 'Données partielles' for places with one to three sources.
findings.verification: opus: NFK.fr carries 'Données partielles' in the TITLE and HERO but also 'Aucune source indépendante ne couvre encore cette destination'. latest.json confirms sources [], advisories {} and dataCompleteness 0. 'Partial' with zero sources is inaccurate wording, but it is low because the grey 'partial data' treatment itself is accepted.

findings.quote: È sicuro viaggiare in Isola Norfolk? Dati parziali (2026)
findings.problem: The TITLE says 'Dati parziali' (partial data). The HERO on the same page says 'Cosa abbiamo Nessuna fonte indipendente copre ancora questa destinazione.' and the FAQ says no government in the dataset publishes an advisory. Zero sources means no data, not partial data, so the title overstates coverage.
findings.expected: Use a 'dati assenti' or 'nessun dato' label for zero-source territories, and keep 'Dati parziali' only when at least one source exists.
findings.verification: opus: The NFK.it title is 'Dati parziali', but latest.json has sources [] and dataCompleteness 0, and the hero says 'Nessuna fonte indipendente copre ancora questa destinazione'. 'Parziali' overstates zero coverage. The grey design itself is accepted, so this is low. The same page has a worse slip: B9 says 'Leggi gli avvisi governativi qui sotto' while the FAQ says no government publishes an advisory for it.

findings.quote: Yes, safe to travel 9 8.5 out of 10
findings.problem: The same displayed score of 8.5/10 gets badge 9 on Portugal but badge 8 on New Zealand and Poland ('Yes, safe to travel 8 8.5 out of 10'). The badge seems to round the unrounded score while the page prints one decimal, so the visible pair contradicts itself.
findings.expected: Derive the badge from the same value that is printed, so equal displayed scores show the same badge.
findings.verification: opus: Unrounded scores: PRT 8.537 shows badge 9, POL 8.460 and NZL 8.496 show badge 8. All three print '8.5 out of 10'. The badge rounds the raw score to an integer while the text rounds to one decimal, so equal printed scores get different badges in the HERO.

findings.quote: Singapour ne présente de risque significatif sur aucun pilier
findings.problem: Very-low-risk pages still show a main risk. SGP DESCRIPTION says 'Risque principal : santé (7.9).' while FAQ Q2 says there is no significant risk on any pillar. SVN has the same pattern ('Risque principal : risques naturels (7.3).' vs 'Slovénie ne présente de risque significatif sur aucun pilier'). Also on SGP, 'le pilier conflit (8.7/10) arrivant en tête' is a tie: PILLAR BARS shows 'Gouvernance 8.7/10 | Conflit 8.7/10', and the tie is not mentioned.
findings.expected: Omit the 'Risque principal' label when every pillar is in the low-risk band, and state the tie (e.g. 'à égalité avec la gouvernance').
findings.verification: opus: SGP DESCRIPTION 'Risque principal : santé (7.9)' and SVN 'Risque principal : risques naturels (7.3)' sit beside FAQ text saying there is no significant risk on any pillar. That is a mild labeling inconsistency. The SGP tie is only a rounding effect: conflict is 0.8671 and governance 0.8667 in the data, so conflict really is top. That part is not a defect.

findings.quote: Uniquement pour voyageurs expérimentés
findings.problem: The HERO verdict is stricter than the rest of the page. DESCRIPTION and SUMMARY place Uganda in the 'prudence élevée' band, and FAQ1 answers 'Oui, mais avec une réelle prudence' (a yes for travellers in general). 'Uniquement pour voyageurs expérimentés' tells a traveller the destination is closed to anyone inexperienced, which is a different verdict from the answer below it.
findings.expected: Align the HERO verdict with the band wording and FAQ1, e.g. 'Faire preuve de prudence' or a verdict that matches 'prudence élevée'.
findings.verification: opus: UGA.fr HERO shows 'Uniquement pour voyageurs expérimentés', while FAQ1 opens with 'Oui, mais avec une réelle prudence… La plupart des voyages se passent bien'. Both come from the same 5–6 band by design, so this is a difference in tone rather than a hard contradiction. Uganda's advisories (2 do-not-travel, 5 reconsider) support the stricter hero wording.

findings.quote: Alle 22 Regierungen, die Reisehinweise für Afghanistan veröffentlichen, raten von allen Reisen ab.
findings.problem: The FAQ on the same page says 'Die meisten Regierungen raten inzwischen von jeder Reise nach Afghanistan ab'. 'Alle 22' and 'die meisten' give different advisory counts for the same fact. The SUMMARY gives no breakdown that would support 'alle'.
findings.expected: One consistent count, e.g. 'X von 22 Regierungen raten ... ab', used in both SUMMARY and FAQ.
findings.verification: opus: All 22 AFG advisories are Stufe 4, so SUMMARY 'Alle 22 ...' is correct. FAQ 'Die meisten Regierungen raten inzwischen von jeder Reise ... ab' is an understatement, not a false or different count. The wording is inconsistent, but only as a minor style issue.

findings.quote: All 22 governments that publish a travel advisory for Afghanistan advise against all travel.
findings.problem: The FAQ on the same page says 'Most governments now advise against all travel to Afghanistan'. The SUMMARY gives the exact count (22 of 22) and the FAQ softens it to 'most', so a reader gets two counts.
findings.expected: Use one count throughout the page, e.g. 'All 22 governments advise against all travel.'
findings.verification: opus: AFG SUMMARY says 'All 22 governments ... advise against all travel' while the FAQ says 'Most governments now advise against all travel'. 'Most' is not false but undersells a unanimous count, so this is style only.

findings.quote: Os 22 governos que publicam alertas para quem viaja ao Afeganistão desaconselham qualquer viagem.
findings.problem: SUMMARY says all 22 governments advise against any travel. FAQ Q3 on the same page says 'A maioria dos governos já desaconselha qualquer viagem ao Afeganistão' (most, not all). Both cannot be right.
findings.expected: One count from the same data, used in both places (for example 'N de 22 governos desaconselham qualquer viagem').
findings.verification: opus: All 22 AFG advisories are Nível 4 and the SUMMARY says so. Q3's 'A maioria dos governos já desaconselha' is not false, only understated, so this is a minor wording inconsistency.

findings.quote: The overall picture is reassuring: most governments advise only normal precautions for Iceland, and none currently raises it above a low-level advisory.
findings.problem: On 22 pages with an advisory breakdown, FAQ 3 says 'none currently raises it above a low-level advisory' while the SUMMARY on the same page counts governments advising increased caution (ISL 2, LVA 1, NOR 1, KIR 2, GRD 6, NAM 6, NLD 6, MUS 5, KAZ 9). 'Low-level advisory' is undefined: if it means 'normal precautions', the sentence is false; if it means 'increased caution', the 'reassuring' framing hides the split.
findings.expected: State the split plainly (for example '17 of 19 advise normal precautions; 2 advise increased caution') and drop 'none currently raises it above a low-level advisory', or define the scale.
findings.verification: opus: The sentence is on ISL, NAM and KAZ (KAZ: 11 normal, 9 increased caution). It is not strictly false if 'low-level' includes increased caution. Still, 'low-level advisory' is undefined, and calling a 11 vs 9 split 'reassuring' hides it. This is vague template wording, not a factual error.

findings.quote: the lowest-rated is exposure to natural hazards: 2.5 out of 10 on the INFORM scale, where 10 is the highest exposure
findings.problem: On pages where every pillar is at least 7/10 (AUT, BEL), the sentence calls natural-hazard exposure the 'lowest-rated' area and then cites a low-risk figure (AUT 2.5/10, BEL 3.4/10, where 10 is the highest exposure). The reader gets a weakness label and a reassuring number in the same sentence. The Natural hazards pillar is 7.7/10 on AUT and 7.1/10 on BEL.
findings.expected: Give the pillar score and the risk value together, for example 'Natural hazards is the lowest-rated area (7.7/10), though exposure itself is low (2.5/10).'
findings.verification: opus: The AUT and BEL sentences read 'All five areas score at least 7 out of 10; the lowest-rated is exposure to natural hazards: 2.5 out of 10...'. Placed right after 'at least 7 out of 10', the '2.5 out of 10' reads as the area's rating. The risk-scale explanation that follows clears it up, but the sentence is confusing. This is a minor template issue.

findings.quote: The main concern is poor public safety: the Global Peace Index rates safety and security at 2.13 on a scale from 1 (safest) to 5
findings.problem: 'Poor public safety' is used for GPI safety scores of 2.13 (LKA), 2.33 (LSO) and 2.58 (MRT). All three are better than the 3.0 midpoint of a 1-to-5 scale where lower is safer, and LKA's Crime bar is 6.6/10. The label overstates what the number shows.
findings.expected: Use a label that matches the value's position on the scale and the pillar band.
findings.verification: opus: The LKA quote is exact; LSO (2.33) and MRT (2.58) use the same 'poor public safety' label. GPI safety & security values around 2.1 to 2.3 are better than the global middle, and LKA's Crime bar is 6.6. The fixed negative label overstates the value. It is the same template family as #8.

findings.quote: The weakest area is weak governance
findings.problem: Templated phrasing. ROU writes 'The weakest area is weak governance' and cites an INFORM value of 4.9/10, which is mid-scale. SVK writes 'The weakest area is weak public administration' on a V-Dem impartiality score of 0.30 (scale about -4 to +4), which sits just above the midpoint, so 'weak' overstates it. The adjective repeats the pillar name and is not backed by the number. Examples: ROU, SVK.
findings.expected: Name the specific lowest input and its value, and drop 'weak' unless the value is clearly below the midpoint.
findings.verification: opus: ROU says 'The weakest area is weak governance' on an INFORM governance value of 4.9/10. SVK says 'The weakest area is weak public administration' on a V-Dem value of 0.30, just above the midpoint of a −4 to +4 scale. The adjective is template filler that the values do not support. Governance is the lowest pillar on both pages, so naming the area is fine.

findings.quote: Ningún factor destaca como crítico en Albania: el área que requiere más atención es riesgos naturales, con 5.8/10.
findings.problem: On 47 pages the SUMMARY names a main concern ('La principal preocupación es ...' / 'El principal riesgo es ...') while FAQ Q2 says 'Ningún factor destaca como crítico en X'. ALB: SUMMARY names natural hazards as the main concern, Q2 says no factor stands out. DEU: SUMMARY names natural hazards (INFORM exposure 4,0 sobre 10) as the main concern while Q2 says no factor stands out. Also AGO, ARG, ESP, CHL. Separately, DESCRIPTION 'Mayor riesgo: ...' appears on the pages whose FAQ says 'Ningún pilar señala un riesgo significativo' (AUT, BEL, BRN, CHE, CYP, CZE, DNK, FIN, GBR).
findings.expected: One framing per page: name a main concern only when one pillar clearly stands out; otherwise drop the principal-concern sentence and the 'Mayor riesgo' label.
findings.verification: opus: Partly valid. 'La principal preocupación es...' next to 'Ningún factor destaca como crítico' (ALB, DEU) is not a real contradiction, since a main concern need not be critical. But AUT's DESCRIPTION shows 'Mayor riesgo: riesgos naturales (7.7)' on a page whose FAQ says 'Ningún pilar señala un riesgo significativo', which labels a top-band pillar as a risk. That is a framing or style issue.

findings.quote: La recomendación predominante es extremar la precaución al visitar Antártida; la advertencia más severa — extremar la precaución — proviene de Estados Unidos y Canadá.
findings.problem: The predominant advice and the 'most severe' advice are the same level, so the second clause repeats the first and reads as machine text. Same pattern with extremar on ATA, BHS, CHN, CIV, CRI, DOM, FRA, and with reconsiderar el viaje on ESH.
findings.expected: Name the highest level actually present (for example, 'ninguna autoridad aconseja no viajar; el nivel más alto es extremar la precaución') or drop the duplicate clause.
findings.verification: opus: ATA and CHN Q3 say the predominant advice is extremar la precaución and then that the most severe is also extremar la precaución. ESH does the same with reconsiderar ('las advertencias más severas... emitidas por Reino Unido', plural for one issuer). The second clause is redundant, machine-sounding text.

findings.quote: se ve lastrada por gobernanza (8.1/10) y, sobre todo, por riesgos naturales (6.1/10)
findings.problem: 'Se ve lastrada' (dragged down) is used for pillars at 7.5 to 8.2 on very-low-risk pages: CAN gobernanza 8.1, DEU criminalidad 8.2, AUS criminalidad 8.2, ESP gobernanza 7.7, FRA conflicto 7.5. The same pages say the five pillars are good, so the wording overstates weakness.
findings.expected: Reserve 'lastrada' for pillars below the band threshold; otherwise name the lowest pillar neutrally.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on CAN.es (overall 8.3, gobernanza 8.1). The same template says 'se ve lastrada por' on DEU (criminalidad 8.2, overall 8.5), AUS (criminalidad 8.2 while the overall is 8.1), ESP and FRA. It calls a near-excellent pillar a drag, which is the generic machine wording the blogger criticised.

findings.quote: la advertencia más severa — extremar la precaución — proviene de Estados Unidos y Canadá
findings.problem: When the predominant advice is already 'extremar la precaución', the 'most severe warning' is the same level as the majority, yet the sentence names two countries as its source, implying they stand out. Seen on HKG, IDN, KGZ, LKA, MDV, MYS and NCL (quote from IDN).
findings.expected: Say that no government goes above 'extremar la precaución', or name the highest level actually issued.
findings.verification: opus: IDN and HKG read 'La recomendación predominante es extremar la precaución…; la advertencia más severa — extremar la precaución — proviene de Estados Unidos y Canadá'. When the most severe level equals the predominant one, crediting it to two countries is redundant and implies they stand out.

findings.quote: le moins bien noté est l’exposition aux risques naturels : 1,6 sur 10 selon INFORM
findings.problem: The SUMMARY calls natural-hazard exposure the least well rated point (ESP calls it the 'principal point de vigilance') while giving a value near the bottom of the scale, where 10 means the highest exposure: EST 1,6; DNK 2,2; CHE 2,3; FIN 2,5; AUT 2,5; BEL 3,4; GBR 3,5; ESP 3,7. The pillar 'Risques naturels' also covers preparedness (boilerplate B15), so the exposure figure does not explain the pillar score shown.
findings.expected: Name the driver of the low pillar, for example preparedness, with its own value and meaning. Do not present a near-zero exposure figure as the main point of vigilance.
findings.verification: opus: EST SUMMARY: 'le moins bien noté est l'exposition aux risques naturels : 1,6 sur 10 selon INFORM, 10 correspondant à l'exposition la plus forte', while the pillar is 8.3. ESP calls an exposure of 3.7 its 'principal point de vigilance'. The quoted figure is near best-in-class and does not explain a weakness. This is confusing rather than false.

findings.quote: Restez attentif aux risques spécifiques détaillés plus bas.
findings.problem: Generic filler [B7], used on 64 pages in the 'Oui, avec quelques précautions' answers. It names no risk and points to detail the sentence does not supply.
findings.expected: Replace it with the named top risk, e.g. 'Le principal point d'attention est la criminalité (5.2/10)'.
findings.verification: opus: [B7] 'Restez attentif aux risques spécifiques détaillés plus bas.' is on 64 pages, e.g. CPV. It is generic filler of the kind the blogger criticised, though the same answer later names the weak pillars, so the harm is minor.

findings.quote: aucun ne le place au-dessus d'un avis de faible niveau
findings.problem: The template claims that no government places the country above a 'faible niveau' advisory, but the same page's SUMMARY reports issuers recommending 'une vigilance renforcée', which is above normal precautions. NRU: SUMMARY '3 recommandent une vigilance renforcée' while FAQ Q4 says 'aucun ne le place au-dessus d'un avis de faible niveau'. POL: 3 'vigilance renforcée' with the same sentence. PLW: 2 'vigilance renforcée' with the same sentence. The sentence is only true if 'faible niveau' is meant to include 'vigilance renforcée', which a reader will not infer.
findings.expected: Replace with the actual distribution ('la plupart recommandent les précautions habituelles ; N recommandent une vigilance renforcée') instead of a comparative claim that the tally contradicts.
findings.verification: opus: The sentence appears where some issuers are at level 2: NRU 3, POL 3, PLW 2, PRI 2, REU 1. It is not strictly false if level 2 counts as low, but right after a SUMMARY that lists 'vigilance renforcée' counts it reads as contradictory or vague. Minor wording issue.

findings.quote: et tout voyage exige une grande prudence
findings.problem: For 'Non' verdicts the FAQ1 template says 'tout voyage exige une grande prudence', which softens the verdict. UKR's SUMMARY reports 21 of 24 governments 'déconseillent formellement tout voyage', YEM 21 of 21 and VEN 6 of 20. The phrase reads as 'travel is possible with care' and is at odds with the 'Non' answer and the advisory counts.
findings.expected: For 'Non' verdicts, state the advisory picture plainly (e.g. 'la plupart des gouvernements déconseillent tout voyage') instead of the generic 'exige une grande prudence'.
findings.verification: opus: The 'Non' FAQ1 template on UKR, YEM and VEN ends with 'et tout voyage exige une grande prudence'. On YEM (21 of 21 do not travel) and UKR (21 of 24) this generic clause implies travel is fine with care. The answer still opens with 'Non' and 'haut risque', so the softening is mild.

findings.quote: l'avviso più severo — usare maggiore prudenza — arriva da Stati Uniti e Canada.
findings.problem: When the prevailing advice is also the most severe level, the sentence calls the same advice 'the most severe' and names two governments as if they stand out. Same on ATA (Antartide), BHS, CHN, CIV ('usare maggiore prudenza — arriva da Germania e Francia'), CRI, DOM and FRA. The reader cannot tell whether any government went further.
findings.expected: State the top-level count (e.g. 'tutti i 5 governi raccomandano maggiore prudenza') or drop 'più severo' when every advisory is equal.
findings.verification: opus: CHN FAQ: 'L'indicazione prevalente è di usare maggiore prudenza in Cina; l'avviso più severo — usare maggiore prudenza — arriva da Stati Uniti e Canada', although 11 of 20 governments are at that level. The same happens on CIV ('arriva da Germania e Francia'). It suggests that only two governments issued the top level.

findings.quote: Per contro, il pilastro rischi naturali ottiene 5.4/10 ed è l'area più solida di Repubblica Democratica del Congo.
findings.problem: The strongest pillar is described as a strength on pages in the 'rischio alto' band: COD (3.8/10) calls rischi naturali 5.4 'l'area più solida'; CAF (3.7/10) 'Per contro, il pilastro rischi naturali ottiene 5.9/10 ed è l'area più solida'; AFG (3.6/10) 'il pilastro criminalità ottiene 5.0/10 ed è l'area più solida di Afghanistan'; BFA (4.1/10) 'ottiene 6.1/10 ed è l'area più solida'. The top-risk sentence is generic too: 'Il rischio principale è un clima di violenza e insicurezza' (AFG SUMMARY) and 'La principale criticità è un clima di violenza e insicurezza' (BHR, BLR, BDI, BRA) name no concrete hazard, and the GPI figure that follows does not say what the danger is.
findings.expected: On high-risk pages describe the strongest pillar as 'meno critico' rather than a strength, and name the concrete hazard behind the GPI value.
findings.verification: opus: The quotes are on the pages (COD 5.4, CAF 5.9, BFA 6.1 'l'area più solida'). 'La principale criticità è un clima di violenza e insicurezza' appears 6 times as a generic stand-in for the GPI overall score. The sentences are relatively true but frame mid-scale values on high-risk pages as solid, and they name no concrete hazard. This is wording quality rather than wrong data, so low.

findings.quote: e viaggiare richiede grande prudenza
findings.problem: On 11 pages (PRK, PSE, RUS, SDN, SOM, SSD, SYR, TCD, UKR, VEN, YEM) FAQ Q1 answers 'No' and says travel 'richiede grande prudenza', while FAQ Q3 on the same page says most governments advise against travel ('La maggior parte dei governi sconsiglia ormai del tutto i viaggi in Ucraina'). UKR: SUMMARY '21 sconsigliano qualsiasi viaggio' out of 24; SSD: 20 of 21; SOM: 16 of 20. Q1 softens a majority 'do not travel' advice into 'grande prudenza'.
findings.expected: When most issuers advise against all travel, Q1 should say so as well (for example 'la maggior parte dei governi sconsiglia di viaggiare').
findings.verification: opus: UKR and SOM Q1 read 'No — … ad alto rischio … e viaggiare richiede grande prudenza', while the same pages report 21/24 and 16/20 issuers saying do not travel. The verdict is already 'No', so this is an understatement, not a reversal, but 'grande prudenza' wrongly suggests that cautious travel is the advice.

findings.quote: O panorama geral é tranquilizador: a maioria dos governos recomenda apenas precauções normais para Aruba e nenhum o coloca acima de um aviso de baixo nível.
findings.problem: 'tranquilizador' appears on 43 of 83 pages. On 16 grey pages (ABW, AIA, ALA, AND, ASM, ATF, BES, BLM, BVT, COK, CUW, CYM, FLK, FRO, GGY, GIB) the same page says the site cannot give a score ('Ainda não podemos dar uma pontuação de segurança oficial', 'menos de quatro fontes independentes') and then calls the overall picture reassuring. On single-advisory pages 'a maioria dos governos' refers to one government (GGY: 'Em outubro de 2026, Guernsey conta com um aviso de viagem governamental.'; BVT and ALA read the same).
findings.expected: No reassurance claim on grey pages. State only what the one or two advisories say, for example 'Um governo recomenda precauções normais; não há pontuação oficial.'
findings.verification: opus: The reassurance on grey pages is about the advisories, which on ABW really are all level 1-2, so that part is not a contradiction. The real defect is on single-advisory pages: GGY, BVT and ALA say 'conta com um aviso de viagem governamental' and then 'a maioria dos governos ... nenhum o coloca', which is illogical with one government. Severity reduced to low.

findings.quote: COMMUNITY: Sentimento da comunidade Comunidade
findings.problem: The community block repeats 'comunidade' in its heading and its first label, on all 83 pages.
findings.expected: One heading ('Sentimento da comunidade') with no duplicate label.
findings.verification: opus: In ui.ts the heading is 'country.pillar.sentiment' ('Sentimento da comunidade') and the badge next to it is 'sentiment.badge' ('Comunidade'), so the community block says 'comunidade' twice (304 occurrences across the pt pages). EN and DE do the same ('Community Sentiment Community'). It is a visible redundancy, though cosmetic.

findings.quote: é fortemente puxada para o lado mais baixo, além do que já indicam seus outros pilares
findings.problem: The advisory-to-score explanation on HTI, IRN, IRQ, LBN, LBY, MLI, MMR and NER uses a calque ('puxada para o lado mais baixo') and a vague clause ('além do que já indicam seus outros pilares') that does not say how much the advisories moved the score.
findings.expected: One plain pt sentence saying what the advisory consensus does to the score.
findings.verification: opus: MLI Q3 does read 'a pontuação geral de Mali é fortemente puxada para o lado mais baixo, além do que já indicam seus outros pilares'. 'Puxada para o lado mais baixo' is an awkward calque (natural pt: 'puxada para baixo'), and 'de Mali' lacks its article. It reads clumsily but is understandable.

findings.quote: Os sinais com a pontuação mais baixa nesta área são governança (INFORM) e corrupção política (V-Dem).
findings.problem: In the governança pillar the 'lowest signals' sentence names 'governança (INFORM)' as a signal of governança, a repeated and uninformative label (MNE, MDV, HUN).
findings.expected: Name the specific INFORM indicator that is lowest.
findings.verification: opus: MNE.pt has 'a área que exige mais atenção é a de governança ... Os sinais com a pontuação mais baixa nesta área são governança (INFORM) e corrupção política (V-Dem)'. This names the pillar as its own weakest signal and tells the reader nothing new. The fix is a more descriptive indicator label (e.g. INFORM institutional/governance fragility), since INFORM has no finer sub-indicator to name here.

findings.quote: Em contrapartida, o pilar de riscos naturais obtém 5.0/10 e é a área mais forte de Sudão.
findings.problem: On high-risk pages the 'área mais forte' is still a poor score: SDN riscos naturais 5.0/10 (overall 3.4, 'risco alto'), SOM saúde 4.1/10 (overall 3.8), SSD riscos naturais 5.2/10 (overall 3.4), YEM 5.1/10 (overall 3.4), SYR saúde 5.5/10 (overall 3.7). TCD ('Seu pilar mais forte é o de riscos naturais, com 5.7/10', overall 4.3) and VEN ('O pilar mais forte de Venezuela é criminalidade (5.6/10)', overall 4.8) read the same way. Presenting the least-bad pillar as a strength contradicts the overall verdict in the same answer.
findings.expected: On pages below 5, write 'o menos fraco dos pilares, ainda em nível de risco alto' or drop the strength sentence; do not call a value under 6 an 'área mais forte'.
findings.verification: opus: SDN FAQ has 'Em contrapartida, o pilar de riscos naturais obtém 5.0/10 e é a área mais forte de Sudão.' The statement is technically the relative maximum, but it is the same generic 'strongest area' machine sentence the blogger criticised, applied where the value is itself poor. This is a style issue, not misleading.

findings.quote: Os sinais com a pontuação mais baixa nesta área são governança (INFORM) e imparcialidade da administração pública (V-Dem)
findings.problem: The 'signals' for governança include 'governança (INFORM)', which makes the sentence circular; SVK repeats the pattern ('imparcialidade da administração pública (V-Dem) e governança (INFORM)'). A reader is not told which governance sub-indicator is weak.
findings.expected: Name the sub-indicator that is actually weak (e.g. 'estado de direito (INFORM)') and state the direction of each scale in words.
findings.verification: opus: SVK.pt reads 'Os sinais com a pontuação mais baixa nesta área são imparcialidade da administração pública (V-Dem) e governança (INFORM)', and 7 pt pages contain 'governança (INFORM)'. Naming 'governança' as the weak signal inside the governance pillar is circular. The summary already uses the clearer 'fragilidade da governança', and this sentence should use that label too.

findings.quote: 目前最严厉的警告——提高警惕——来自美国和加拿大。
findings.problem: When the highest advisory level is 2 (提高警惕), the template still says 目前最严厉的警告 (the strictest warning). ATA, BHS, CHN, CIV, CRI, DOM and FRA present a mild level as the strictest, implying a severe warning from the named governments. Cause: zh a3Consensus.caution (src/lib/country-faq-copy.ts, about lines 594-600) always uses 最严厉的警告 whatever the level.
findings.expected: For a caution maximum: '最高级别的建议为提高警惕，来自…' (no government advises more than increased caution).
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on CHN, FRA, BHS and others. It is accurate in that level 2 is the max, but 最严厉 (harshest) dramatises a mild level. 来自美国和加拿大 also implies only those two, when for example 11 of 21 governments advise caution on FRA. Style-level only, not broken.

findings.quote: 最需关注的是流行病传播：INFORM评分为7.4/10，10分表示风险最高（INFORM Risk 2026）。
findings.problem: Headline names drift from the indicator names used in the FAQ boilerplate. The INFORM indicator is epidemic and disease RISK (boilerplate B17 names it 流行病与疾病风险（INFORM）), but 流行病传播 (epidemic spread) reads as an active outbreak. Same drift: 就医不便 in SUMMARY vs 医疗服务可及性（INFORM）in the FAQ. 流行病传播 appears on AZE, BOL, BRB, BRN, BTN, CIV and GHA.
findings.expected: Use the indicator names: 流行病与疾病风险（INFORM）and 医疗服务可及性（INFORM）.
findings.verification: opus: The SUMMARY on BOL, AZE and others says 最需关注的是流行病传播, while the FAQ boilerplate (B15/B17) calls the same INFORM indicator 流行病与疾病风险（INFORM）. AGO's SUMMARY 就医不便 likewise differs from 医疗服务可及性（INFORM）. The English source ('spread of epidemics') is translated faithfully, so the drift lives in the template and is minor.

findings.quote: 该领域得分最低的指标是谋杀率（世界银行）和社会安全与治安（全球和平指数）。
findings.problem: The same World Bank homicide indicator is '每10万人中有17.7起故意杀人案' in the SUMMARY and '谋杀率（世界银行）' in the FAQ on this page (CRI; also ATG, BHS, BLZ, DMA, ECU).
findings.expected: One term in both places, e.g. 故意杀人率（每10万人）.
findings.verification: opus: CRI's SUMMARY says '每10万人中有17.7起故意杀人案' while its FAQ says '该领域得分最低的指标是谋杀率（世界银行）…'. The same World Bank intentional-homicide indicator gets two terms, and 谋杀 (murder) is not the same as 故意杀人 (intentional homicide). This repeats on about 29 pages.

findings.quote: 自然灾害（4.4/10）是海地表现最强的支柱，而拉低总分的主要是冲突（3.2/10），尤其是治理（2.4/10）。
findings.problem: On the 9 pages scoring below 5 the FAQ calls the highest pillar the strongest, though it is still in the danger or high-caution band: HTI 4.4 (page 3.7), MLI 4.9 (3.7), IRQ 5.4 (4.4), NER 5.5 (4.1), NGA 5.5 (4.9), MMR 5.6 (4.1), IRN 5.7 (3.9), LBN 5.7 (4.6), LBY 6.6 (4.8). This is the least-bad-area-as-strength pattern; HTI repeats it as 相比之下，自然灾害得分为 4.4/10，是海地表现最强的领域。
findings.expected: On pages under 5, do not call a pillar the strongest; say it is the least severe pillar, or say no pillar is reassuring.
findings.verification: opus: HTI says 自然灾害（4.4/10）是海地表现最强的支柱, and MLI and NER do the same with 4.9 and 5.5. The statement is literally true as a ranking but presents a weak pillar as a strength. This is the pattern the blogger criticised, but it is wording rather than a false fact.

findings.quote: 造成这一低分的主要指标是谋杀率（世界银行）。
findings.problem: '这一低分' (this low score) is attached to pillars that are not low: LIE crime 6.6 (page total 8.2) and GRD crime 6.2. Boilerplate B19 (造成这一低分的主要指标是自然灾害暴露程度（INFORM）。) is used whatever the score: GRC natural 6.3, MNG 6.8, MDA 6.8. B18 (造成这一低分的主要指标是社会安全与治安（全球和平指数）。) appears on KGZ crime 6.8, LKA 6.6 and LSO 6.1.
findings.expected: Use the low-score wording only below a cut-off (e.g. pillar under 5); above it say 'the weakest of its pillars is X'.
findings.verification: opus: LIE (犯罪 6.6, total 8.2) and GRD (6.2) use 造成这一低分的主要指标是谋杀率（世界银行）, calling a moderate pillar 'low'. It is only relatively low, so this is wording.

findings.quote: 这还是在其他支柱已有表现的基础之上
findings.problem: Calque-like phrasing on 9 pages (PRK, PSE, RUS, SDN, SOM, SSD, SYR, UKR, YEM). The sentence about severe warnings ends with 这还是在其他支柱已有表现的基础之上. A native editor would not write it, and it turns a travel-advisory answer into a formula explanation.
findings.expected: One natural sentence in a methodology context, for example: 当多数政府建议避免前往时，这一信号会明显拉低总分，叠加在其他支柱的表现之上.
findings.verification: opus: The sentence appears verbatim on the severe-advisory FAQ answer of many pages (also AFG, BFA, BLR, PRK). It reads as translationese and is understandable, so it is a style and template issue, not a misleading one.

findings.quote: 请留意下方列出的具体风险。
findings.problem: Filler marker [B7] on 64 pages. The sentence says nothing concrete, the list it points to is not shown in the answer, and it sits between the verdict and the strongest-pillar sentence.
findings.expected: Name the top risk in the same sentence, for example the lowest pillar and its score, or drop the filler.
findings.verification: opus: B7 points to 'specific risks listed below', but what follows (for example on AGO and BEN) is three sentences of formula boilerplate before any risk is named. It is generic filler of the kind the blogger criticised.

findings.quote: the strongest current warning — exercise increased caution — comes from United States and Canada.
findings.problem: On seven pages (HKG, IDN, KGZ, LKA, MDV, MYS, NCL) the 'strongest current warning' is the same level as the 'prevailing guidance' stated one clause earlier ('exercise increased caution'). The superlative adds nothing and suggests a stronger warning exists when it does not.
findings.expected: If no government advises more than increased caution, say so directly, for example 'No government advises more than increased caution; the most common advice is to exercise increased caution.'
findings.verification: opus: HKG FAQ: 'The prevailing guidance is to exercise increased caution ...; the strongest current warning — exercise increased caution — comes from United States and Canada.' The same pattern appears on 23 en pages. IDN names US and Canada as the source although 19 governments advise increased caution, and MYS names UK and Germany out of 14. The superlative is redundant and singles out two issuers arbitrarily.

findings.quote: die schärfste aktuelle Warnung — erhöhte Vorsicht walten lassen — stammt von Vereinigte Staaten und Australien
findings.problem: On PAN, PER, PRY, SLV, SWZ, TKM, TLS, UZB and XKX the 'schärfste aktuelle Warnung' is the moderate label 'erhöhte Vorsicht walten lassen', which is also the prevailing recommendation in the same answer. The superlative and the attribution make a moderate level sound like the top warning, and 'Warnung' is used for what is a 'Hinweis' level.
findings.expected: Say 'die strengste Empfehlung auf dieser Seite ist erhöhte Vorsicht (von X und Y)', or name the highest level present explicitly.
findings.verification: opus: PAN FAQ: 'Die vorherrschende Empfehlung lautet, ... erhöhte Vorsicht walten zu lassen; die schärfste aktuelle Warnung — erhöhte Vorsicht walten lassen — stammt von Vereinigte Staaten und Australien.' When the strictest level equals the prevailing one, the clause is redundant. Crediting it to only two issuers implies they are stricter than the rest. 'von Vereinigte Staaten' also lacks the article and case ('von den Vereinigten Staaten'). This is mainly a style problem.

findings.quote: l'avertissement le plus sévère — redoubler de vigilance — émane de Canada et Australie
findings.problem: The 'most severe' warning is labelled with the same wording as the dominant one in the sentence before it ('La consigne dominante est de redoubler de vigilance'). The reader cannot tell which level is the strictest, and it is also a missing-article case ('émane de Canada et Australie').
findings.expected: Give the strictest issuer's real label and level, e.g. 'l'avertissement le plus sévère, « vigilance renforcée », émane du Canada et de l'Australie', distinct from the dominant consigne.
findings.verification: opus: SLV FAQ reads 'La consigne dominante est de redoubler de vigilance … l'avertissement le plus sévère — redoubler de vigilance — émane de Canada et Australie'. The SLV advisories max out at Niveau 2 (14 issuers), so the strictest level equals the dominant one. The clause is redundant and arbitrarily singles out two of 14 level-2 issuers. The same text is on PRY and TKM.

findings.quote: Japan has a safety score of 8.1/10
findings.problem: Judgement call, and close to violating an ordering. Japan (8.1, rank 33) sits below Italy (8.2, rank 29), although Japan has lower homicide (0.2 vs 0.6 per 100,000), lower GPI overall (1.49 vs 1.71) and GPI safety-and-security (1.30 vs 1.66), and better INFORM governance (1.9 vs 4.1). Italy's edge comes from natural hazards (Japan exposure 8.3 vs Italy 4.9, weighted 10%) and health access. Most travel-risk comparisons would put Japan ahead.
findings.expected: Japan should rank at or above Italy, or the formula should explain why natural-hazard exposure outweighs crime and governance.
findings.verification: opus: Data confirm JPN 8.14 vs ITA 8.22. Japan is better on conflict (0.86 vs 0.82), crime (0.87 vs 0.83) and governance (0.80 vs 0.72), and loses only on health and natural hazards (0.44, partly from 2 transient GDACS alerts). Ranking Japan below Italy goes against the usual travel-risk consensus. The gap is small, so this is low severity, but the ordering constraint is sensible.

findings.quote: LIE | Liechtenstein | 8.2 | 30 | excellent | conf=9.0 crim=6.6 heal=9.3 gove=7.2 envi=8.3 | L1x18 | 5.1 (2021) | 0 (2025) | none (0 votes)
findings.problem: Liechtenstein's crime pillar (6.6) is well below Italy's (8.3) and Canada's (8.3). The likely cause is the 2021 homicide rate of 5.1 per 100k, which for a population of roughly 40,000 is about two homicides. All 18 listed advisories are Level 1, and Liechtenstein is widely regarded as one of Europe's lowest-crime countries. The small-population damping meant to prevent this kind of noise does not seem to be doing its job here. The band (excellent) does not change.
findings.expected: Liechtenstein at or above 8.5, in line with Denmark and Ireland (8.8), given Level 1 advisories and very low crime.
findings.verification: opus: LIE is 8.2, tied with ITA (8.2) and well below its neighbours CHE (8.9) and AUT (8.7), even though all 18 of its advisories are L1. latest.json shows the cause is not the 5.1 homicide rate, which normalises to 0.91 and is heavily damped. The real cause is that GPI does not cover Liechtenstein, so the crime pillar (0.66) and conflict/governance collapse toward the conservative prior. I replaced the absolute 8.5 bound with a relative one that survives a change of scale: Liechtenstein, with L1 advisories and no terrorism or hazard profile, is clearly safer for travellers than Italy (L2 advisories, petty crime, terrorism, seismic and volcanic hazards).

findings.quote: SDN | Sudan | 3.4 | rank 192 | danger ; SSD | South Sudan | 3.4 | rank 191 | danger
findings.problem: Sudan and South Sudan are tied at 3.4, but Sudan is the far more violent place: 75,044 UCDP conflict deaths in 2025 against 280 in South Sudan, a conflict pillar of 2.1 against 3.2, and 18 L4 advisories against 20 for South Sudan. Almost any travel-safety expert would rank Sudan as the more dangerous of the two. The tie is a sign the formula saturates at the bottom of the scale.
findings.expected: Sudan should sit clearly below South Sudan, by at least 0.3 points.
findings.verification: opus: Rows check out: both 3.4, Sudan conflict pillar 2.1 vs 3.2 and 75,044 vs 280 UCDP deaths. In October 2026 Sudan is still in a full-scale civil war, with famine, mass atrocities, embassies suspended and airports hit. South Sudan is extremely dangerous too, but Juba stays operational for NGOs and the UN. Sudan below South Sudan is robust; I loosened the margin to a strict ordering (at least 0.1-0.2), because both sit at the floor of the scale.

findings.quote: SDN | Sudan | 3.4 | 192 | danger | conf=2.1 crim=3.9 heal=4.3 gove=2.5 envi=5.0 | L3x2 L4x18 | - | 75,044 (2025)  ||  SSD | South Sudan | 3.4 | 191 | danger | conf=3.2 crim=2.9 heal=4.1 gove=1.6 envi=5.2 | L3x1 L4x20 | - | 280 (2025)
findings.problem: Sudan and South Sudan both show 3.4. Sudan ranks last only by a rounding margin. Sudan had 75,044 UCDP conflict deaths in 2025 against 280 for South Sudan, and its conflict pillar is 2.1 against 3.2. Sudan's war is the deadliest active conflict in this batch, so an expert would rank Sudan clearly less safe. The current order holds by under 0.3 points, so a formula that ties or inverts the pair should be penalised.
findings.expected: Sudan rated less safe than South Sudan by at least 0.3, given the conflict-death gap of roughly 270 times.
findings.verification: opus: The rows are correct: both places are 3.4, SDN with 75,044 UCDP deaths and conflict 2.1, SSD with 280 deaths and conflict 3.2. Sudan's nationwide civil war (the RSF, the fall of El Fasher, the world's largest displacement crisis, embassies closed) makes it less safe than South Sudan by expert consensus, even though South Sudan is also all-L4 with severe crime. Because both sit at the scale floor, the constraint should use only a small margin rather than 0.3.

findings.quote: TCD | Chad | 4.3 | 176 | danger | conf=4.7 crim=4.1 heal=3.9 gove=1.6 envi=5.7 | L2x3 L3x10 L4x8 | - | 41 (2025)  ||  BFA | Burkina Faso | 4.1 | 177 | danger | conf=2.9 crim=4.5 heal=4.7 gove=4.7 envi=6.1 | L3x6 L4x14 | - | 4,333 (2025)
findings.problem: The current order is correct, but the margin is only 0.2. Burkina Faso has 4,333 UCDP conflict deaths in 2025 against 41 for Chad, and its conflict pillar is 2.9 against Chad's 4.7. Burkina also has 14 Level 4 advisories out of 20, against 8 of 21 for Chad. Almost any travel-safety expert would put Chad ahead of Burkina Faso, so a formula that narrows or inverts this gap should be penalised.
findings.expected: Chad rated safer than Burkina Faso by at least 0.3, given the conflict gap and the advisory gap.
findings.verification: opus: The rows are correct: TCD is 4.3 (conflict 4.7, 41 UCDP deaths, 8 of 21 advisories at L4) and BFA is 4.1 (conflict 2.9, 4,333 deaths, 14 of 20 at L4). Burkina Faso is among the world's most terrorism-affected countries, with most of its territory under jihadist threat and nearly every government at L4. Chad is dangerous but less so, with N'Djamena comparatively stable, so the ordering is robust; the margin required in the comparison should stay modest.

findings.quote: Community Noch nicht genügend Stimmen (1/30 Stimmen, 0/3 Herkunftsländer)
findings.problem: One vote is reported from zero origin countries. Other pages with one vote show one origin country, e.g. BDI: 'Community Noch nicht genügend Stimmen (1/30 Stimmen, 1/3 Herkunftsländer)'. The same figures appear in the COMMUNITY line.
findings.expected: Count origin countries from the same vote set (one vote means at least one origin), or show 'Herkunftsland unbekannt'.
findings.verification: opus: GGY.de shows '(1/30 Stimmen, 0/3 Herkunftsländer)', and latest.json has GGY community votes=1, origins=0. One vote counted with zero origin countries is inconsistent; the vote was probably stored with no country code and the origin count skips it.

findings.quote: 投票还不够（1/30 票，来自 0/3 个国家或地区）
findings.problem: One vote cannot come from zero countries. The same figure appears in the HERO of this grey page. Vote count and country count are apparently computed from different sources, or the vote has no country code.
findings.expected: Show the country tally from the votes actually received (1 of 3 if the vote has a country), or omit the country tally when the vote's country is unknown.
findings.verification: opus: The GGY HERO and COMMUNITY block show '1/30 票，来自 0/3 个国家或地区'. One vote from zero countries is nonsense on display, probably a vote with an unknown country_iso being counted in votes but not in countries.

findings.quote: Non ci sono ancora abbastanza voti (1/30 voti, 0/3 paesi di provenienza)
findings.problem: One vote is shown with zero countries of origin (JEY; NLD shows the same '1/30 voti, 0/3 paesi di provenienza'). Votes store a country code from request.cf.country, so a vote with no code could be legitimate, but the page shows a number that reads as an error. This is a data check, not a language fix.
findings.expected: Show votes without a country under their own figure, or explain 'voti senza paese' on the page.
findings.verification: opus: latest.json has JEY community votes:1, origins:0 and NLD votes:1, origins:0, and the pages show '1/30 voti, 0/3 paesi di provenienza'. A vote counted with no country of origin (request.cf.country missing or unknown) looks like an error to readers.

findings.quote: A principal preocupação é a criminalidade violenta: 5,1 homicídios por 100 mil habitantes (Banco Mundial, 2021).
findings.problem: The year is labelled, so this is not shown as current. But the 'principal preocupação' rests on a 2021 figure, while other pages cite 2023 World Bank data for the same indicator, so the vintage is inconsistent across the site.
findings.expected: Use the latest available year for the indicator, or do not call it the main concern.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on LIE.pt. 2021 is the only and latest WB homicide value in latest.json for LIE, so the 'inconsistent vintage' claim is wrong. The real problem: in a country of about 39k people, 5.1/100k is about 2 killings, statistical noise, yet the summary makes it the 'principal preocupação' of an 8.2/10 country (crime pillar 6.6 is fed only by this indicator). That is the 'biggest concern' framing the blogger criticised.

findings.quote: （1/30 票，来自 0/3 个国家或地区）
findings.problem: The community line reports 1 vote from 0 of 3 countries or regions. A vote needs at least one country; other pages with one vote show 1/3.
findings.expected: Show at least 1 country when there is at least 1 vote, for example 1/30 票，来自 1/3 个国家或地区.
findings.verification: opus: TUN.zh shows （1/30 票，来自 0/3 个国家或地区）. Six zh pages show 1 vote from 0 countries, while 69 others show 1/3, so a vote with no stored voter country is counted as a vote but not as a country. Accurate to the stored data, but it reads as impossible.

findings.quote: TWN | Taiwan | 7.9 | 41 | good | conf=8.5 crim=7.5 heal=6.7 gove=8.0 envi=6.2 | L1x17 | - | 0 (2025) | none (4 votes)
findings.problem: All 17 government advisories for Taiwan are Level 1 (normal precautions), with no Level 2 or higher in this batch. Taiwan has one of the world's best universal healthcare systems, yet its health pillar (6.7) sits below China (7.2) and Mongolia (7.7). That pillar pulls Taiwan to 7.9, just under the 8.0 'excellent' threshold, while Japan (8.1, with four Level 2 advisories) passes it.
findings.expected: Taiwan at 8.0 or higher, to match its advisory profile and the healthcare evidence. The current score is only 0.1 below the excellent band.
findings.verification: opus: In latest.json Taiwan's health and environment pillars have no indicators at all (INFORM does not cover Taiwan), and the crime pillar has no homicide input (the World Bank does not cover Taiwan). So the 6.7 health score is just the prior, which puts Taiwan below China and Mongolia; it is not real evidence. The exact 8.0 band-edge bound is calibration taste: Taiwan's GPI is worse than Japan's because of cross-strait tension, and its real natural-hazard exposure is high. I loosened the bound to 7.5, which still holds with a margin for a place where all 17 advisories are Level 1 and crime is low.

findings.quote: Impartial public administration (V-Dem)
findings.problem: Three V-Dem rows sit in the traveller table beside disaster, health and crime rows: Rule of law, Impartial public administration (a latent scale described only as 'about -4 to +4'), and Political corruption. They describe long-run institutions, and a traveller cannot act on them. Impartial public administration is the least actionable and its scale is not explained beyond that phrase. Examples: ERI (-1.72), DOM (0.44), EST (3.32).
findings.expected: Move these rows to a background group or to the methodology page, with a one-line plain-language note on what they mean for a visitor. Keep the traveller-actionable rows (disasters, health access, crime) in the main table.
findings.verification: opus: On every scored page with V-Dem, three V-Dem rows sit in the traveller table. 'Impartial public administration' is explained only as 'scale about −4 to +4', e.g. EGY −0.99 and DOM 0.44. This is the kind of indicator a traveller cannot use that the blogger criticised, but it is low impact.

findings.quote: Impartial public administration (V-Dem) | −1.29
findings.problem: V-Dem governance rows (rule of law, impartial public administration, political corruption) appear on 24 of the 26 scored pages, and INFORM governance on all 26; together they make up the Governance pillar (15%). They are national institutional indices on abstract scales (e.g. 'scale about −4 to +4'), and a traveller cannot act on them directly. Corruption has some practical bearing (bribe demands), but impartial public administration does not; HTI's '−1.29' tells a traveller nothing actionable.
findings.expected: Keep the governance context in a methodology note, or relabel the rows with a traveller-facing consequence, and drop impartial public administration from the displayed traveller indicators.
findings.verification: opus: The quoted row is on HTI.en ('Impartial public administration (V-Dem) | −1.29 | scale about −4 to +4'). The same three V-Dem rows appear on DEU.en (3.99) and ECU.en (−0.94), and on 174 English pages in total. The raw value on an abstract latent scale means nothing to a traveller and is the same kind of 'irrelevant indicator' the blogger complained about. It still feeds a real pillar, so this is a presentation problem, not a data error.

findings.quote: Sentiment della community Community Non ci sono ancora abbastanza voti
findings.problem: The label repeats 'community' ('Sentiment della community Community') in the HERO and COMMUNITY blocks of every page that has them. 'Sentiment' is also an English word in the label.
findings.expected: A single label, e.g. 'Opinione della community' or 'Community'.
findings.verification: opus: In SentimentBlock the h2 'Sentiment della community' sits directly next to a pill badge 'Community', so the label is visibly redundant. 'Sentiment' is a common Italian anglicism and not an error. This is a style issue only.

findings.quote: 最高级别的警告——切勿前往——已由美国和加拿大等国发布。
findings.problem: The top advisory tier is 避免一切旅行 in the SUMMARY but 切勿前往 in the FAQ on the same page (19 pages, for example PRK: 12个建议避免一切旅行 in the SUMMARY and 切勿前往 in the FAQ).
findings.expected: One label per advisory tier per page, matching the wording used on the advisory cards.
findings.verification: opus: The PRK.zh SUMMARY says 12个建议避免一切旅行, while the FAQ on the same page says 最高级别的警告——切勿前往. 51 zh pages use 切勿前往, so one tier carries two labels on the same page.

findings.quote: 最需关注的是流行病传播
findings.problem: SUMMARY names indicators differently from the boilerplate: 流行病传播 (boilerplate: 流行病与疾病风险（INFORM）), 就医不便 (boilerplate: 医疗服务可及性（INFORM）), 社会治安欠佳 (boilerplate: 社会安全与治安（全球和平指数）). PRY and OMN use the first set while the FAQ boilerplate uses the second, on the same pages.
findings.expected: Use the same indicator names in SUMMARY, FAQ and boilerplate.
findings.verification: opus: The same INFORM epidemic indicator has three names on PRY/OMN: 流行病传播 in the SUMMARY, 流行病风险（INFORM） in the pillar bars and 流行病与疾病风险（INFORM） in the FAQ. 流行病传播 in the SUMMARY also suggests an outbreak is under way, which a risk index does not show.

findings.quote: Is It Safe to Travel to Saint Barthelemy Right Now?
findings.problem: The English name is missing the é ('Saint Barthélemy'). The only accepted spelling exception is the Åland name, so this should be fixed. The same spelling appears in the SUMMARY.
findings.expected: Saint Barthélemy, in the HERO, title and SUMMARY.
findings.verification: opus: The BLM HERO and SUMMARY say 'Saint Barthelemy'. The standard English and ISO name is 'Saint Barthélemy', and only the Åland spelling is on the accepted list.

findings.quote: TITLE: Is Congo Safe? 5.6/10 Safety Score (2026)
findings.problem: The page is the Republic of the Congo, but 'Congo' alone is ambiguous with the Democratic Republic of the Congo page ('Is the Democratic Republic of the Congo Safe?', COD).
findings.expected: 'Is the Republic of the Congo Safe?' in TITLE, H1 and the FAQ.
findings.verification: opus: COG TITLE 'Is Congo Safe?' and H1 'Is It Safe to Travel to Congo Right Now?' are next to COD's 'Democratic Republic of the Congo'. 'Congo' is the UN short name, but on a travel-safety site it is ambiguous with the far more dangerous DRC.

findings.quote: Latest published value: the World Bank publishes with a 1–2 year lag. | 4.0 | per 100,000 people | World Bank | 2021
findings.problem: The row is labelled 'Latest published value' and the note says the World Bank lags 1–2 years, but the year shown is 2021 (AFG). BEL shows 1.1 for 2021 with the same wording. Both are about five years before the page's 'Last updated: October 15, 2026'. The value still feeds the crime pillar as if it were current. The year is shown, so this is a wording and staleness issue rather than a hidden one.
findings.expected: Say that the figure is the latest available and how old it is, or drop the 'Latest published value' wording where the year is more than about two years old. Check whether newer World Bank values exist.
